texts.2sa.19.9: Y todo el pueblo porfiaba en todas las tribus de Israel, diciendo: El rey nos ha librado de mano de nuestros enemigos, y él nos ha salvado de mano de los Filisteos; y ahora había huído, de la tierra por miedo de Abaslom.
texts.2sa.19.10: Y Absalom, á quien habíamos ungido sobre nosotros, es muerto en la batalla. ¿Por qué pues os estáis ahora quedos en orden á hacer volver al rey?
texts.2sa.19.11: Y el rey David envió á Sadoc y á Abiathar sacerdotes, diciendo: Hablad á los ancianos de Judá y decidles: ¿Por qué seréis vosotros los postreros en volver el rey á su casa, ya que la palabra de todo Israel ha venido al rey de volverle á su casa?
texts.2sa.19.12: Vosotros sois mis hermanos; mis huesos y mi carne sois: ¿por qué pues seréis vosotros los postreros en volver al rey?
texts.2sa.19.13: Asimismo diréis á Amasa: ¿No eres tú también hueso mío y carne mía? Así me haga Dios, y así me añada, si no fueres general del ejército delante de mí para siempre, en lugar de Joab.
texts.2sa.19.14: Así inclinó el corazón de todos los varones de Judá, como el de un solo hombre, para que enviasen á decir al rey: Vuelve tú, y todos tus siervos.
texts.2sa.19.15: Volvió pues el rey, y vino hasta el Jordán. Y Judá vino á Gilgal, á recibir al rey y pasarlo el Jordán.
texts.2sa.19.16: Y Semei hijo de Gera, hijo de Benjamín, que era de Bahurim, dióse priesa á venir con los hombres de Judá á recibir al rey David;
texts.2sa.19.17: Y con él venían mil hombres de Benjamín; asimismo Siba criado de la casa de Saúl, con sus quince hijos y sus veinte siervos, los cuales pasaron el Jordán delante del rey.
texts.2sa.19.18: Atravesó después la barca para pasar la familia del rey, y para hacer lo que le pluguiera. Entonces Semei hijo de Gera se postró delante del rey cuando él había pasado el Jordán.
texts.2sa.19.19: Y dijo al rey: No me impute mi señor iniquidad, ni tengas memoria de los males que tu siervo hizo el día que mi señor el rey salió de Jerusalem, para guardarlos el rey en su corazón;
texts.2sa.19.20: Porque yo tu siervo conozco haber pecado, y he venido hoy el primero de toda la casa de José, para descender á recibir á mi señor el rey.
texts.2sa.19.21: Y Abisai hijo de Sarvia responidió y dijo: ¿No ha de morir por esto Semei, que maldijo al ungido de Jehová?
texts.2sa.19.22: David entonces dijo: ¿Qué tenéis vosotros conmigo, hijos de Sarvia, que me habéis de ser hoy adversarios? ¿ha de morir hoy alguno en Israel? ¿no conozco yo que hoy soy rey sobre Israel?
texts.2sa.19.23: Y dijo el rey á Semei: No morirás. Y el rey se lo juró.
texts.2sa.19.24: También Mephi-boseth hijo de Saúl descendió á recibir al rey: no había lavado sus pies, ni había cortado su barba, ni tampoco había lavado sus vestidos, desde el día que el rey salió hasta el día que vino en paz.
texts.2sa.19.25: Y luego que vino él á Jerusalem á recibir al rey, el rey le dijo: Mephi-boseth, ¿Por qué no fuiste conmigo?
texts.2sa.19.26: Y él dijo: Rey señor mío, mi siervo me ha engañado; pues había tu siervo dicho: Enalbardaré un asno, y subiré en él, é iré al rey; porque tu siervo es cojo.
texts.2sa.19.27: Empero él revolvió á tu siervo delante de mi señor el rey; mas mi señor el rey es como un ángel de Dios: haz pues lo que bien te pareciere.
texts.2sa.19.28: Porque toda la casa de mi padre era digna de muerte delante de mi señor el rey, y tú pusiste á tu siervo entre los convidados de tu mesa. ¿Qué derecho pues tengo aún para quejarme más contra el rey?
texts.2sa.19.29: Y el rey le dijo: ¿Para qué hablas más palabras? Yo he determinado que tú y Siba partáis las tierras.
texts.2sa.19.30: Y Mephi-boseth dijo al rey: Y aun tómelas él todas, pues que mi señor el rey ha vuelto en paz á su casa.
texts.2sa.19.31: También Barzillai Galaadita descendió de Rogelim, y pasó el Jordán con el rey, para acompañarle de la otra parte del Jordán.
texts.2sa.19.32: Y era Barzillai muy viejo, de ochenta años, el cual había dado provisión al rey cuando estaba en Mahanaim, porque era hombre muy rico.
texts.2sa.19.33: Y el rey dijo á Barzillai: Pasa conmigo, y yo te daré de comer conmigo en Jerusalem.
texts.2sa.19.34: Mas Barzillai dijo al rey: ¿Cuántos son los días del tiempo de mi vida, para que yo suba con el rey á Jerusalem?
texts.2sa.19.35: Yo soy hoy día de edad de ochenta años, que ya no haré diferencia entre lo bueno y lo malo: ¿tomará gusto ahora tu siervo en lo que comiere ó bebiere? ¿oiré más la voz de los cantores y de las cantoras? ¿para qué, pues, sería aún tu siervo molesto á mi se
texts.2sa.19.36: Pasará tu siervo un poco el Jordán con el rey: ¿por qué me ha de dar el rey tan grande recompensa?
texts.2sa.19.37: Yo te ruego que dejes volver á tu siervo, y que muera en mi ciudad, junto al sepulcro de mi padre y de mi madre. He aquí tu siervo Chimham; que pase él con mi señor el rey, y hazle lo que bien te pareciere.
texts.2sa.19.38: Y el rey dijo: Pues pase conmigo Chimham, y yo haré con él como bien te parezca: y todo lo que tú pidieres de mí, yo lo haré.
texts.2sa.19.39: Y todo el pueblo pasó el Jordán: y luego que el rey hubo también pasado, el rey besó á Barzillai, y bendíjolo; y él se volvió á su casa.
texts.2sa.19.40: El rey entonces pasó á Gilgal, y con él pasó Chimham; y todo el pueblo de Judá, con la mitad del pueblo de Israel, pasaron al rey.
texts.2sa.19.41: Y he aquí todos los varones de Israel vinieron al rey, y le dijeron: ¿Por qué los hombres de Judá, nuestros hermanos, te han llevado, y han hecho pasar el Jordán al rey y á su familia, y á todos los varones de David con él?
texts.2sa.19.42: Y todos los varones de Judá respondieron á todos los de Israel: Porque el rey es nuestro pariente. Mas ¿por qué os enojáis vosotros de eso? ¿hemos nosotros comido algo del rey? ¿hemos recibido de él algún don?
texts.2sa.19.43: Entonces respondieron los varones de Israel, y dijeron á los de Judá: Nosotros tenemos en el rey diez partes, y en el mismo David más que vosotros: ¿por qué pues nos habéis tenido en poco? ¿no hablamos nosotros primero en volver á nuestro rey? Y el razona
texts.2sa.20.1: Y ACAECIO estar allí un hombre perverso que se llamaba Seba, hijo de Bichri, hombre de Benjamín, el cual tocó la corneta, y dijo: No tenemos nosotros parte en David, ni heredad en el hijo de Isaí: Israel, ­cada uno á sus estancias!
texts.2sa.20.2: Así se fueron de en pos de David todos los hombres de Israel, y seguían á Seba hijo de Bichri: mas los de Judá fueron adheridos á su rey, desde el Jordán hasta Jerusalem.
texts.2sa.20.3: Y luego que llegó David á su casa en Jerusalem, tomó el rey las diez mujeres concubinas que había dejado para guardar la casa, y púsolas en una casa en guarda, y dióles de comer: pero nunca más entró á ellas, sino que quedaron encerradas hasta que muriero
texts.2sa.20.4: Después dijo el rey á Amasa: Júntame los varones de Judá para dentro de tres días, y hállate tú aquí presente.
texts.2sa.20.5: Fué pues Amasa á juntar á Judá; pero detúvose más del tiempo que le había sido señalado.
texts.2sa.20.6: Y dijo David á Abisai: Seba hijo de Bichri nos hará ahora más mal que Absalom: toma pues tú los siervos de tu señor, y ve tras él, no sea que halle las ciudades fortificadas, y se nos vaya de delante.
texts.2sa.20.7: Entonces salieron en pos de él los hombres de Joab, y los Ceretheos y Peletheos, y todos los valientes: salieron de Jerusalem para ir tras Seba hijo de Bichri.
texts.2sa.20.8: Y estando ellos cerca de la grande peña que está en Gabaón, salióles Amasa al encuentro. Ahora bien, la vestidura que Joab tenía sobrepuesta estábale ceñida, y sobre ella el cinto de una daga pegada á sus lomos en su vaina, de la que así como él avanzó, c
texts.2sa.20.9: Entonces Joab dijo á Amasa: ¿Tienes paz, hermano mío? Y tomó Joab con la diestra la barba de Amasa, para besarlo.
texts.2sa.20.10: Y como Amasa no se cuidó de la daga que Joab en la mano tenía, hirióle éste con ella en la quinta costilla, y derramó sus entrañas por tierra, y cayó muerto sin darle segundo golpe. Después Joab y su hermano Abisai fueron en seguimiento de Seba hijo de Bi
texts.2sa.20.11: Y uno de los criados de Joab se paró junto á él, diciendo: Cualquiera que amare á Joab y á David vaya en pos de Joab.
texts.2sa.20.12: Y Amasa se había revolcado en la sangre en mitad del camino: y viendo aquel hombre que todo el pueblo se paraba, apartó á Amasa del camino al campo, y echó sobre él una vestidura, porque veía que todos los que venían se paraban junto á él.
texts.2sa.20.13: Luego, pues, que fué apartado del camino, pasaron todos los que seguían á Joab, para ir tras Seba hijo de Bichri.
texts.2sa.20.14: Y él pasó por todas las tribus de Israel hasta Abel y Beth-maachâ y todo Barim: y juntáronse, y siguiéronlo también.
texts.2sa.20.15: Y vinieron y cercáronlo en Abel de Beth-maachâ, y pusieron baluarte contra la ciudad; y puesto que fué al muro, todo el pueblo que estaba con Joab trabajaba por derribar la muralla.
texts.2sa.20.16: Entonces una mujer sabia dió voces en la ciudad, diciendo: Oid, oid; ruégoos que digáis á Joab se llegue á acá, para que yo hable con él.
texts.2sa.20.17: Y como él se acercó á ella, dijo la mujer: ¿Eres tú Joab? Y él respondió: Yo soy. Y ella le dijo: Oye las palabras de tu sierva. Y él respondió: Oigo.
texts.2sa.20.18: Entonces tornó ella á hablar, diciendo: Antiguamente solían hablar, diciendo: Quien preguntare, pregunte en Abel: y así concluían.
texts.2sa.20.19: Yo soy de las pacíficas y fieles de Israel: y tú procuras destruir una ciudad que es madre de Israel: ¿por qué destruyes la heredad de Jehová?
texts.2sa.20.20: Y Joab respondió, diciendo: Nunca tal, nunca tal me acontezca, que yo destruya ni deshaga.
texts.2sa.20.21: La cosa no es así: mas un hombre del monte de Ephraim, que se llama Seba hijo de Bichri, ha levantado su mano contra el rey David: entregad á ése solamente, y me iré de la ciudad. Y la mujer dijo á Joab: He aquí su cabeza te será echada desde el muro.
texts.2sa.20.22: La mujer fué luego á todo el pueblo con su sabiduría; y ellos cortaron la cabeza á Seba hijo de Bichri, y echáronla á Joab. Y él tocó la corneta, y esparciéronse de la ciudad, cada uno á su estancia. Y Joab se volvió al rey á Jerusalem.
texts.2sa.20.23: Así quedó Joab sobre todo el ejército de Israel; y Benaía hijo de Joiada sobre los Ceretheos y Peletheos;
texts.2sa.20.24: Y Adoram sobre los tributos; y Josaphat hijo de Ahillud, el canciller;
texts.2sa.20.25: Y Seba, escriba; y Sadoc y Abiathar, sacerdotes;
texts.2sa.20.26: é Ira Jaireo fué un jefe principal cerca de David.
texts.2sa.21.1: Y EN los días de David hubo hambre por tres años consecutivos. Y David consultó á Jehová, y Jehová le dijo: Es por Saúl, y por aquella casa de sangre; porque mató á los Gabaonitas.
texts.2sa.21.2: Entonces el rey llamó á los Gabaonitas, y hablóles. (Los Gabaonitas no eran de los hijos de Israel, sino del residuo de los Amorrheos, á los cuales los hijos de Israel habían hecho juramento: mas Saúl había procurado matarlos con motivo de celo por los hi
texts.2sa.21.3: Dijo pues David á los Gabaonitas: ¿Qué os haré, y con qué expiaré para que bendigáis á la heredad de Jehová?
texts.2sa.21.4: Y los Gabaonitas le respondieron: No tenemos nosotros querella sobre plata ni sobre oro con Saúl, y con su casa: ni queremos que muera hombre de Israel. Y él les dijo: Lo que vosotros dijereis os haré.
texts.2sa.21.5: Y ellos respondieron al rey: De aquel hombre que nos destruyó, y que maquinó contra nosotros, para extirparnos sin dejar nada de nosotros en todo el término de Israel;
texts.2sa.21.6: Dénsenos siete varones de sus hijos, para que los ahorquemos á Jehová en Gabaa de Saúl, el escogido de Jehová. Y el rey dijo: Yo los daré.
texts.2sa.21.7: Y perdonó el rey á Mephi-boseth, hijo de Jonathán, hijo de Saúl, por el juramento de Jehová que hubo entre ellos, entre David y Jonathán hijo de Saúl.
texts.2sa.21.8: Mas tomó el rey dos hijos de Rispa hija de Aja, los cuales ella había parido á Saúl, á saber, á Armoni y á Mephi-boseth; y cinco hijos de Michâl hija de Saúl, los cuales ella había parido á Adriel, hijo de Barzillai Molathita;
texts.2sa.21.9: Y entrególos en manos de los Gabaonitas, y ellos los ahorcaron en el monte delante de Jehová: y murieron juntos aquellos siete, lo cuales fueron muertos en el tiempo de la siega, en los primeros días, en el principio de la siega de las cebadas.
texts.2sa.21.10: Tomando luego Rispa hija de Aja un saco, tendióselo sobre un peñasco, desde el principio de la siega hasta que llovió sobre ellos agua del cielo; y no dejó á ninguna ave del cielo asentarse sobre ellos de día, ni bestias del campo de noche.
texts.2sa.21.11: Y fué dicho á David lo que hacía Rispa hija de Aja, concubina de Saúl.
texts.2sa.21.12: Entonces David fué, y tomó los huesos de Saúl y los huesos de Jonathán su hijo, de los hombres de Jabes de Galaad, que los habían hurtado de la plaza de Beth-san, donde los habían colgado los Filisteos, cuando deshicieron los Filisteos á Saúl en Gilboa:
texts.2sa.21.13: E hizo llevar de allí los huesos de Saúl y los huesos de Jonathán su hijo; y juntaron también los huesos de los ahorcados.
texts.2sa.21.14: Y sepultaron los huesos de Saúl y los de su hijo Jonathán en tierra de Benjamín, en Sela, en el sepulcro de Cis su padre; é hicieron todo lo que el rey había mandado. Después se aplacó Dios con la tierra.
texts.2sa.21.15: Y como los Filisteos tornaron á hacer guerra á Israel, descendió David y sus siervos con él, y pelearon con los Filisteos: y David se cansó.
texts.2sa.21.16: En esto Isbi-benob, el cual era de los hijos del gigante, y el peso de cuya lanza era de trescientos siclos de metal, y tenía él ceñida una nueva espada, trató de herir á David:
texts.2sa.21.17: Mas Abisai hijo de Sarvia le socorrió, é hirió al Filisteo, y matólo. Entonces los hombres de David le juraron, diciendo: Nunca más de aquí adelante saldrás con nosotros á batalla, porque no apagues la lámpara de Israel.
texts.2sa.21.18: Otra segunda guerra hubo después en Gob contra los Filisteos: entonces Sibechâi Husathita hirió á Saph, que era de los hijos del gigante.
texts.2sa.21.19: Otra guerra hubo en Gob contra los Filisteos, en la cual Elhanan, hijo de Jaare-oregim de Beth-lehem, hirió á Goliath Getheo, el asta de cuya lanza era como un enjullo de telar.
texts.2sa.21.20: Después hubo otra guerra en Gath, donde hubo un hombre de grande altura, el cual tenía doce dedos en las manos, y otros doce en los pies, veinticuatro en todos: y también era de lo hijos del gigante.
texts.2sa.21.21: Este desafió á Israel, y matólo Jonathán, hijo de Sima hermano de David.
texts.2sa.21.22: Estos cuatro le habían nacido al gigante en Gath, los cuales cayeron por la mano de David, y por la mano de sus siervos.
texts.2sa.22.1: Y HABLO David á Jehová las palabras de este cántico, el día que Jehová le había librado de la mano de todos sus enemigos, y de la mano de Saúl.
texts.2sa.22.2: Y dijo: Jehová es mi roca, y mi fortaleza, y mi libertador;
texts.2sa.22.3: Dios de mi roca, en él confiaré: Mi escudo, y el cuerno de mi salud, mi fortaleza, y mi refugio; Mi salvador, que me librarás de violencia.
texts.2sa.22.4: Invocaré á Jehová, digno de ser loado. Y seré salvo de mis enemigos.
texts.2sa.22.5: Cuando me cercaron ondas de muerte, Y arroyos de iniquidad me asombraron,
texts.2sa.22.6: Me rodearon los dolores del infierno, Y me tomaron descuidado lazos de muerte.
texts.2sa.22.7: Tuve angustia, invoqué á Jehová, Y clamé á mi Dios: Y él oyó mi voz desde su templo; Llegó mi clamor á sus oídos.
texts.2sa.22.8: La tierra se removió, y tembló; Los fundamentos de los cielos fueron movidos, Y se estremecieron, porque él se airó.
texts.2sa.22.9: Subió humo de sus narices, Y de su boca fuego consumidor, Por el cual se encendieron carbones.
texts.2sa.22.10: Y abajo los cielos, y descendió: Una oscuridad debajo de sus pies.
texts.2sa.22.11: Subió sobre el querubín, y voló: Aparecióse sobre las alas del viento.
texts.2sa.22.12: Puso tinieblas alrededor de sí á modo de pabellones; Aguas negras y espesas nubes.
texts.2sa.22.13: Del resplandor de su presencia Se encendieron ascuas ardientes.
texts.2sa.22.14: Jehová tronó desde los cielos, Y el Altísimo dió su voz;
texts.2sa.22.15: Arrojó saetas, y desbaratólos; Relampagueó, y consumiólos.
texts.2sa.22.16: Entonces aparecieron los manantiales de la mar, Y los fundamentos del mundo fueron descubiertos, A la reprensión de Jehová, Al resoplido del aliento de su nariz.
texts.2sa.22.17: Extendió su mano de lo alto, y arrebatóme, Y sacóme de copiosas aguas.
texts.2sa.22.18: Libróme de fuertes enemigos, De aquellos que me aborrecían, los cuales eran más fuertes que yo.
texts.2sa.22.19: Asaltáronme en el día de mi calamidad; Mas Jehová fué mi sostén.
texts.2sa.22.20: Sacóme á anchura; Libróme, porque puso su voluntad en mí.
texts.2sa.22.21: Remuneróme Jehová conforme á mi justicia: Y conforme á la limpieza de mis manos, me dió la paga.
texts.2sa.22.22: Porque yo guardé los caminos de Jehová; Y no me aparté impíamente de mi Dios.
texts.2sa.22.23: Porque delante de mí tengo todas sus ordenanzas; Y atento á sus fueros, no me retiraré de ellos.
texts.2sa.22.24: Y fuí íntegro para con él, Y guardéme de mi iniquidad.
texts.2sa.22.25: Remuneróme por tanto Jehová conforme á mi justicia, Y conforme á mi limpieza delante de sus ojos.
texts.2sa.22.26: Con el bueno eres benigno, Y con el íntegro te muestras íntegro;
texts.2sa.22.27: Limpio eres para con el limpio, Mas con el perverso eres rígido.
texts.2sa.22.28: Y tú salvas al pueblo humilde; Mas tus ojos sobre los altivos, para abatirlos.
texts.2sa.22.29: Porque tú eres mi lámpara, oh Jehová: Jehová da luz á mis tinieblas.
texts.2sa.22.30: Porque en ti romperé ejércitos, Y con mi Dios saltaré las murallas.
texts.2sa.22.31: Dios, perfecto su camino: La palabra de Jehová purificada, Escudo es de todos los que en él esperan.
texts.2sa.22.32: Porque ¿qué Dios hay sino Jehová? ¿O quién es fuerte sino nuestro Dios?
texts.2sa.22.33: Dios es el que con virtud me corrobora, y el que despeja mi camino;
texts.2sa.22.34: El que hace mis pies como de ciervas, Y el que me asienta en mis alturas;
texts.2sa.22.35: El que enseña mis manos para la pelea, y da que con mis brazos quiebre el arco de acero.
texts.2sa.22.36: Tú me diste asimismo el escudo de tu salud, Y tu benignidad me ha acrecentado.
texts.2sa.22.37: Tú ensanchaste mis pasos debajo de mí, Para que no titubeasen mis rodillas.
texts.2sa.22.38: Perseguiré á mis enemigos, y quebrantarélos; Y no me volveré hasta que los acabe.
texts.2sa.22.39: Los consumiré, y los heriré, y no se levantarán; Y caerán debajo de mis pies.
texts.2sa.22.40: Ceñísteme de fortaleza para la batalla, Y postraste debajo de mí los que contra mí se levantaron.
texts.2sa.22.41: Tú me diste la cerviz de mis enemigos, De mis aborrecedores, y que yo los destruyese.
texts.2sa.22.42: Miraron, y no hubo quien los librase; A Jehová, mas no les respondió.
texts.2sa.22.43: Yo los desmenuzaré como polvo de la tierra; Hollarélos como á lodo de las plazas, y los disiparé.
texts.2sa.22.44: Tú me libraste de contiendas de pueblos: Tú me guardaste para que fuese cabeza de gentes: Pueblos que no conocía, me sirvieron.
texts.2sa.22.45: Los extraños titubeaban á mí: En oyendo, me obedecían.
texts.2sa.22.46: Los extraños desfallecían, Y temblaban en sus escondrijos.
texts.2sa.22.47: Viva Jehová, y sea bendita mi roca; Sea ensalzado el Dios, la roca de mi salvamento:
texts.2sa.22.48: El Dios que me ha vengado, Y sujeta los pueblos debajo de mí:
texts.2sa.22.49: Y que me saca de entre mis enemigos: Tu me sacaste en alto de entre los que se levantaron contra mi: Librásteme del varón de iniquidades.
texts.2sa.22.50: Por tanto yo te confesaré entre las gentes, oh Jehová, Y cantaré á tu nombre.
texts.2sa.22.51: El que engrandece las saludes de su rey, Y hace misericordia á su ungido, A David, y á su simiente, para siempre.
texts.2sa.23.1: ESTAS son las postreras palabras de David. Dijo David hijo de Isaí, Dijo aquel varón que fué levantado alto, El ungido del Dios de Jacob, El suave en cánticos de Israel:
texts.2sa.23.2: El espíritu de Jehová ha hablado por mí, Y su palabra ha sido en mi lengua.
texts.2sa.23.3: El Dios de Israel ha dicho, Hablóme el Fuerte de Israel: El señoreador de los hombres será justo. Señoreador en temor de Dios.
texts.2sa.23.4: Será como la luz de la mañana cuando sale el sol, De la mañana sin nubes; Cuando la hierba de la tierra brota Por medio del resplandor después de la lluvia.
texts.2sa.23.5: No así mi casa para con Dios: Sin embargo él ha hecho conmigo pacto perpetuo, Ordenado en todas las cosas, y será guardado; Bien que toda esta mi salud, y todo mi deseo No lo haga él florecer todavía.
texts.2sa.23.6: Mas los de Belial serán todos ellos como espinas arrancadas, Las cuales nadie toma con la mano;
texts.2sa.23.7: Sino que el que quiere tocar en ellas, Armase de hierro y de asta de lanza, Y son quemadas en su lugar.
texts.2sa.23.8: Estos son los nombres de los valientes que tuvo David: El Tachmonita, que se sentaba en cátedra, principal de los capitanes: era éste Adino el Eznita, que mató en una ocasión sobre ochocientos hombres.
texts.2sa.23.9: Después de éste, Eleazar, hijo de Dodo de Ahohi, fué de los tres valientes que estaban con David, cuando desafiaron á los Filisteos que se habían juntado allí á la batalla, y subieron los de Israel.
texts.2sa.23.10: Este, levantándose, hirió á los Filisteos, hasta que su mano se cansó, y quedósele contraída á la espada. Aquel día Jehová hizo gran salud: y volvióse el pueblo en pos de él solamente á tomar el despojo.
texts.2sa.23.11: Después de éste fué Samma, hijo de Age Araita: que habiéndose juntado los Filisteos en una aldea, había allí una suerte de tierra llena de lentejas, y el pueblo había huído delante de los Filisteos:
texts.2sa.23.12: El entonces se paró en medio de la suerte de tierra, y defendióla, é hirió á los Filisteos; y Jehová hizo una gran salud.
texts.2sa.23.13: Y tres de los treinta principales descendieron y vinieron en tiempo de la siega á David á la cueva de Adullam: y el campo de los Filisteos estaba en el valle de Raphaim.
texts.2sa.23.14: David entonces estaba en la fortaleza, y la guarnición de los Filisteos estaba en Beth-lehem.
texts.2sa.23.15: Y David tuvo deseo, y dijo: ­Quién me diera á beber del agua de la cisterna de Beth-lehem, que está á la puerta!
texts.2sa.23.16: Entonces los tres valientes rompieron por el campo de los Filisteos, y sacaron agua de la cisterna de Beth-lehem, que estaba á la puerta; y tomaron, y trajéronla á David: mas él no la quiso beber, sino derramóla á Jehová, diciendo:
texts.2sa.23.17: Lejos sea de mí, oh Jehová, que yo haga esto. ¿He de beber yo la sangre de los varones que fueron con peligro de su vida? Y no quiso beberla. Los tres valientes hicieron esto.
texts.2sa.23.18: Y Abisai hermano de Joab, hijo de Sarvia, fué el principal de los tres; el cual alzó su lanza contra trescientos, que mató; y tuvo nombre entre los tres.
texts.2sa.23.19: El era el más aventajado de los tres, y el primero de ellos; mas no llegó á los tres primeros.
texts.2sa.23.20: Después, Benaía hijo de Joiada, hijo de un varón esforzado, grande en hechos, de Cabseel. Este hirió dos leones de Moab: y él mismo descendió, é hirió un león en medio de un foso en el tiempo de la nieve:
texts.2sa.23.21: También hirió él á un Egipcio, hombre de grande estatura: y tenía el Egipcio una lanza en su mano; mas descendió á él con un palo, y arrebató al Egipcio la lanza de la mano, y matólo con su propia lanza.
texts.2sa.23.22: Esto hizo Benaía hijo de Joiada, y tuvo nombre entre los tres valientes.
texts.2sa.23.23: De los treinta fué el más aventajado; pero no llegó á los tres primeros. Y púsolo David en su consejo.
texts.2sa.23.24: Asael hermano de Joab fué de los treinta; Elhaanan hijo de Dodo de Beth-lehem;
texts.2sa.23.25: Samma de Harodi, Elica de Harodi;
texts.2sa.23.26: Heles de Palti, Hira, hijo de Jecces, de Tecoa;
texts.2sa.23.27: Abiezer de Anathoth, Mebunnai de Husa;
texts.2sa.23.28: Selmo de Hahoh, Maharai de Netophath;
texts.2sa.23.29: Helec hijo de Baana de Netophath, Ittai hijo de Ribai de Gabaa de los hijos de Benjamín;
texts.2sa.23.30: Benaía Pirathonita, Hiddai del arroyo de Gaas;
texts.2sa.23.31: Abi-albon de Arbath, Asmaveth de Barhum;
texts.2sa.23.32: Elihaba de Saalbón, Jonathán de los hijo de Jassén;
texts.2sa.23.33: Samma de Arar, Ahiam hijo de Sarar de Arar.
texts.2sa.23.34: Elipheleth hijo de Asbai hijo de Maachâti; Eliam hijo de Achîtophel de Gelón;
texts.2sa.23.35: Hesrai del Carmelo, Pharai de Arbi;
texts.2sa.23.36: Igheal hijo de Nathán de Soba, Bani de Gadi;
texts.2sa.23.37: Selec de Ammón, Naharai de Beeroth, escudero de Joab hijo de Sarvia;
texts.2sa.23.38: Ira de Ithri, Gareb de Ithri;
texts.2sa.23.39: Uría Hetheo. Entre todos treinta y siete.
texts.2sa.24.1: Y VOLVIO el furor de Jehová á encenderse contra Israel, é incitó á David contra ellos á que dijese: Ve, cuenta á Israel y á Judá.
texts.2sa.24.2: Y dijo el rey á Joab, general del ejército que tenía consigo: Rodea todas las tribus de Israel, desde Dan hasta Beer-seba, y contad el pueblo, para que yo sepa el número de la gente.
texts.2sa.24.3: Y Joab respondió al rey: Añada Jehová tu Dios al pueblo cien veces tanto como son, y que lo vea mi señor al rey; mas ¿para qué quiere esto mi señor el rey?
texts.2sa.24.4: Empero la palabra del rey pudo más que Joab, y que los capitanes del ejército. Salió pues Joab, con los capitanes del ejército, de delante del rey, para contar el pueblo de Israel.
texts.2sa.24.5: Y pasando el Jordán asentaron en Aroer, á la mano derecha de la ciudad que está en medio de la arroyada de Gad y junto á Jazer.
texts.2sa.24.6: Después vinieron á Galaad, y á la tierra baja de Absi: y de allí vinieron á Dan-jaán y alrededor de Sidón.
texts.2sa.24.7: Y vinieron luego á la fortaleza de Tiro, y á todas las ciudades de los Heveos y de los Cananeos; y salieron al mediodía de Judá, á Beer-seba.
texts.2sa.24.8: Y después que hubieron andado toda la tierra, volvieron á Jerusalem al cabo de nueve meses y veinte días.
texts.2sa.24.9: Y Joab dió la cuenta del número del pueblo al rey; y fueron los de Israel ochocientos mil hombres fuertes que sacaban espada; y de los de Judá quinientos mil hombres.
texts.2sa.24.10: Y después que David hubo contado el pueblo, punzóle su corazón; y dijo David á Jehová: Yo he pecado gravemente por haber hecho esto; mas ahora, oh Jehová, ruégote que quites el pecado de tu siervo, porque yo he obrado muy neciamente.
texts.2sa.24.11: Y por la mañana, cuando David se hubo levantado, fué palabra de Jehová á Gad profeta, vidente de David, diciendo:
texts.2sa.24.12: Ve, y di á David: Así ha dicho Jehová: Tres cosas te ofrezco: tú te escogerás una de ellas, la cual yo haga.
texts.2sa.24.13: Vino pues Gad á David, é intimóle, y díjole: ¿Quieres que te vengan siete años de hambre en tu tierra? ¿ó que huyas tres meses delante de tus enemigos, y que ellos te persigan? ¿o que tres días haya pestilencia en tu tierra? Piensa ahora, y mira qué respo
texts.2sa.24.14: Entonces David dijo á Gad: En grande angustia estoy: ruego que caiga en la mano de Jehová, porque sus miseraciones son muchas, y que no caiga yo en manos de hombres.
texts.2sa.24.15: Y envió Jehová pestilencia á Israel desde la mañana hasta el tiempo señalado: y murieron del pueblo, desde Dan hasta Beer-seba, setenta mil hombres.
texts.2sa.24.16: Y como el ángel extendió su mano sobre Jerusalem para destruirla, Jehová se arrepintió de aquel mal, y dijo al ángel que destruía el pueblo: Basta ahora; detén tu mano. Entonces el ángel de Jehová estaba junto á la era de Arauna Jebuseo.
texts.2sa.24.17: Y David dijo á Jehová, cuando vió al ángel que hería al pueblo: Yo pequé, yo hice la maldad: ¿qué hicieron estas ovejas? Ruégote que tu mano se torne contra mí, y contra la casa de mi padre.
texts.2sa.24.18: Y Gad vino á David aquel día, y díjole: Sube, y haz un altar á Jehová en la era de Arauna Jebuseo.
texts.2sa.24.19: Y subió David, conforme al dicho de Gad, que Jehová le había mandado.
texts.2sa.24.20: Y mirando Arauna, vió al rey y á sus siervos que pasaban á él. Saliendo entonces Arauna, inclinóse delante del rey hacia tierra.
texts.2sa.24.21: Y Arauna dijo: ¿Por qué viene mi señor el rey á su siervo? Y David respondió: Para comprar de ti la era, para edificar altar á Jehová, á fin de que la mortandad cese del pueblo.
texts.2sa.24.22: Y Arauna dijo á David: Tome y sacrifique mi señor el rey lo que bien le pareciere; he aquí bueyes para el holocausto; y trillos y otros pertrechos de bueyes para leña:
texts.2sa.24.23: Todo lo da como un rey Arauna al rey. Luego dijo Arauna al rey: Jehová tu Dios te sea propicio.
texts.2sa.24.24: Y el rey dijo á Arauna: No, sino por precio te lo compraré; porque no ofreceré á Jehová mi Dios holocaustos por nada. Entonces David compró la era y los bueyes por cincuenta siclos de plata.
texts.2sa.24.25: Y edificó allí David un altar á Jehová, y sacrificó holocaustos y pacíficos; y Jehová se aplacó con la tierra, y cesó la plaga de Israel.

texts.2sa.1.1: And it came to pass after the death of Saul, when David was returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites, and David had abode two days in Ziklag;
texts.2sa.1.2: it came to pass on the third day, that, behold, a man came out of the camp from Saul, with his clothes rent, and earth upon his head: and so it was, when he came to David, that he fell to the earth, and did obeisance.
texts.2sa.1.3: And David said unto him, From whence comest thou? And he said unto him, Out of the camp of Israel am I escaped.
texts.2sa.1.4: And David said unto him, How went the matter? I pray thee, tell me. And he answered, The people are fled from the battle, and many of the people also are fallen and dead; and Saul and Jonathan his son are dead also.
texts.2sa.1.5: And David said unto the young man that told him, How knowest thou that Saul and Jonathan his son are dead?
texts.2sa.1.6: And the young man that told him said, As I happened by chance upon mount Gilboa, behold, Saul was leaning upon his spear; and, lo, the chariots and the horsemen followed hard after him.
texts.2sa.1.7: And when he looked behind him, he saw me, and called unto me. And I answered, Here am I.
texts.2sa.1.8: And he said unto me, Who art thou? And I answered him, I am an Amalekite.
texts.2sa.1.9: And he said unto me, Stand, I pray thee, beside me, and slay me; for anguish hath taken hold of me, because my life is yet whole in me.
texts.2sa.1.10: So I stood beside him, and slew him, because I was sure that he could not live after that he was fallen: and I took the crown that was upon his head, and the bracelet that was on his arm, and have brought them hither unto my lord.
texts.2sa.1.11: Then David took hold on his clothes, and rent them; and likewise all the men that were with him:
texts.2sa.1.12: and they mourned, and wept, and fasted until even, for Saul, and for Jonathan his son, and for the people of Jehovah, and for the house of Israel; because they were fallen by the sword.
texts.2sa.1.13: And David said unto the young man that told him, Whence art thou? And he answered, I am the son of a sojourner, an Amalekite.
texts.2sa.1.14: And David said unto him, How wast thou not afraid to put forth thy hand to destroy Jehovah's anointed?
texts.2sa.1.15: And David called one of the young men, and said, Go near, and fall upon him. And he smote him, so that he died.
texts.2sa.1.16: And David said unto him, Thy blood be upon thy head; for thy mouth hath testified against thee, saying, I have slain Jehovah's anointed.
texts.2sa.1.17: And David lamented with this lamentation over Saul and over Jonathan his son
texts.2sa.1.18: (and he bade them teach the children of Judah [the song of] the bow: behold, it is written in the book of Jashar):
texts.2sa.1.19: Thy glory, O Israel, is slain upon thy high places! How are the mighty fallen!
texts.2sa.1.20: Tell it not in Gath, Publish it not in the streets of Ashkelon; Lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, Lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph.
texts.2sa.1.21: Ye mountains of Gilboa, Let there be no dew nor rain upon you, neither fields of offerings: For there the shield of the mighty was vilely cast away, The shield of Saul, not anointed with oil.
texts.2sa.1.22: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, The bow of Jonathan turned not back, And the sword of Saul returned not empty.
texts.2sa.1.23: Saul and Jonathan were lovely and pleasant in their lives, And in their death they were not divided: They were swifter than eagles, They were stronger than lions.
texts.2sa.1.24: Ye daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, Who clothed you in scarlet delicately, Who put ornaments of gold upon your apparel.
texts.2sa.1.25: How are the mighty fallen in the midst of the battle! Jonathan is slain upon thy high places.
texts.2sa.1.26: I am distressed for thee, my brother Jonathan: Very pleasant hast thou been unto me: Thy love to me was wonderful, Passing the love of women.
texts.2sa.1.27: How are the mighty fallen, And the weapons of war perished!
texts.2sa.2.1: And it came to pass after this, that David inquired of Jehovah, saying, Shall I go up into any of the cities of Judah? And Jehovah said unto him, Go up. And David said, Whither shall I go up? And he said, Unto Hebron.
texts.2sa.2.2: So David went up thither, and his two wives also, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
texts.2sa.2.3: And his men that were with him did David bring up, every man with his household: and they dwelt in the cities of Hebron.
texts.2sa.2.4: And the men of Judah came, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah. And they told David, saying, The men of Jabesh-gilead were they that buried Saul.
texts.2sa.2.5: And David sent messengers unto the men of Jabesh-gilead, and said unto them, Blessed be ye of Jehovah, that ye have showed this kindness unto your lord, even unto Saul, and have buried him.
texts.2sa.2.6: And now Jehovah show lovingkindness and truth unto you: and I also will requite you this kindness, because ye have done this thing.
texts.2sa.2.7: Now therefore let your hands be strong, and be ye valiant; for Saul your lord is dead, and also the house of Judah have anointed me king over them.
texts.2sa.2.8: Now Abner the son of Ner, captain of Saul's host, had taken Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, and brought him over to Mahanaim;
texts.2sa.2.9: and he made him king over Gilead, and over the Ashurites, and over Jezreel, and over Ephraim, and over Benjamin, and over all Israel.
texts.2sa.2.10: Ish-bosheth, Saul's son, was forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and he reigned two years. But the house of Judah followed David.
texts.2sa.2.11: And the time that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.
texts.2sa.2.12: And Abner the son of Ner, and the servants of Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.
texts.2sa.2.13: And Joab the son of Zeruiah, and the servants of David, went out, and met them by the pool of Gibeon; and they sat down, the one on the one side of the pool, and the other on the other side of the pool.
texts.2sa.2.14: And Abner said to Joab, Let the young men, I pray thee, arise and play before us. And Joab said, Let them arise.
texts.2sa.2.15: Then they arose and went over by number: twelve for Benjamin, and for Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, and twelve of the servants of David.
texts.2sa.2.16: And they caught every one his fellow by the head, and [thrust] his sword in his fellow's side; so they fell down together: wherefore that place was called Helkath-hazzurim, which is in Gibeon.
texts.2sa.2.17: And the battle was very sore that day: and Abner was beaten, and the men of Israel, before the servants of David.
texts.2sa.2.18: And the three sons of Zeruiah were there, Joab, and Abishai, and Asahel: and Asahel was as light of foot as a wild roe.
texts.2sa.2.19: And Asahel pursued after Abner; and in going he turned not to the right hand nor to the left from following Abner.
texts.2sa.2.20: Then Abner looked behind him, and said, Is it thou, Asahel? And he answered, It is I.
texts.2sa.2.21: And Abner said to him, Turn thee aside to thy right hand or to thy left, and lay thee hold on one of the young men, and take thee his armor. But Asahel would not turn aside from following him.
texts.2sa.2.22: And Abner said again to Asahel, Turn thee aside from following me: wherefore should I smite thee to the ground? how then should I hold up my face to Joab thy brother?
texts.2sa.2.23: Howbeit he refused to turn aside: wherefore Abner with the hinder end of the spear smote him in the body, so that the spear came out behind him; and he fell down there, and died in the same place: and it came to pass, that as many as came to the place where Asahel fell down and died stood still.
texts.2sa.2.24: But Joab and Abishai pursued after Abner: and the sun went down when they were come to the hill of Ammah, that lieth before Giah by the way of the wilderness of Gibeon.
texts.2sa.2.25: And the children of Benjamin gathered themselves together after Abner, and became one band, and stood on the top of a hill.
texts.2sa.2.26: Then Abner called to Joab, and said, Shall the sword devour for ever? knowest thou not that it will be bitterness in the latter end? how long shall it be then, ere thou bid the people return from following their brethren?
texts.2sa.2.27: And Joab said, As God liveth, if thou hadst not spoken, surely then in the morning the people had gone away, nor followed every one his brother.
texts.2sa.2.28: So Joab blew the trumpet; and all the people stood still, and pursued after Israel no more, neither fought they any more.
texts.2sa.2.29: And Abner and his men went all that night through the Arabah; and they passed over the Jordan, and went through all Bithron, and came to Mahanaim.
texts.2sa.2.30: And Joab returned from following Abner: and when he had gathered all the people together, there lacked of David's servants nineteen men and Asahel.
texts.2sa.2.31: But the servants of David had smitten of Benjamin, and of Abner's men, [so that] three hundred and threescore men died.
texts.2sa.2.32: And they took up Asahel, and buried him in the sepulchre of his father, which was in Beth-lehem. And Joab and his men went all night, and the day brake upon them at Hebron.
texts.2sa.3.1: Now there was long war between the house of Saul and the house of David: and David waxed stronger and stronger, but the house of Saul waxed weaker and weaker.
texts.2sa.3.2: And unto David were sons born in Hebron: and his first-born was Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess;
texts.2sa.3.3: and his second, Chileab, of Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite; and the third, Absalom the son of Maacah the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur;
texts.2sa.3.4: and the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith; and the fifth, Shephatiah the son of Abital;
texts.2sa.3.5: and the sixth, Ithream, of Eglah, David's wife. These were born to David in Hebron.
texts.2sa.3.6: And it came to pass, while there was war between the house of Saul and the house of David, that Abner made himself strong in the house of Saul.
texts.2sa.3.7: Now Saul had a concubine, whose name was Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah: and [Ish-bosheth] said to Abner, Wherefore hast thou gone in unto my father's concubine?
texts.2sa.3.8: Then was Abner very wroth for the words of Ish-bosheth, and said, Am I a dog's head that belongeth to Judah? This day do I show kindness unto the house of Saul thy father, to his brethren, and to his friends, and have not delivered thee into the hand of David; and yet thou chargest me this day with a fault concerning this woman.
texts.2sa.3.9: God do so to Abner, and more also, if, as Jehovah hath sworn to David, I do not even so to him;
texts.2sa.3.10: to transfer the kingdom from the house of Saul, and to set up the throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan even to Beer-sheba.
texts.2sa.3.11: And he could not answer Abner another word, because he feared him.
texts.2sa.3.12: And Abner sent messengers to David on his behalf, saying, Whose is the land? saying [also], Make thy league with me, and, behold, my hand shall be with thee, to bring about all Israel unto thee.
texts.2sa.3.13: And he said, Well; I will make a league with thee; but one thing I require of thee: that is, thou shalt not see my face, except thou first bring Michal, Saul's daughter, when thou comest to see my face.
texts.2sa.3.14: And David sent messengers to Ish-bosheth, Saul's son, saying, Deliver me my wife Michal, whom I betrothed to me for a hundred foreskins of the Philistines.
texts.2sa.3.15: And Ish-bosheth sent, and took her from her husband, even from Paltiel the son of Laish.
texts.2sa.3.16: And her husband went with her, weeping as he went, and followed her to Bahurim. Then said Abner unto him, Go, return: and he returned.
texts.2sa.3.17: And Abner had communication with the elders of Israel, saying, In times past ye sought for David to be king over you:
texts.2sa.3.18: now then do it; for Jehovah hath spoken of David, saying, By the hand of my servant David I will save my people Israel out of the hand of the Philistines, and out of the hand of all their enemies.
texts.2sa.3.19: And Abner also spake in the ears of Benjamin: and Abner went also to speak in the ears of David in Hebron all that seemed good to Israel, and to the whole house of Benjamin.
texts.2sa.3.20: So Abner came to David to Hebron, and twenty men with him. And David made Abner and the men that were with him a feast.
texts.2sa.3.21: And Abner said unto David, I will arise and go, and will gather all Israel unto my lord the king, that they may make a covenant with thee, and that thou mayest reign over all that thy soul desireth. And David sent Abner away; and he went in peace.
texts.2sa.3.22: And, behold, the servants of David and Joab came from a foray, and brought in a great spoil with them: but Abner was not with David in Hebron; for he had sent him away, and he was gone in peace.
texts.2sa.3.23: When Joab and all the host that was with him were come, they told Joab, saying, Abner the son of Ner came to the king, and he hath sent him away, and he is gone in peace.
texts.2sa.3.24: Then Joab came to the king, and said, What hast thou done? behold, Abner came unto thee; why is it that thou hast sent him away, and he is quite gone?
texts.2sa.3.25: Thou knowest Abner the son of Ner, that he came to deceive thee, and to know thy going out and thy coming in, and to know all that thou doest.
texts.2sa.3.26: And when Joab was come out from David, he sent messengers after Abner, and they brought him back from the well of Sirah: but David knew it not.
texts.2sa.3.27: And when Abner was returned to Hebron, Joab took him aside into the midst of the gate to speak with him quietly, and smote him there in the body, so that he died, for the blood of Asahel his brother.
texts.2sa.3.28: And afterward, when David heard it, he said, I and my kingdom are guiltless before Jehovah for ever of the blood of Abner the son of Ner:
texts.2sa.3.29: let it fall upon the head of Joab, and upon all his father's house; and let there not fail from the house of Joab one that hath an issue, or that is a leper, or that leaneth on a staff, or that falleth by the sword, or that lacketh bread.
texts.2sa.3.30: So Joab and Abishai his brother slew Abner, because he had killed their brother Asahel at Gibeon in the battle.
texts.2sa.3.31: And David said to Joab, and to all the people that were with him, Rend your clothes, and gird you with sackcloth, and mourn before Abner. And king David followed the bier.
texts.2sa.3.32: And they buried Abner in Hebron: and the king lifted up his voice, and wept at the grave of Abner; and all the people wept.
texts.2sa.3.33: And the king lamented for Abner, and said, Should Abner die as a fool dieth?
texts.2sa.3.34: Thy hands were not bound, nor thy feet put into fetters: As a man falleth before the children of iniquity, so didst thou fall. And all the people wept again over him.
texts.2sa.3.35: And all the people came to cause David to eat bread while it was yet day; but David sware, saying, God do so to me, and more also, if I taste bread, or aught else, till the sun be down.
texts.2sa.3.36: And all the people took notice of it, and it pleased them; as whatsoever the king did pleased all the people.
texts.2sa.3.37: So all the people and all Israel understood that day that it was not of the king to slay Abner the son of Ner.
texts.2sa.3.38: And the king said unto his servants, Know ye not that there is a prince and a great man fallen this day in Israel?
texts.2sa.3.39: And I am this day weak, though anointed king; and these men the sons of Zeruiah are too hard for me: Jehovah reward the evil-doer according to his wickedness.
texts.2sa.4.1: And when [Ish-bosheth], Saul's son, heard that Abner was dead in Hebron, his hands became feeble, and all the Israelites were troubled.
texts.2sa.4.2: And [Ish-bosheth], Saul's son, [had] two men that were captains of bands: the name of the one was Baanah, and the name of the other Rechab, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, of the children of Benjamin (for Beeroth also is reckoned to Benjamin:
texts.2sa.4.3: and the Beerothites fled to Gittaim, and have been sojourners there until this day).
texts.2sa.4.4: Now Jonathan, Saul's son, had a son that was lame of his feet. He was five years old when the tidings came of Saul and Jonathan out of Jezreel; and his nurse took him up, and fled: and it came to pass, as she made haste to flee, that he fell, and became lame. And his name was Mephibosheth.
texts.2sa.4.5: And the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, went, and came about the heat of the day to the house of Ish-bosheth, as he took his rest at noon.
texts.2sa.4.6: And they came thither into the midst of the house, as though they would have fetched wheat; and they smote him in the body: and Rechab and Baanah his brother escaped.
texts.2sa.4.7: Now when they came into the house, as he lay on his bed in his bedchamber, they smote him, and slew him, and beheaded him, and took his head, and went by the way of the Arabah all night.
texts.2sa.4.8: And they brought the head of Ish-bosheth unto David to Hebron, and said to the king, Behold, the head of Ish-bosheth, the son of Saul, thine enemy, who sought thy life; and Jehovah hath avenged my lord the king this day of Saul, and of his seed.
texts.2sa.4.9: And David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said unto them, As Jehovah liveth, who hath redeemed my soul out of all adversity,
texts.2sa.4.10: when one told me, saying, Behold, Saul is dead, thinking to have brought good tidings, I took hold of him, and slew him in Ziklag, which was the reward I gave him for his tidings.
texts.2sa.4.11: How much more, when wicked men have slain a righteous person in his own house upon his bed, shall I not now require his blood of your hand, and take you away from the earth?
texts.2sa.4.12: And David commanded his young men, and they slew them, and cut off their hands and their feet, and hanged them up beside the pool in Hebron. But they took the head of Ish-bosheth, and buried it in the grave of Abner in Hebron.
texts.2sa.5.1: Then came all the tribes of Israel to David unto Hebron, and spake, saying, Behold, we are thy bone and thy flesh.
texts.2sa.5.2: In times past, when Saul was king over us, it was thou that leddest out and broughtest in Israel: and Jehovah said to thee, Thou shalt be shepherd of my people Israel, and thou shalt be prince over Israel.
texts.2sa.5.3: So all the elders of Israel came to the king to Hebron; and king David made a covenant with them in Hebron before Jehovah: and they anointed David king over Israel.
texts.2sa.5.4: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.
texts.2sa.5.5: In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months; and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty and three years over all Israel and Judah.
texts.2sa.5.6: And the king and his men went to Jerusalem against the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, who spake unto David, saying, Except thou take away the blind and the lame, thou shalt not come in hither; thinking, David cannot come in hither.
texts.2sa.5.7: Nevertheless David took the stronghold of Zion; the same is the city of David.
texts.2sa.5.8: And David said on that day, Whosoever smiteth the Jebusites, let him get up to the watercourse, and [smite] the lame and the blind, that are hated of David's soul. Wherefore they say, There are the blind and the lame; he cannot come into the house.
texts.2sa.5.9: And David dwelt in the stronghold, and called it the city of David. And David built round about from Millo and inward.
texts.2sa.5.10: And David waxed greater and greater; for Jehovah, the God of hosts, was with him.
texts.2sa.5.11: And Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, and cedar-trees, and carpenters, and masons; and they built David a house.
texts.2sa.5.12: And David perceived that Jehovah had established him king over Israel, and that he had exalted his kingdom for his people Israel's sake.
texts.2sa.5.13: And David took him more concubines and wives out of Jerusalem, after he was come from Hebron; and there were yet sons and daughters born to David.
texts.2sa.5.14: And these are the names of those that were born unto him in Jerusalem: Shammua, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon,
texts.2sa.5.15: and Ibhar, and Elishua, and Nepheg, and Japhia,
texts.2sa.5.16: and Elishama, and Eliada, and Eliphelet.
texts.2sa.5.17: And when the Philistines heard that they had anointed David king over Israel, all the Philistines went up to seek David; and David heard of it, and went down to the stronghold.
texts.2sa.5.18: Now the Philistines had come and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.
texts.2sa.5.19: And David inquired of Jehovah, saying, Shall I go up against the Philistines? wilt thou deliver them into my hand? And Jehovah said unto David, Go up; for I will certainly deliver the Philistines into thy hand.
texts.2sa.5.20: And David came to Baal-perazim, and David smote them there; and he said, Jehovah hath broken mine enemies before me, like the breach of waters. Therefore he called the name of that place Baal-perazim.
texts.2sa.5.21: And they left their images there; and David and his men took them away.
texts.2sa.5.22: And the Philistines came up yet again, and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.
texts.2sa.5.23: And when David inquired of Jehovah, he said, Thou shalt not go up: make a circuit behind them, and come upon them over against the mulberry-trees.
texts.2sa.5.24: And it shall be, when thou hearest the sound of marching in the tops of the mulberry-trees, that then thou shalt bestir thyself; for then is Jehovah gone out before thee to smite the host of the Philistines.
texts.2sa.5.25: And David did so, as Jehovah commanded him, and smote the Philistines from Geba until thou come to Gezer.
texts.2sa.6.1: And David again gathered together all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand.
texts.2sa.6.2: And David arose, and went with all the people that were with him, from Baale-judah, to bring up from thence the ark of God, which is called by the Name, even the name of Jehovah of hosts that sitteth [above] the cherubim.
texts.2sa.6.3: And they set the ark of God upon a new cart, and brought it out of the house of Abinadab that was in the hill: and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, drove the new cart.
texts.2sa.6.4: And they brought it out of the house of Abinadab, which was in the hill, with the ark of God: and Ahio went before the ark.
texts.2sa.6.5: And David and all the house of Israel played before Jehovah with all manner of [instruments made of] fir-wood, and with harps, and with psalteries, and with timbrels, and with castanets, and with cymbals.
texts.2sa.6.6: And when they came to the threshing-floor of Nacon, Uzzah put forth [his hand] to the ark of God, and took hold of it; for the oxen stumbled.
texts.2sa.6.7: And the anger of Jehovah was kindled against Uzzah; and God smote him there for his error; and there he died by the ark of God.
texts.2sa.6.8: And David was displeased, because Jehovah had broken forth upon Uzzah; and he called that place Perez-uzzah, unto this day.
texts.2sa.6.9: And David was afraid of Jehovah that day; and he said, How shall the ark of Jehovah come unto me?
texts.2sa.6.10: So David would not remove the ark of Jehovah unto him into the city of David; but David carried it aside into the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
texts.2sa.6.11: And the ark of Jehovah remained in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite three months: and Jehovah blessed Obed-edom, and all his house.
texts.2sa.6.12: And it was told king David, saying, Jehovah hath blessed the house of Obed-edom, and all that pertaineth unto him, because of the ark of God. And David went and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obed-edom into the city of David with joy.
texts.2sa.6.13: And it was so, that, when they that bare the ark of Jehovah had gone six paces, he sacrificed an ox and a fatling.
texts.2sa.6.14: And David danced before Jehovah with all his might; and David was girded with a linen ephod.
texts.2sa.6.15: So David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of Jehovah with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet.
texts.2sa.6.16: And it was so, as the ark of Jehovah came into the city of David, that Michal the daughter of Saul looked out at the window, and saw king David leaping and dancing before Jehovah; and she despised him in her heart.
texts.2sa.6.17: And they brought in the ark of Jehovah, and set it in its place, in the midst of the tent that David had pitched for it; and David offered burnt-offerings and peace-offerings before Jehovah.
texts.2sa.6.18: And when David had made an end of offering the burnt-offering and the peace-offerings, he blessed the people in the name of Jehovah of hosts.
texts.2sa.6.19: And he dealt among all the people, even among the whole multitude of Israel, both to men and women, to every one a cake of bread, and a portion [of flesh], and a cake of raisins. So all the people departed every one to his house.
texts.2sa.6.20: Then David returned to bless his household. And Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David, and said, How glorious was the king of Israel to-day, who uncovered himself to-day in the eyes of the handmaids of his servants, as one of the vain fellows shamelessly uncovereth himself!
texts.2sa.6.21: And David said unto Michal, [It was] before Jehovah, who chose me above thy father, and above all his house, to appoint me prince over the people of Jehovah, over Israel: therefore will I play before Jehovah.
texts.2sa.6.22: And I will be yet more vile than this, and will be base in mine own sight: but of the handmaids of whom thou hast spoken, of them shall I be had in honor.
texts.2sa.6.23: And Michal the daughter of Saul had no child unto the day of her death.
texts.2sa.7.1: And it came to pass, when the king dwelt in his house, and Jehovah had given him rest from all his enemies round about,
texts.2sa.7.2: that the king said unto Nathan the prophet, See now, I dwell in a house of cedar, but the ark of God dwelleth within curtains.
texts.2sa.7.3: And Nathan said to the king, Go, do all that is in thy heart; for Jehovah is with thee.
texts.2sa.7.4: And it came to pass the same night, that the word of Jehovah came unto Nathan, saying,
texts.2sa.7.5: Go and tell my servant David, Thus saith Jehovah, Shalt thou build me a house for me to dwell in?
texts.2sa.7.6: for I have not dwelt in a house since the day that I brought up the children of Israel out of Egypt, even to this day, but have walked in a tent and in a tabernacle.
texts.2sa.7.7: In all places wherein I have walked with all the children of Israel, spake I a word with any of the tribes of Israel, whom I commanded to be shepherd of my people Israel, saying, Why have ye not built me a house of cedar?
texts.2sa.7.8: Now therefore thus shalt thou say unto my servant David, Thus saith Jehovah of hosts, I took thee from the sheepcote, from following the sheep, that thou shouldest be prince over my people, over Israel;
texts.2sa.7.9: and I have been with thee whithersoever thou wentest, and have cut off all thine enemies from before thee; and I will make thee a great name, like unto the name of the great ones that are in the earth.
texts.2sa.7.10: And I will appoint a place for my people Israel, and will plant them, that they may dwell in their own place, and be moved no more; neither shall the children of wickedness afflict them any more, as at the first,
texts.2sa.7.11: and [as] from the day that I commanded judges to be over my people Israel; and I will cause thee to rest from all thine enemies. Moreover Jehovah telleth thee that Jehovah will make thee a house.
texts.2sa.7.12: When thy days are fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will set up thy seed after thee, that shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom.
texts.2sa.7.13: He shall build a house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom for ever.
texts.2sa.7.14: I will be his father, and he shall be my son: if he commit iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men;
texts.2sa.7.15: but my lovingkindness shall not depart from him, as I took it from Saul, whom I put away before thee.
texts.2sa.7.16: And thy house and thy kingdom shall be made sure for ever before thee: thy throne shall be established for ever.
texts.2sa.7.17: According to all these words, and according to all this vision, so did Nathan speak unto David.
texts.2sa.7.18: Then David the king went in, and sat before Jehovah; and he said, Who am I, O Lord Jehovah, and what is my house, that thou hast brought me thus far?
texts.2sa.7.19: And this was yet a small thing in thine eyes, O Lord Jehovah; but thou hast spoken also of thy servant's house for a great while to come; and this [too] after the manner of men, O Lord Jehovah!
texts.2sa.7.20: And what can David say more unto thee? for thou knowest thy servant, O Lord Jehovah.
texts.2sa.7.21: For thy word's sake, and according to thine own heart, hast thou wrought all this greatness, to make thy servant know it.
texts.2sa.7.22: Wherefore thou art great, O Jehovah God: for there is none like thee, neither is there any God besides thee, according to all that we have heard with our ears.
texts.2sa.7.23: And what one nation in the earth is like thy people, even like Israel, whom God went to redeem unto himself for a people, and to make him a name, and to do great things for you, and terrible things for thy land, before thy people, whom thou redeemest to thee out of Egypt, [from] the nations and their gods?
texts.2sa.7.24: And thou didst establish to thyself thy people Israel to be a people unto thee for ever; and thou, Jehovah, becamest their God.
texts.2sa.7.25: And now, O Jehovah God, the word that thou hast spoken concerning thy servant, and concerning his house, confirm thou it for ever, and do as thou hast spoken.
texts.2sa.7.26: And let thy name be magnified for ever, saying, Jehovah of hosts is God over Israel; and the house of thy servant David shall be established before thee.
texts.2sa.7.27: For thou, O Jehovah of hosts, the God of Israel, hast revealed to thy servant, saying, I will build thee a house: therefore hath thy servant found in his heart to pray this prayer unto thee.
texts.2sa.7.28: And now, O Lord Jehovah, thou art God, and thy words are truth, and thou hast promised this good thing unto thy servant:
texts.2sa.7.29: now therefore let it please thee to bless the house of thy servant, that it may continue for ever before thee; for thou, O Lord Jehovah, hast spoken it: and with thy blessing let the house of thy servant be blessed for ever.
texts.2sa.8.1: And after this it came to pass, that David smote the Philistines, and subdued them: and David took the bridle of the mother city out of the hand of the Philistines.
texts.2sa.8.2: And he smote Moab, and measured them with the line, making them to lie down on the ground; and he measured two lines to put to death, and one full line to keep alive. And the Moabites became servants to David, and brought tribute.
texts.2sa.8.3: David smote also Hadadezer the son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he went to recover his dominion at the River.
texts.2sa.8.4: And David took from him a thousand and seven hundred horsemen, and twenty thousand footmen: and David hocked all the chariot horses, but reserved of them for a hundred chariots.
texts.2sa.8.5: And when the Syrians of Damascus came to succor Hadadezer king of Zobah, David smote of the Syrians two and twenty thousand men.
texts.2sa.8.6: Then David put garrisons in Syria of Damascus; and the Syrians became servants to David, and brought tribute. And Jehovah gave victory to David whithersoever he went.
texts.2sa.8.7: And David took the shields of gold that were on the servants of Hadadezer, and brought them to Jerusalem.
texts.2sa.8.8: And from Betah and from Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, king David took exceeding much brass.
texts.2sa.8.9: And when Toi king of Hamath heard that David had smitten all the host of Hadadezer,
texts.2sa.8.10: then Toi sent Joram his son unto king David, to salute him, and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer and smitten him: for Hadadezer had wars with Toi. And [Joram] brought with him vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and vessels of brass:
texts.2sa.8.11: These also did king David dedicate unto Jehovah, with the silver and gold that he dedicated of all the nations which he subdued;
texts.2sa.8.12: of Syria, and of Moab, and of the children of Ammon, and of the Philistines, and of Amalek, and of the spoil of Hadadezer, son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
texts.2sa.8.13: And David gat him a name when he returned from smiting the Syrians in the Valley of Salt, even eighteen thousand men.
texts.2sa.8.14: And he put garrisons in Edom; throughout all Edom put he garrisons, and all the Edomites became servants to David. And Jehovah gave victory to David whithersoever he went.
texts.2sa.8.15: And David reigned over all Israel; and David executed justice and righteousness unto all his people.
texts.2sa.8.16: And Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the host; and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder;
texts.2sa.8.17: and Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, were priests; and Seraiah was scribe;
texts.2sa.8.18: and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada [was over] the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and David's sons were chief ministers.
texts.2sa.9.1: And David said, Is there yet any that is left of the house of Saul, that I may show him kindness for Jonathan's sake?
texts.2sa.9.2: And there was of the house of Saul a servant whose name was Ziba, and they called him unto David; and the king said unto him, Art thou Ziba? And he said, Thy servant is he.
texts.2sa.9.3: And the king said, Is there not yet any of the house of Saul, that I may show the kindness of God unto him? And Ziba said unto the king, Jonathan hath yet a son, who is lame of his feet.
texts.2sa.9.4: And the king said unto him, Where is he? And Ziba said unto the king, Behold, he is in the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, in Lo-debar.
texts.2sa.9.5: Then king David sent, and fetched him out of the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, from Lo-debar.
texts.2sa.9.6: And Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came unto David, and fell on his face, and did obeisance. And David said, Mephibosheth. And he answered, Behold, thy servant!
texts.2sa.9.7: And David said unto him, Fear not; for I will surely show thee kindness for Jonathan thy father's sake, and will restore thee all the land of Saul thy father; and thou shalt eat bread at my table continually.
texts.2sa.9.8: And he did obeisance, and said, What is thy servant, that thou shouldest look upon such a dead dog as I am?
texts.2sa.9.9: Then the king called to Ziba, Saul's servant, and said unto him, All that pertained to Saul and to all his house have I given unto thy master's son.
texts.2sa.9.10: And thou shalt till the land for him, thou, and thy sons, and thy servants; and thou shalt bring in [the fruits], that thy master's son may have bread to eat: but Mephibosheth thy master's son shall eat bread alway at my table. Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.
texts.2sa.9.11: Then said Ziba unto the king, According to all that my lord the king commandeth his servant, so shall thy servant do. As for Mephibosheth, [said the king], he shall eat at my table, as one of the king's sons.
texts.2sa.9.12: And Mephibosheth had a young son, whose name was Mica. And all that dwelt in the house of Ziba were servants unto Mephibosheth.
texts.2sa.9.13: So Mephibosheth dwelt in Jerusalem; for he did eat continually at the king's table. And he was lame in both his feet.
texts.2sa.10.1: And it came to pass after this, that the king of the children of Ammon died, and Hanun his son reigned in his stead.
texts.2sa.10.2: And David said, I will show kindness unto Hanun the son of Nahash, as his father showed kindness unto me. So David sent by his servants to comfort him concerning his father. And David's servants came into the land of the children of Ammon.
texts.2sa.10.3: But the princes of the children of Ammon said unto Hanun their lord, Thinkest thou that David doth honor thy father, in that he hath sent comforters unto thee? hath not David sent his servants unto thee to search the city, and to spy it out, and to overthrow it?
texts.2sa.10.4: So Hanun took David's servants, and shaved off the one half of their beards, and cut off their garments in the middle, even to their buttocks, and sent them away.
texts.2sa.10.5: When they told it unto David, he sent to meet them; for the men were greatly ashamed. And the king said, Tarry at Jericho until your beards be grown, and then return.
texts.2sa.10.6: And when the children of Ammon saw that they were become odious to David, the children of Ammon sent and hired the Syrians of Beth-rehob, and the Syrians of Zobah, twenty thousand footmen, and the king of Maacah with a thousand men, and the men of Tob twelve thousand men.
texts.2sa.10.7: And when David heard of it, he sent Joab, and all the host of the mighty men.
texts.2sa.10.8: And the children of Ammon came out, and put the battle in array at the entrance of the gate: and the Syrians of Zobah and of Rehob, and the men of Tob and Maacah, were by themselves in the field.
texts.2sa.10.9: Now when Joab saw that the battle was set against him before and behind, he chose of all the choice men of Israel, and put them in array against the Syrians:
texts.2sa.10.10: And the rest of the people he committed into the hand of Abishai his brother; and he put them in array against the children of Ammon.
texts.2sa.10.11: And he said, If the Syrians be too strong for me, then thou shalt help me; but if the children of Ammon be too strong for thee, then I will come and help thee.
texts.2sa.10.12: Be of good courage, and let us play the man for our people, and for the cities of our God: and Jehovah do that which seemeth him good.
texts.2sa.10.13: So Joab and the people that were with him drew nigh unto the battle against the Syrians: and they fled before him.
texts.2sa.10.14: And when the children of Ammon saw that the Syrians were fled, they likewise fled before Abishai, and entered into the city. Then Joab returned from the children of Ammon, and came to Jerusalem.
texts.2sa.10.15: And when the Syrians saw that they were put to the worse before Israel, they gathered themselves together.
texts.2sa.10.16: And Hadarezer sent, and brought out the Syrians that were beyond the River: and they came to Helam, with Shobach the captain of the host of Hadarezer at their head.
texts.2sa.10.17: And it was told David; and he gathered all Israel together, and passed over the Jordan, and came to Helam. And the Syrians set themselves in array against David, and fought with him.
texts.2sa.10.18: And the Syrians fled before Israel; and David slew of the Syrians [the men of] seven hundred chariots, and forty thousand horsemen, and smote Shobach the captain of their host, so that he died there.
texts.2sa.10.19: And when all the kings that were servants to Hadarezer saw that they were put to the worse before Israel, they made peace with Israel, and served them. So the Syrians feared to help the children of Ammon any more.
texts.2sa.11.1: And it came to pass, at the return of the year, at the time when kings go out [to battle], that David sent Joab, and his servants with him, and all Israel; and they destroyed the children of Ammon, and besieged Rabbah. But David tarried at Jerusalem.
texts.2sa.11.2: And it came to pass at eventide, that David arose from off his bed, and walked upon the roof of the king's house: and from the roof he saw a woman bathing; and the woman was very beautiful to look upon.
texts.2sa.11.3: And David send and inquired after the woman. And one said, Is not this Bath-sheba, the daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?
texts.2sa.11.4: And David sent messengers, and took her; and she came in unto him, and he lay with her (for she was purified from her uncleanness); and she returned unto her house.
texts.2sa.11.5: And the woman conceived; and she sent and told David, and said, I am with child.
texts.2sa.11.6: And David sent to Joab, [saying], Send me Uriah the Hittite. And Joab sent Uriah to David.
texts.2sa.11.7: And when Uriah was come unto him, David asked of him how Joab did, and how the people fared, and how the war prospered.
texts.2sa.11.8: And David said to Uriah, Go down to thy house, and wash thy feet. And Uriah departed out of the king's house, and there followed him a mess [of food] from the king.
texts.2sa.11.9: But Uriah slept at the door of the king's house with all the servants of his lord, and went not down to his house.
texts.2sa.11.10: And when they had told David, saying, Uriah went not down unto his house, David said unto Uriah, Art thou not come from a journey? wherefore didst thou not go down unto thy house?
texts.2sa.11.11: And Uriah said unto David, The ark, and Israel, and Judah, abide in booths; and my lord Joab, and the servants of my lord, are encamped in the open field; shall I then go into my house, to eat and to drink, and to lie with my wife? as thou livest, and as thy soul liveth, I will not do this thing.
texts.2sa.11.12: And David said to Uriah, Tarry here to-day also, and to-morrow I will let thee depart. So Uriah abode in Jerusalem that day, and the morrow.
texts.2sa.11.13: And when David had called him, he did eat and drink before him; and he made him drunk: and at even he went out to lie on his bed with the servants of his lord, but went not down to his house.
texts.2sa.11.14: And it came to pass in the morning, that David wrote a letter to Joab, and sent it by the hand of Uriah.
texts.2sa.11.15: And he wrote in the letter, saying, Set ye Uriah in the forefront of the hottest battle, and retire ye from him, that he may be smitten, and die.
texts.2sa.11.16: And it came to pass, when Joab kept watch upon the city, that he assigned Uriah unto the place where he knew that valiant men were.
texts.2sa.11.17: And the men of the city went out, and fought with Joab: and there fell some of the people, even of the servants of David; and Uriah the Hittite died also.
texts.2sa.11.18: Then Joab sent and told David all the things concerning the war;
texts.2sa.11.19: and he charged the messenger, saying, When thou hast made an end of telling all the things concerning the war unto the king,
texts.2sa.11.20: it shall be that, if the king's wrath arise, and he say unto thee, Wherefore went ye so nigh unto the city to fight? knew ye not that they would shoot from the wall?
texts.2sa.11.21: who smote Abimelech the son of Jerubbesheth? did not a woman cast an upper millstone upon him from the wall, so that he died at Thebez? why went ye so nigh the wall? then shalt thou say, Thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.
texts.2sa.11.22: So the messenger went, and came and showed David all that Joab had sent him for.
texts.2sa.11.23: And the messenger said unto David, The men prevailed against us, and came out unto us into the field, and we were upon them even unto the entrance of the gate.
texts.2sa.11.24: And the shooters shot at thy servants from off the wall; and some of the king's servants are dead, and thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.
texts.2sa.11.25: Then David said unto the messenger, Thus shalt thou say unto Joab, Let not this thing displease thee, for the sword devoureth one as well as another; make thy battle more strong against the city, and overthrow it: and encourage thou him.
texts.2sa.11.26: And when the wife of Uriah heard that Uriah her husband was dead, she made lamentation for her husband.
texts.2sa.11.27: And when the mourning was past, David sent and took her home to his house, and she became his wife, and bare him a son. But the thing that David had done displeased Jehovah.
texts.2sa.12.1: And Jehovah sent Nathan unto David. And he came unto him, and said unto him, There were two men in one city; the one rich, and the other poor.
texts.2sa.12.2: The rich man had exceeding many flocks and herds;
texts.2sa.12.3: but the poor man had nothing, save one little ewe lamb, which he had bought and nourished up: and it grew up together with him, and with his children; it did eat of his own morsel, and drank of his own cup, and lay in his bosom, and was unto him as a daughter.
texts.2sa.12.4: And there came a traveller unto the rich man, and he spared to take of his own flock and of his own herd, to dress for the wayfaring man that was come unto him, but took the poor man's lamb, and dressed it for the man that was come to him.
texts.2sa.12.5: And David's anger was greatly kindled against the man; and he said to Nathan, As Jehovah liveth, the man that hath done this is worthy to die:
texts.2sa.12.6: and he shall restore the lamb fourfold, because he did this thing, and because he had no pity.
texts.2sa.12.7: And Nathan said to David, Thou art the man. Thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel, I anointed thee king over Israel, and I delivered thee out of the hand of Saul;
texts.2sa.12.8: and I gave thee thy master's house, and thy master's wives into thy bosom, and gave thee the house of Israel and of Judah; and if that had been too little, I would have added unto thee such and such things.
texts.2sa.12.9: Wherefore hast thou despised the word of Jehovah, to do that which is evil in his sight? thou hast smitten Uriah the Hittite with the sword, and hast taken his wife to be thy wife, and hast slain him with the sword of the children of Ammon.
texts.2sa.12.10: Now therefore the sword shall never depart from thy house, because thou hast despised me, and hast taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be thy wife.
texts.2sa.12.11: Thus saith Jehovah, Behold, I will raise up evil against thee out of thine own house; and I will take thy wives before thine eyes, and give them unto thy neighbor, and he shall lie with thy wives in the sight of this sun.
texts.2sa.12.12: For thou didst it secretly: but I will do this thing before all Israel, and before the sun.
texts.2sa.12.13: And David said unto Nathan, I have sinned against Jehovah. And Nathan said unto David, Jehovah also hath put away thy sin; thou shalt not die.
texts.2sa.12.14: Howbeit, because by this deed thou hast given great occasion to the enemies of Jehovah to blaspheme, the child also that is born unto thee shall surely die.
texts.2sa.12.15: And Nathan departed unto his house. And Jehovah struck the child that Uriah's wife bare unto David, and it was very sick.
texts.2sa.12.16: David therefore besought God for the child; and David fasted, and went in, and lay all night upon the earth.
texts.2sa.12.17: And the elders of his house arose, [and stood] beside him, to raise him up from the earth: but he would not, neither did he eat bread with them.
texts.2sa.12.18: And it came to pass on the seventh day, that the child died. And the servants of David feared to tell him that the child was dead; for they said, Behold, while the child was yet alive, we spake unto him, and he hearkened not unto our voice: how will he then vex himself, if we tell him that the child is dead!
texts.2sa.12.19: But when David saw that his servants were whispering together, David perceived that the child was dead; and David said unto his servants, Is the child dead? And they said, He is dead.
texts.2sa.12.20: Then David arose from the earth, and washed, and anointed himself, and changed his apparel; and he came into the house of Jehovah, and worshipped: then he came to his own house; and when he required, they set bread before him, and he did eat.
texts.2sa.12.21: Then said his servants unto him, What thing is this that thou hast done? thou didst fast and weep for the child, while it was alive; but when the child was dead, thou didst rise and eat bread.
texts.2sa.12.22: And he said, While the child was yet alive, I fasted and wept: for I said, Who knoweth whether Jehovah will not be gracious to me, that the child may live?
texts.2sa.12.23: But now he is dead, wherefore should I fast? can I bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he will not return to me.
texts.2sa.12.24: And David comforted Bath-sheba his wife, and went in unto her, and lay with her: and she bare a son, and he called his name Solomon. And Jehovah loved him;
texts.2sa.12.25: and he sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet; and he called his name Jedidiah, for Jehovah's sake.
texts.2sa.12.26: Now Joab fought against Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and took the royal city.
texts.2sa.12.27: And Joab sent messengers to David, and said, I have fought against Rabbah; yea, I have taken the city of waters.
texts.2sa.12.28: Now therefore gather the rest of the people together, and encamp against the city, and take it; lest I take the city, and it be called after my name.
texts.2sa.12.29: And David gathered all the people together, and went to Rabbah, and fought against it, and took it.
texts.2sa.12.30: And he took the crown of their king from off his head; and the weight thereof was a talent of gold, and [in it were] precious stones; and it was set on David's head. And he brought forth the spoil of the city, exceeding much.
texts.2sa.12.31: And he brought forth the people that were therein, and put them under saws, and under harrows of iron, and under axes of iron, and made them pass through the brickkiln: and thus did he unto all the cities of the children of Ammon. And David and all the people returned unto Jerusalem.
texts.2sa.13.1: And it came to pass after this, that Absalom the son of David had a fair sister, whose name was Tamar; and Amnon the son of David loved her.
texts.2sa.13.2: And Amnon was so vexed that he fell sick because of his sister Tamar; for she was a virgin; and it seemed hard to Amnon to do anything unto her.
texts.2sa.13.3: But Amnon had a friend, whose name was Jonadab, the son of Shimeah, David's brother; and Jonadab was a very subtle man.
texts.2sa.13.4: And he said unto him, Why, O son of the king, art thou thus lean from day to day? wilt thou not tell me? And Amnon said unto him, I love Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister.
texts.2sa.13.5: And Jonadab said unto him, Lay thee down on thy bed, and feign thyself sick: and when thy father cometh to see thee, say unto him, Let my sister Tamar come, I pray thee, and give me bread to eat, and dress the food in my sight, that I may see it, and eat it from her hand.
