texts.2sa.19.15: Então o rei voltou, e chegou até ao Jordão; e Judah veiu a Gilgal, para ir encontrar-se com o rei, á outra banda do Jordão.
texts.2sa.19.16: E apressou-se Simei, filho de Gera, filho de Jemini, que era de Bahurim: e desceu com os homens de Judah a encontrar-se com o rei David,
texts.2sa.19.17: E com elle mil varões de Benjamin, como tambem Ziba, servo da casa de Saul, e seus quinze filhos, e seus vinte servos com elle: e promptamente passaram o Jordão adiante do rei.
texts.2sa.19.18: E, passando a barca, para fazer passar a casa do rei e para trazer o que bem parecesse aos seus olhos, então Simei, filho de Gera, se prostrou diante do rei, passando elle o Jordão.
texts.2sa.19.19: E disse ao rei: Não me impute meu senhor a minha culpa, e não te lembres do que tão perversamente fez teu servo, no dia em que o rei meu senhor saiu de Jerusalem, para o rei conserval-o no coração.
texts.2sa.19.20: Porque teu servo devéras confessa que eu pequei: porém eis que eu sou o primeiro que de toda a casa de José desci a encontrar-me com o rei meu senhor.
texts.2sa.19.21: Então respondeu Abisai, filho de Zeruia, e disse: Não morreria pois Simei por isto, havendo amaldiçoado ao ungido do Senhor?
texts.2sa.19.22: Porém David disse: Que tenho eu comvosco, filhos de Zeruia, para que hoje me sejaes adversarios? morreria alguem hoje em Israel? porque porventura não sei que hoje fui feito rei sobre Israel?
texts.2sa.19.23: E disse o rei a Simei: Não morrerás. E o rei lh’o jurou.
texts.2sa.19.24: Tambem Mephiboseth, filho de Saul, desceu a encontrar-se com o rei, e não tinha lavado os pés, nem tinha feito a barba, nem tinha lavado os seus vestidos desde o dia em que o rei tinha saido até ao dia em que voltou em paz.
texts.2sa.19.25: E succedeu que, vindo elle a Jerusalem a encontrar-se com o rei, disse-lhe o rei: Porque não foste comigo, Mephiboseth?
texts.2sa.19.26: E disse elle: Ó rei meu senhor, o meu servo me enganou; porque o teu servo dizia: Albardarei um jumento, e n’elle montarei, e irei com o rei; pois o teu servo é côxo.
texts.2sa.19.27: De mais d’isto, falsamente accusou a teu servo diante do rei meu senhor; porém o rei meu senhor é como um anjo de Deus; faze pois o que parecer bem aos teus olhos.
texts.2sa.19.28: Porque toda a casa de meu pae não era senão de homens dignos de morte diante do rei meu senhor; e comtudo puzeste a teu servo entre os que comem á tua mesa: e que mais direito tenho eu de clamar ao rei?
texts.2sa.19.29: E disse-lhe o rei: Porque ainda mais fallas de teus negocios? já disse eu: Tu e Ziba reparti as terras.
texts.2sa.19.30: E disse Mephiboseth ao rei: Tome elle tambem tudo; pois já veiu o rei meu senhor em paz á sua casa.
texts.2sa.19.31: Tambem Barzillai, o gileadita, desceu de Rogelim, e passou com o rei o Jordão, para o acompanhar á outra banda do Jordão.
texts.2sa.19.32: E era Barzillai mui velho, da edade de oitenta annos; e elle tinha sustentado o rei, quando tinha a sua morada em Mahanaim, porque era homem mui grande.
texts.2sa.19.33: E disse o rei a Barzillai: Passa tu comigo, e sustentar-te-hei comigo em Jerusalem.
texts.2sa.19.34: Porém Barzillai disse ao rei: Quantos serão os dias dos annos da minha vida, para que suba com o rei a Jerusalem?
texts.2sa.19.35: Da edade de oitenta annos sou eu hoje; poderia eu discernir entre bom e mau? poderia o teu servo ter gosto no que comer e beber? Poderia eu mais ouvir a voz dos cantores e cantoras? E porque será o teu servo ainda pesado ao rei meu senhor?
texts.2sa.19.36: Com o rei passará teu servo ainda um pouco mais além do Jordão: e porque me recompensará o rei com tal recompensa?
texts.2sa.19.37: Deixa voltar o teu servo, e morrerei na minha cidade, junto á sepultura de meu pae e de minha mãe: mas eis ahi está o teu servo Chimham, o qual passe com o rei meu senhor, e faze-lhe o que bem parecer aos teus olhos.
texts.2sa.19.38: Então disse o rei: Chimham passará comigo, e eu lhe farei como bem parecer aos teus olhos, e tudo quanto me pedires te farei.
texts.2sa.19.39: Havendo pois todo o povo passado o Jordão, e passando tambem o rei, beijou o rei a Barzillai, e o abençoou: e elle voltou para o seu logar.
texts.2sa.19.40: E d’ali passou o rei a Gilgal, e Chimham passou com elle: e todo o povo de Judah conduziu o rei, como tambem a metade do povo d’Israel.
texts.2sa.19.41: E eis que todos os homens d’Israel vieram ao rei, e disseram ao rei: Porque te furtaram nossos irmãos, os homens de Judah, e conduziram o rei e a sua casa d’além do Jordão, e todos os homens de David com elles?
texts.2sa.19.42: Então responderam todos os homens de Judah aos homens de Israel: Porquanto o rei é nosso parente; e porque vos iraes por isso? Porventura comemos ás costas do rei, ou nos apresentou algum presente?
texts.2sa.19.43: E responderam os homens d’Israel aos homens de Judah, e disseram: Dez partes temos no rei, e até em David mais temos nós do que vós; porque pois não fizestes conta de nós, para que a nossa palavra não fosse a primeira, para tornar a trazer o nosso rei? Porém a palavra dos homens de Judah foi mais forte do que a palavra dos homens d’Israel.
texts.2sa.20.1: Então se achou ali por acaso um homem de Belial, cujo nome era Seba, filho de Bichri, homem de Benjamin, o qual tocou a buzina, e disse: Não temos parte em David, nem herança no filho de Jessé; cada um ás suas tendas, ó Israel.
texts.2sa.20.2: Então todos os homens d’Israel subiram de detraz de David, e seguiram Seba, filho de Bichri; porém os homens de Judah se uniram ao seu rei desde o Jordão até Jerusalem.
texts.2sa.20.3: Vindo pois David para sua casa, a Jerusalem, tomou o rei as dez mulheres, suas concubinas, que deixara para guardarem a casa, e as poz n’uma casa em guarda, e as sustentava; porém não entrou a ellas: e estiveram encerradas até ao dia da sua morte, vivendo como viuvas.
texts.2sa.20.4: Disse mais o rei a Amasa: Convoca-me os homens de Judah para o terceiro dia: e tu então apresenta-te aqui.
texts.2sa.20.5: E foi Amasa para convocar a Judah: porém demorou-se além do tempo que lhe tinha designado.
texts.2sa.20.6: Então disse David a Abisai: Mais mal agora nos fará Seba, o filho de Bichri, do que Absalão: pelo que toma tu os servos de teu senhor, e persegue-o, para que porventura não ache para si cidades fortes, e escape dos nossos olhos.
texts.2sa.20.7: Então sairam atraz d’elle os homens de Joab, e os cheretheos, e os peletheos, e todos os valentes: estes sairam de Jerusalem para irem atraz de Seba, filho de Bichri.
texts.2sa.20.8: Chegando elles pois á pedra grande que está junto a Gibeon, Amasa veiu: e estava Joab cingido da sua roupa que vestiu, e sobre ella um cinto, ao qual estava pegada a espada a seus lombos na sua bainha; e, adiantando-se elle, lhe caiu.
texts.2sa.20.9: E disse Joab a Amasa: Vae comtigo bem, meu irmão? E Joab, com a mão direita, pegou da barba de Amasa, para o beijar.
texts.2sa.20.10: E Amasa não se resguardou da espada que estava na mão de Joab, de sorte que este o feriu com ella na quinta costella, e lhe derramou por terra as entranhas, e não o feriu segunda vez, e morreu: então Joab e Abisai, seu irmão, foram atraz de Seba, filho de Bichri.
texts.2sa.20.11: Mas algum d’entre os moços de Joab parou junto a elle, e disse: Quem ha que bem queira a Joab? e quem seja por David siga a Joab.
texts.2sa.20.12: E Amasa estava envolto no seu sangue no meio do caminho: e, vendo aquelle homem que todo o povo parava, desviou a Amasa do caminho para o campo, e lançou sobre elle um manto; porque via que todo aquelle que chegava a elle parava.
texts.2sa.20.13: E, como estava apartado do caminho, todos os homens seguiram a Joab, para perseguirem a Seba, filho de Bichri.
texts.2sa.20.14: E passou por todas as tribus d’Israel até Abel, a saber, a Beth-maaca e a todos os beritas: e ajuntaram-se, e tambem o seguiram.
texts.2sa.20.15: E vieram, e o cercaram em Abel de Beth-maaca, e levantaram uma tranqueira contra a cidade, assim que já estava em frente do antemuro: e todo o povo que estava com Joab batia o muro, para o derribar.
texts.2sa.20.16: Então uma mulher sabia gritou de dentro da cidade: Ouvi, ouvi, peço-vos que digaes a Joab: Chega-te cá, para que eu te falle.
texts.2sa.20.17: Chegou-se a ella, e disse a mulher: Tu és Joab? E disse elle: Eu sou. E ella lhe disse: Ouve as palavras de tua serva. E disse elle: Ouço.
texts.2sa.20.18: Então fallou ella, dizendo: Antigamente costumava-se fallar, dizendo: Certamente pediram conselho a Abel; e assim o concluiam.
texts.2sa.20.19: Sou eu uma das pacificas e das fieis em Israel: e tu procuras matar uma cidade que é madre em Israel: porque pois devorarias a herança do Senhor?
texts.2sa.20.20: Então respondeu Joab, e disse: Longe, longe de mim que eu tal faça, que eu devore ou arruine!
texts.2sa.20.21: A coisa não é assim; porém um só homem do monte d’Ephraim, cujo nome é Seba, filho de Bichri, levantou a mão contra o rei, contra David; entregae-me só este, e retirar-me-hei da cidade. Então disse a mulher a Joab; Eis que te será lançada a sua cabeça pelo muro.
texts.2sa.20.22: E a mulher, na sua sabedoria, entrou a todo o povo, e cortaram a cabeça de Seba, filho de Bichri, e a lançaram a Joab; então tocou a buzina, e se retiraram da cidade, cada um para as suas tendas, e Joab voltou a Jerusalem, ao rei.
texts.2sa.20.23: E Joab estava sobre todo o exercito d’Israel; e Benaia, filho de Joiada, sobre os cheretheos e sobre os peletheos;
texts.2sa.20.24: E Adoram sobre os tributos; e Josaphat, filho de Ahilud, era o chanceller;
texts.2sa.20.25: E Seva o escrivão; e Zadok e Abiathar os sacerdotes;
texts.2sa.20.26: E tambem Ira, o jairita, era o official-mór de David.
texts.2sa.21.1: E houve em dias de David uma fome de tres annos, de anno em anno; e David consultou ao Senhor, e o Senhor lhe disse: É por causa de Saul e da sua casa sanguinaria, porque matou os gibeonitas.
texts.2sa.21.2: Então chamou o rei aos gibeonitas, e lhes fallou (ora os gibeonitas não eram dos filhos de Israel, mas do resto dos amorrheos, e os filhos de Israel lhes tinham jurado, porém Saul procurou feril-os no seu zelo á causa dos filhos de Israel e de Judah).
texts.2sa.21.3: Disse pois David aos gibeonitas: Que quereis que eu vos faça? e que satisfação vos darei, para que abençoeis a herança do Senhor?
texts.2sa.21.4: Então os gibeonitas lhe disseram: Não é por prata nem oiro que temos questão com Saul e com sua casa; nem tão pouco pretendemos matar pessoa alguma em Israel. E disse elle: Que é pois que quereis que vos faça?
texts.2sa.21.5: E disseram ao rei: O homem que nos destruiu, e intentou contra nós que fossemos assollados, sem que podessemos subsistir em termo algum de Israel,
texts.2sa.21.6: De seus filhos se nos dêem sete homens, para que os enforquemos ao Senhor em Gibeah de Saul, o eleito do Senhor. E disse o rei: Eu os darei.
texts.2sa.21.7: Porém o rei poupou a Mephiboseth, filho de Jonathan, filho de Saul, por causa do juramento do Senhor, que entre elles houvera, entre David e Jonathan, filho de Saul.
texts.2sa.21.8: Porém tomou o rei os dois filhos de Rispa, filha d’Aia, que tinha parido a Saul, a saber a Armoni e a Mephiboseth; como tambem os cinco filhos da irmã de Michal, filha de Saul, que parira a Adriel, filho de Barzillai, meholathita.
texts.2sa.21.9: E os entregou na mão dos gibeonitas, os quaes os enforcaram no monte, perante o Senhor; e cairam estes sete juntamente: e foram mortos nos dias da sega, nos dias primeiros, no principio da sega das cevadas.
texts.2sa.21.10: Então Rispa, filha d’Aia, tomou um panno de cilicio, e estendeu-lh’o sobre uma penha, desde o principio da sega, até que distillou a agua sobre elles do céu: e não deixou as aves do céu pousar sobre elles de dia, nem os animaes do campo de noite.
texts.2sa.21.11: E foi dito a David o que fizera Rispa, filha d’Aia, concubina de Saul.
texts.2sa.21.12: Então foi David, e tomou os ossos de Saul, e os ossos de Jonathan seu filho, dos moradores de Jabéz-gilead, os quaes os furtaram da rua de Beth-san, onde os philisteos os tinham pendurado, quando os philisteos feriram a Saul em Gilboa.
texts.2sa.21.13: E fez subir d’ali os ossos de Saul, e os ossos de Jonathan seu filho: e ajuntaram tambem os ossos dos enforcados.
texts.2sa.21.14: Enterraram os ossos de Saul, e de Jonathan seu filho na terra de Benjamin, em Zela, na sepultura de seu pae Kis, e fizeram tudo o que o rei ordenara; e depois d’isto Deus se aplacou com a terra.
texts.2sa.21.15: Tiveram mais os philisteos uma peleja contra Israel: e desceu David, e com elle os seus servos: e tanto pelejaram contra os philisteos, que David se cançou.
texts.2sa.21.16: E Isbi-benob, que era dos filhos do gigante, e o peso de cuja lança tinha trezentos siclos de peso de cobre, e que cingia uma espada nova, este intentou ferir a David.
texts.2sa.21.17: Porém Abisai, filho de Zeruia, o soccorreu, e feriu o philisteo, e o matou: então os homens de David lhe juraram, dizendo: Nunca mais sairás comnosco á peleja, para que não apagues a lampada de Israel.
texts.2sa.21.18: E aconteceu depois d’isto que houve em Gob ainda outra peleja contra os philisteos: então Sibbechai, o husatita, feriu a Saph, que era dos filhos do gigante.
texts.2sa.21.19: Houve mais outra peleja contra os philisteos em Gob: e El-hanan, filho de Jaaré-oregim, o beth-lehemita feriu Goliath, o getheo, de cuja lança era a haste como orgão de tecelão.
texts.2sa.21.20: Houve ainda tambem outra peleja em Gath, onde estava um homem d’alta estatura, que tinha em cada mão seis dedos, e em cada pé outros seis, vinte e quatro por todos, e tambem este nascera do gigante.
texts.2sa.21.21: E injuriava a Israel: porém Jonathan, filho de Simea, irmão de David, o feriu.
texts.2sa.21.22: Estes quatro nasceram ao gigante em Gath: e cairam pela mão de David e pela mão de seus servos.
texts.2sa.22.1: E fallou David ao Senhor as palavras d’este cantico, no dia em que o Senhor o livrou das mãos de todos os seus inimigos e das mãos de Saul.
texts.2sa.22.2: Disse pois: O Senhor é o meu rochedo, e o meu logar forte, e o meu libertador.
texts.2sa.22.3: Deus é o meu rochedo, n’elle confiarei: o meu escudo, e a força da minha salvação, o meu alto retiro, e o meu refugio. O meu Salvador, de violencia me salvaste.
texts.2sa.22.4: O Senhor, digno de louvor, invoquei, e de meus inimigos fiquei livre.
texts.2sa.22.5: Porque me cercaram as ondas de morte: as torrentes de Belial me assombraram.
texts.2sa.22.6: Cordas do inferno me cingiram; encontraram-me laços de morte.
texts.2sa.22.7: Estando em angustia, invoquei ao Senhor, e a meu Deus clamei: do seu templo ouviu elle a minha voz, e o meu clamor chegou aos seus ouvidos.
texts.2sa.22.8: Então se abalou e tremeu a terra, os fundamentos dos céus se moveram e abalaram, porque elle se irou.
texts.2sa.22.9: Subiu o fumo de seus narizes, e da sua bocca um fogo devorador: carvões se incenderam d’elle.
texts.2sa.22.10: E abaixou os céus, e desceu: e uma escuridão havia debaixo de seus pés.
texts.2sa.22.11: E subiu sobre um cherubim, e voou: e foi visto sobre as azas do vento.
texts.2sa.22.12: E por tendas poz as trevas ao redor de si: ajuntamento d’aguas, nuvens dos céus.
texts.2sa.22.13: Pelo resplendor da sua presença brasas de fogo se accendem.
texts.2sa.22.14: Trovejou desde os céus o Senhor: e o Altissimo fez soar a sua voz.
texts.2sa.22.15: E disparou frechas, e os dissipou: raios e os perturbou.
texts.2sa.22.16: E appareceram as profundezas do mar, os fundamentos do mundo se descobriram: pela reprehensão do Senhor, pelo sopro do vento dos seus narizes.
texts.2sa.22.17: Desde o alto enviou, e me tomou: tirou-me das muitas aguas.
texts.2sa.22.18: Livrou-me do meu possante inimigo, e d’aquelles que me tinham odio, porque eram mais fortes do que eu.
texts.2sa.22.19: Encontraram-me no dia da minha calamidade: porém o Senhor se fez o meu esteio.
texts.2sa.22.20: E tirou-me á largura, e arrebatou-me d’ali; porque tinha prazer em mim.
texts.2sa.22.21: Recompensou-me o Senhor conforme á minha justiça: conforme á pureza de minhas mãos me retribuiu.
texts.2sa.22.22: Porque guardei os caminhos do Senhor: e não me apartei impiamente do meu Deus.
texts.2sa.22.23: Porque todos os seus juizos estavam diante de mim: e de seus estatutos me não desviei.
texts.2sa.22.24: Porém fui sincero perante elle: e guardei-me da minha iniquidade.
texts.2sa.22.25: E me retribuiu o Senhor conforme á minha justiça, conforme á minha pureza diante dos seus olhos.
texts.2sa.22.26: Com o benigno te mostras benigno: com o varão sincero te mostras sincero.
texts.2sa.22.27: Com o puro te mostras puro: mas com o perverso te mostras avesso.
texts.2sa.22.28: E o povo afflicto livras: mas teus olhos são contra os altivos, e tu os abaterás.
texts.2sa.22.29: Porque tu, Senhor, és a minha candeia: e o Senhor esclarece as minhas trevas.
texts.2sa.22.30: Porque comtigo passo pelo meio d’um esquadrão: pelo meu Deus salto um muro.
texts.2sa.22.31: O caminho de Deus é perfeito, e a palavra do Senhor refinada; e é o escudo de todos os que n’elle confiam.
texts.2sa.22.32: Porque, quem é Deus, senão o Senhor? e quem é rochedo, senão o nosso Deus?
texts.2sa.22.33: Deus é a minha fortaleza e a minha força, e elle perfeitamente desembaraça o meu caminho.
texts.2sa.22.34: Faz elle os meus pés como os das cervas, e me põe sobre as minhas alturas.
texts.2sa.22.35: Instrue as minhas mãos para a peleja, de maneira que um arco de cobre se quebra pelos meus braços.
texts.2sa.22.36: Tambem me déste o escudo da tua salvação, e pela tua brandura me vieste a engrandecer.
texts.2sa.22.37: Alargaste os meus passos debaixo de mim, e não vacillaram os meus artelhos.
texts.2sa.22.38: Persegui os meus inimigos, e os derrotei, e nunca me tornei até que os consumisse.
texts.2sa.22.39: E os consumi, e os atravessei, de modo que nunca mais se levantaram, mas cairam debaixo dos meus pés.
texts.2sa.22.40: Porque me cingiste de força para a peleja, fizeste abater-se debaixo de mim os que se levantaram contra mim.
texts.2sa.22.41: E deste-me o pescoço de meus inimigos, d’aquelles que me tinham odio, e os destrui.
texts.2sa.22.42: Olharam, porém não houve libertador: sim, para o Senhor, porém não lhes respondeu.
texts.2sa.22.43: Então os moí como o pó da terra; como a lama das ruas os trilhei e dissipei.
texts.2sa.22.44: Tambem me livraste das contendas do meu povo; guardaste-me para cabeça das nações; o povo que não conhecia me servirá.
texts.2sa.22.45: Os filhos de estranhos se me sujeitaram; ouvindo a minha voz, me obedeceram.
texts.2sa.22.46: Os filhos de estranhos descairam; e, cingindo-se, sairam dos seus encerramentos.
texts.2sa.22.47: Vive o Senhor, e bemdito seja o meu rochedo; e exaltado seja Deus, a rocha da minha salvação:
texts.2sa.22.48: O Deus que me dá inteira vingança, e sujeita os povos debaixo de mim.
texts.2sa.22.49: E o que me tira d’entre os meus inimigos: e tu me exaltas sobre os que contra mim se levantam; do homem violento me livras.
texts.2sa.22.50: Por isso, ó Senhor, te louvarei entre as gentes, e entoarei louvores ao teu nome.
texts.2sa.22.51: Elle é a torre das salvações do seu rei, e usa de benignidade com o seu ungido, com David, e com a sua semente para sempre.
texts.2sa.23.1: E estas são as ultimas palavras de David: Diz David, filho de Jessé, e diz o homem que foi levantado em altura, o ungido do Deus de Jacob, e o suave em psalmos d’Israel:
texts.2sa.23.2: O espirito do Senhor fallou por mim, e a sua palavra esteve em minha bocca.
texts.2sa.23.3: Disse o Deus d’Israel, a Rocha d’Israel a mim me fallou: Haverá um justo que domine sobre os homens, que domine no temor de Deus.
texts.2sa.23.4: E será como a luz da manhã, quando sae o sol, da manhã sem nuvens, quando pelo seu resplandor e pela chuva a herva brota da terra.
texts.2sa.23.5: Ainda que a minha casa não seja tal para com Deus, comtudo estabeleceu comigo um concerto eterno, que em tudo será bem ordenado e guardado, pois toda a minha salvação e todo o meu prazer está n’elle, apezar de que ainda não o faz brotar.
texts.2sa.23.6: Porém os filhos de Belial todos serão como os espinhos que se lançam fóra, porque se lhes não pode pegar com a mão.
texts.2sa.23.7: Mas qualquer que os tocar se armará de ferro e da haste de uma lança; e a fogo serão totalmente queimados no mesmo logar.
texts.2sa.23.8: Estes são os nomes dos valentes que David teve: Joseb-bashebeth, filho de Tachemoni, o principal dos capitães: este era Adino, o esnita, que se oppozera a oitocentos, e os feriu d’uma vez.
texts.2sa.23.9: E depois d’elle Eleazar, filho de Dodó, filho de Ahohi, entre os tres valentes que estavam com David quando provocaram os philisteos que ali se ajuntaram á peleja, e quando d’Israel os homens subiram.
texts.2sa.23.10: Este se levantou, e feriu os philisteos, até lhe cançar a mão e ficar a mão pegada á espada: e n’aquelle dia o Senhor obrou um grande livramento; e o povo voltou atraz d’elle, sómente a tomar o despojo.
texts.2sa.23.11: E depois d’elle Samma, filho de Agé, o hararita, quando os philisteos se ajuntaram n’uma multidão, onde havia um pedaço de terra cheio de lentilhas, e o povo fugira de diante dos philisteos.
texts.2sa.23.12: Este pois se poz no meio d’aquelle pedaço de terra, e o defendeu, e feriu os philisteos: e o Senhor obrou um grande livramento.
texts.2sa.23.13: Tambem tres dos trinta cabeças desceram, e vieram no tempo da sega a David, á caverna de Adullam: e a multidão dos philisteos acampara no valle de Rephaim.
texts.2sa.23.14: David estava então n’um logar forte, e a guarnição dos philisteos estava então em Beth-lehem.
texts.2sa.23.15: E teve David desejo, e disse: Quem me déra beber da agua da cisterna de Beth-lehem, que está junto á porta!
texts.2sa.23.16: Então aquelles tres valentes romperam pelo arraial dos philisteos, e tiraram agua da cisterna de Beth-lehem, que está junto á porta, e a tomaram, e a trouxeram a David; porém elle não a quiz beber, mas derramou-a perante o Senhor,
texts.2sa.23.17: E disse: Guarda-me, ó Senhor, de que tal faça; beberia eu o sangue dos homens que foram a risco da sua vida? De maneira que não a quiz beber: isto fizeram aquelles tres valentes.
texts.2sa.23.18: Tambem Abisai, irmão de Joab, filho de Zeruia, era cabeça de tres; e este alçou a sua lança contra trezentos feridos: e tinha nome entre os tres.
texts.2sa.23.19: Porventura este não era o mais nobre d’entre estes tres? pois era o primeiro d’elles; porém aos primeiros tres não chegou.
texts.2sa.23.20: Tambem Benaia, filho de Joiada, filho d’um homem valoroso de Cabseel, grande em obras, este feriu dois fortes leões de Moab; e desceu elle, e feriu um leão no meio d’uma cova, no tempo da neve.
texts.2sa.23.21: Tambem este feriu um homem egypcio, homem de respeito; e na mão do egypcio havia uma lança, porém elle desceu a elle com um cajado, e arrancou a lança da mão do egypcio, e o matou com a sua propria lança.
texts.2sa.23.22: Estas coisas fez Benaia, filho de Joiada, pelo que teve nome entre tres valentes.
texts.2sa.23.23: D’entre os trinta elle era o mais nobre, porém aos tres primeiros não chegou: e David o poz sobre os seus guardas.
texts.2sa.23.24: Asael, irmão de Joab, estava entre os trinta, que eram: El-hanan, filho de Dodó, de Beth-lehem,
texts.2sa.23.26: Heles, paltita, Ira, filho de Ikkes, tekoita,
texts.2sa.23.29: Heleb, filho de Baena, netophathita, Ittai, filho de Ribai, de Gibeah dos filhos de Benjamin,
texts.2sa.23.30: Benaia, pirhathonita, Hiddai, do ribeiro de Gaás,
texts.2sa.23.32: Eliaba, saalbonita, os filhos de Jasen e Jonathan,
texts.2sa.23.33: Samma, hararita, Ahiam, filho de Sarar, ararita,
texts.2sa.23.34: Eliphelet, filho de Ahasbai, filho d’um maacathita, Eliam, filho de Achitophel, gilonita,
texts.2sa.23.36: Ighal, filho de Nathan, de Zoba, Bani, gadita,
texts.2sa.23.37: Zelek, ammonita, Naharai, beerothita, o que trazia as armas de Joab, filho de Zeruia,
texts.2sa.23.39: Urias, hetheo: trinta e sete por todos.
texts.2sa.24.1: E a ira do Senhor se tornou a accender contra Israel: e incitou a David contra elles, dizendo: Vae, numera a Israel e a Judah.
texts.2sa.24.2: Disse pois o rei a Joab, chefe do exercito, o qual tinha comsigo: Agora rodeia por todas as tribus de Israel, desde Dan até Berseba, e numera o povo: para que eu saiba o numero do povo.
texts.2sa.24.3: Então disse Joab ao rei: Ora, multiplique o Senhor teu Deus a este povo cem vezes tanto quanto agora é, e os olhos do rei meu senhor o vejam: mas porque deseja o rei meu senhor este negocio?
texts.2sa.24.4: Porém a palavra do rei prevaleceu contra Joab, e contra os chefes do exercito: Joab pois saiu com os chefes do exercito diante da face do rei, a numerar o povo de Israel.
texts.2sa.24.5: E passaram o Jordão: e pozeram-se em campo junto a Aroer, á direita da cidade que está no meio do ribeiro de Gad, e junto a Jazer.
texts.2sa.24.6: E vieram a Gilead, e á terra baixa de Hodsi: tambem vieram até Dan-jaan, e ao redor de Zidon.
texts.2sa.24.7: E vieram á fortaleza de Tyro, e a todas as cidades dos heveos e dos cananeos; e sairam para a banda do sul de Judah, a Berseba.
texts.2sa.24.8: Assim rodeiaram por toda a terra: e ao cabo de nove mezes e vinte dias voltaram a Jerusalem.
texts.2sa.24.9: E Joab deu ao rei a somma do numero do povo contado: e havia em Israel oitocentos mil homens de guerra, que arrancavam espada; e os homens de Judah eram quinhentos mil homens.
texts.2sa.24.10: E o coração feriu a David, depois de haver numerado o povo: e disse David ao Senhor: Muito pequei no que fiz: porém agora, ó Senhor, peço-te que traspasses a iniquidade do teu servo; porque tenho feito mui loucamente.
texts.2sa.24.11: Levantando-se pois David pela manhã, veiu a palavra do Senhor ao propheta Gad, vidente de David, dizendo:
texts.2sa.24.12: Vae, e dize a David: Assim diz o Senhor: Tres coisas te offereço; escolhe uma d’ellas, para que t’a faça.
texts.2sa.24.13: Veiu pois Gad a David, e fez-lh’o saber; e disse-lhe: Queres que sete annos de fome te venham á tua terra; ou que por tres mezes fujas diante de teus inimigos, e elles te persigam; ou que por tres dias haja peste na tua terra? Delibera agora, e vê que resposta hei de tornar ao que me enviou.
texts.2sa.24.14: Então disse David a Gad: Estou em grande angustia: porém caiamos nas mãos do Senhor, porque muitas são as suas misericordias; mas nas mãos dos homens não caia eu.
texts.2sa.24.15: Então enviou o Senhor a peste a Israel, desde pela manhã até ao tempo determinado: e desde Dan até Berseba, morreram setenta mil homens do povo.
texts.2sa.24.16: Estendendo pois o anjo a sua mão sobre Jerusalem, para a destruir, o Senhor se arrependeu d’aquelle mal; e disse ao anjo que fazia a destruição entre o povo: Basta, agora retira a tua mão. E o anjo do Senhor estava junto á eira d’Arauna, o jebuseo.
texts.2sa.24.17: E, vendo David ao anjo que feria o povo, fallou ao Senhor, e disse: Eis que eu sou o que pequei, e eu o que iniquamente obrei; porém estas ovelhas que fizeram? seja pois a tua mão contra mim, e contra a casa de meu pae.
texts.2sa.24.18: E Gad veiu n’aquelle mesmo dia a David; e disse-lhe: Sobe, levanta ao Senhor um altar na eira de Arauna, o jebuseo.
texts.2sa.24.19: David subiu conforme á palavra de Gad, como o Senhor lhe tinha ordenado.
texts.2sa.24.20: E olhou Arauna, e viu que vinham para elle o rei e os seus servos: saiu pois Arauna, e inclinou-se diante do rei com o rosto em terra.
texts.2sa.24.21: E disse Arauna: Porque vem o rei meu Senhor ao seu servo? E disse David: Para comprar de ti esta eira, afim de edificar n’ella um altar ao Senhor, para que este castigo cesse de sobre o povo.
texts.2sa.24.22: Então disse Arauna a David: Tome, e offereça o rei meu senhor o que bem parecer aos seus olhos: eis ahi bois para o holocausto, e os trilhos, e o apparelho dos bois para a lenha.
texts.2sa.24.23: Tudo isto deu Arauna ao rei; disse mais Arauna ao rei; O Senhor teu Deus tome prazer em ti.
texts.2sa.24.24: Porém o rei disse a Arauna: Não, porém por certo preço t’o comprarei, porque não offerecerei ao Senhor meu Deus holocaustos que me não custem nada. Assim David comprou a eira e os bois por cincoenta siclos de prata.
texts.2sa.24.25: E edificou ali David ao Senhor um altar, e offereceu holocaustos, e offertas pacificas. Assim o Senhor se aplacou com a terra, e cessou aquelle castigo de sobre Israel.

texts.2sa.1.1: Now it came to pass after the death of Saul, when David had returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites, and David had abode two days in Ziklag;
texts.2sa.1.2: It came even to pass on the third day, that behold, a man came out of the camp from Saul with his clothes rent, and earth upon his head: and so it was, when he came to David, that he fell to the earth, and did obeisance.
texts.2sa.1.3: And David said to him, From whence comest thou? And he said to him, Out of the camp of Israel have I escaped.
texts.2sa.1.4: And David said to him, How went the matter? I pray thee, tell me. And he answered, That the people have fled from the battle, and many of the people also have fallen, and are dead; and Saul and Jonathan his son are dead also.
texts.2sa.1.5: And David said to the young man that told him, How knowest thou that Saul and Jonathan his son are dead?
texts.2sa.1.6: And the young man that told him said, As I happened by chance upon mount Gilboa, behold, Saul leaned upon his spear; and lo, the chariots and horsemen followed hard after him.
texts.2sa.1.7: And when he looked behind him, he saw me, and called to me. And I answered, Here am I.
texts.2sa.1.8: And he said to me, Who art thou? And I answered him, I am an Amalekite.
texts.2sa.1.9: He said to me again, Stand, I pray thee, upon me, and slay me: for anguish is come upon me, because my life is yet whole in me.
texts.2sa.1.10: So I stood upon him, and slew him, because I was sure that he could not live after that he had fallen: and I took the crown that was upon his head, and the bracelet that was on his arm, and have brought them hither to my lord.
texts.2sa.1.11: Then David took hold on his clothes, and rent them; and likewise all the men that were with him:
texts.2sa.1.12: And they mourned and wept, and fasted until evening, for Saul and for Jonathan his son, and for the people of the LORD, and for the house of Israel; because they had fallen by the sword.
texts.2sa.1.13: And David said to the young man that told him, Whence art thou? And he answered, I am the son of a stranger, an Amalekite.
texts.2sa.1.14: And David said to him, How wast thou not afraid to stretch forth thy hand to destroy the LORD'S anointed?
texts.2sa.1.15: And David called one of the young men, and said, Go near, and fall upon him. And he smote him that he died.
texts.2sa.1.16: And David said to him, Thy blood be upon thy head; for thy mouth hath testified against thee, saying, I have slain the LORD'S anointed.
texts.2sa.1.17: And David lamented with this lamentation over Saul, and over Jonathan his son:
texts.2sa.1.18: (Also he bade them teach the children of Judah the use of the bow: behold, it is written in the book of Jasher.)
texts.2sa.1.19: The beauty of Israel is slain upon thy high places: how are the mighty fallen!
texts.2sa.1.20: Tell it not in Gath, publish it not in the streets of Askelon; lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph.
texts.2sa.1.21: Ye mountains of Gilboa, let there be no dew, neither rain upon you, nor fields of offerings: for there the shield of the mighty is vilely cast away, the shield of Saul, as though he had not been anointed with oil.
texts.2sa.1.22: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan turned not back, and the sword of Saul returned not empty.
texts.2sa.1.23: Saul and Jonathan were lovely and pleasant in their lives, and in their death they were not divided: they were swifter than eagles, they were stronger than lions.
texts.2sa.1.24: Ye daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who clothed you in scarlet, with other delights, who put ornaments of gold upon your apparel.
texts.2sa.1.25: How are the mighty fallen in the midst of the battle! O Jonathan thou wast slain in thy high places.
texts.2sa.1.26: I am distressed for thee, my brother Jonathan: very pleasant hast thou been to me: thy love to me was wonderful, passing the love of women.
texts.2sa.1.27: How have the mighty fallen, and the weapons of war perished!
texts.2sa.2.1: And it came to pass after this, that David inquired of the LORD, saying, Shall I go up into any of the cities of Judah? And the LORD said to him, Go up. And David said, Whither shall I go up? And he said, To Hebron.
texts.2sa.2.2: So David went up thither, and his two wives also, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail, Nabal's wife the Carmelite.
texts.2sa.2.3: And his men that were with him did David bring up, every man with his household: and they dwelt in the cities of Hebron.
texts.2sa.2.4: And the men of Judah came, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah. And they told David, saying, That the men of Jabesh-gilead were they that buried Saul.
texts.2sa.2.5: And David sent messengers to the men of Jabesh-gilead, and said to them, Blessed be ye of the LORD, that ye have shown this kindness to your lord, even to Saul, and have buried him.
texts.2sa.2.6: And now the LORD show kindness and truth to you: and I also will requite you this kindness, because ye have done this thing.
texts.2sa.2.7: Therefore now let your hands be strengthened, and be ye valiant: for your master Saul is dead, and also the house of Judah have anointed me king over them.
texts.2sa.2.8: But Abner the son of Ner, captain of Saul's host, took Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, and brought him over to Mahanaim;
texts.2sa.2.9: And he made him king over Gilead, and over the Ashurites, and over Jezreel, and over Ephraim, and over Benjamin, and over all Israel.
texts.2sa.2.10: Ish-bosheth, Saul's son, was forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and he reigned two years: but the house of Judah followed David.
texts.2sa.2.11: And the time that David was king in Hebron, over the house of Judah, was seven years and six months.
texts.2sa.2.12: And Abner the son of Ner, and the servants of Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.
texts.2sa.2.13: And Joab the son of Zeruiah, and the servants of David went out, and met together by the pool of Gibeon: and they sat down, the one on the one side of the pool, and the other on the other side of the pool.
texts.2sa.2.14: And Abner said to Joab, Let the young men now arise, and play before us. And Joab said, Let them arise.
texts.2sa.2.15: Then there arose, and went over by number twelve of Benjamin, who pertained to Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, and twelve of the servants of David.
texts.2sa.2.16: And they caught every one his fellow by the head, and thrust his sword in his fellow's side: so they fell down together: wherefore that place was called Helkath-hazzurim, which is in Gibeon.
texts.2sa.2.17: And there was a very severe battle that day; and Abner was defeated, and the men of Israel, before the servants of David.
texts.2sa.2.18: And there were three sons of Zeruiah there, Joab, and Abishai, and Asahel: and Asahel was as light of foot as a wild roe.
texts.2sa.2.19: And Asahel pursued after Abner; and in going he turned not to the right hand nor to the left from following Abner.
texts.2sa.2.20: Then Abner looked behind him, and said, Art thou Asahel? And he answered, I am.
texts.2sa.2.21: And Abner said to him, Turn thee aside to thy right hand or to thy left, and lay hold on one of the young men, and take to thee his armor. But Asahel would not turn aside from following him.
texts.2sa.2.22: And Abner said again to Asahel, Turn thee aside from following me: Why should I smite thee to the ground? how then should I hold up my face to Joab thy brother?
texts.2sa.2.23: But he refused to turn aside: wherefore Abner with the hinder end of the spear smote him under the fifth rib, that the spear came out behind him; and he fell down there, and died in the same place: and it came to pass, that as many as came to the place where Asahel fell down and died, stood still.
texts.2sa.2.24: Joab also, and Abishai pursued Abner: and the sun went down when they had come to the hill of Ammah, that lieth before Giah by the way of the wilderness of Gibeon.
texts.2sa.2.25: And the children of Benjamin assembled themselves after Abner, and became one troop, and stood on the top of a hill.
texts.2sa.2.26: Then Abner called to Joab, and said, Shall the sword devour for ever? knowest thou not that it will be bitterness in the latter end? how long shall it be then, ere thou wilt bid the people return from following their brethren?
texts.2sa.2.27: And Joab said, As God liveth, unless thou hadst spoken, surely then in the morning the people had gone up every one from following his brother.
texts.2sa.2.28: So Joab blew a trumpet, and all the people stood still, and pursued Israel no more, neither fought they any more.
texts.2sa.2.29: And Abner and his men walked all that night through the plain, and passed over Jordan, and went through all Bithron, and they came to Mahanaim.
texts.2sa.2.30: And Joab returned from following Abner: and when he had assembled all the people, there lacked of David's servants nineteen men, and Asahel.
texts.2sa.2.31: But the servants of David had smitten of Benjamin, and of Abner's men, so that three hundred and sixty men died.
texts.2sa.2.32: And they took up Asahel, and buried him in the sepulcher of his father, which was in Beth-lehem. And Joab and his men went all night, and they came to Hebron at break of day.
texts.2sa.3.1: Now there was long war between the house of Saul and the house of David: but David grew stronger and stronger, and the house of Saul became weaker and weaker.
texts.2sa.3.2: And to David were sons born in Hebron: and his first-born was Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess;
texts.2sa.3.3: And his second, Chileab, of Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite; and the third, Absalom the son of Maacah, the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur;
texts.2sa.3.4: And the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith; and the fifth, Shephatiah the son of Abital;
texts.2sa.3.5: And the sixth, Ithream, by Eglah David's wife. These were born to David in Hebron.
texts.2sa.3.6: And it came to pass, while there was war between the house of Saul and the house of David, that Abner made himself strong for the house of Saul.
texts.2sa.3.7: And Saul had a concubine, whose name was Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah: and Ish-bosheth said to Abner, Why hast thou gone in to my father's concubine?
texts.2sa.3.8: Then was Abner very wroth for the words of Ish-bosheth, and said, Am I a dog's head, who against Judah do show kindness this day to the house of Saul thy father, to his brethren, and to his friends, and have not delivered thee into the hand of David, that thou chargest me to-day with a fault concerning this woman?
texts.2sa.3.9: So do God to Abner, and more also, except, as the LORD hath sworn to David, even so I do to him;
texts.2sa.3.10: To translate the kingdom from the house of Saul, and to set up the throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan even to Beer-sheba.
texts.2sa.3.11: And he could not answer Abner a word again, because he feared him.
texts.2sa.3.12: And Abner sent messengers to David on his behalf, saying, Whose is the land? saying also, Make thy league with me, and behold, my hand shall be with thee, to bring about all Israel to thee.
texts.2sa.3.13: And he said, Well; I will make a league with thee: but one thing I require of thee, that is, Thou shalt not see my face, except thou shalt first bring Michal, Saul's daughter, when thou comest to see my face.
texts.2sa.3.14: And David sent messengers to Ish-bosheth, Saul's son, saying, Deliver to me my wife Michal, whom I espoused to me for a hundred foreskins of the Philistines.
texts.2sa.3.15: And Ish-bosheth sent, and took her from her husband, even from Phaltiel the son of Laish.
texts.2sa.3.16: And her husband went with her, weeping behind her to Bahurim. Then said Abner to him, Go, return. And he returned.
texts.2sa.3.17: And Abner had communication with the elders of Israel, saying, Ye sought for David in times past to be king over you:
texts.2sa.3.18: Now then do it: for the LORD hath spoken of David, saying, By the hand of my servant David I will save my people Israel from the hand of the Philistines, and from the hand of all their enemies.
texts.2sa.3.19: And Abner also spoke in the ears of Benjamin: and Abner went also to speak in the ears of David in Hebron all that seemed good to Israel, and that seemed good to the whole house of Benjamin.
texts.2sa.3.20: So Abner came to David in Hebron, and twenty men with him: and David made Abner and the men that were with him, a feast.
texts.2sa.3.21: And Abner said to David, I will arise and go, and will gather all Israel to my lord the king, that they may make a league with thee, and that thou mayest reign over all that thy heart desireth. And David sent Abner away; and he went in peace.
texts.2sa.3.22: And behold, the servants of David and Joab came from pursuing a troop, and brought in a great spoil with them: but Abner was not with David in Hebron; for he had sent him away, and he had gone in peace.
texts.2sa.3.23: When Joab and all the host that was with him had come, they told Joab, saying, Abner the son of Ner came to the king, and he hath sent him away, and he hath gone in peace.
texts.2sa.3.24: Then Joab came to the king, and said, What hast thou done? behold, Abner came to thee; why is it that thou hast sent him away, and he is quite gone?
texts.2sa.3.25: Thou knowest Abner the son of Ner, that he came to deceive thee, and to know thy going-out and thy coming-in, and to know all that thou doest.
texts.2sa.3.26: And when Joab had come out from David, he sent messengers after Abner, who brought him again from the well of Sirah: but David knew it not.
texts.2sa.3.27: And when Abner had returned to Hebron, Joab took him aside in the gate to speak with him quietly, and smote him there under the fifth rib that he died, for the blood of Asahel his brother.
texts.2sa.3.28: And afterward when David heard it, he said, I and my kingdom are guiltless before the LORD for ever from the blood of Abner the son of Ner:
texts.2sa.3.29: Let it rest on the head of Joab, and on all his father's house; and let there not fail from the house of Joab one that hath an issue, or that is a leper, or that leaneth on a staff, or that falleth on the sword, or that lacketh bread.
texts.2sa.3.30: So Joab and Abishai his brother slew Abner, because he had slain their brother Asahel at Gibeon in the battle.
texts.2sa.3.31: And David said to Joab, and to all the people that were with him, Rend your clothes, and gird you with sackcloth, and mourn before Abner. And king David himself followed the bier.
texts.2sa.3.32: And they buried Abner in Hebron: and the king lifted up his voice and wept at the grave of Abner; and all the people wept.
texts.2sa.3.33: And the king lamented over Abner, and said, Died Abner as a fool dieth?
texts.2sa.3.34: Thy hands were not bound, nor thy feet put into fetters: as a man falleth before wicked men, so fellest thou. And all the people wept again over him.
texts.2sa.3.35: And when all the people came to cause David to eat food while it was yet day, David swore, saying, So do God to me, and more also, If I taste bread or aught else, till the sun is down.
texts.2sa.3.36: And all the people took notice of it, and it pleased them: as what ever the king did pleased all the people.
texts.2sa.3.37: For all the people and all Israel understood that day that it was not of the king to slay Abner the son of Ner.
texts.2sa.3.38: And the king said to his servants, Know ye not that there hath a prince and a great man fallen this day in Israel?
texts.2sa.3.39: And I am this day weak, though anointed king; and these men the sons of Zeruiah are too hard for me. The LORD shall reward the doer of evil according to his wickedness.
texts.2sa.4.1: And when Saul's son heard that Abner was dead in Hebron, his hands were feeble, and all the Israelites were troubled.
texts.2sa.4.2: And Saul's son had two men that were captains of bands: the name of the one was Baanah, and the name of the other Rechab, the sons of Rimmon a Beerothite, of the children of Benjamin: (For Beeroth also was reckoned to Benjamin:
texts.2sa.4.3: And the Beerothites fled to Gittaim, and have been sojourners there until this day.)
texts.2sa.4.4: And Jonathan, Saul's son, had a son that was lame of his feet: he was five years old when the tidings came of Saul and Jonathan out of Jezreel, and his nurse took him up, and fled: and it came to pass, as she made haste to flee, that he fell, and became lame. And his name was Mephibosheth.
texts.2sa.4.5: And the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, went, and came about the heat of the day to the house of Ish-bosheth, who lay on a bed at noon.
texts.2sa.4.6: And they came thither into the midst of the house, as though they would have fetched wheat; and they smote him under the fifth rib: and Rechab and Baanah his brother escaped.
texts.2sa.4.7: For when they came into the house, he lay on his bed in his bed-chamber, and they smote him, and slew him, and beheaded him, and took his head, and went away through the plain all night.
texts.2sa.4.8: And they brought the head of Ish-bosheth to David to Hebron, and said to the king, Behold the head of Ish-bosheth the son of Saul thy enemy, who sought thy life; and the LORD hath avenged my lord the king this day of Saul and of his seed.
texts.2sa.4.9: And David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said to them, As the LORD liveth, who hath redeemed my soul out of all adversity,
texts.2sa.4.10: When one told me, saying, Behold, Saul is dead, (thinking to have brought good tidings,) I took hold of him, and slew him in Ziklag, who thought that I would have given him a reward for his tidings:
texts.2sa.4.11: How much more, when wicked men have slain a righteous person in his own house upon his bed? shall I not therefore now require his blood of your hand, and take you away from the earth?
texts.2sa.4.12: And David commanded his young men, and they slew them, and cut off their hands and their feet, and hanged them over the pool in Hebron. But they took the head of Ish-bosheth, and buried it in the sepulcher of Abner in Hebron.
texts.2sa.5.1: Then came all the tribes of Israel to David to Hebron, and spoke, saying, Behold, we are thy bone and thy flesh.
texts.2sa.5.2: Also in time past, when Saul was king over us, thou wast he that leddest out and broughtest in Israel: and the LORD said to thee, Thou shalt feed my people Israel, and thou shalt be a captain over Israel.
texts.2sa.5.3: So all the elders of Israel came to the king to Hebron; and king David made a league with them in Hebron before the LORD: and they anointed David king over Israel.
texts.2sa.5.4: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.
texts.2sa.5.5: In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months: and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty and three years over all Israel and Judah.
texts.2sa.5.6: And the king and his men went to Jerusalem to the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land: who spoke to David, saying, Except thou shalt take away the blind and the lame, thou shalt not come in hither: thinking, David cannot come in hither.
texts.2sa.5.7: Nevertheless, David took the strong hold of Zion: the same is the city of David.
texts.2sa.5.8: And David said on that day, Whoever getteth up to the gutter, and smiteth the Jebusites, and the lame and the blind, that are hated by David's soul, he shall be chief and captain: Wherefore they said, The blind and the lame shall not come into the house.
texts.2sa.5.9: So David dwelt in the fort, and called it the city of David. And David built around from Millo and inward.
texts.2sa.5.10: And David went on, and grew great, and the LORD God of hosts was with him.
texts.2sa.5.11: And Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, and cedar-trees, and carpenters, and masons: and they built David a house.
texts.2sa.5.12: And David perceived that the LORD had established him king over Israel, and that he had exalted his kingdom for his people Israel's sake.
texts.2sa.5.13: And David took him more concubines and wives out of Jerusalem, after he had come from Hebron: and there were yet sons and daughters born to David.
texts.2sa.5.14: And these are the names of those that were born to him in Jerusalem; Shammuah, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon,
texts.2sa.5.15: Ibhar also, and Elishua, and Nepheg, and Japhia,
texts.2sa.5.16: And Elishama, and Eliada, and Eliphalet.
texts.2sa.5.17: But when the Philistines heard that they had anointed David king over Israel, all the Philistines came up to seek David; and David heard of it, and went down to the hold.
texts.2sa.5.18: The Philistines also came and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.
texts.2sa.5.19: And David inquired of the LORD, saying, Shall I go up to the Philistines? wilt thou deliver them into my hand? And the LORD said to David, Go up: for I will doubtless deliver the Philistines into thy hand.
texts.2sa.5.20: And David came to Baal-perazim, and David smote them there, and said, The LORD hath broken forth upon my enemies before me, as the breach of waters. Therefore he called the name of that place Baal-perazim.
texts.2sa.5.21: And there they left their images, and David and his men burned them.
texts.2sa.5.22: And the Philistines came yet again, and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.
texts.2sa.5.23: And when David inquired of the LORD, he said, Thou shalt not go up: but fetch a compass behind them, and come upon them over against the mulberry-trees.
texts.2sa.5.24: And let it be, when thou hearest the sound of a going in the tops of the mulberry-trees, that then thou shalt bestir thyself: for then shall the LORD go out before thee, to smite the host of the Philistines.
texts.2sa.5.25: And David did so as the LORD had commanded him; and smote the Philistines from Geba until thou comest to Gazer.
texts.2sa.6.1: Again, David assembled all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand,
texts.2sa.6.2: And David arose, and went with all the people that were with him from Baale of Judah, to bring up from thence the ark of God, whose name is called by the name of the LORD of hosts that dwelleth between the cherubim.
texts.2sa.6.3: And they set the ark of God upon a new cart, and brought it out of the house of Abinadab that was in Gibeah: and Uzzah and Ahio the sons of Abinadab drove the new cart.
texts.2sa.6.4: And they brought it out of the house of Abinadab, which was at Gibeah, accompanying the ark of God: and Ahio went before the ark.
texts.2sa.6.5: And David and all the house of Israel played before the LORD on all manner of instruments made of fir wood, even on harps, and on psalteries, and on timbrels, and on cornets, and on cymbals.
texts.2sa.6.6: And when they came to Nachon's threshing-floor, Uzzah put forth his hand to the ark of God, and took hold of it: for the oxen shook it.
texts.2sa.6.7: And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Uzzah, and God smote him there for his error; and there he died by the ark of God.
texts.2sa.6.8: And David was displeased, because the LORD had made a breach upon Uzzah: and he called the name of the place Perez-uzzah to this day.
texts.2sa.6.9: And David was afraid of the LORD that day, and said, How shall the ark of the LORD come to me?
texts.2sa.6.10: So David would not remove the ark of the LORD to him into the city of David: but David carried it aside into the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
texts.2sa.6.11: And the ark of the LORD continued in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite three months: and the LORD blessed Obed-edom and all his household.
texts.2sa.6.12: And it was told king David, saying, The LORD hath blessed the house of Obed-edom, and all that pertaineth to him, because of the ark of God. So David went and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obed-edom into the city of David with gladness.
texts.2sa.6.13: And it was so, that when they that bore the ark of the LORD had gone six paces, he sacrificed oxen and fatlings.
texts.2sa.6.14: And David danced before the LORD with all his might; and David was girded with a linen ephod.
texts.2sa.6.15: So David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the LORD with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet.
texts.2sa.6.16: And as the ark of the LORD came into the city of David, Michal, Saul's daughter, looked through a window, and saw king David leaping and dancing before the LORD; and she despised him in her heart.
texts.2sa.6.17: And they brought in the ark of the LORD, and set it in its place, in the midst of the tabernacle that David had pitched for it: and David offered burnt-offerings and peace-offerings before the LORD.
texts.2sa.6.18: And as soon as David had made an end of offering burnt-offerings and peace-offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of hosts.
texts.2sa.6.19: And he dealt among all the people, even among the whole multitude of Israel, as well to the women as men, to every one a cake of bread, and a good piece of flesh, and a flagon of wine. So all the people departed every one to his house.
texts.2sa.6.20: Then David returned to bless his household. And Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David, and said, How glorious was the king of Israel to-day, who uncovered himself to-day in the eyes of the handmaids of his servants, as one of the vain fellows shamelessly uncovereth himself!
texts.2sa.6.21: And David said to Michal, It was before the LORD, who chose me before thy father, and before all his house, to appoint me ruler over the people of the LORD, over Israel: therefore will I play before the LORD.
texts.2sa.6.22: And I shall yet be more vile than thus, and shall be base in my own sight: and by the maid-servants which thou hast spoken of, by them shall I be had in honor.
texts.2sa.6.23: Therefore Michal the daughter of Saul had no child until the day of her death.
texts.2sa.7.1: And it came to pass, when the king sat in his house, and the LORD had given him rest around from all his enemies;
texts.2sa.7.2: That the king said to Nathan the prophet, See now, I dwell in a house of cedar, but the ark of God dwelleth within curtains.
texts.2sa.7.3: And Nathan said to the king, Go, do all that is in thy heart: for the LORD is with thee.
texts.2sa.7.4: And it came to pass that night, that the word of the LORD came to Nathan, saying,
texts.2sa.7.5: Go and tell my servant David, Thus saith the LORD, Wilt thou build me a house for me to dwell in?
texts.2sa.7.6: Whereas I have not dwelt in any house since the time that I brought the children of Israel out of Egypt, even to this day, but have walked in a tent, and in a tabernacle.
texts.2sa.7.7: In all the places in which I have walked with all the children of Israel have I spoken a word with any of the tribes of Israel, whom I commanded to feed my people Israel, saying, Why do ye not build me a house of cedar?
texts.2sa.7.8: Now therefore so shalt thou say to my servant David, thus saith the LORD of hosts, I took thee from the sheep-cote, from following the sheep, to be ruler over my people, over Israel:
texts.2sa.7.9: And I was with thee whithersoever thou wentest, and have cut off all thy enemies out of thy sight, and have made thee a great name, like to the name of the great men that are in the earth.
texts.2sa.7.10: Moreover, I will appoint a place for my people Israel, and will plant them, that they may dwell in a place of their own, and move no more; neither shall the children of wickedness afflict them any more, as formerly.
texts.2sa.7.11: And as since the time that I commanded judges to be over my people Israel, and have caused thee to rest from all thy enemies. Also the LORD telleth thee that he will make thee a house.
texts.2sa.7.12: And when thy days shall be fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom.
texts.2sa.7.13: He shall build a house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom for ever.
texts.2sa.7.14: I will be his father, and he shall be my son. If he shall commit iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men:
texts.2sa.7.15: But my mercy shall not depart from him, as I took it from Saul, whom I put away before thee.
texts.2sa.7.16: And thy house and thy kingdom shall be established for ever before thee: thy throne shall be established for ever.
texts.2sa.7.17: According to all these words, and according to all this vision, so did Nathan speak to David.
texts.2sa.7.18: Then king David went in, and sat before the LORD, and he said, Who am I, O Lord GOD? and what is my house, that thou hast brought me hitherto;
texts.2sa.7.19: And this was yet a small thing in thy sight, O Lord GOD; but thou hast spoken also of thy servant's house for a great while to come. And is this the manner of man, O Lord GOD?
texts.2sa.7.20: And what can David say more to thee? for thou, Lord GOD, knowest thy servant.
texts.2sa.7.21: For thy word's sake, and according to thy own heart, hast thou done all these great things, to make thy servant know them.
texts.2sa.7.22: Wherefore thou art great, O LORD God: for there is none like thee, neither is there any God besides thee, according to all that we have heard with our ears.
texts.2sa.7.23: And what one nation in the earth is like thy people, even like Israel, whom God went to redeem for a people to himself, and to make him a name, and to do for you great things and terrible, for thy land, before thy people which thou redeemedst to thee from Egypt, from the nations and their gods?
texts.2sa.7.24: For thou hast confirmed to thyself thy people Israel to be a people to thee for ever: and thou, LORD, art become their God.
texts.2sa.7.25: And now, O LORD God, the word that thou hast spoken concerning thy servant, and concerning his house, establish it for ever, and do as thou hast said.
texts.2sa.7.26: And let thy name be magnified for ever, saying, The LORD of hosts is the God over Israel: and let the house of thy servant David be established before thee.
texts.2sa.7.27: For thou, O LORD of hosts, God of Israel, hast revealed to thy servant, saying, I will build thee a house: therefore hath thy servant found in his heart to pray this prayer to thee.
texts.2sa.7.28: And now, O Lord GOD, thou art that God, and thy words are true, and thou hast promised this goodness to thy servant:
texts.2sa.7.29: Therefore now let it please thee to bless the house of thy servant, that it may continue for ever before thee: for thou, O Lord GOD, hast spoken it: and with thy blessing let the house of thy servant be blessed for ever.
texts.2sa.8.1: And after this it came to pass, that David smote the Philistines, and subdued them: and David took Metheg-ammah out of the hand of the Philistines.
texts.2sa.8.2: And he smote Moab, and measured them with a line, casting them down to the ground; even with two lines he measured to put to death, and with one full line to keep alive. And so the Moabites became David's servants, and brought gifts.
texts.2sa.8.3: David smote also Hadadezer, the son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he went to recover his border at the river Euphrates.
texts.2sa.8.4: And David took from him a thousand chariots, and seven hundred horsemen, and twenty thousand footmen: and David houghed all the chariot-horses, but reserved of them for a hundred chariots.
texts.2sa.8.5: And when the Syrians of Damascus came to succor Hadadezer king of Zobah, David slew of the Syrians two and twenty thousand men.
texts.2sa.8.6: Then David put garrisons in Syria of Damascus: and the Syrians became servants to David, and brought gifts. And the LORD preserved David whithersoever he went.
texts.2sa.8.7: And David took the shields of gold that were on the servants of Hadadezer, and brought them to Jerusalem.
texts.2sa.8.8: And from Betah, and from Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, king David took very much brass.
texts.2sa.8.9: When Toi king of Hamath heard that David had smitten all the host of Hadadezer,
texts.2sa.8.10: Then Toi sent Joram his son to king David, to salute him, and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer, and smitten him: (for Hadadezer had wars with Toi) and Joram brought with him vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and vessels of brass:
texts.2sa.8.11: Which also king David dedicated to the LORD, with the silver and gold that he had dedicated of all nations which he subdued;
texts.2sa.8.12: Of Syria, and of Moab, and of the children of Ammon, and of the Philistines, and of Amalek, and of the spoil of Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
texts.2sa.8.13: And David made him a name when he returned from smiting of the Syrians in the valley of Salt, being eighteen thousand men.
texts.2sa.8.14: And he put garrisons in Edom; throughout all Edom he put garrisons, and all they of Edom became David's servants. And the LORD preserved David whithersoever he went.
texts.2sa.8.15: And David reigned over all Israel; and David executed judgment and justice to all his people.
texts.2sa.8.16: And Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the host; and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder;
texts.2sa.8.17: And Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, were the priests: and Seraiah was the scribe;
texts.2sa.8.18: And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over both the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and David's sons were chief rulers.
texts.2sa.9.1: And David said, Is there yet any that is left of the house of Saul, that I may show him kindness for Jonathan's sake?
texts.2sa.9.2: And there was of the house of Saul a servant whose name was Ziba. And when they had called him to David, the king said to him, Art thou Ziba? And he said, Thy servant is he.
texts.2sa.9.3: And the king said, Is there not yet any of the house of Saul, that I may show the kindness of God to him? and Ziba said to the king, Jonathan hath yet a son, who is lame in his feet.
texts.2sa.9.4: And the king said to him, Where is he? And Ziba said to the king, Behold, he is in the house of Machir, the son of Ammiel, in Lo-debar.
texts.2sa.9.5: Then king David sent, and brought him from the house of Machir, the son of Ammiel, from Lo-debar.
texts.2sa.9.6: Now when Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, had come to David, he fell on his face, and did reverence. And David said, Mephibosheth. And he answered, Behold thy servant!
texts.2sa.9.7: And David said to him, Fear not: for I will surely show thee kindness for the sake of Jonathan thy father, and will restore thee all the land of Saul thy father; and thou shalt eat bread at my table continually.
texts.2sa.9.8: And he bowed himself, and said, What is thy servant, that thou shouldst look upon such a dead dog as I am?
texts.2sa.9.9: Then the king called to Ziba, Saul's servant, and said to him, I have given to thy master's son all that pertained to Saul, and to all his house.
texts.2sa.9.10: Thou therefore, and thy sons, and thy servants, shall till the land for him, and thou shalt bring in the fruits, that thy master's son may have food to eat: but Mephibosheth thy master's son shall eat bread always at my table. Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.
texts.2sa.9.11: Then said Ziba to the king, According to all that my lord the king hath commanded his servant, so shall thy servant do. As for Mephibosheth, said the king, he shall eat at my table, as one of the king's sons.
texts.2sa.9.12: And Mephibosheth had a young son, whose name was Micah. And all that dwelt in the house of Ziba were servants to Mephibosheth.
texts.2sa.9.13: So Mephibosheth dwelt in Jerusalem: for he ate continually at the king's table; and was lame in both his feet.
texts.2sa.10.1: And it came to pass after this, that the king of the children of Ammon died, and Hanun his son reigned in his stead.
texts.2sa.10.2: Then said David, I will show kindness to Hanun the son of Nahash, as his father showed kindness to me. And David sent to comfort him by the hand of his servants for his father. And David's servants came into the land of the children of Ammon.
texts.2sa.10.3: And the princes of the children of Ammon said to Hanun their lord, Thinkest thou that David doth honor thy father, that he hath sent comforters to thee? hath not David rather sent his servants to thee, to search the city, and to spy it out, and to overthrow it?
texts.2sa.10.4: Wherefore Hanun took David's servants, and shaved off the one half of their beards, and cut off their garments in the middle, even to their buttocks, and sent them away.
texts.2sa.10.5: When they told it to David, he sent to meet them, because the men were greatly ashamed. And the king said, Tarry at Jericho until your beards are grown, and then return.
texts.2sa.10.6: And when the children of Ammon saw that they had made themselves odious before David, the children of Ammon sent and hired the Syrians of Beth-rehob, and the Syrians of Zoba, twenty thousand footmen, and of king Maacah a thousand men, and of Ish-tob twelve thousand men.
texts.2sa.10.7: And when David heard of it, he sent Joab, and all the host of the mighty men.
texts.2sa.10.8: And the children of Ammon came out, and put the battle in array at the entrance of the gate: and the Syrians of Zoba, and of Rehob, and Ish-tob, and Maacah, were by themselves in the field.
texts.2sa.10.9: When Joab saw that the front of the battle was against him before and behind, he selected of all the choice men of Israel, and put them in array against the Syrians:
texts.2sa.10.10: And the rest of the people he delivered into the hand of Abishai his brother, that he might put them in array against the children of Ammon.
texts.2sa.10.11: And he said, If the Syrians shall be too strong for me, then thou shalt help me: but if the children of Ammon shall be too strong for thee, then I will come and help thee.
texts.2sa.10.12: Be of good courage, and let us play the men for our people, and for the cities of our God: and the LORD do that which seemeth him good.
texts.2sa.10.13: And Joab and the people that were with him drew near to the battle against the Syrians: and they fled before him.
texts.2sa.10.14: And when the children of Ammon saw that the Syrians had fled, then fled they also before Abishai, and entered into the city. So Joab returned from the children of Ammon, and came to Jerusalem.
texts.2sa.10.15: And when the Syrians saw that they were smitten before Israel, they assembled themselves.
texts.2sa.10.16: And Hadarezer sent, and brought out the Syrians that were beyond the river: and they came to Helam; and Shobach the captain of the host of Hadarezer went before them.
texts.2sa.10.17: And when it was told David, he assembled all Israel, and passed over Jordan, and came to Helam. And the Syrians set themselves in array against David, and fought with him.
texts.2sa.10.18: And the Syrians fled before Israel; and David slew the men of seven hundred chariots of the Syrians, and forty thousand horsemen, and smote Shobach the captain of their host, who died there.
texts.2sa.10.19: And when all the kings that were servants to Hadarezer saw that they were smitten before Israel, they made peace with Israel, and served them. So the Syrians feared to help the children of Ammon any more.
texts.2sa.11.1: And it came to pass, after the year had expired, at the time when kings go forth to battle, that David sent Joab, and his servants with him, and all Israel; and they destroyed the children of Ammon, and destroyed Rabbah. But David tarried still at Jerusalem.
texts.2sa.11.2: And it came to pass in an evening, that David arose from off his bed, and walked upon the roof of the king's house: and from the roof he saw a woman washing herself; and the woman was very beautiful to look upon.
texts.2sa.11.3: And David sent and inquired after the woman. And one said, Is not this Bath-sheba, the daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?
texts.2sa.11.4: And David sent messengers, and took her; and she came in to him, and he lay with her; for she was purified from her uncleanness: and she returned to her house.
texts.2sa.11.5: And the woman conceived, and sent and told David, and said, I am with child.
texts.2sa.11.6: And David sent to Joab, saying, Send me Uriah the Hittite. And Joab sent Uriah to David.
texts.2sa.11.7: And when Uriah had come to him, David inquired of him how Joab did, and how the people did, and how the war prospered.
texts.2sa.11.8: And David said to Uriah, Go down to thy house, and wash thy feet. And Uriah departed out of the king's house, and there followed him a mess of meat from the king.
texts.2sa.11.9: But Uriah slept at the door of the king's house with all the servants of his lord, and went not down to his house.
texts.2sa.11.10: And when they had told David, saying, Uriah went not down to his house, David said to Uriah, Camest thou not from thy journey? why then didst thou not go down to thy house?
texts.2sa.11.11: And Uriah said to David, The ark, and Israel, and Judah, abide in tents; and my lord Joab, and the servants of my lord are encamped in the open fields; shall I then go into my house, to eat and to drink, and to lie with my wife? as thou livest, and as thy soul liveth, I will not do this thing.
texts.2sa.11.12: And David said to Uriah, Tarry here to-day also, and to-morrow I will let thee depart. So Uriah abode in Jerusalem that day and the morrow.
texts.2sa.11.13: And when David had called him, he ate and drank before him; and he made him drunk: and at evening he went out to lie on his bed with the servants of his lord, but went not down to his house.
texts.2sa.11.14: And it came to pass in the morning, that David wrote a letter to Joab, and sent it by the hand of Uriah.
texts.2sa.11.15: And he wrote in the letter, saying, Set ye Uriah in the front of the hottest battle, and retire ye from him, that he may be smitten, and die.
texts.2sa.11.16: And it came to pass, when Joab observed the city, that he assigned Uriah to a place where he knew that valiant men were.
texts.2sa.11.17: And the men of the city went out, and fought with Joab: and there fell some of the people of the servants of David; and Uriah the Hittite died also.
texts.2sa.11.18: Then Joab sent and told David all the things concerning the war;
texts.2sa.11.19: And charged the messenger, saying, When thou hast made an end of telling the matters of the war to the king,
texts.2sa.11.20: And if the king's wrath shall rise, and he shall say to thee, Why approached ye so nigh to the city for the fight? knew ye not that they would shoot from the wall?
texts.2sa.11.21: Who smote Abimelech the son of Jerubbesheth? did not a woman cast a piece of a millstone upon him from the wall, that he died in Thebez? why went ye nigh the wall? then say thou, Thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.
texts.2sa.11.22: So the messenger went, and came and showed David all that Joab had sent him for.
texts.2sa.11.23: And the messenger said to David, Surely the men prevailed against us, and came out to us into the field, and we were upon them even to the entrance of the gate.
texts.2sa.11.24: And the shooters shot from off the wall upon thy servants: and some of the king's servants are dead, and thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.
texts.2sa.11.25: Then David said to the messenger, Thus shalt thou say to Joab, Let not this thing displease thee, for the sword devoureth one as well as another: make thy battle more strong against the city, and overthrow it: and encourage thou him.
texts.2sa.11.26: And when the wife of Uriah heard that Uriah her husband was dead, she mourned for her husband.
texts.2sa.11.27: And when the mourning was past, David sent and brought her to his house, and she became his wife, and bore him a son. But the thing that David had done displeased the LORD.
texts.2sa.12.1: And the LORD sent Nathan to David. And he came to him, and said to him, There were two men in one city; the one rich, and the other poor.
texts.2sa.12.2: The rich man had very numerous flocks and herds:
texts.2sa.12.3: But the poor man had nothing save one little ewe-lamb, which he had bought and nourished: and it grew up together with him, and with his children: it fed of his own meat, and drank of his own cup, and lay in his bosom, and was to him as a daughter.
texts.2sa.12.4: And there came a traveler to the rich man, and he spared to take of his own flock and of his own herd, to dress for the way-faring man that had come to him; but took the poor man's lamb, and dressed it for the man that had come to him.
texts.2sa.12.5: And David's anger was greatly kindled against the man; and he said to Nathan, As the LORD liveth, the man that hath done this thing shall surely die:
texts.2sa.12.6: And he shall restore the lamb four-fold, because he did this thing, and because he had no pity.
texts.2sa.12.7: And Nathan said to David, Thou art the man. Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, I anointed thee king over Israel, and I delivered thee from the hand of Saul;
texts.2sa.12.8: And I gave thee thy master's house, and thy master's wives into thy bosom, and gave thee the house of Israel and of Judah; and if that had been too little, I would moreover have given to thee such and such things.
texts.2sa.12.9: Why hast thou despised the commandment of the LORD, to do evil in his sight? thou hast killed Uriah the Hittite with the sword, and hast taken his wife to be thy wife, and hast slain him with the sword of the children of Ammon.
texts.2sa.12.10: Now therefore the sword shall never depart from thy house; because thou hast despised me, and hast taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be thy wife.
texts.2sa.12.11: Thus saith the LORD, Behold, I will raise up evil against thee out of thy own house, and I will take thy wives before thy eyes, and give them to thy neighbor, and he shall lie with thy wives in the sight of this sun.
texts.2sa.12.12: For thou didst it secretly: but I will do this thing before all Israel, and before the sun.
texts.2sa.12.13: And David said to Nathan, I have sinned against the LORD. And Nathan said to David, The LORD also hath put away thy sin; thou shalt not die.
texts.2sa.12.14: But, because by this deed thou hast given great occasion to the enemies of the LORD to blaspheme, the child also that is born to thee shall surely die.
texts.2sa.12.15: And Nathan departed to his house. And the LORD struck the child that Uriah's wife bore to David, and it was very sick.
texts.2sa.12.16: David therefore besought God for the child; and David fasted, and went in, and lay all night upon the earth.
texts.2sa.12.17: And the elders of his house arose, and went to him, to raise him from the earth: but he would not, neither did he eat bread with them.
texts.2sa.12.18: And it came to pass on the seventh day, that the child died. And the servants of David feared to tell him that the child was dead: for they said, Behold while the child was yet alive, we spoke to him, and he would not hearken to our voice: how will he then be grieved, if we tell him that the child is dead?
texts.2sa.12.19: But when David saw that his servants whispered, David perceived that the child was dead: therefore David said to his servants, Is the child dead? And they said, He is dead.
texts.2sa.12.20: Then David arose from the earth, and washed, and anointed himself, and changed his apparel, and came into the house of the LORD, and worshiped: then he came to his own house; and when he required, they set bread before him, and he ate.
texts.2sa.12.21: Then said his servants to him, What thing is this that thou hast done? thou didst fast and weep for the child, while it was alive; but after the child was dead, thou didst rise and eat bread.
texts.2sa.12.22: And he said, While the child was yet alive, I fasted, and wept: for I said, Who can tell whether GOD will be gracious to me, that the child may live?
texts.2sa.12.23: But now he is dead, Why should I fast? can I bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he will not return to me.
texts.2sa.12.24: And David comforted Bath-sheba his wife, and went in to her, and lay with her: and she bore a son, and he called his name Solomon: and the LORD loved him.
texts.2sa.12.25: And he sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet; and he called his name Jedidiah, because of the LORD.
texts.2sa.12.26: And Joab fought against Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and took the royal city.
texts.2sa.12.27: And Joab sent messengers to David, and said, I have fought against Rabbah, and have taken the city of waters.
texts.2sa.12.28: Now therefore collect the rest of the people, and encamp against the city, and take it: lest I take the city, and it be called after my name.
texts.2sa.12.29: And David collected all the people, and went to Rabbah, and fought against it, and took it.
texts.2sa.12.30: And he took their king's crown from off his head, the weight of which was a talent of gold with the precious stones: and it was set on David's head. And he brought forth the spoil of the city in great abundance.
texts.2sa.12.31: And he brought forth the people that were in it, and put them under saws, and under harrows of iron, and under axes of iron, and made them pass through the brick-kiln: and thus he did to all the cities of the children of Ammon. So David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.
texts.2sa.13.1: And it came to pass after this, that Absalom the son of David had a fair sister, whose name was Tamar; and Amnon the son of David loved her.
texts.2sa.13.2: And Amnon was so afflicted, that he fell sick for his sister Tamar; for she was a virgin; and Amnon thought it hard for him to do any thing to her.
texts.2sa.13.3: But Amnon had a friend, whose name was Jonadab, the son of Shimeah David's brother: and Jonadab was a very subtil man.
texts.2sa.13.4: And he said to him, Why art thou, being the king's son, pining from day to day? wilt thou not tell me? And Amnon said to him, I love Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister.
texts.2sa.13.5: And Jonadab said to him, Lay thee down on thy bed, and make thyself sick: and when thy father cometh to see thee, say to him, I pray thee, let my sister Tamar come, and give me food, and dress the food in my sight, that I may see it, and eat it at her hand.
texts.2sa.13.6: So Amnon lay down and made himself sick: and when the king came to see him, Amnon said to the king, I pray thee, let Tamar my sister come, and make for me a couple of cakes in my sight, that I may eat at her hand.
texts.2sa.13.7: Then David sent home to Tamar, saying, Go now to thy brother Amnon's house, and dress meat for him.
texts.2sa.13.8: So Tamar went to her brother Amnon's house; and he was laid down. And she took flour, and kneaded it, and made cakes in his sight, and baked the cakes.
texts.2sa.13.9: And she took a pan, and poured them out before him; but he refused to eat. And Amnon said, Have out all men from me. And they went out every man from him.
texts.2sa.13.10: And Amnon said to Tamar, Bring the food into the chamber, that I may eat from thy hand. And Tamar took the cakes which she had made, and brought them into the chamber to Amnon her brother.
texts.2sa.13.11: And when she had brought them to him to eat, he took hold of her, and said to her, Come, lie with me, my sister.
texts.2sa.13.12: And she answered him, Nay, my brother, do not force me; for no such thing ought to be done in Israel: do not thou this folly.
texts.2sa.13.13: And I, whither shall I cause my shame to go? and as for thee, thou wilt be as one of the fools in Israel. Now therefore, I pray thee, speak to the king; for he will not withhold me from thee.
