texts.2sa.20.16: And a wise woman cried out of the city, Hear, hear: say, I pray you, unto Joab, Come near hither, that I may speak with thee.
texts.2sa.20.17: And he came near to her; and the woman said, Art thou Joab? And he said, I [am he]. And she said to him, Listen to the words of thy handmaid. And he said, I am listening.
texts.2sa.20.18: And she spoke saying, They were wont to speak in old time saying, Just inquire in Abel; and so they ended.
texts.2sa.20.19: I am peaceable [and] faithful in Israel: thou seekest to destroy a city and a mother in Israel. Why wilt thou swallow up the inheritance of Jehovah?
texts.2sa.20.20: And Joab answered and said, Far be it, far be it from me, that I should swallow up or destroy.
texts.2sa.20.21: The matter is not so; but a man of mount Ephraim, Sheba the son of Bichri by name, has lifted up his hand against the king, against David: give up him only, and I will depart from the city. And the woman said to Joab, Behold, his head shall be thrown to thee over the wall.
texts.2sa.20.22: Then the woman went to all the people in her wisdom. And they cut off the head of Sheba the son of Bichri, and cast it to Joab. And he blew a trumpet, and they dispersed from the city, every man to his tent. And Joab returned to Jerusalem to the king.
texts.2sa.20.23: And Joab was over all the host of Israel; and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and over the Pelethites;
texts.2sa.20.24: and Adoram was over the levy; and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder;
texts.2sa.20.25: and Sheva was scribe; and Zadok and Abiathar were priests;
texts.2sa.20.26: and Ira also, the Jairite, was David's chief ruler.
texts.2sa.21.1: And there was a famine in the days of David three years, year after year; and David inquired of Jehovah. And Jehovah said, It is for Saul, and for [his] house of blood, because he slew the Gibeonites.
texts.2sa.21.2: And the king called the Gibeonites, and spoke to them. (Now the Gibeonites were not of the children of Israel, but of the remainder of the Amorites; and the children of Israel had sworn to them; and Saul sought to smite them in his zeal for the children of Israel and Judah.)
texts.2sa.21.3: And David said to the Gibeonites, What shall I do for you? and with what shall I make atonement, that ye may bless the inheritance of Jehovah?
texts.2sa.21.4: And the Gibeonites said to him, As to Saul and his house, it is with us no question of receiving silver or gold, neither is it for us to have any man put to death in Israel. And he said, What ye say will I do for you.
texts.2sa.21.5: And they said to the king, The man that consumed us, and that devised against us that we should be destroyed from remaining in all the borders of Israel,
texts.2sa.21.6: let seven men of his sons be given up to us, and we will hang them up to Jehovah in Gibeah of Saul, the chosen of Jehovah. And the king said, I will give [them].
texts.2sa.21.7: But the king spared Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan the son of Saul, because of Jehovah's oath that was between them, between David and Jonathan the son of Saul.
texts.2sa.21.8: And the king took the two sons of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, whom she had borne to Saul, Armoni and Mephibosheth; and the five sons of [the sister of] Michal the daughter of Saul, whom she had borne to Adriel the son of Barzillai the Meholathite;
texts.2sa.21.9: and he gave them into the hands of the Gibeonites, and they hanged them on the hill before Jehovah. And they fell all seven together, and were put to death in the first days of the harvest, in the beginning of barley harvest.
texts.2sa.21.10: Then Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackcloth, and spread it for her upon the rock, from the beginning of harvest until water poured on them out of the heavens, and suffered neither the fowl of the heavens to rest on them by day, nor the beasts of the field by night.
texts.2sa.21.11: And it was told David what Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, the concubine of Saul, had done.
texts.2sa.21.12: And David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the men of Jabesh-Gilead, who had stolen them from the open place of Beth-shan, where the Philistines had hanged them, the day the Philistines had smitten Saul in Gilboa;
texts.2sa.21.13: and he brought up from thence the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son; and they gathered the bones of them that were hanged.
texts.2sa.21.14: And they buried [them] with the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son in the country of Benjamin in Zela, in the sepulchre of Kish his father; and they did all that the king had commanded. And afterwards God was propitious to the land.
texts.2sa.21.15: And the Philistines had yet war again with Israel; and David went down, and his servants with him, and fought with the Philistines. And David was exhausted.
texts.2sa.21.16: And Ishbibenob, who was of the children of Raphah -- the weight of his lance was three hundred shekels of bronze, and he was girded with new [armour] -- thought to smite David.
texts.2sa.21.17: And Abishai the son of Zeruiah succoured him, and smote the Philistine and killed him. Then the men of David swore to him, saying, Thou shalt go no more out with us to battle, that thou quench not the lamp of Israel.
texts.2sa.21.18: And it came to pass after this, that there was again a battle with the Philistines, at Gob; then Sibbechai the Hushathite smote Saph, who was of the children of Raphah.
texts.2sa.21.19: And there was again a battle at Gob with the Philistines; and Elhanan the son of Jaare-oregim, a Bethlehemite, smote Goliath the Gittite; now the shaft of his spear was like a weaver's beam.
texts.2sa.21.20: And there was again a battle, at Gath; and there was a man [there] of great stature, that had on each hand six fingers, and on each foot six toes, four and twenty in number; and he also was born to Raphah.
texts.2sa.21.21: And he defied Israel; but Jonathan the son of Shimea David's brother smote him.
texts.2sa.21.22: These four were born to Raphah, in Gath; and they fell by the hand of David, and by the hand of his servants.
texts.2sa.22.1: And David spoke to Jehovah the words of this song in the day that Jehovah had delivered him out of the hand of all his enemies, and out of the hand of Saul.
texts.2sa.22.2: And he said, Jehovah is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer;
texts.2sa.22.3: God is my rock, in him will I trust -- My shield, and the horn of my salvation, My high tower, and my refuge, My saviour: thou wilt save me from violence.
texts.2sa.22.4: I will call upon Jehovah, who is to be praised; So shall I be saved from mine enemies.
texts.2sa.22.5: For the waves of death encompassed me, Torrents of Belial made me afraid.
texts.2sa.22.6: The bands of Sheol surrounded me; The cords of death encountered me;
texts.2sa.22.7: In my distress I called upon Jehovah, And I cried to my God; And he heard my voice out of his temple, And my cry [came] into his ears.
texts.2sa.22.8: Then the earth shook, and quaked; The foundations of the heavens trembled And shook because he was wroth.
texts.2sa.22.9: There went up a smoke out of his nostrils, And fire out of his mouth devoured: Coals burned forth from it.
texts.2sa.22.10: And he bowed the heavens, and came down; And darkness was under his feet.
texts.2sa.22.11: And he rode upon a cherub, and did fly; And he was seen upon the wings of the wind.
texts.2sa.22.12: And he made darkness round about him a tent, Gatherings of waters, thick clouds of the skies.
texts.2sa.22.13: From the brightness before him Burned forth coals of fire.
texts.2sa.22.14: Jehovah thundered from the heavens, And the Most High uttered his voice.
texts.2sa.22.15: And he sent arrows, and scattered [mine enemies]; Lightning, and discomfited them.
texts.2sa.22.16: And the beds of the sea were seen, The foundations of the world were uncovered At the rebuke of Jehovah, At the blast of the breath of his nostrils.
texts.2sa.22.17: He reached forth from above, he took me, He drew me out of great waters;
texts.2sa.22.18: He delivered me from my strong enemy, From them that hated me; For they were mightier than I.
texts.2sa.22.19: They encountered me in the day of my calamity; But Jehovah was my stay.
texts.2sa.22.20: And he brought me forth into a large place; He delivered me, because he delighted in me.
texts.2sa.22.21: Jehovah hath rewarded me according to my righteousness, According to the cleanness of my hands hath he recompensed me.
texts.2sa.22.22: For I have kept the ways of Jehovah, And have not wickedly departed from my God.
texts.2sa.22.23: For all his ordinances were before me, And his statutes, I did not depart from them,
texts.2sa.22.24: And I was upright before him, And kept myself from mine iniquity.
texts.2sa.22.25: And Jehovah hath recompensed me according to my righteousness, According to my cleanness in his sight.
texts.2sa.22.26: With the gracious thou dost shew thyself gracious; With the upright man thou dost shew thyself upright;
texts.2sa.22.27: With the pure thou dost shew thyself pure; And with the perverse thou dost shew thyself contrary.
texts.2sa.22.28: And the afflicted people thou dost save; And thine eyes are upon the haughty, [whom] thou bringest down.
texts.2sa.22.29: For thou art my lamp, Jehovah; And Jehovah enlighteneth my darkness.
texts.2sa.22.30: For by thee I have run through a troop; By my God have I leaped over a wall.
texts.2sa.22.31: As for ùGod, his way is perfect; The word of Jehovah is tried: He is a shield to all that trust in him.
texts.2sa.22.32: For who is ùGod, save Jehovah? And who is a rock, save our God?
texts.2sa.22.33: ùGod is my strong fortress, And he maketh my way perfectly smooth.
texts.2sa.22.34: He maketh my feet like hinds' [feet], And setteth me upon my high places.
texts.2sa.22.35: He teacheth my hands to war, And mine arms bend a bow of brass.
texts.2sa.22.36: And thou didst give me the shield of thy salvation, And thy condescending gentleness hath made me great.
texts.2sa.22.37: Thou enlargedst my steps under me; And mine ankles did not slip.
texts.2sa.22.38: I pursued mine enemies, and destroyed them, And I turned not again till they were consumed.
texts.2sa.22.39: And I have consumed them and have crushed them, and they rose not again; Yea, they fell under my feet.
texts.2sa.22.40: And thou girdedst me with strength to battle: Thou didst subdue under me those that rose up against me.
texts.2sa.22.41: And mine enemies didst thou make to turn their backs unto me, And those that hated me I destroyed.
texts.2sa.22.42: They looked, and there was none to save -- Unto Jehovah, and he answered them not.
texts.2sa.22.43: And I did beat them small as the dust of the earth, I trod them as the mire of the streets; I stamped upon them.
texts.2sa.22.44: And thou hast delivered me from the strivings of my people, Thou hast kept me to be head of the nations: A people I knew not doth serve me:
texts.2sa.22.45: Strangers come cringing unto me: At the hearing of the ear, they obey me.
texts.2sa.22.46: Strangers have faded away, And they come trembling forth from their close places.
texts.2sa.22.47: Jehovah liveth; and blessed be my rock; And exalted be the God, the rock of my salvation,
texts.2sa.22.48: The ùGod who hath avenged me, And hath brought the peoples under me.
texts.2sa.22.49: He brought me forth from mine enemies: Yea, thou hast lifted me up above them that rose up against me; From the man of violence hast thou delivered me.
texts.2sa.22.50: Therefore will I give thanks to thee, Jehovah, among the nations, And will sing psalms to thy name.
texts.2sa.22.51: [It is he] who giveth great deliverances to his king, And sheweth loving-kindness to his anointed, To David, and to his seed for evermore.
texts.2sa.23.1: Now these are the last words of David: David the son of Jesse saith, And the man who was raised up on high, The anointed of the God of Jacob, And the sweet psalmist of Israel saith,
texts.2sa.23.2: The Spirit of Jehovah spoke by me, And his word was on my tongue.
texts.2sa.23.3: The God of Israel said, The Rock of Israel spoke to me, The ruler among men shall be just, Ruling in the fear of God;
texts.2sa.23.4: And [he shall be] as the light or the morning, [like] the rising of the sun, A morning without clouds; [When] from the sunshine, after rain, The green grass springeth from the earth.
texts.2sa.23.5: Although my house be not so before ùGod, Yet he hath made with me an everlasting covenant, Ordered in every way and sure; For [this is] all my salvation, and every desire, Although he make [it] not to grow.
texts.2sa.23.6: But [the sons] of Belial [are] all of them as thorns thrust away, Because they cannot be taken with hands;
texts.2sa.23.7: And the man that will touch them provideth himself with iron and the staff of a spear; And they shall be utterly burned with fire in [their] place.
texts.2sa.23.8: These are the names of the mighty men whom David had: Joseb-Bassebeth, Tachkemonite the chief of the captains: he was Adino the Eznite; he [fought] against eight hundred, slain [by him] at one time.
texts.2sa.23.9: And after him, Eleazar the son of Dodo the son of an Ahohite: he was one of the three mighty men with David, when they had defied the Philistines that were there gathered together to battle, and the men of Israel were gone up.
texts.2sa.23.10: He arose and smote the Philistines until his hand was weary, and his hand clave to the sword; and Jehovah wrought a great deliverance that day; and the people returned after him only to spoil.
texts.2sa.23.11: And after him, Shammah the son of Agee the Hararite: the Philistines were gathered into a troop, and there was there a plot of ground full of lentils, and the people had fled before the Philistines;
texts.2sa.23.12: and he stood in the midst of the plot and delivered it, and smote the Philistines, and Jehovah wrought a great deliverance.
texts.2sa.23.13: And three of the thirty chiefs went down, and came to David in the harvest time to the cave of Adullam, when the troop of the Philistines was encamped in the valley of Rephaim.
texts.2sa.23.14: And David was then in the stronghold; and the Philistines' garrison was then at Bethlehem.
texts.2sa.23.15: And David longed, and said, Oh that one would give me to drink of the water of the well of Bethlehem, which is in the gate!
texts.2sa.23.16: And the three mighty men broke through the camp of the Philistines, and drew water out of the well of Bethlehem, which is in the gate, and took it, and brought it to David; however he would not drink of it, but poured it out to Jehovah.
texts.2sa.23.17: And he said, Be it far from me, Jehovah, that I should do this thing! is it not the blood of the men that went at the risk of their lives? Therefore he would not drink it. These things did the three mighty men.
texts.2sa.23.18: And Abishai, the brother of Joab, the son of Zeruiah, was the chief of three; and he brandished his spear against three hundred and slew them; and he had a name among the three.
texts.2sa.23.19: Was he not most honourable of three? and he was their captain; but he did not attain to the [first] three.
texts.2sa.23.20: And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, son of a valiant man, great in exploits, of Kabzeel: he it was that smote two lions of Moab; and he went down and smote a lion in the midst of a pit on a snowy day.
texts.2sa.23.21: He also smote the Egyptian, an imposing man: and the Egyptian had a spear in his hand; and he went down to him with a staff, and plucked the spear out of the Egyptian's hand, and slew him with his own spear.
texts.2sa.23.22: These things did Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and he had a name among the three mighty men.
texts.2sa.23.23: He was honoured above the thirty, but he did not attain to the [first] three. And David set him in his council.
texts.2sa.23.24: Asahel the brother of Joab was one of the thirty; Elhanan the son of Dodo of Bethlehem,
texts.2sa.23.25: Shammah the Harodite, Elika the Harodite,
texts.2sa.23.26: Helez the Paltite, Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite,
texts.2sa.23.27: Abiezer the Anathothite, Mebunnai the Hushathite,
texts.2sa.23.28: Zalmon the Ahohite, Maharai the Netophathite,
texts.2sa.23.29: Heleb the son of Baanah, the Netophathite, Ittai the son of Ribai of Gibeah of the children of Benjamin,
texts.2sa.23.30: Benaiah a Pirathonite, Hiddai of the brooks of Gaash,
texts.2sa.23.31: Abi-albon the Arbathite, Azmaveth the Barhumite,
texts.2sa.23.32: Eliahba the Shaalbonite, of the sons of Jashen, Jonathan,
texts.2sa.23.33: Shammah the Ararite, Ahiam the son of Sharar the Ararite,
texts.2sa.23.34: Eliphelet the son of Ahasbai, the son of the Maachathite, Eliam the son of Ahithophel the Gilonite,
texts.2sa.23.35: Hezrai the Carmelite, Paarai the Arbite,
texts.2sa.23.36: Igal the son of Nathan of Zobah, Bani the Gadite,
texts.2sa.23.37: Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Beerothite, the armour-bearer of Joab the son of Zeruiah,
texts.2sa.23.38: Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,
texts.2sa.23.39: Uriah the Hittite: thirty-seven in all.
texts.2sa.24.1: And again the anger of Jehovah was kindled against Israel, and he moved David against them saying, Go, number Israel and Judah.
texts.2sa.24.2: And the king said to Joab the captain of the host, who was with him, Go, I pray thee, through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan even to Beer-sheba, and count the people, that I may know the number of the people.
texts.2sa.24.3: And Joab said to the king, May Jehovah thy God even add to the people, how many soever they be, a hundredfold, and that the eyes of my lord the king may see [it]; but why does my lord the king delight in this thing?
texts.2sa.24.4: But the king's word prevailed against Joab, and against the captains of the army. And Joab and the captains of the army went out from the presence of the king to count the people of Israel.
texts.2sa.24.5: And they passed over the Jordan, and encamped in Aroer, on the right side of the city that is in the midst of the ravine of Gad, and toward Jaazer.
texts.2sa.24.6: And they came to Gilead, and to the land of Tahtim-hodshi; and came to Dan-jaan, and to the environs of Sidon;
texts.2sa.24.7: and they came to the fortified city of Tyre, and to all the cities of the Hivites and of the Canaanites; and went out to the south of Judah, to Beer-sheba.
texts.2sa.24.8: And they went through all the land, and came to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.
texts.2sa.24.9: And Joab gave the sum of the number of the people to the king; and there were of Israel eight hundred thousand valiant men that drew sword; and the men of Judah were five hundred thousand men.
texts.2sa.24.10: And David's heart smote him after he had numbered the people. And David said to Jehovah, I have sinned greatly in what I have done; and now, I beseech thee, Jehovah, put away the iniquity of thy servant; for I have done very foolishly.
texts.2sa.24.11: And when David arose in the morning, the word of Jehovah came to the prophet Gad, David's seer, saying,
texts.2sa.24.12: Go and say to David, Thus saith Jehovah: I impose on thee three [things]; choose one of them that I may do it unto thee.
texts.2sa.24.13: And Gad came to David, and told him, and said to him, Shall seven years of famine come to thee in thy land? or wilt thou flee three months before thine adversaries while they pursue thee? or shall there be three days' pestilence in thy land? Now be aware and consider what word I shall bring again to him that sent me.
texts.2sa.24.14: And David said to Gad, I am in a great strait: let us fall, I pray thee, into the hand of Jehovah; for his mercies are great; but let me not fall into the hand of man.
texts.2sa.24.15: And Jehovah sent a pestilence upon Israel from the morning even to the set time; and there died of the people from Dan even to Beer-sheba seventy thousand men.
texts.2sa.24.16: And the angel stretched out his hand upon Jerusalem to destroy it; but Jehovah repented him of the evil, and said to the angel that destroyed among the people, It is enough: withdraw now thine hand. And the angel of Jehovah was by the threshing-floor of Araunah the Jebusite.
texts.2sa.24.17: And David spoke to Jehovah when he saw the angel that smote among the people, and said, Behold, it is I that have sinned, and it is I that have committed iniquity; but these sheep, what have they done? let thy hand, I pray thee, be on me, and on my father's house!
texts.2sa.24.18: And Gad came that day to David, and said to him, Go up, rear an altar to Jehovah in the threshing-floor of Araunah the Jebusite.
texts.2sa.24.19: And David, according to the saying of Gad, went up as Jehovah had commanded.
texts.2sa.24.20: And Araunah looked, and saw the king and his servants coming on towards him; and Araunah went out, and bowed himself before the king with his face to the ground.
texts.2sa.24.21: And Araunah said, Why is my lord the king come to his servant? And David said, To buy the threshing-floor of thee, to build an altar to Jehovah, that the plague may be stayed from the people.
texts.2sa.24.22: And Araunah said to David, Let my lord the king take and offer up that which is good in his sight: see, [here are] oxen for the burnt-offering, and the threshing-sledges and implements of the oxen for wood.
texts.2sa.24.23: All these things, O king, doth Araunah give to the king. And Araunah said to the king, Jehovah thy God accept thee.
texts.2sa.24.24: And the king said to Araunah, No; but I will in any case buy [them] of thee at a price: neither will I offer up to Jehovah my God burnt-offerings without cost. And David bought the threshing-floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
texts.2sa.24.25: And David built there an altar to Jehovah, and offered up burnt-offerings and peace-offerings. And Jehovah was propitious to the land, and the plague was stayed from Israel.

texts.2sa.1.1: And it cometh to pass, after the death of Saul, that David hath returned from smiting the Amalekite, and David dwelleth in Ziklag two days,
texts.2sa.1.2: and it cometh to pass, on the third day, that lo, a man hath come in out of the camp from Saul, and his garments [are] rent, and earth on his head; and it cometh to pass, in his coming in unto David, that he falleth to the earth, and doth obeisance.
texts.2sa.1.3: And David saith to him, `Whence comest thou?' and he saith unto him, `Out of the camp of Israel I have escaped.'
texts.2sa.1.4: And David saith unto him, `What hath been the matter? declare, I pray thee, to me.' And he saith, that `The people hath fled from the battle, and also a multitude hath fallen of the people, and they die; and also Saul and Jonathan his son have died.'
texts.2sa.1.5: And David saith unto the youth who is declaring [it] to him, `How hast thou known that Saul and Jonathan his son [are] dead?'
texts.2sa.1.6: And the youth who is declaring [it] to him saith, I happened to meet in mount Gilboa, and lo, Saul is leaning on his spear; and lo, the chariots and those possessing horses have followed him;
texts.2sa.1.7: and he turneth behind him, and seeth me, and calleth unto me, and I say, Here [am] I.
texts.2sa.1.8: And he saith to me, Who [art] thou? and I say unto him, An Amalekite I [am].'
texts.2sa.1.9: `And he saith unto me, Stand, I pray thee, over me, and put me to death, for seized me hath the arrow, for all my soul [is] still in me.
texts.2sa.1.10: And I stand over him, and put him to death, for I knew that he doth not live after his falling, and I take the crown which [is] on his head, and the bracelet which [is] on his arm, and bring them in unto my lord hither.'
texts.2sa.1.11: And David taketh hold on his garments, and rendeth them, and also all the men who [are] with him,
texts.2sa.1.12: and they mourn, and weep, and fast till the evening, for Saul, and for Jonathan his son, and for the people of Jehovah, and for the house of Israel, because they have fallen by the sword.
texts.2sa.1.13: And David saith unto the youth who is declaring [it] to him, `Whence [art] thou?' and he saith, `Son of a sojourner, an Amalekite, I [am].'
texts.2sa.1.14: And David saith unto him, `How wast thou not afraid to put forth thy hand to destroy the anointed of Jehovah?'
texts.2sa.1.15: And David calleth to one of the youths, and saith, `Draw nigh -- fall upon him;' and he smiteth him, and he dieth;
texts.2sa.1.16: and David saith unto him, `Thy blood [is] on thine own head, for thy mouth hath testified against thee, saying, I -- I put to death the anointed of Jehovah.'
texts.2sa.1.17: And David lamenteth with this lamentation over Saul, and over Jonathan his son;
texts.2sa.1.18: and he saith to teach the sons of Judah `The Bow;' lo, it is written on the book of the Upright: --
texts.2sa.1.19: `The Roebuck, O Israel, On thy high places [is] wounded; How have the mighty fallen!
texts.2sa.1.20: Declare [it] not in Gath, Proclaim not the tidings in the streets of Ashkelon, Lest they rejoice -- The daughters of the Philistines, Lest they exult -- The daughters of the Uncircumcised!
texts.2sa.1.21: Mountains of Gilboa! No dew nor rain be on you, And fields of heave-offerings! For there hath become loathsome The shield of the mighty, The shield of Saul -- without the anointed with oil.
texts.2sa.1.22: From the blood of the wounded, From the fat of the mighty, The bow of Jonathan Hath not turned backward; And the sword of Saul doth not return empty.
texts.2sa.1.23: Saul and Jonathan! They are loved and pleasant in their lives, And in their death they have not been parted. Than eagles they have been lighter, Than lions they have been mightier!
texts.2sa.1.24: Daughters of Israel! for Saul weep ye, Who is clothing you [in] scarlet with delights. Who is lifting up ornaments of gold on your clothing.
texts.2sa.1.25: How have the mighty fallen In the midst of the battle! Jonathan! on thy high places wounded!
texts.2sa.1.26: I am in distress for thee, my brother Jonathan, Very pleasant wast thou to me; Wonderful was thy love to me, Above the love of women!
texts.2sa.1.27: How have the mighty fallen, Yea, the weapons of war perish!'
texts.2sa.2.1: And it cometh to pass afterwards, that David asketh at Jehovah, saying, `Do I go up into one of the cities of Judah?' and Jehovah saith unto him, `Go up.' And David saith, `Whither do I go up?' and He saith, `To Hebron.'
texts.2sa.2.2: And David goeth up thither, and also his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail wife of Nabal the Carmelite;
texts.2sa.2.3: and his men who [are] with him hath David brought up -- a man and his household -- and they dwell in the cities of Hebron.
texts.2sa.2.4: And the men of Judah come, and anoint there David for king over the house of Judah; and they declare to David, saying, `The men of Jabesh-Gilead [are] they who buried Saul.'
texts.2sa.2.5: And David sendeth messengers unto the men of Jabesh-Gilead, and saith unto them, `Blessed [are] ye of Jehovah, in that ye have done this kindness with your lord, with Saul, that ye bury him.
texts.2sa.2.6: `And, now, Jehovah doth with you kindness and truth, and also, I do with you this good because ye have done this thing;
texts.2sa.2.7: and now, are your hands strong, and be ye for sons of valour, for your lord Saul. [is] dead, and also -- me have the house of Judah anointed for king over them.'
texts.2sa.2.8: And Abner, son of Ner, head of the host which Saul hath, hath taken Ish-Bosheth, son of Saul, and causeth him to pass over to Mahanaim,
texts.2sa.2.9: and causeth him to reign over Gilead, and over the Ashurite, and over Jezreel, and over Ephraim, and over Benjamin, and over Israel -- all of it.
texts.2sa.2.10: A son of forty years, [is] Ish-Bosheth son of Saul, in his reigning over Israel, and two years he hath reigned, only the house of Judah have been after David.
texts.2sa.2.11: And the number of the days that David hath been king in Hebron, over the house of Judah, is seven years and six months.
texts.2sa.2.12: And Abner son of Ner goeth out, and servants of Ish-Bosheth son of Saul, from Mahanaim to Gibeon.
texts.2sa.2.13: And Joab son of Zeruiah, and servants of David, have gone out, and they meet by the pool of Gibeon together, and sit down, these by the pool on this [side], and these by the pool on that.
texts.2sa.2.14: And Abner saith unto Joab, `Let the youths rise, I pray thee, and they play before us;' and Joab saith, `Let them rise.'
texts.2sa.2.15: And they rise and pass over, in number twelve of Benjamin, even of Ish-Bosheth son of Saul, and twelve of the servants of David.
texts.2sa.2.16: And they lay hold, each on the head of his companion, and his sword [is] in the side of his companion, and they fall together, and [one] calleth that place Helkath-Hazzurim, which [is] in Gibeon,
texts.2sa.2.17: and the battle is very hard on that day, and Abner is smitten, and the men of Israel, before the servants of David.
texts.2sa.2.18: And there are there three sons of Zeruiah, Joab, and Abishai, and Asahel, and Asahel [is] light on his feet, as one of the roes which [are] in the field,
texts.2sa.2.19: And Asahel pursueth after Abner, and hath not turned aside to go to the right or to the left, from after Abner.
texts.2sa.2.20: And Abner looketh behind him, and saith, `Art thou he -- Asahel?' and he saith, `I [am].'
texts.2sa.2.21: And Abner saith to him, `Turn thee aside to thy right hand or to thy left, and seize for thee one of the youths, and take to thee his armour;' and Asahel hath not been willing to turn aside from after him.
texts.2sa.2.22: And Abner addeth again, saying unto Asahel, `Turn thee aside from after me, why do I smite thee to the earth? and how do I lift up my face unto Joab thy brother?'
texts.2sa.2.23: And he refuseth to turn aside, and Abner smiteth him with the hinder part of the spear unto the fifth [rib], and the spear cometh out from behind him, and he falleth there, and dieth under it; and it cometh to pass, every one who hath come unto the place where Asahel hath fallen and dieth -- they stand still.
texts.2sa.2.24: And Joab and Abishai pursue after Abner, and the sun hath gone in, and they have come in unto the height of Ammah, which [is] on the front of Giah, the way of the wilderness of Gibeon.
texts.2sa.2.25: And the sons of Benjamin gather themselves together after Abner, and become one troop, and stand on the top of a certain height,
texts.2sa.2.26: and Abner calleth unto Joab, and saith, `For ever doth the sword consume? hast thou not known that it is bitterness in the latter end? and till when dost thou not say to the people to turn back from after their brethren?'
texts.2sa.2.27: And Joab saith, `God liveth! for unless thou hadst spoken, surely then from the morning had the people gone up each from after his brother.'
texts.2sa.2.28: And Joab bloweth with a trumpet, and all the people stand still, and pursue no more after Israel, nor have they added any more to fight.
texts.2sa.2.29: And Abner and his men have gone through the plain all that night, and pass over the Jordan, and go on [through] all Bithron, and come in to Mahanaim.
texts.2sa.2.30: And Joab hath turned back from after Abner, and gathereth all the people, and there are lacking of the servants of David nineteen men, and Asahel;
texts.2sa.2.31: and the servants of David have smitten of Benjamin, even among the men of Abner, three hundred and sixty men -- they died.
texts.2sa.2.32: And they lift up Asahel, and bury him in the burying-place of his father, which [is] in Beth-Lehem, and they go all the night -- Joab and his men -- and it is light to them in Hebron.
texts.2sa.3.1: And the war is long between the house of Saul and the house of David, and David is going on and [is] strong, and the house of Saul are going on and [are] weak.
texts.2sa.3.2: And there are born to David sons in Hebron, and his first-born is Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess,
texts.2sa.3.3: and his second [is] Chileab, of Abigail wife of Nabal the Carmelite, and the third [is] Absalom son of Maacah daughter of Talmai king of Geshur,
texts.2sa.3.4: and the fourth [is] Adonijah son of Haggith, and the fifth [is] Shephatiah son of Abital,
texts.2sa.3.5: and the sixth [is] Ithream, of Eglah wife of David; these have been born to David in Hebron.
texts.2sa.3.6: And it cometh to pass, in the war being between the house of Saul and the house of David, that Abner hath been strengthening himself in the house of Saul,
texts.2sa.3.7: and Saul hath a concubine, and her name [is] Rizpah daughter of Aiah, and [Ish-Bosheth] saith unto Abner, `Wherefore hast thou gone in unto the concubine of my father?'
texts.2sa.3.8: And it is displeasing to Abner exceedingly, because of the words of Ish-Bosheth, and he saith, `The head of a dog [am] I -- that in reference to Judah to-day I do kindness with the house of Saul thy father, unto his brethren, and unto his friends, and have not delivered thee into the hand of David -- that thou chargest against me iniquity concerning the woman to-day?
texts.2sa.3.9: thus doth God to Abner, and thus He doth add to him, surely as Jehovah hath sworn to David -- surely so I do to him:
texts.2sa.3.10: to cause the kingdom to pass over from the house of Saul, and to raise up the throne of David over Israel, and over Judah, from Dan even unto Beer-Sheba.'
texts.2sa.3.11: And he is not able any more to turn back Abner a word, because of his fearing him.
texts.2sa.3.12: And Abner sendeth messengers unto David for himself, saying, `Whose [is] the land?' saying, `Make thy covenant with me, and lo, my hand [is] with thee, to bring round unto thee all Israel.'
texts.2sa.3.13: And he saith, `Good -- I make with thee a covenant; only, one thing I am asking of thee, that is, Thou dost not see my face, except thou dost first bring in Michal, daughter of Saul in thy coming into see my face.'
texts.2sa.3.14: And David sendeth messengers unto Ish-Bosheth son of Saul, saying, `Give up my wife Michal, whom I betrothed to myself with a hundred foreskins of the Philistines.'
texts.2sa.3.15: And Ish-Bosheth sendeth, and taketh her from a man, from Phaltiel son of Laish,
texts.2sa.3.16: and her husband goeth with her, going on and weeping behind her, unto Bahurim, and Abner saith unto him, `Go, turn back;' and he turneth back.
texts.2sa.3.17: And the word of Abner was with the elders of Israel, saying, `Heretofore ye have been seeking David for king over you,
texts.2sa.3.18: and now, do [it], for Jehovah hath spoken of David saying, By the hand of David my servant -- to save My people Israel out of the hand of the Philistines, and out of the hand of all their enemies.'
texts.2sa.3.19: And Abner speaketh also in the ears of Benjamin, and Abner goeth also to speak in the ears of David in Hebron all that [is] good in the eyes of Israel, and in the eyes of all the house of Benjamin,
texts.2sa.3.20: and Abner cometh in unto David, to Hebron, and with him twenty men, and David maketh for Abner, and for the men who [are] with him, a banquet.
texts.2sa.3.21: And Abner saith unto David, `I arise, and go, and gather unto my lord the king the whole of Israel, and they make with thee a covenant, and thou hast reigned over all that thy soul desireth;' and David sendeth away Abner, and he goeth in peace.
texts.2sa.3.22: And lo, the servants of David, and Joab, have come from the troop, and much spoil have brought with them, and Abner is not with David in Hebron, for he hath sent him away, and he goeth in peace;
texts.2sa.3.23: and Joab and all the host that [is] with him have come, and they declare to Joab, saying, `Abner son of Ner hath come unto the king, and he sendeth him away, and he goeth in peace.'
texts.2sa.3.24: And Joab cometh unto the king, and saith, `What hast thou done? lo, Abner hath come unto thee! why [is] this -- thou hast sent him away, and he is really gone?
texts.2sa.3.25: Thou hast known Abner son of Ner, that to deceive thee he came, and to know thy going out and thy coming in, and to know all that thou art doing.'
texts.2sa.3.26: And Joab goeth out from David, and sendeth messengers after Abner, and they bring him back from the well of Sirah, and David knew not.
texts.2sa.3.27: And Abner turneth back to Hebron, and Joab turneth him aside unto the midst of the gate to speak with him quietly, and smiteth him there in the fifth [rib] -- and he dieth -- for the blood of Asahel his brother.
texts.2sa.3.28: And David heareth afterwards and saith, `Acquitted [am] I, and my kingdom, by Jehovah, unto the age, from the blood of Abner son of Ner;
texts.2sa.3.29: it doth stay on the head of Joab, and on all the house of his father, and there is not cut off from the house of Joab one having an issue, and leprous, and laying hold on a staff, and falling by a sword, and lacking bread.'
texts.2sa.3.30: And Joab and Abishai his brother slew Abner because that he put to death Asahel their brother, in Gibeon, in battle.
texts.2sa.3.31: And David saith unto Joab, and unto all the people who [are] with him, `Rend your garments, and gird on sackcloth, and mourn before Abner;' and king David is going after the bier.
texts.2sa.3.32: And they bury Abner in Hebron, and the king lifteth up his voice, and weepeth at the grave of Abner, and all the people weep;
texts.2sa.3.33: and the king lamenteth for Abner, and saith: -- `As the death of a fool doth Abner die?
texts.2sa.3.34: Thy hands not bound, And thy feet to fetters not brought nigh! As one falling before sons of evil -- Thou hast fallen!' and all the people add to weep over him.
texts.2sa.3.35: And all the people come to cause David to eat bread while yet day, and David sweareth, saying, `Thus doth God to me, and thus He doth add, for -- before the going in of the sun, I taste no bread or any other thing.'
texts.2sa.3.36: And all the people have discerned [it], and it is good in their eyes, as all that the king hath done is good in the eyes of all the people;
texts.2sa.3.37: and all the people know, even all Israel, in that day, that it hath not been from the king -- to put to death Abner son of Ner.
texts.2sa.3.38: And the king saith unto his servants, `Do ye not know that a prince and a great one hath fallen this day in Israel?
texts.2sa.3.39: and I to-day [am] tender, and an anointed king: and these men, sons of Zeruiah, [are] too hard for me; Jehovah doth recompense to the doer of the evil according to his evil.'
texts.2sa.4.1: And the son of Saul heareth that Abner [is] dead in Hebron, and his hands are feeble, and all Israel have been troubled.
texts.2sa.4.2: And two men, heads of troops, have been [to] the son of Saul, the name of the one [is] Baanah, and the name of the second Rechab, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, of the sons of Benjamin, for also Beeroth is reckoned to Benjamin,
texts.2sa.4.3: and the Beerothites flee to Gittaim, and are there sojourners unto this day.
texts.2sa.4.4: And to Jonathan son of Saul [is] a son -- lame; he was a son of five years at the coming in of the rumour of [the death of] Saul and Jonathan, out of Jezreel, and his nurse lifteth him up, and fleeth, and it cometh to pass in her hasting to flee, that he falleth, and becometh lame, and his name [is] Mephibosheth.
texts.2sa.4.5: And the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, go, and come in at the heat of the day unto the house of Ish-Bosheth, and he is lying down -- the lying down of noon;
texts.2sa.4.6: and thither they have come, unto the midst of the house, taking wheat, and they smite him unto the fifth [rib], and Rechab and Baanah his brother have escaped;
texts.2sa.4.7: yea, they come in to the house, and he is lying on his bed, in the inner part of his bed-chamber, and they smite him, and put him to death, and turn aside his head, and they take his head, and go the way of the plain all the night,
texts.2sa.4.8: and bring in the head of Ish-Bosheth unto David in Hebron, and say unto the king, `Lo, the head of Ish-Bosheth, son of Saul, thine enemy, who sought thy life; and Jehovah doth give to my lord the king vengeance this day, of Saul and of his seed.'
texts.2sa.4.9: And David answereth Rechab and Baanah his brother, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and saith to them, `Jehovah liveth, who hath redeemed my soul out of all adversity,
texts.2sa.4.10: when one is declaring to me, saying, Lo, Saul is dead, and he was as a bearer of tidings in his own eyes, then I take hold on him, and slay him in Ziklag, instead of my giving to him [for] the tidings.
texts.2sa.4.11: Also -- when wicked men have slain the righteous man in his own house, on his bed; and now, do not I require his blood of your hand, and have taken you away from the earth?'
texts.2sa.4.12: And David commandeth the young men, and they slay them, and cut off their hands and their feet, and hang [them] over the pool in Hebron, and the head of Ish-Bosheth they have taken, and bury [it] in the burying-place of Abner in Hebron.
texts.2sa.5.1: And all the tribes of Israel come unto David, to Hebron, and speak, saying, `Lo, we [are] thy bone and thy flesh;
texts.2sa.5.2: also heretofore, in Saul's being king over us, thou hast been he who is bringing out and bringing in Israel, and Jehovah saith to thee, Thou dost feed My people Israel, and thou art for leader over Israel.'
texts.2sa.5.3: And all the elders of Israel come unto the king, to Hebron, and king David maketh with them a covenant in Hebron before Jehovah, and they anoint David for king over Israel.
texts.2sa.5.4: A son of thirty years [is] David in his being king; forty years he hath reigned;
texts.2sa.5.5: in Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty and three years, over all Israel and Judah.
texts.2sa.5.6: And the king goeth, and his men, to Jerusalem, unto the Jebusite, the inhabitant of the land, and they speak to David, saying, `Thou dost not come in hither, except thou turn aside the blind and the lame;' saying, `David doth not come in hither.'
texts.2sa.5.7: And David captureth the fortress of Zion, it [is] the city of David.
texts.2sa.5.8: And David saith on that day, `Any one smiting the Jebusite, (let him go up by the watercourse), and the lame and the blind -- the hated of David's soul,' -- because the blind and lame say, `He doth not come into the house.'
texts.2sa.5.9: And David dwelleth in the fortress, and calleth it -- City of David, and David buildeth round about, from Millo and inward,
texts.2sa.5.10: and David goeth, going on and becoming great, and Jehovah, God of Hosts, [is] with him.
texts.2sa.5.11: And Hiram king of Tyre sendeth messengers unto David, and cedar-trees, and artificers of wood, and artificers of stone, for walls, and they build a house for David,
texts.2sa.5.12: and David knoweth that Jehovah hath established him for king over Israel, and that He hath lifted up his kingdom, because of His people Israel.
texts.2sa.5.13: And David taketh again concubines and wives out of Jerusalem, after his coming from Hebron, and there are born again to David sons and daughters.
texts.2sa.5.14: And these [are] the names of those born to him in Jerusalem: Shammuah, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon,
texts.2sa.5.15: and Ibhar, and Elishua, and Nepheg, and Japhia,
texts.2sa.5.16: and Elishama, and Eliada, and Eliphalet.
texts.2sa.5.17: And the Philistines hear that they have anointed David for king over Israel, and all the Philistines come up to seek David, and David heareth, and goeth down unto the fortress,
texts.2sa.5.18: and the Philistines have come, and are spread out in the valley of Rephaim.
texts.2sa.5.19: And David asketh of Jehovah, saying, `Do I go up unto the Philistines? dost Thou give them into my hand?' And Jehovah saith unto David, `Go up, for I certainly give the Philistines into thy hand.'
texts.2sa.5.20: And David cometh in to Baal-Perazim, and David smiteth them there, and saith, `Jehovah hath broken forth [on] mine enemies before me, as the breaking forth of waters;' therefore he hath called the name of that place Baal-Perazim.
texts.2sa.5.21: And they forsake there their idols, and David and his men lift them up.
texts.2sa.5.22: And the Philistines add again to come up, and are spread out in the valley of Rephaim,
texts.2sa.5.23: and David asketh of Jehovah, and He saith, `Thou dost not go up, turn round unto their rear, and thou hast come to them over-against the mulberries,
texts.2sa.5.24: and it cometh to pass, in thy hearing the sound of a stepping in the tops of the mulberries, then thou dost move sharply, for then hath Jehovah gone out before thee to smite in the camp of the Philistines.'
texts.2sa.5.25: And David doth so, as Jehovah commanded him, and smiteth the Philistines from Geba unto thy coming to Gazer.
texts.2sa.6.1: And David gathered again every chosen one in Israel, thirty thousand,
texts.2sa.6.2: and David riseth and goeth, and all the people who [are] with him, from Baale-Judah, to bring up thence the ark of God, whose name hath been called -- the name of Jehovah of Hosts, inhabiting the cherubs -- upon it.
texts.2sa.6.3: And they cause the ark of God to ride on a new cart, and lift it up from the house of Abinadab, which [is] in the height, and Uzzah and Ahio sons of Abinadab are leading the new cart;
texts.2sa.6.4: and they lift it up from the house of Abinadab, which [is] in the height, with the ark of God, and Ahio is going before the ark,
texts.2sa.6.5: and David and all the house of Israel are playing before Jehovah, with all kinds of [instruments] of fir-wood, even with harps, and with psalteries, and with timbrels, and with cornets, and with cymbals.
texts.2sa.6.6: And they come unto the threshing-floor of Nachon, and Uzzah putteth forth [his hand] unto the ark of God, and layeth hold on it, for they released the oxen;
texts.2sa.6.7: and the anger of Jehovah burneth against Uzzah, and God smiteth him there for the error, and he dieth there by the ark of God.
texts.2sa.6.8: And it is displeasing to David, because that Jehovah hath broken forth a breach upon Uzzah, and [one] calleth that place Perez-Uzzah, unto this day;
texts.2sa.6.9: and David feareth Jehovah on that day, and saith, `How doth the ark of Jehovah come in unto me?'
texts.2sa.6.10: And David hath not been willing to turn aside unto himself the ark of Jehovah, to the city of David, and David turneth it aside to the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite,
texts.2sa.6.11: and the ark of Jehovah doth inhabit the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite three months, and Jehovah blesseth Obed-Edom and all his house.
texts.2sa.6.12: And it is declared to king David, saying, `Jehovah hath blessed the house of Obed-Edom, and all that he hath, because of the ark of God;' and David goeth and bringeth up the ark of God from the house of Obed-Edom to the city of David with joy.
texts.2sa.6.13: And it cometh to pass, when those bearing the ark of Jehovah have stepped six steps, that he sacrificeth an ox and a fatling.
texts.2sa.6.14: And David is dancing with all strength before Jehovah, and David is girded with a linen ephod,
texts.2sa.6.15: and David and all the house of Israel are bringing up the ark of Jehovah with shouting, and with the voice of a trumpet,
texts.2sa.6.16: and it hath come to pass, the ark of Jehovah hath come in to the city of David, and Michal daughter of Saul, hath looked through the window, and seeth king David moving and dancing before Jehovah, and despiseth him in her heart.
texts.2sa.6.17: And they bring in the ark of Jehovah, and set it up in its place, in the midst of the tent which David hath spread out for it, and David causeth to ascend burnt-offerings before Jehovah, and peace-offerings.
texts.2sa.6.18: And David finisheth from causing to ascend the burnt-offering, and the peace-offerings, and blesseth the people in the name of Jehovah of Hosts,
texts.2sa.6.19: and he apportioneth to all the people, to all the multitude of Israel, from man even unto woman, to each, one cake of bread, and one eshpar, and one ashisha, and all the people go, each to his house.
texts.2sa.6.20: And David turneth back to bless his house, and Michal daughter of Saul goeth out to meet David, and saith, `How honourable to-day was the king of Israel, who was uncovered to-day before the eyes of the handmaids of his servants, as one of the vain ones is openly uncovered!'
texts.2sa.6.21: And David saith unto Michal, `-- Before Jehovah, who fixed on me above thy father, and above all his house, to appoint me leader over the people of Jehovah, and over Israel, -- yea, I played before Jehovah;
texts.2sa.6.22: and I have been more vile than this, and have been low in mine eyes, and with the handmaids whom thou hast spoken of, with them I am honoured.'
texts.2sa.6.23: As to Michal daughter of Saul, she had no child till the day of her death.
texts.2sa.7.1: And it cometh to pass, when the king sat in his house, and Jehovah hath given rest to him round about, from all his enemies,
texts.2sa.7.2: that the king saith unto Nathan the prophet, `See, I pray thee, I am dwelling in a house of cedars, and the ark of God is dwelling in the midst of the curtain.'
texts.2sa.7.3: And Nathan saith unto the king, `All that [is] in thine heart -- go, do, for Jehovah [is] with thee.'
texts.2sa.7.4: And it cometh to pass in that night, that the word of Jehovah is unto Nathan, saying,
texts.2sa.7.5: `Go, and thou hast said unto My servant, unto David, Thus said Jehovah, Dost thou build for Me a house for My dwelling in?
texts.2sa.7.6: for I have not dwelt in a house even from the day of My bringing up the sons of Israel out of Egypt, even unto this day, and am walking up and down in a tent and in a tabernacle.
texts.2sa.7.7: During all [the time] that I have walked up and down among all the sons of Israel, a word have I spoken with one of the tribes of Israel which I commanded to feed my people Israel, saying, `Why have ye not built to Me a house of cedars?
texts.2sa.7.8: and now, thus dost thou say to My servant, to David: `Thus said Jehovah of Hosts, I have taken thee from the comely place, from after the flock, to be leader over My people, over Israel;
texts.2sa.7.9: and I am with thee whithersoever thou hast gone, and I cut off all thine enemies from thy presence, and have made for thee a great name, as the name of the great ones who [are] in the earth,
texts.2sa.7.10: and I have appointed a place for My people, for Israel, and have planted it, and it hath tabernacled in its place, and it is not troubled any more, and the sons of perverseness do not add to afflict it any more, as in the beginning,
texts.2sa.7.11: even from the day that I appointed judges over My people Israel; and I have given rest to thee from all thine enemies, and Jehovah hath declared to thee that Jehovah doth make for thee a house.
texts.2sa.7.12: `When thy days are full, and thou hast lain with thy fathers, then I have raised up thy seed after thee which goeth out from thy bowels, and have established his kingdom;
texts.2sa.7.13: He doth build a house for My Name, and I have established the throne of his kingdom unto the age.
texts.2sa.7.14: I am to him for a father, and he is to Me for a son; whom in his dealings perversely I have even reproved with a rod of men, and with strokes of the sons of Adam,
texts.2sa.7.15: and My kindness doth not turn aside from him, as I turned it aside from Saul, whom I turned aside from before thee,
texts.2sa.7.16: and stedfast [is] thy house and thy kingdom unto the age before thee, thy throne is established unto the age.'
texts.2sa.7.17: According to all these words, and according to all this vision, so spake Nathan unto David.
texts.2sa.7.18: And king David cometh in and sitteth before Jehovah, and saith, `Who [am] I, Lord Jehovah? and what my house, that Thou hast brought me hitherto?
texts.2sa.7.19: And yet this [is] little in Thine eyes, Lord Jehovah, and Thou dost speak also concerning the house of Thy servant afar off; and this [is] the law of the Man, Lord Jehovah.
texts.2sa.7.20: And what doth David add more to speak unto Thee? and Thou, Thou hast known Thy servant, Lord Jehovah.
texts.2sa.7.21: Because of Thy word, and according to Thy heart, Thou hast done all this greatness, to cause Thy servant to know [it].
texts.2sa.7.22: Therefore Thou hast been great, Jehovah God, for there is none like Thee, and there is no God save Thee, according to all that we have heard with our ears.
texts.2sa.7.23: `And who [is] as Thy people, as Israel -- one nation in the earth, whom God hath gone to redeem to Him for a people, and to make for Him a name -- and to do for you the greatness -- even fearful things for Thy land, at the presence of Thy people, whom Thou hast redeemed to Thee out of Egypt -- [among the] nations and their gods?
texts.2sa.7.24: Yea, Thou dost establish to Thee Thy people Israel, to Thee for a people unto the age, and Thou, Jehovah, hast been to them for God.
texts.2sa.7.25: `And now, Jehovah God, the word which Thou hast spoken concerning Thy servant, and concerning his house, establish unto the age, and do as Thou hast spoken;
texts.2sa.7.26: And Thy Name is great unto the age, saying, Jehovah of Hosts [is] God over Israel, and the house of Thy servant David is established before Thee,
texts.2sa.7.27: For Thou, Jehovah of Hosts, God of Israel, Thou hast uncovered the ear of Thy servant, saying, A house I build for thee, therefore hath Thy servant found his heart to pray unto Thee this prayer;
texts.2sa.7.28: And now, Lord Jehovah, Thou [art] God Himself, and Thy words are truth, and Thou speakest unto Thy servant this goodness,
texts.2sa.7.29: And now, begin and bless the house of Thy servant, to be unto the age before Thee, for Thou, Lord Jehovah, hast spoken, and by Thy blessing is the house of Thy servant blessed -- to the age.'
texts.2sa.8.1: And it cometh to pass afterwards that David smiteth the Philistines, and humbleth them, and David taketh the bridle of the metropolis out of the hand of the Philistines.
texts.2sa.8.2: And he smiteth Moab, and measureth them with a line, causing them to lie down on the earth, and he measureth two lines to put to death, and the fulness of the line to keep alive, and the Moabites are to David for servants, bearers of a present.
texts.2sa.8.3: And David smiteth Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah, in his going to bring back his power by the River [Euphrates;]
texts.2sa.8.4: and David captureth from him a thousand and seven hundred horsemen, and twenty thousand footmen, and David destroyeth utterly the whole of the charioteers, only he leaveth of them a hundred charioteers.
texts.2sa.8.5: And Aram of Damascus cometh to give help to Hadadezer king of Zobah, and David smiteth of Aram twenty and two thousand men;
texts.2sa.8.6: and David putteth garrisons in Aram of Damascus, and Aram is to David for a servant, bearing a present; and Jehovah saveth David whithersoever he hath gone;
texts.2sa.8.7: and David taketh the shields of gold which were on the servants of Hadadezer, and bringeth them to Jerusalem;
texts.2sa.8.8: and from Betah, and from Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, hath king David taken very much brass.
texts.2sa.8.9: And Toi king of Hamath heareth that David hath smitten all the force of Hadadezer,
texts.2sa.8.10: and Toi sendeth Joram his son unto king David to ask of him of welfare, and to bless him, (because that he hath fought against Hadadezer, and smiteth him, for a man of wars [with] Toi had Hadadezer been), and in his hand have been vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and vessels of brass,
texts.2sa.8.11: also them did king David sanctify to Jehovah, with the silver and the gold which he sanctified of all the nations which he subdued:
texts.2sa.8.12: of Aram, and of Moab, and of the Bene-Ammon, and of the Philistines, and of Amalek, and of the spoil of Hadadezer son of Rehob king of Zobah.
texts.2sa.8.13: And David maketh a name in his turning back from his smiting Aram in the valley of Salt -- eighteen thousand;
texts.2sa.8.14: and he putteth in Edom garrisons -- in all Edom he hath put garrisons, and all Edom are servants to David; and Jehovah saveth David whithersoever he hath gone.
texts.2sa.8.15: And David reigneth over all Israel, and David is doing judgment and righteousness to all his people,
texts.2sa.8.16: and Joab son of Zeruiah [is] over the host, and Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud [is] remembrancer,
texts.2sa.8.17: and Zadok son of Ahitub, and Ahimelech son of Abiathar, [are] priests, and Seraiah [is] scribe,
texts.2sa.8.18: and Benaiah son of Jehoiada [is over] both the Cherethite and the Pelethite, and the sons of David have been ministers.
texts.2sa.9.1: And David saith, `Is there yet any left to the house of Saul, and I do with him kindness because of Jonathan?'
texts.2sa.9.2: And the house of Saul hath a servant, and his name [is] Ziba, and they call for him unto David; and the king saith unto him, `Art thou Ziba?' and he saith, `Thy servant.'
texts.2sa.9.3: And the king saith, `Is there not yet a man to the house of Saul, and I do with him the kindness of God?' And Ziba saith unto the king, `Jonathan hath yet a son -- lame.'
texts.2sa.9.4: And the king saith to him, `Where [is] he?' and Ziba saith unto the king, `Lo, he [is] in the house of Machir, son of Ammiel, in Lo-Debar.'
texts.2sa.9.5: And king David sendeth, and taketh him out of the house of Machir son of Ammiel, of Lo-Debar,
texts.2sa.9.6: and Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, son of Saul, cometh unto David, and falleth on his face, and doth obeisance, and David saith, `Mephibosheth;' and he saith, `Lo, thy servant.'
texts.2sa.9.7: And David saith to him, `Be not afraid; for I certainly do with thee kindness because of Jonathan thy father, and have given back to thee all the field of Saul thy father, and thou dost eat bread at my table continually.'
texts.2sa.9.8: And he boweth himself, and saith, `What [is] thy servant, that thou hast turned unto the dead dog -- such as I?'
texts.2sa.9.9: And the king calleth unto Ziba servant of Saul, and saith unto him, `All that was to Saul and to all his house, I have given to the son of thy lord,
texts.2sa.9.10: and thou hast served for him the land, thou and thy sons, and thy servants, and hast brought in, and there hath been to the son of thy lord bread, and he hath eaten it; and Mephibosheth son of thy lord doth eat continually bread at my table;' and Ziba hath fifteen sons and twenty servants.
texts.2sa.9.11: And Ziba saith unto the king, `According to all that my lord the king commandeth his servant, so doth thy servant;' as to Mephibosheth, `he is eating at my table ([saith the king]) as one of the sons of the king.'
texts.2sa.9.12: And Mephibosheth hath a young son, and his name [is] Micha, and every one dwelling in the house of Ziba [are] servants to Mephibosheth.
texts.2sa.9.13: And Mephibosheth is dwelling in Jerusalem, for at the table of the king he is eating continually, and he [is] lame of his two feet.
texts.2sa.10.1: And it cometh to pass afterwards, that the king of the Bene-Ammon dieth, and Hanun his son reigneth in his stead,
texts.2sa.10.2: and David saith, `I do kindness with Hanun son of Nahash, as his father did with me kindness;' and David sendeth to comfort him by the hand of his servants concerning his father, and the servants of David come in to the land of the Bene-Ammon.
texts.2sa.10.3: And the heads of the Bene-Ammon say unto Hanun their lord, `Is David honouring thy father in thine eyes because he hath sent to thee comforters? for to search the city, and to spy it, and to overthrow it, hath not David sent his servants unto thee?'
texts.2sa.10.4: And Hanun taketh the servants of David, and shaveth off the half of their beard, and cutteth off their long robes in the midst -- unto their buttocks, and sendeth them away;
texts.2sa.10.5: and they declare [it] to David, and he sendeth to meet them, for the men have been greatly ashamed, and the king saith, `Abide in Jericho till your beard doth spring up -- then ye have returned.'
texts.2sa.10.6: And the Bene-Ammon see that they have been abhorred by David, and the Bene-Ammon send and hire Aram of Beth-Rehob, and Aram of Zoba, twenty thousand footmen, and the king of Maacah [with] a thousand men, and Ish-Tob [with] twelve thousand men;
texts.2sa.10.7: and David heareth, and sendeth Joab, and all the host -- the mighty men.
texts.2sa.10.8: And the Bene-Ammon come out, and set battle in array, at the opening of the gate, and Aram of Zoba, and Rehob, and Ish-Tob, and Maacah, [are] by themselves in the field;
texts.2sa.10.9: and Joab seeth that the front of the battle hath been unto him before and behind, and he chooseth of all the chosen in Israel, and setteth in array to meet Aram,
texts.2sa.10.10: and the rest of the people he hath given into the hand of Abishai his brother, and setteth in array to meet the Bene-Ammon.
texts.2sa.10.11: And he saith, `If Aram be stronger than I, then thou hast been to me for salvation, and if the Bene-Ammon be stronger than thou, then I have come to give salvation to thee;
texts.2sa.10.12: be strong and strengthen thyself for our people, and for the cities of our God, and Jehovah doth that which is good in His eyes.'
texts.2sa.10.13: And Joab draweth nigh, and the people who [are] with him, to battle against Aram, and they flee from his presence;
texts.2sa.10.14: and the Bene-Ammon have seen that Aram hath fled, and they flee from the presence of Abishai, and go in to the city; and Joab turneth back from the Bene-Ammon, and cometh in to Jerusalem.
texts.2sa.10.15: And Aram seeth that it is smitten before Israel, and they are gathered together;
texts.2sa.10.16: and Hadadezer sendeth, and bringeth out Aram which [is] beyond the River, and they come in to Helam, and Shobach head of the host of Hadadezer [is] before them.
texts.2sa.10.17: And it is declared to David, and he gathereth all Israel, and passeth over the Jordan, and cometh in to Helam, and Aram setteth itself in array to meet David, and they fight with him;
texts.2sa.10.18: and Aram fleeth from the presence of Israel, and David slayeth of Aram seven hundred charioteers, and forty thousand horsemen, and Shobach head of its host he hath smitten, and he dieth there.
texts.2sa.10.19: And all the kings -- servants of Hadadezer -- see that they have been smitten before Israel, and make peace with Israel, and serve them; and Aram is afraid to help any more the Bene-Ammon.
texts.2sa.11.1: And it cometh to pass, at the revolution of the year -- at the time of the going out of the messengers -- that David sendeth Joab, and his servants with him, and all Israel, and they destroy the Bene-Ammon, and lay siege against Rabbah. And David is dwelling in Jerusalem,
texts.2sa.11.2: and it cometh to pass, at evening-time, that David riseth from off his couch, and walketh up and down on the roof of the king's house, and seeth from the roof a woman bathing, and the woman [is] of very good appearance,
texts.2sa.11.3: and David sendeth and inquireth about the woman, and saith, `Is not this Bath-Sheba, daughter of Eliam, wife of Uriah the Hittite?'
texts.2sa.11.4: And David sendeth messengers, and taketh her, and she cometh unto him, and he lieth with her -- and she is purifying herself from her uncleanness -- and she turneth back unto her house;
texts.2sa.11.5: and the woman conceiveth, and sendeth, and declareth to David, and saith, `I [am] conceiving.'
texts.2sa.11.6: And David sendeth unto Joab, `Send unto me Uriah the Hittite,' and Joab sendeth Uriah unto David;
texts.2sa.11.7: and Uriah cometh unto him, and David asketh of the prosperity of Joab, and of the prosperity of the people, and of the prosperity of the war.
texts.2sa.11.8: And David saith to Uriah, `Go down to thy house, and wash thy feet;' and Uriah goeth out of the king's house, and there goeth out after him a gift from the king,
texts.2sa.11.9: and Uriah lieth down at the opening of the king's house, with all the servants of his lord, and hath not gone down unto his house.
texts.2sa.11.10: And they declare to David, saying, `Uriah hath not gone down unto his house;' and David saith unto Uriah, `Hast thou not come from a journey? wherefore hast thou not gone down unto thy house?'
texts.2sa.11.11: And Uriah saith unto David, `The ark, and Israel, and Judah, are abiding in booths, and my lord Joab, and the servants of my lord, on the face of the field are encamping; and I -- I go in unto my house to eat and to drink, and to lie with my wife! -- thy life, and the life of thy soul -- if I do this thing.'
texts.2sa.11.12: And David saith unto Uriah, `Abide in this [place] also to-day, and to-morrow I send thee away;' and Uriah abideth in Jerusalem, on that day, and on the morrow,
texts.2sa.11.13: and David calleth for him, and he eateth before him, and drinketh, and he causeth him to drink, and he goeth out in the evening to lie on his couch with the servants of his lord, and unto his house he hath not gone down.
texts.2sa.11.14: And it cometh to pass in the morning, that David writeth a letter unto Joab, and sendeth by the hand of Uriah;
texts.2sa.11.15: and he writeth in the letter, saying, `Place ye Uriah over-against the front of the severest battle, and ye have turned back from after him, and he hath been smitten, and hath died.'
texts.2sa.11.16: And it cometh to pass in Joab's watching of the city, that he appointeth Uriah unto the place where he knew that valiant men [are];
texts.2sa.11.17: and the men of the city go out and fight with Joab, and there fall [some] of the people, of the servants of David; and there dieth also Uriah the Hittite.
texts.2sa.11.18: And Joab sendeth and declareth to David all the matters of the war,
texts.2sa.11.19: and commandeth the messenger, saying, `At thy finishing all the matters of the war to speak unto the king,
texts.2sa.11.20: then, it hath been, if the king's fury ascend, and he hath said to thee, Wherefore did ye draw nigh unto the city to fight? did ye not know that they shoot from off the wall?
texts.2sa.11.21: Who smote Abimelech son of Jerubbesheth? did not a woman cast on him a piece of a rider from the wall, and he dieth in Thebez? why drew ye nigh unto the wall? that thou hast said, Also thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead.'
texts.2sa.11.22: And the messenger goeth, and cometh in, and declareth to David all that with which Joab sent him,
texts.2sa.11.23: and the messenger saith unto David, `Surely the men have been mighty against us, and come out unto us into the field, and we are upon them unto the opening of the gate,
texts.2sa.11.24: and those shooting shoot at thy servants from off the wall, and [some] of the servants of the king are dead, and also, thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead.
texts.2sa.11.25: And David saith unto the messenger, `Thus dost thou say unto Joab, Let not this thing be evil in thine eyes; for thus and thus doth the sword devour; strengthen thy warfare against the city, and throw it down -- and strengthen thou him.'
texts.2sa.11.26: And the wife of Uriah heareth that Uriah her husband [is] dead, and lamenteth for her lord;
texts.2sa.11.27: and the mourning passeth by, and David sendeth and gathereth her unto his house, and she is to him for a wife, and beareth to him a son; and the thing which David hath done is evil in the eyes of Jehovah.
texts.2sa.12.1: And Jehovah sendeth Nathan unto David, and he cometh unto him, and saith to him: `Two men have been in one city; One rich and one poor;
texts.2sa.12.2: The rich hath flocks and herds very many;
texts.2sa.12.3: And the poor one hath nothing, Except one little ewe-lamb, Which he hath bought, and keepeth alive, And it groweth up with him, And with his sons together; Of his morsel it eateth, And from his cup it drinketh, And in his bosom it lieth, And it is to him as a daughter;
texts.2sa.12.4: And there cometh a traveller to the rich man, And he spareth to take Of his own flock, and of his own herd, To prepare for the traveller Who hath come to him, And he taketh the ewe-lamb of the poor man, And prepareth it for the man Who hath come unto him.'
texts.2sa.12.5: And the anger of David burneth against the man exceedingly, and he saith unto Nathan, `Jehovah liveth, surely a son of death [is] the man who is doing this,
texts.2sa.12.6: and the ewe-lamb he doth repay fourfold, because that he hath done this thing, and because that he had no pity.'
texts.2sa.12.7: And Nathan saith unto David, `Thou [art] the man! Thus said Jehovah, God of Israel, I anointed thee for king over Israel, and I delivered thee out of the hand of Saul;
texts.2sa.12.8: and I give to thee the house of thy lord, and the wives of thy lord, into thy bosom, and I give to thee the house of Israel and of Judah; and if little, then I add to thee such and such [things].
texts.2sa.12.9: `Wherefore hast thou despised the word of Jehovah, to do the evil thing in His eyes? Uriah the Hittite thou hast smitten by the sword, and his wife thou hast taken to thee for a wife, and him thou hast slain by the sword of the Bene-Ammon.
texts.2sa.12.10: `And now, the sword doth not turn aside from thy house unto the age, because thou hast despised Me, and dost take the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be to thee for a wife;
texts.2sa.12.11: thus said Jehovah, Lo, I am raising up against thee evil, out of thy house, and have taken thy wives before thine eyes, and given to thy neighbour, and he hath lain with thy wives before the eyes of this sun;
texts.2sa.12.12: for thou hast done [it] in secret, and I do this thing before all Israel, and before the sun.'
texts.2sa.12.13: And David saith unto Nathan, `I have sinned against Jehovah.' And Nathan saith unto David, `Also -- Jehovah hath caused thy sin to pass away; thou dost not die;
texts.2sa.12.14: only, because thou hast caused the enemies of Jehovah greatly to despise by this thing, also the son who is born to thee doth surely die.'
texts.2sa.12.15: And Nathan goeth unto his house, and Jehovah smiteth the lad, whom the wife of Uriah hath born to David, and it is incurable;
texts.2sa.12.16: and David seeketh God for the youth, and David keepeth a fast, and hath gone in and lodged, and lain on the earth.
texts.2sa.12.17: And the elders of his house rise against him, to raise him up from the earth, and he hath not been willing, nor hath he eaten with them bread;
texts.2sa.12.18: and it cometh to pass on the seventh day, that the lad dieth, and the servants of David fear to declare to him that the lad is dead, for they said, `Lo, in the lad being alive we spake unto him, and he did not hearken to our voice; and how do we say unto him, The lad is dead? -- then he hath done evil.'
texts.2sa.12.19: And David seeth that his servants are whispering, and David understandeth that the lad is dead, and David saith unto his servants, `Is the lad dead?' and they say, `Dead.'
texts.2sa.12.20: And David riseth from the earth, and doth bathe and anoint [himself], and changeth his raiment, and cometh in to the house of Jehovah, and boweth himself, and cometh unto his house, and asketh and they place for him bread, and he eateth.
texts.2sa.12.21: And his servants say unto him, `What [is] this thing thou hast done? because of the living lad thou hast fasted and dost weep, and when the lad is dead thou hast risen and dost eat bread.'
texts.2sa.12.22: And he saith, `While the lad is alive I have fasted, and weep, for I said, Who knoweth? -- Jehovah doth pity me, and the lad hath lived;
texts.2sa.12.23: and now, he hath died, why [is] this -- I fast? am I able to bring him back again? I am going unto him, and he doth not turn back unto me.'
texts.2sa.12.24: And David comforteth Bath-Sheba his wife, and goeth in unto her, and lieth with her, and she beareth a son, and he calleth his name Solomon; and Jehovah hath loved him,
texts.2sa.12.25: and sendeth by the hand of Nathan the prophet, and calleth his name Jedidiah, because of Jehovah.
texts.2sa.12.26: And Joab fighteth against Rabbah of the Bene-Ammon, and captureth the royal city,
texts.2sa.12.27: and Joab sendeth messengers unto David, and saith, `I have fought against Rabbah -- also I have captured the city of waters;
texts.2sa.12.28: and now, gather the rest of the people, and encamp against the city, and capture it, lest I capture the city, and my name hath been called upon it.'
texts.2sa.12.29: And David gathereth all the people, and goeth to Rabbah, and fighteth against it, and captureth it;
texts.2sa.12.30: and he taketh the crown of their king from off his head, and its weight [is] a talent of gold, and precious stones, and it is on the head of David; and the spoil of the city he hath brought out, very much;
texts.2sa.12.31: and the people who [are] in it he hath brought out, and setteth to the saw, and to cutting instruments of iron, and to axes of iron, and hath caused them to pass over into the brick-kiln; and so he doth to all the cities of the Bene-Ammon; and David turneth back, and all the people, to Jerusalem.
texts.2sa.13.1: And it cometh to pass afterwards that Absalom son of David hath a fair sister, and her name [is] Tamar, and Amnon son of David loveth her.
texts.2sa.13.2: And Amnon hath distress -- even to become sick, because of Tamar his sister, for she [is] a virgin, and it is hard in the eyes of Amnon to do anything to her.
texts.2sa.13.3: And Amnon hath a friend, and his name [is] Jonadab, son of Shimeah, David's brother, and Jonadab [is] a very wise man,
texts.2sa.13.4: and saith to him, `Wherefore [art] thou thus lean, O king's son, morning by morning? dost thou not declare to me?' And Amnon saith to him, `Tamar -- sister of Absalom my brother -- I am loving.'
texts.2sa.13.5: And Jonadab saith to him, `Lie down on thy couch, and feign thyself sick, and thy father hath come in to see thee, and thou hast said unto him, `Let, I pray thee, Tamar my sister come in and give me bread to eat; and she hath made the food before mine eyes so that I see [it], and have eaten from her hand.'
texts.2sa.13.6: And Amnon lieth down, and feigneth himself sick, and the king cometh in to see him, and Amnon saith unto the king, `Let, I pray thee, Tamar my sister come, and she maketh before mine eyes two cakes, and I eat from her hand.'
texts.2sa.13.7: And David sendeth unto Tamar, to the house, saying, `Go, I pray thee, to the house of Amnon thy brother, and make for him food.'
texts.2sa.13.8: And Tamar goeth to the house of Amnon her brother, and he is lying down, and she taketh the dough, and kneadeth, and maketh cakes before his eyes, and cooketh the cakes,
texts.2sa.13.9: and taketh the frying-pan, and poureth out before him, and he refuseth to eat, and Amnon saith, `Take ye out every one from me;' and they go out every one from him.
texts.2sa.13.10: And Amnon saith unto Tamar, `Bring the food into the inner chamber, and I eat from thy hand;' and Tamar taketh the cakes that she hath made, and bringeth in to Amnon her brother, into the inner chamber,
texts.2sa.13.11: and she bringeth nigh unto him to eat, and he layeth hold on her, and saith to her, `Come, lie with me, my sister.'
texts.2sa.13.12: And she saith to him, `Nay, my brother, do not humble me, for it is not done so in Israel; do not this folly.
texts.2sa.13.13: And I -- whither do I cause my reproach to go? and thou -- thou art as one of the fools in Israel; and now, speak, I pray thee, unto the king; for he doth not withhold me from thee.'
texts.2sa.13.14: And he hath not been willing to hearken to her voice, and is stronger than she, and humbleth her, and lieth with her.
texts.2sa.13.15: And Amnon hateth her -- a very great hatred -- that greater [is] the hatred with which he hath hated her than the love with which he loved her, and Amnon saith to her, `Rise, go.'
texts.2sa.13.16: And she saith to him, `Because of the circumstances this evil is greater than the other that thou hast done with me -- to send me away;' and he hath not been willing to hearken to her,
texts.2sa.13.17: and calleth his young man, his servant, and saith, `Send away, I pray thee, this one from me without, and bolt the door after her;'
texts.2sa.13.18: -- and upon her [is] a long coat, for such upper robes do daughters of the king who [are] virgins put on, -- and his servant taketh her out without, and hath bolted the door after her.
texts.2sa.13.19: And Tamar taketh ashes for her head, and the long coat that [is] on her she hath rent, and putteth her hand on her head, and goeth, going on and crying;
texts.2sa.13.20: and Absalom her brother saith unto her, `Hath Amnon thy brother been with thee? and now, my sister, keep silent, he [is] thy brother; set not thy heart to this thing;' and Tamar dwelleth -- but desolate -- in the house of Absalom her brother.
texts.2sa.13.21: And king David hath heard all these things, and it is very displeasing to him;
texts.2sa.13.22: and Absalom hath not spoken with Amnon either evil or good, for Absalom is hating Amnon, because that he humbled Tamar his sister.
texts.2sa.13.23: And it cometh to pass, after two years of days, that Absalom hath shearers in Baal-Hazor, which [is] with Ephraim, and Absalom calleth for all the sons of the king.
texts.2sa.13.24: And Absalom cometh unto the king, and saith, `Lo, I pray thee, thy servant hath shearers, let the king go, I pray thee, and his servants, with thy servant.'
texts.2sa.13.25: And the king saith unto Absalom, `Nay, my son, let us not all go, I pray thee, and we are not too heavy on thee;' and he presseth on him, and he hath not been willing to go, and he blesseth him.
texts.2sa.13.26: And Absalom saith, `If not -- let, I pray thee, Amnon my brother go with us;' and the king saith to him, `Why doth he go with thee?'
texts.2sa.13.27: and Absalom urgeth on him, and he sendeth with him Amnon, and all the sons of the king.
texts.2sa.13.28: And Absalom commandeth his young men, saying, `See, I pray thee, when the heart of Amnon [is] glad with wine, and I have said unto you, Smite Amnon, that ye have put him to death; fear not; is it not because I have commanded you? be strong, yea, become sons of valour.'
texts.2sa.13.29: And the young men of Absalom do to Amnon as Absalom commanded, and rise do all the sons of the king, and they ride, each on his mule, and flee.
texts.2sa.13.30: And it cometh to pass -- they [are] in the way -- and the report hath come unto David, saying, `Absalom hath smitten all the sons of the king, and there is not left of them one;'
texts.2sa.13.31: and the king riseth, and rendeth his garments, and lieth on the earth, and all his servants are standing by [with] rent garments.
texts.2sa.13.32: And Jonadab son of Shimeah, David's brother, answereth and saith, `Let not my lord say, The whole of the young men, the sons of the king, they have put to death; for Amnon alone [is] dead, for by the command of Absalom it hath been appointed from the day of his humbling Tamar his sister;
texts.2sa.13.33: and now, let not my lord the king lay unto his heart the word, saying, All the sons of the king have died, for Amnon alone [is] dead.'
texts.2sa.13.34: And Absalom fleeth, and the young man who is watching lifteth up his eyes and looketh, and lo, much people are coming by the way behind him, on the side of the hill.
texts.2sa.13.35: And Jonadab saith unto the king, `Lo, the sons of the king have come; as the word of thy servant, so it hath been.'
texts.2sa.13.36: And it cometh to pass at his finishing to speak, that lo, the sons of the king have come, and they lift up their voice, and weep, and also the king and all his servants have wept -- a very great weeping.
texts.2sa.13.37: And Absalom hath fled, and goeth unto Talmai, son of Ammihud, king of Geshur, and [David] mourneth for his son all the days.
texts.2sa.13.38: And Absalom hath fled, and goeth to Geshur, and is there three years;
texts.2sa.13.39: and [the soul of] king David determineth to go out unto Absalom, for he hath been comforted for Amnon, for [he is] dead.
