texts.2sa.14.1: And Joab son of Zeruial knoweth that the heart of the king [is] on Absalom,
texts.2sa.14.2: and Joab sendeth to Tekoah, and taketh thence a wise woman, and saith unto her, `Feign thyself a mourner, I pray thee, and put on, I pray thee, garments of mourning, and anoint not thyself with oil, and thou hast been as a woman these many days mourning for the dead,
texts.2sa.14.3: and thou hast gone unto the king, and spoken unto him, according to this word;' and Joab putteth the words into her mouth.
texts.2sa.14.4: And the woman of Tekoah speaketh unto the king, and falleth on her face to the earth, and doth obeisance, and saith, `Save, O king.'
texts.2sa.14.5: And the king saith to her, `What -- to thee?' and she saith, `Truly a widow woman [am] I, and my husband dieth,
texts.2sa.14.6: and thy maid-servant hath two sons; and they strive both of them in a field, and there is no deliverer between them, and the one smiteth the other, and putteth him to death;
texts.2sa.14.7: and lo, the whole family hath risen against thy maid-servant, and say, Give up him who smiteth his brother, and we put him to death for the life of his brother whom he hath slain, and we destroy also the heir; and they have quenched my coal which is left -- so as not to set to my husband a name and remnant on the face of the ground.'
texts.2sa.14.8: And the king saith unto the woman, `Go to thine house, and I give charge concerning thee.'
texts.2sa.14.9: And the woman of Tekoah saith unto the king, `On me, my lord, O king, [is] the iniquity, and on the house of my father; and the king and his throne [are] innocent.'
texts.2sa.14.10: And the king saith, `He who speaketh [aught] unto thee, and thou hast brought him unto me, then he doth not add any more to come against thee.'
texts.2sa.14.11: And she saith, `Let, I pray thee, the king remember by Jehovah thy God, that the redeemer of blood add not to destroy, and they destroy not my son;' and he saith, `Jehovah liveth; if there doth fall of the hair of thy son to the earth.'
texts.2sa.14.12: And the woman saith, `Let, I pray thee, thy maid-servant speak unto my lord the king a word;' and he saith, `Speak.'
texts.2sa.14.13: And the woman saith, `And why hast thou thought thus concerning the people of God? yea, the king is speaking this thing as a guilty one, in that the king hath not brought back his outcast;
texts.2sa.14.14: for we do surely die, and [are] as water which is running down to the earth, which is not gathered, and God doth not accept a person, and hath devised devices in that the outcast is not outcast by Him.
texts.2sa.14.15: `And now that I have come to speak unto the king my lord this word, [it is] because the people made me afraid, and thy maid-servant saith, Let me speak, I pray thee, unto the king; it may be the king doth do the word of his handmaid,
texts.2sa.14.16: for the king doth hearken to deliver his handmaid out of the paw of the man [seeking] to destroy me and my son together out of the inheritance of God,
texts.2sa.14.17: and thy maid-servant saith, Let, I pray thee, the word of my lord the king be for ease; for as a messenger of God so [is] my lord the king, to understand the good and the evil; and Jehovah thy God is with thee.'
texts.2sa.14.18: And the king answereth and saith unto the woman, `Do not, I pray thee, hide from me the thing that I am asking thee;' and the woman saith, `Let, I pray thee, my lord the king speak.'
texts.2sa.14.19: And the king saith, `Is the hand of Joab with thee in all this?' And the woman answereth and saith, `Thy soul liveth, my lord, O king, none [doth turn] to the right or to the left from all that my lord the king hath spoken; for thy servant Joab he commanded me, and he put in the mouth of thy maid-servant all these words;
texts.2sa.14.20: in order to bring round the appearance of the thing hath thy servant Joab done this thing, and my lord [is] wise, according to the wisdom of a messenger of God, to know all that [is] in the land.'
texts.2sa.14.21: And the king saith unto Joab, `Lo, I pray thee, thou hast done this thing; and go, bring back the young man Absalom.'
texts.2sa.14.22: And Joab falleth on his face to the earth, and doth obeisance, and blesseth the king, and Joab saith, `To-day hath thy servant known that I have found grace in thine eyes, my lord, O king, in that the king hath done the word of his servant.'
texts.2sa.14.23: And Joab riseth and goeth to Geshur, and bringeth in Absalom to Jerusalem,
texts.2sa.14.24: and the king saith, `Let him turn round unto his house, and my face he doth not see.' And Absalom turneth round unto his house, and the face of the king he hath not seen.
texts.2sa.14.25: And like Absalom there was no man [so] fair in all Israel, to praise greatly; from the sole of his foot even unto his crown there was no blemish in him;
texts.2sa.14.26: and in his polling his head -- and it hath been at the end of year by year that he polleth [it], for it [is] heavy on him, and he hath polled it -- he hath even weighed out the hair of his head -- two hundred shekels by the king's weight.
texts.2sa.14.27: And there are born to Absalom three sons, and one daughter, and her name [is] Tamar; she was a woman of a fair appearance.
texts.2sa.14.28: And Absalom dwelleth in Jerusalem two years of days, and the face of the king he hath not seen;
texts.2sa.14.29: and Absalom sendeth unto Joab, to send him unto the king, and he hath not been willing to come unto him; and he sendeth again a second time, and he hath not been willing to come.
texts.2sa.14.30: And he saith unto his servants, `See, the portion of Joab [is] by the side of mine, and he hath barley there; go, and burn it with fire;' and the servants of Absalom burn the portion with fire.
texts.2sa.14.31: And Joab riseth and cometh unto Absalom in the house, and saith unto him, `Why have thy servants burned the portion that I have with fire?'
texts.2sa.14.32: And Absalom saith unto Joab, `Lo, I sent unto thee, saying, Come hither, and I send thee unto the king to say, Why have I come in from Geshur? -- good for me while I [am] there -- and now, let me see the king's face, and if there is in me iniquity then thou hast put me to death.'
texts.2sa.14.33: And Joab cometh unto the king, and declareth [it] to him, and he calleth unto Absalom, and he cometh unto the king, and boweth himself to him, on his face, to the earth, before the king, and the king giveth a kiss to Absalom.
texts.2sa.15.1: And it cometh to pass afterwards, that Absalom prepareth for himself a chariot, and horses, and fifty men are running before him;
texts.2sa.15.2: and Absalom hath risen early, and stood by the side of the way of the gate, and it cometh to pass, every man who hath a pleading to come unto the king for judgment, that Absalom calleth unto him, and saith, `Of what city [art] thou?' and he saith, `Of one of the tribes of Israel [is] thy servant.'
texts.2sa.15.3: And Absalom saith unto him, `See, thy matters [are] good and straightforward -- and there is none hearkening to thee from the king.'
texts.2sa.15.4: And Absalom saith, `Who doth make me a judge in the land, that unto me doth come every man who hath a plea and judgment? -- then I have declared him righteous.'
texts.2sa.15.5: And it hath come to pass, in the drawing nearing of any one to bow himself to him, that he hath put forth his hand, and laid hold on him, and given a kiss to him;
texts.2sa.15.6: and Absalom doth according to this thing to all Israel who come in for judgment unto the king, and Absalom stealeth the heart of the men of Israel.
texts.2sa.15.7: And it cometh to pass, at the end of forty years, that Absalom saith unto the king, `Let me go, I pray thee, and I complete my vow, that I vowed to Jehovah in Hebron,
texts.2sa.15.8: for a vow hath thy servant vowed in my dwelling in Geshur, in Aram, saying, If Jehovah doth certainly bring me back to Jerusalem, then I have served Jehovah.'
texts.2sa.15.9: And the king saith to him, `Go in peace;' and he riseth and goeth to Hebron,
texts.2sa.15.10: and Absalom sendeth spies through all the tribes of Israel, saying, `At your hearing the voice of the trumpet, then ye have said, Absalom hath reigned in Hebron.'
texts.2sa.15.11: And with Absalom have gone two hundred men, out of Jerusalem, invited ones, and they are going in their simplicity, and have not known anything;
texts.2sa.15.12: and Absalom sendeth Ahithophel the Gilonite, a counsellor of David, out of his city, out of Gilo, in his sacrificing sacrifices; and the conspiracy is strong, and the people are going and increasing with Absalom.
texts.2sa.15.13: And he who is declaring tidings cometh in unto David, saying, `The heart of the men of Israel hath been after Absalom.'
texts.2sa.15.14: And David saith to all his servants who [are] with him in Jerusalem, `Rise, and we flee, for we have no escape from the face of Absalom; haste to go, lest he hasten, and have overtaken us, and forced on us evil, and smitten the city by the mouth of the sword.'
texts.2sa.15.15: And the servants of the king say unto the king, `According to all that my lord the king chooseth -- lo, thy servants [do].'
texts.2sa.15.16: And the king goeth out, and all his household at his feet, and the king leaveth ten women -- concubines -- to keep the house.
texts.2sa.15.17: And the king goeth out, and all the people at his feet, and they stand still at the farthest off house.
texts.2sa.15.18: And all his servants are passing on at his side, and all the Cherethite, and all the Pelethite, and all the Gittites, six hundred men who came at his feet from Gath, are passing on at the front of the king.
texts.2sa.15.19: And the king saith unto Ittai the Gittite, `Why dost thou go -- thou also -- with us? turn back -- and abide with the king, for thou [art] a stranger, and also an exile thou -- to thy place.
texts.2sa.15.20: Yesterday [is] thy coming in, and to-day I move thee to go with us, and I am going on that which I am going! -- turn back, and take back thy brethren with thee, -- kindness and truth.'
texts.2sa.15.21: And Ittai answereth the king and saith, `Jehovah liveth, and my lord the king liveth, surely in the place where my lord the king is -- if for death, if for life, surely there is thy servant.'
texts.2sa.15.22: And David saith unto Ittai, `Go and pass over;' and Ittai the Gittite passeth over, and all his men, and all the infants who [are] with him.
texts.2sa.15.23: And all the land are weeping -- a great voice, and all the people are passing over; and the king is passing over through the brook Kidron, and all the people are passing over on the front of the way of the wilderness;
texts.2sa.15.24: and lo, also Zadok, and all the Levites with him, bearing the ark of the covenant of God, and they make the ark of God firm, and Abiathar goeth up, till the completion of all the people to pass over out of the city.
texts.2sa.15.25: And the king saith to Zadok, `Take back the ark of God to the city; if I find grace in the eyes of Jehovah, then He hath brought me back, and shewn me it and His habitation;
texts.2sa.15.26: and if thus He say, I have not delighted in thee; here [am] I, He doth to me as [is] good in His eyes.'
texts.2sa.15.27: And the king saith unto Zadok the priest, `Art thou a seer? turn back to the city in peace, and Ahimaaz thy son, and Jonathan son of Abiathar, your two sons with you;
texts.2sa.15.28: see ye, I am tarrying in the plains of the wilderness till the coming in of a word from you to declare to me.'
texts.2sa.15.29: And Zadok taketh back -- and Abiathar -- the ark of God to Jerusalem, and they abide there.
texts.2sa.15.30: And David is going up in the ascent of the olives, going up and weeping, and he hath the head covered, and he is going barefooted, and all the people who [are] with him have covered each his head, and have gone up, going up and weeping;
texts.2sa.15.31: and David declared, saying, `Ahithophel [is] among the conspirators with Absalom;' and David saith, `Make foolish, I pray Thee, the counsel of Ahithophel, O Jehovah.'
texts.2sa.15.32: And it cometh to pass, David hath come unto the top, where he boweth himself to God, and lo, to meet him [is] Hushai the Archite, his coat rent, and earth on his head;
texts.2sa.15.33: and David saith to him, `If thou hast passed on with me then thou hast been on me for a burden,
texts.2sa.15.34: and if to the city thou dost turn back, and hast said to Absalom, Thy servant I am, O king; servant of thy father I [am] also hitherto, and now, I [am] also thy servant; then thou hast made void for me the counsel of Ahithophel;
texts.2sa.15.35: and are there not with thee there Zadok and Abiathar the priests? and it hath been, the whole of the matter that thou hearest from the house of the king thou dost declare to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests.
texts.2sa.15.36: Lo, there with them [are] their two sons, Ahimaaz to Zadok, and Jonathan to Abiathar, and ye have sent by their hand unto me anything that ye hear.'
texts.2sa.15.37: And Hushai, David's friend, cometh in to the city, and Absalom cometh in to Jerusalem.
texts.2sa.16.1: And David hath passed on a little from the top, and lo, Ziba, servant of Mephibosheth -- to meet him, and a couple of asses saddled, and upon them two hundred loaves, and a hundred bunches of raisins, and a hundred [of] summer-fruit, and a bottle of wine.
texts.2sa.16.2: And the king saith unto Ziba, `What -- these to thee?' and Ziba saith, `The asses for the household of the king to ride on, and the bread and the summer-fruit for the young men to eat, and the wine for the wearied to drink in the wilderness.'
texts.2sa.16.3: And the king saith, `And where [is] the son of thy lord?' and Ziba saith unto the king, `Lo, he is abiding in Jerusalem, for he said, To-day do the house of Israel give back to me the kingdom of my father.'
texts.2sa.16.4: And the king saith to Ziba, `Lo, thine [are] all that Mephibosheth hath;' and Ziba saith, `I have bowed myself -- I find grace in thine eyes, my lord, O king.'
texts.2sa.16.5: And king David hath come in unto Bahurim, and lo, thence a man is coming out, of the family of the house of Saul, and his name [is] Shimei, son of Gera, he cometh out, coming out and reviling;
texts.2sa.16.6: and he stoneth David with stones, and all the servants of king David, and all the people, and all the mighty men on his right and on his left.
texts.2sa.16.7: And thus said Shimei in his reviling, `Go out, go out, O man of blood, and man of worthlessness!
texts.2sa.16.8: Jehovah hath turned back on thee all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose stead thou hast reigned, and Jehovah doth give the kingdom in to the hand of Absalom thy son; and lo, thou [art] in thine evil, for a man of blood thou [art].'
texts.2sa.16.9: And Abishai son of Zeruiah saith unto the king, `Why doth this dead dog revile my lord the king? let me pass over, I pray thee, and I turn aside his head.'
texts.2sa.16.10: And the king saith, `What -- to me and to you, O sons of Zeruiah? for -- let him revile; even because Jehovah hath said to him, Revile David; and who saith, Wherefore hast Thou done so?'
texts.2sa.16.11: And David saith unto Abishai, and unto all his servants, `Lo, my son who came out of my bowels is seeking my life, and also surely now the Benjamite; leave him alone, and let him revile, for Jehovah hath said [so] to him;
texts.2sa.16.12: it may be Jehovah doth look on mine affliction, and Jehovah hath turned back to me good for his reviling this day.'
texts.2sa.16.13: And David goeth with his men in the way, and Shimei is going at the side of the hill over-against him, going on, and he revileth, and stoneth with stones over-against him, and hath dusted with dust.
texts.2sa.16.14: And the king cometh in, and all the people who [are] with him, wearied, and they are refreshed there.
texts.2sa.16.15: And Absalom and all the people, the men of Israel, have come in to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him,
texts.2sa.16.16: and it cometh to pass, when Hushai the Archite, David's friend, hath come unto Absalom, that Hushai saith unto Absalom, `Let the king live! let the king live!'
texts.2sa.16.17: And Absalom saith unto Hushai, `This thy kindness with thy friend! why hast thou not gone with thy friend?'
texts.2sa.16.18: And Hushai saith unto Absalom, `Nay, for he whom Jehovah hath chosen, and this people, even all the men of Israel, his I am, and with him I abide;
texts.2sa.16.19: and secondly, for whom do I labour? is it not before his son? as I served before thy father so am I before thee.'
texts.2sa.16.20: And Absalom saith unto Ahithophel, `Give for you counsel what we do.'
texts.2sa.16.21: And Ahithophel saith unto Absalom, `Go in unto the concubines of thy father, whom he left to keep the house, and all Israel hath heard that thou hast been abhorred by thy father, and the hands of all who [are] with thee have been strong.'
texts.2sa.16.22: And they spread out for Absalom the tent on the roof, and Absalom goeth in unto the concubines of his father before the eyes of all Israel.
texts.2sa.16.23: And the counsel of Ahithophel which he counselled in those days [is] as [when] one inquireth at the word of God; so [is] all the counsel of Ahithophel both to David and to Absalom.
texts.2sa.17.1: And Ahithophel said unto Absalom, `Let me choose, I pray thee, twelve thousand men, and I arise and pursue after David to-night,
texts.2sa.17.2: and come upon him, and he weary and feeble-handed, and I have caused him to tremble, and all the people have fled who [are] with him, and I have smitten the king by himself,
texts.2sa.17.3: and I bring back all the people unto thee -- as the turning back of the whole [is] the man whom thou art seeking -- all the people are peace.
texts.2sa.17.4: And the thing is right in the eyes of Absalom, and in the eyes of all the elders of Israel.
texts.2sa.17.5: And Absalom saith, `Call, I pray thee, also for Hushai the Archite, and we hear what [is] in his mouth -- even he.'
texts.2sa.17.6: And Hushai cometh in unto Absalom, and Absalom speaketh unto him, saying, `According to this word hath Ahithophel spoken; do we do his word? if not, thou -- speak thou.'
texts.2sa.17.7: And Hushai saith unto Absalom, `Not good [is] the counsel that Ahithophel hath counselled at this time.'
texts.2sa.17.8: And Hushai saith, `Thou hast known thy father and his men, that they [are] heroes, and they are bitter in soul as a bereaved bear in a field, and thy father [is] a man of war, and doth not lodge with the people;
texts.2sa.17.9: lo, now, he is hidden in one of the pits, or in one of the places, and it hath been, at the falling among them at the commencement, that the hearer hath heard, and said, There hath been a slaughter among the people who [are] after Absalom;
texts.2sa.17.10: and he also, the son of valour, whose heart [is] as the heart of the lion, doth utterly melt, for all Israel doth know that thy father is a hero, and sons of valour [are] those with him.
texts.2sa.17.11: `So that I have counselled: Let all Israel be diligently gathered unto thee, from Dan even unto Beer-Sheba, as the sand that [is] by the sea for multitude, and thou thyself art going in the midst;
texts.2sa.17.12: and we have come in unto him in one of the places where he is found, and we [are] upon him as the dew falleth on the ground, and there hath not been left of him and of all the men who [are] with him even one.
texts.2sa.17.13: And if unto a city he is gathered, then they have caused all Israel to bear unto that city ropes, and we have drawn it unto the brook till that there hath not been found there even a stone.'
texts.2sa.17.14: And Absalom saith -- and all the men of Israel -- `Better [is] the counsel of Hushai the Archite than the counsel of Ahithophel;' and Jehovah willed to make void the good counsel of Ahithophel for the sake of Jehovah's bringing unto Absalom the evil.
texts.2sa.17.15: And Hushai saith unto Zadok and unto Abiathar the priests, `Thus and thus hath Ahithophel counselled Absalom and the elders of Israel, and thus and thus I have counselled;
texts.2sa.17.16: and now, send hastily, and declare to David, saying, Lodge not to-night in the plains of the wilderness, and also, certainly pass over, lest there be a swallowing up of the king and of all the people who are with him.'
texts.2sa.17.17: And Jonathan and Ahimaaz are standing at En-Rogel, and the maid-servant hath gone and declared to them -- and they go and have declared [it] to king David -- for they are not able to be seen to go in to the city.
texts.2sa.17.18: And a youth seeth them, and declareth to Absalom; and they go on both of them hastily, and come in unto the house of a man in Bahurim, and he hath a well in his court, and they go down there,
texts.2sa.17.19: and the woman taketh and spreadeth the covering over the face of the well, and spreadeth on it the ground corn, and the thing hath not been known.
texts.2sa.17.20: And the servants of Absalom come in unto the woman to the house, and say, `Where [are] Ahimaaz and Jonathan?' and the woman saith to them, `They passed over the brook of water;' and they seek, and have not found, and turn back to Jerusalem.
texts.2sa.17.21: And it cometh to pass, after their going on, that they come up out of the well, and go and declare to king David, and say unto David, `Rise ye, and pass over hastily the waters, for thus hath Ahithophel counselled against you.'
texts.2sa.17.22: And David riseth, and all the people who [are] with him, and they pass over the Jordan, till the light of the morning, till one hath not been lacking who hath not passed over the Jordan.
texts.2sa.17.23: And Ahithophel hath seen that his counsel was not done, and he saddleth the ass, and riseth and goeth unto his house, unto his city, and giveth charge unto his household, and strangleth himself, and dieth, and he is buried in the burying-place of his father.
texts.2sa.17.24: And David came to Mahanaim, and Absalom passed over the Jordan, he and all the men of Israel with him;
texts.2sa.17.25: and Amasa hath Absalom set instead of Joab over the host, and Amasa [is] a man's son whose name is Ithra the Israelite who hath gone in unto Abigail, daughter of Nahash, sister of Zeruiah, mother of Joab;
texts.2sa.17.26: and Israel encampeth with Absalom [in] the land of Gilead.
texts.2sa.17.27: And it cometh to pass at the coming in of David to Mahanaim, that Shobi, son of Nahash, from Rabbah of the Bene-Ammon, and Machir son of Ammiel, from Lo-Debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite, from Rogelim,
texts.2sa.17.28: couch, and basin, and earthen vessel, and wheat, and barley, and flour, and roasted [corn], and beans, and lentiles, and roasted [pulse],
texts.2sa.17.29: and honey, and butter, and sheep, and cheese of kine, have brought nigh for David, and for the people who [are] with him to eat, for they said, `Thy people [is] hungry, and weary, and thirsty, in the wilderness.'
texts.2sa.18.1: And David inspecteth the people who [are] with him, and setteth over them heads of thousands and heads of hundreds,
texts.2sa.18.2: and David sendeth the third of the people by the hand of Joab, and the third by the hand of Abishai, son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, and the third by the hand of Ittai the Gittite, and the king saith unto the people, `I certainly go out -- I also -- with you.'
texts.2sa.18.3: And the people say, `Thou dost not go out, for if we utterly flee, they do not set [their] heart upon us; and if half of us die, they do not set [their] heart unto us -- for now like us [are] ten thousand; and now, better that thou be to us from the city for an helper.'
texts.2sa.18.4: And the king saith unto them, `That which is good in your eyes I do;' and the king standeth at the side of the gate, and all the people have gone out by hundreds and by thousands,
texts.2sa.18.5: and the king chargeth Joab, and Abishai, and Ittai, saying, `Gently -- for me, for the youth, for Absalom;' and all the people heard in the king's charging all the heads concerning Absalom.
texts.2sa.18.6: And the people goeth out into the field to meet Israel, and the battle is in a forest of Ephraim;
texts.2sa.18.7: and smitten there are the people of Israel before the servants of David, and the smiting there is great on that day -- twenty thousand;
texts.2sa.18.8: and the battle is there scattered over the face of all the land, and the forest multiplieth to devour among the people more than those whom the sword hath devoured in that day.
texts.2sa.18.9: And Absalom meeteth before the servants of David, and Absalom is riding on the mule, and the mule cometh in under an entangled bough of the great oak, and his head taketh hold on the oak, and he is placed between the heavens and the earth, and the mule that [is] under him hath passed on.
texts.2sa.18.10: And one man seeth, and declareth to Joab, and saith, `Lo, I saw Absalom hanged in an oak.'
texts.2sa.18.11: And Joab saith to the man who is declaring [it] to him, `And lo, thou hast seen -- and wherefore didst thou not smite him there to the earth -- and on me to give to thee ten silverlings and one girdle?'
texts.2sa.18.12: And the man saith unto Joab, `Yea, though I am weighing on my hand a thousand silverlings, I do not put forth my hand unto the son of the king; for in our ears hath the king charged thee, and Abishai, and Ittai, saying, Observe ye who [is] against the youth -- against Absalom;
texts.2sa.18.13: or I had done against my soul a vain thing, and no matter is hid from the king, and thou -- thou dost station thyself over-against.'
texts.2sa.18.14: And Joab saith, `Not right -- I tarry before thee;' and he taketh three darts in his hand, and striketh them into the heart of Absalom, while he [is] alive, in the midst of the oak.
texts.2sa.18.15: And they go round -- ten youths bearing weapons of Joab -- and smite Absalom, and put him to death.
texts.2sa.18.16: And Joab bloweth with a trumpet, and the people turneth back from pursuing after Israel, for Joab hath kept back the people;
texts.2sa.18.17: and they take Absalom and cast him in the forest unto the great pit, and set up over him a very great heap of stones, and all Israel have fled -- each to his tent.
texts.2sa.18.18: And Absalom hath taken, and setteth up for himself in his life, the standing-pillar that [is] in the king's valley, for he said, `I have no son to cause my name to be remembered;' and he calleth the standing-pillar by his own name, and it is called `The monument of Absalom' unto this day.
texts.2sa.18.19: And Ahimaaz son of Zadok said, `Let me run, I pray thee, and I bear the king tidings, for Jehovah hath delivered him out of the hand of his enemies;'
texts.2sa.18.20: and Joab saith to him, `Thou art not a man of tidings this day, but thou hast borne tidings on another day, and this day thou dost not bear tidings, because the king's son [is] dead.'
texts.2sa.18.21: And Joab saith to Cushi, `Go, declare to the king that which thou hast seen;' and Cushi boweth himself to Joab, and runneth.
texts.2sa.18.22: And Ahimaaz son of Zadok addeth again, and saith unto Joab, `And whatever it be, let me run, I pray thee, I also, after the Cushite.' And Joab saith, `Why [is] this -- thou art running, my son, and for thee there are no tidings found?' --
texts.2sa.18.23: `And, whatever it be, [said he,] let me run.' And he saith to him, `Run;' and Ahimaaz runneth the way of the circuit, and passeth by the Cushite.
texts.2sa.18.24: And David is sitting between the two gates, and the watchman goeth unto the roof of the gate, unto the wall, and lifteth up his eyes, and looketh, and lo, a man running by himself.
texts.2sa.18.25: And the watchman calleth, and declareth to the king, and the king saith, `If by himself, tidings [are] in his mouth;' and he cometh, coming on and drawing near.
texts.2sa.18.26: And the watchman seeth another man running, and the watchman calleth unto the gatekeeper, and saith, `Lo, a man running by himself;' and the king saith, `Also this one is bearing tidings.'
texts.2sa.18.27: And the watchman saith, `I see the running of the first as the running of Ahimaaz son of Zadok.' And the king saith, `This [is] a good man, and with good tidings he cometh.'
texts.2sa.18.28: And Ahimaaz calleth and saith unto the king, `Peace;' and he boweth himself to the king, on his face, to the earth, and saith, `Blessed [is] Jehovah thy God who hath shut up the men who lifted up their hand against my lord the king.'
texts.2sa.18.29: And the king saith, `Peace to the youth -- to Absalom?' And Ahimaaz saith, `I saw the great multitude, at the sending away of the servant of the king, even thy servant [by] Joab, and I have not known what [it is].'
texts.2sa.18.30: And the king saith, `Turn round, station thyself here;' and he turneth round and standeth still.
texts.2sa.18.31: And lo, the Cushite hath come, and the Cushite saith, `Let tidings be proclaimed, my lord, O king; for Jehovah hath delivered thee to-day out of the hand of all those rising up against thee.'
texts.2sa.18.32: And the king saith unto the Cushite, `Peace to the youth -- to Absalom?' And the Cushite saith, `Let them be -- as the youth -- the enemies of my lord the king, and all who have risen up against thee for evil.'
texts.2sa.18.33: And the king trembleth, and goeth up on the upper chamber of the gate, and weepeth, and thus he hath said in his going, `My son! Absalom my son; my son Absalom; oh that I had died for thee, Absalom, my son, my son.'
texts.2sa.19.1: And it is declared to Joab, `Lo, the king is weeping and mourning for Absalom;'
texts.2sa.19.2: and the salvation on that day becometh mourning to all the people, for the people hath heard on that day, saying, `The king hath been grieved for his son.'
texts.2sa.19.3: And the people stealeth away, on that day, to go in to the city, as the people steal away, who are ashamed, in their fleeing in battle;
texts.2sa.19.4: and the king hath covered his face, yea, the king crieth -- a loud voice -- `My son Absalom, Absalom, my son, my son.'
texts.2sa.19.5: And Joab cometh in unto the king to the house, and saith, `Thou hast put to shame to-day the faces of all thy servants, those delivering thy life to-day, and the life of thy sons, and of thy daughters, and the life of thy wives, and the life of thy concubines,
texts.2sa.19.6: to love thine enemies, and to hate those loving thee, for thou hast declared to-day that thou hast no princes and servants, for I have known to-day that if Absalom [were] alive, and all of us to-day dead, that then it were right in thine eyes.
texts.2sa.19.7: `And now, rise, go out and speak unto the heart of thy servants, for by Jehovah I have sworn, that -- thou art not going out -- there doth not lodge a man with thee to-night; and this [is] worse for thee than all the evil that hath come upon thee from thy youth till now.'
texts.2sa.19.8: And the king riseth, and sitteth in the gate, and to all the people they have declared, saying, `Lo, the king is sitting in the gate;' and all the people come in before the king, and Israel hath fled, each to his tents.
texts.2sa.19.9: And it cometh to pass, all the people are contending through all the tribes of Israel, saying, `The king delivered us out of the hand of our enemies, yea, he himself delivered us out of the hand of the Philistines, and now he hath fled out of the land because of Absalom,
texts.2sa.19.10: and Absalom whom we anointed over us [is] dead in battle, and now, why are ye silent -- to bring back the king?'
texts.2sa.19.11: And king David sent unto Zadok and unto Abiathar the priests, saying, `Speak ye unto the elders of Judah, saying, Why are ye last to bring back the king unto his house? (and the word of all Israel hath come unto the king, unto his house;)
texts.2sa.19.12: my brethren ye [are], my bone and my flesh ye [are], and why are ye last to bring back the king?
texts.2sa.19.13: And to Amasa say ye, Art not thou my bone and my flesh? Thus doth God do to me, and thus He doth add, if thou art not head of the host before me all the days instead of Joab.'
texts.2sa.19.14: And he inclineth the heart of all the men of Judah as one man, and they send unto the king, `Turn back, thou, and all thy servants.'
texts.2sa.19.15: And the king turneth back, and cometh in unto the Jordan, and Judah hath come to Gilgal, to go to meet the king, to bring the king over the Jordan,
texts.2sa.19.16: and Shimei son of Gera, the Benjamite, who [is] from Bahurim, hasteth, and cometh down with the men of Judah, to meet king David,
texts.2sa.19.17: and a thousand men [are] with him from Benjamin, and Ziba servant of the house of Saul, and his fifteen sons and his twenty servants with him, and they have gone prosperously over the Jordan before the king.
texts.2sa.19.18: And passed over hath the ferry-boat to carry over the household of the king, and to do that which [is] good in his eyes, and Shimei son of Gera hath fallen before the king in his passing over into Jordan,
texts.2sa.19.19: and saith unto the king, `Let not my lord impute to me iniquity; neither do thou remember that which thy servant did perversely in the day that my lord the king went out from Jerusalem, -- for the king to set [it] unto his heart;
texts.2sa.19.20: for thy servant hath known that I have sinned; and lo, I have come to-day, first of all the house of Joseph, to go down to meet my lord the king.'
texts.2sa.19.21: And Abishai son of Zeruiah answereth and saith, `For this is not Shimei put to death -- because he reviled the anointed of Jehovah?'
texts.2sa.19.22: And David saith, `What -- to me and to you, O sons of Zeruiah, that ye are to me to-day for an adversary? to-day is any man put to death in Israel? for have I not known that to-day I [am] king over Israel?'
texts.2sa.19.23: And the king saith unto Shimei, `Thou dost not die;' and the king sweareth to him.
texts.2sa.19.24: And Mephibosheth son of Saul hath come down to meet the king -- and he prepared not his feet, nor did he prepare his upper lip, yea, his garments he washed not, even from the day of the going away of the king, till the day that he came in peace --
texts.2sa.19.25: and it cometh to pass, when he hath come to Jerusalem to meet the king, that the king saith to him, `Why didst thou not go with me, Mephibosheth?'
texts.2sa.19.26: And he saith, `My lord, O king, my servant deceived me, for thy servant said, I saddle for me the ass, and ride on it, and go with the king, for thy servant [is] lame;
texts.2sa.19.27: and he uttereth slander against thy servant unto my lord the king, and my lord the king [is] as a messenger of God; and do thou that which is good in thine eyes,
texts.2sa.19.28: for all the house of my father have been nothing except men of death before my lord the king, and thou dost set thy servant among those eating at thy table, and what right have I any more -- even to cry any more unto the king?'
texts.2sa.19.29: And the king saith to him, `Why dost thou speak any more of thy matters? I have said, Thou and Ziba -- share ye the field.'
texts.2sa.19.30: And Mephibosheth saith unto the king, `Yea, the whole let him take, after that my lord the king hath come in peace unto his house.'
texts.2sa.19.31: And Barzillai the Gileadite hath gone down from Rogelim, and passeth over the Jordan with the king, to send him away over the Jordan;
texts.2sa.19.32: and Barzillai [is] very aged, a son of eighty years, and he hath sustained the king in his abiding in Mahanaim, for he [is] a very great man;
texts.2sa.19.33: and the king saith unto Barzillai, `Pass thou over with me, and I have sustained thee with me in Jerusalem.'
texts.2sa.19.34: And Barzillai saith unto the king, `How many [are] the days of the years of my life, that I go up with the king to Jerusalem?
texts.2sa.19.35: A son of eighty years I [am] to-day; do I know between good and evil? doth thy servant taste that which I am eating, and that which I drink? do I hearken any more to the voice of singers and songstresses? and why is thy servant any more for a burden unto my lord the king?
texts.2sa.19.36: As a little thing, thy servant doth pass over the Jordan with the king, and why doth the king recompense me this recompense?
texts.2sa.19.37: Let, I pray thee, thy servant turn back again, and I die in mine own city, near the burying-place of my father and of my mother, -- and lo, thy servant Chimham, let him pass over with my lord the king, and do thou to him that which [is] good in thine eyes.'
texts.2sa.19.38: And the king saith, `With me doth Chimham go over, and I do to him that which [is] good in thine eyes, yea, all that thou dost fix on me I do to thee.'
texts.2sa.19.39: And all the people pass over the Jordan, and the king hath passed over, and the king giveth a kiss to Barzillai, and blesseth him, and he turneth back to his place.
texts.2sa.19.40: And the king passeth over to Gilgal, and Chimham hath passed over with him, and all the people of Judah, and they bring over the king, and also the half of the people of Israel.
texts.2sa.19.41: And, lo, all the men of Israel are coming unto the king, and they say unto the king, `Wherefore have they stolen thee -- our brethren, the men of Judah?' (and they bring the king and his household over the Jordan, and all the men of David with him).
texts.2sa.19.42: And all the men of Judah answer against the men of Israel, `Because the king [is] near unto us, and why [is] this -- ye are displeased about this matter? have we at all eaten of the king's [substance?] a gift hath he lifted up to us?'
texts.2sa.19.43: And the men of Israel answer the men of Judah, and say, `Ten parts we have in the king, and also in David more than you; and wherefore have ye lightly esteemed us, that our word hath not been first to bring back our king?' And the word of the men of Judah is sharper than the word of the men of Israel.
texts.2sa.20.1: And there hath been called there a man of worthlessness, and his name [is] Sheba, son of Bichri, a Benjamite, and he bloweth with a trumpet, and saith, `We have no portion in David, and we have no inheritance in the son of Jesse; each to his tents, O Israel.'
texts.2sa.20.2: And every man of Israel goeth up from after David, after Sheba son of Bichri, and the men of Judah have cleaved to their king, from the Jordan even unto Jerusalem.
texts.2sa.20.3: And David cometh in unto his house at Jerusalem, and the king taketh the ten women-concubines -- whom he had left to keep the house, and putteth them in a house of ward, and sustaineth them, and unto them he hath not gone in, and they are shut up unto the day of their death, in widowhood living.
texts.2sa.20.4: And the king saith unto Amasa, `Call for me the men of Judah [in] three days, and thou, stand here,'
texts.2sa.20.5: and Amasa goeth to call Judah, and tarrieth beyond the appointed time that he had appointed him;
texts.2sa.20.6: and David saith unto Abishai, `Now doth Sheba son of Bichri do evil to us more than Absalom; thou, take the servants of thy lord, and pursue after him, lest he have found for himself fenced cities, and delivered himself [from] our eye.'
texts.2sa.20.7: And the men of Joab go out after him, and the Cherethite, and the Pelethite, and all the mighty men, and they go out from Jerusalem to pursue after Sheba son of Bichri;
texts.2sa.20.8: they [are] near the great stone that [is] in Gibeon, and Amasa hath gone before them, and Joab [is] girded; his long robe he hath put on him, and upon it a girdle -- a sword [is] fastened upon his loins in its sheath; and he hath gone out, and it falleth.
texts.2sa.20.9: And Joab saith to Amasa, `Art thou [in] peace, my brother?' and the right hand of Joab layeth hold on the beard of Amasa to give a kiss to him;
texts.2sa.20.10: and Amasa hath not been watchful of the sword that [is] in the hand of Joab, and he smiteth him with it unto the fifth [rib], and sheddeth out his bowels to the earth, and he hath not repeated [it] to him, and he dieth; and Joab and Abishai his brother have pursued after Sheba son of Bichri.
texts.2sa.20.11: And a man hath stood by him, of the young men of Joab, and saith, `He who hath delight in Joab, and he who [is] for David -- after Joab!'
texts.2sa.20.12: And Amasa is rolling himself in blood, in the midst of the highway, and the man seeth that all the people have stood still, and he bringeth round Amasa out of the highway to the field, and casteth over him a garment, when he hath seen that every one who hath come by him -- hath stood still.
texts.2sa.20.13: When he hath been removed out of the highway, every man hath passed on after Joab, to pursue after Sheba son of Bichri.
texts.2sa.20.14: And he passeth over through all the tribes of Israel to Abel, and to Beth-Maachah, and to all the Berites, and they are assembled, and go in also after him,
texts.2sa.20.15: and they go in and lay siege against him, in Abel of Beth-Maachah, and cast up a mount against the city, and it standeth in a trench, and all the people who are [are] with Joab are destroying, to cause the wall to fall.
texts.2sa.20.16: And a wise woman calleth out of the city, `Hear, hear; say, I pray you, unto Joab, Come near hither, and I speak unto thee.'
texts.2sa.20.17: And he cometh near unto her, and the woman saith, `Art thou Joab?' and he saith, `I [am].' And she saith to him, `Hear the words of thy handmaid;' and he saith, `I am hearing.'
texts.2sa.20.18: and she speaketh, saying, `They spake often in former times, saying, Let them diligently ask at Abel, and so they finished.
texts.2sa.20.19: I [am] of the peaceable -- faithful ones of Israel; thou art seeking to destroy a city, and a mother in Israel; why dost thou swallow up the inheritance of Jehovah?
texts.2sa.20.20: And Joab answereth and saith, `Far be it -- far be it from me; I do not swallow up nor destroy.
texts.2sa.20.21: The matter [is] not so; for a man of the hill-country of Ephraim -- Sheba son of Bichri his name -- hath lifted up his hand against the king, against David; give ye up him by himself, and I go away from the city.' And the woman saith unto Joab, `Lo, his head is cast unto thee over the wall.'
texts.2sa.20.22: And the woman cometh unto all the people in her wisdom, and they cut off the head of Sheba son of Bichri, and cast [it] unto Joab, and he bloweth with a trumpet, and they are scattered from the city, each to his tents, and Joab hath turned back to Jerusalem unto the king.
texts.2sa.20.23: And Joab [is] over all the host of Israel, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada [is] over the Cherethite, and over the Pelethite,
texts.2sa.20.24: and Adoram [is] over the tribute, and Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud [is] the remembrancer,
texts.2sa.20.25: and Sheva [is] scribe, and Zadok and Abiathar [are] priests,
texts.2sa.20.26: and also, Ira the Jairite hath been minister to David.
texts.2sa.21.1: And there is a famine in the days of David three years, year after year, and David seeketh the face of Jehovah, and Jehovah saith, `For Saul and for the bloody house, because that he put to death the Gibeonites.'
texts.2sa.21.2: And the king calleth for the Gibeonites, and saith unto them -- as to the Gibeonites, they [are] not of the sons of Israel, but of the remnant of the Amorite, and the sons of Israel had sworn to them, and Saul seeketh to smite them in his zeal for the sons of Israel and Judah --
texts.2sa.21.3: yea, David saith unto the Gibeonites, `What do I do for you? and with what do I make atonement? and bless ye the inheritance of Jehovah.'
texts.2sa.21.4: And the Gibeonites say to him, `We have no silver and gold by Saul and by his house, and we have no man to put to death in Israel;' and he saith, `What ye are saying I do to you.'
texts.2sa.21.5: And they say unto the king, `The man who consumed us, and who devised against us -- we have been destroyed from stationing ourselves in all the border of Israel --
texts.2sa.21.6: let there be given to us seven men of his sons, and we have hanged them before Jehovah, in the height of Saul, the chosen of Jehovah.' And the king saith, `I do give;'
texts.2sa.21.7: and the king hath pity on Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, son of Saul, because of the oath of Jehovah that [is] between them, between David and Jonathan son of Saul;
texts.2sa.21.8: and the king taketh the two sons of Rizpah daughter of Aiah, whom she bore to Saul, Armoni and Mephibosheth, and the five sons of Michal daughter of Saul whom she bare to Adriel son of Barzillai the Meholathite,
texts.2sa.21.9: and giveth them into the hand of the Gibeonites, and they hang them in the hill before Jehovah; and the seven fall together, and they have been put to death in the days of harvest, in the first [days], the commencement of barley-harvest.
texts.2sa.21.10: And Rizpah daughter of Aiah taketh the sackcloth, and stretcheth it out for herself on the rock, from the commencement of harvest till water hath been poured out upon them from the heavens, and hath not suffered a fowl of the heavens to rest upon them by day, or the beast of the field by night.
texts.2sa.21.11: And it is declared to David that which Rizpah daughter of Aiah, concubine of Saul, hath done,
texts.2sa.21.12: and David goeth and taketh the bones of Saul, and the bones of Jonathan his son, from the possessors of Jabesh-Gilead, who had stolen them from the broad place of Beth-Shan, where the Philistines hanged them, in the day of the Philistines smiting Saul in Gilboa;
texts.2sa.21.13: and he bringeth up thence the bones of Saul, and the bones of Jonathan his son, and they gather the bones of those hanged,
texts.2sa.21.14: and bury the bones of Saul and of Jonathan his son in the land of Benjamin, in Zelah, in the burying-place of Kish his father, and do all that the king commanded, and God is entreated for the land afterwards.
texts.2sa.21.15: And again have the Philistines war with Israel, and David goeth down, and his servants with him, and they fight with the Philistines; and David is weary,
texts.2sa.21.16: and Ishbi-Benob, who [is] among the children of the giant -- the weight of his spear [is] three hundred [shekels] weight of brass, and he is girded with a new one -- speaketh of smiting David,
texts.2sa.21.17: and Abishai son of Zeruiah giveth help to him, and smiteth the Philistine, and putteth him to death; then swear the men of David to him, saying, `Thou dost not go out again with us to battle, nor quench the lamp of Israel.'
texts.2sa.21.18: And it cometh to pass afterwards, that the battle is again in Gob with the Philistines, then hath Sibbechai the Hushathite smitten Saph, who [is] among the children of the giant.
texts.2sa.21.19: And the battle is again in Gob with the Philistines, and Elhanan son of Jaare-Oregim, the Beth-Lehemite, smiteth [a brother of] Goliath the Gittite, and the wood of his spear [is] like a beam of weavers.
texts.2sa.21.20: And the battle is again in Gath, and there is a man of stature, and the fingers of his hands [are] six, and the toes of his feet [are] six, twenty and four in number, and he also hath been born to the giant,
texts.2sa.21.21: and he reproacheth Israel, and smite him doth Jonathan son of Shimeah, brother of David;
texts.2sa.21.22: these four have been born to the giant in Gath, and they fall by the hand of David, and by the hand of his servants.
texts.2sa.22.1: And David speaketh to Jehovah the words of this song in the day Jehovah hath delivered him out of the hand of all his enemies, and out of the hand of Saul,
texts.2sa.22.2: and he saith: `Jehovah [is] my rock, And my bulwark, and a deliverer to me,
texts.2sa.22.3: My God [is] my rock -- I take refuge in Him; My shield, and the horn of my salvation, My high tower, and my refuge! My Saviour, from violence Thou savest me!
texts.2sa.22.4: The Praised One, I call Jehovah: And from mine enemies I am saved.
texts.2sa.22.5: When the breakers of death compassed me, The streams of the worthless terrify me,
texts.2sa.22.6: The cords of Sheol have surrounded me, Before me have been the snares of death.
texts.2sa.22.7: In mine adversity I call Jehovah, And unto my God I call, And He heareth from His temple my voice, And my cry [is] in His ears,
texts.2sa.22.8: And shake and tremble doth the earth, Foundations of the heavens are troubled, And are shaken, for He hath wrath!
texts.2sa.22.9: Gone up hath smoke by His nostrils. And fire from His mouth devoureth, Brands have been kindled by it.
texts.2sa.22.10: And He inclineth heaven, and cometh down, And thick darkness [is] under His feet.
texts.2sa.22.11: And He rideth on a cherub, and doth fly, And is seen on the wings of the wind.
texts.2sa.22.12: And He setteth darkness Round about Him -- tabernacles, Darkness of waters -- thick clouds of the skies.
texts.2sa.22.13: From the brightness before Him Were brands of fire kindled!
texts.2sa.22.14: Thunder from the heavens doth Jehovah, And the Most High giveth forth His voice.
texts.2sa.22.15: And He sendeth forth arrows, And scattereth them; Lightning, and troubleth them;
texts.2sa.22.16: And seen are the streams of the sea, Revealed are foundations of the world, By the rebuke of Jehovah, From the breath of the spirit of His anger.
texts.2sa.22.17: He sendeth from above -- He taketh me, He draweth me out of many waters.
texts.2sa.22.18: He delivereth me from my strong enemy, From those hating me, For they were stronger than I.
texts.2sa.22.19: They are before me in a day of my calamity, And Jehovah is my support,
texts.2sa.22.20: And He bringeth me out to a large place, He draweth me out for He delighted in me.
texts.2sa.22.21: Jehovah recompenseth me, According to my righteousness, According to the cleanness of my hands, He doth return to me.
texts.2sa.22.22: For I have kept the ways of Jehovah, And have not done wickedly against my God.
texts.2sa.22.23: For all His judgments [are] before me, As to His statutes, I turn not from them.
texts.2sa.22.24: And I am perfect before Him, And I keep myself from mine iniquity.
texts.2sa.22.25: And Jehovah returneth to me, According to my righteousness, According to my cleanness before His eyes.
texts.2sa.22.26: With the kind Thou shewest Thyself kind, With the perfect man Thou shewest Thyself perfect,
texts.2sa.22.27: With the pure Thou shewest Thyself pure, And with the perverse Thou shewest Thyself a wrestler.
texts.2sa.22.28: And the poor people Thou dost save, And Thine eyes on the high causest to fall.
texts.2sa.22.29: For Thou [art] my lamp, O Jehovah, And Jehovah doth lighten my darkness.
texts.2sa.22.30: For by Thee I run -- a troop, By my God I leap a wall.
texts.2sa.22.31: God! Perfect [is] His way, The saying of Jehovah is tried, A shield He [is] to all those trusting in Him.
texts.2sa.22.32: For who is God save Jehovah? And who a Rock save our God?
texts.2sa.22.33: God -- my bulwark, [my] strength, And He maketh perfect my way;
texts.2sa.22.34: Making my feet like hinds, And on my high places causeth me to stand,
texts.2sa.22.35: Teaching my hands for battle, And brought down was a bow of brass by mine arms,
texts.2sa.22.36: And Thou givest to me the shield of Thy salvation, And Thy lowliness maketh me great.
texts.2sa.22.37: Thou enlargest my step under me, And mine ankles have not slidden.
texts.2sa.22.38: I pursue mine enemies and destroy them, And I turn not till they are consumed.
texts.2sa.22.39: And I consume them, and smite them, And they rise not, and fall under my feet.
texts.2sa.22.40: And Thou girdest me [with] strength for battle, Thou causest my withstanders to bow under me.
texts.2sa.22.41: And mine enemies -- Thou givest to me the neck, Those hating me -- and I cut them off.
texts.2sa.22.42: They look, and there is no saviour; Unto Jehovah, and He hath not answered them.
texts.2sa.22.43: And I beat them as dust of the earth, As mire of the streets I beat them small -- I spread them out!
texts.2sa.22.44: And -- Thou dost deliver me From the strivings of my people, Thou placest me for a head of nations; A people I have not known do serve me.
texts.2sa.22.45: Sons of a stranger feign obedience to me, At the hearing of the ear they hearken to me.
texts.2sa.22.46: Sons of a stranger fade away, And gird themselves by their close places.
texts.2sa.22.47: Jehovah liveth, and blessed [is] my Rock, And exalted is my God -- The Rock of my salvation.
texts.2sa.22.48: God -- who is giving vengeance to me, And bringing down peoples under me,
texts.2sa.22.49: And bringing me forth from mine enemies, Yea, above my withstanders Thou raisest me up. From a man of violence Thou deliverest me.
texts.2sa.22.50: Therefore I confess Thee, O Jehovah, among nations. And to Thy name I sing praise.
texts.2sa.22.51: Magnifying the salvations of His king, And doing loving-kindness to His anointed, To David, and to his seed -- unto the age!'
texts.2sa.23.1: And these [are] the last words of David: -- `The affirmation of David son of Jesse -- And the affirmation of the man raised up -- Concerning the Anointed of the God of Jacob, And the Sweetness of the Songs of Israel:
texts.2sa.23.2: The Spirit of Jehovah hath spoken by me, And His word [is] on my tongue.
texts.2sa.23.3: He said -- the God of Israel -- to me, He spake -- the Rock of Israel: He who is ruling over man [is] righteous, He is ruling in the fear of God.
texts.2sa.23.4: And as the light of morning he riseth, A morning sun -- no clouds! By the shining, by the rain, Tender grass of the earth!
texts.2sa.23.5: For -- not so [is] my house with God; For -- a covenant age-during He made with me, Arranged in all things, and kept; For -- all my salvation, and all desire, For -- He hath not caused [it] to spring up.
texts.2sa.23.6: As to the worthless -- As a thorn driven away [are] all of them, For -- not by hand are they taken;
texts.2sa.23.7: And the man who cometh against them Is filled with iron and the staff of a spear, And with fire they are utterly burnt In the cessation.'
texts.2sa.23.8: These [are] the names of the mighty ones whom David hath: sitting in the seat [is] the Tachmonite, head of the captains -- he [is] Adino, who hardened himself against eight hundred -- wounded at one time.
texts.2sa.23.9: And after him [is] Eleazar son of Dodo, son of Ahohi, of the three mighty men with David; in their exposing themselves among the Philistines -- they have been gathered there to battle, and the men of Israel go up --
texts.2sa.23.10: he hath arisen, and smiteth among the Philistines till that his hand hath been weary, and his hand cleaveth unto the sword, and Jehovah worketh a great salvation on that day, and the people turn back after him only to strip off.
texts.2sa.23.11: And after him [is] Shammah son of Agee the Hararite, and the Philistines are gathered into a company, and there is there a portion of the field full of lentiles, and the people hath fled from the presence of the Philistines,
texts.2sa.23.12: and he stationeth himself in the midst of the portion, and delivereth it, and smiteth the Philistines, and Jehovah worketh a great salvation.
texts.2sa.23.13: And three of the thirty heads go down and come unto the harvest, unto David, unto the cave of Adullam, and the company of the Philistines are encamping in the valley of Rephaim,
texts.2sa.23.14: and David [is] then in a fortress, and the station of the Philistines [is] then in Beth-Lehem,
texts.2sa.23.15: and David longeth and saith, `Who doth give me a drink of the water of the well of Beth-Lehem, which [is] by the gate?'
texts.2sa.23.16: And the three mighty ones cleave through the camp of the Philistines, and draw water out of the well of Beth-Lehem, which [is] by the gate, and take [it] up, and bring in unto David; and he was not willing to drink it, and poureth it out to Jehovah,
texts.2sa.23.17: and saith, `Far be it from me, O Jehovah, to do this; is it the blood of the men who are going with their lives?' and he was not willing to drink it; these [things] did the three mighty ones.
texts.2sa.23.18: And Abishai brother of Joab, son of Zeruiah, he [is] head of three, and he is lifting up his spear against three hundred -- wounded, and he hath a name among three.
texts.2sa.23.19: Of the three is he not the honoured? and he becometh their head; and unto the [first] three he hath not come.
texts.2sa.23.20: And Benaiah son of Jehoiada (son of a man of valour, great in deeds from Kabzeel), he hath smitten two lion-like men of Moab, and he hath gone down and smitten the lion in the midst of the pit in a day of snow.
texts.2sa.23.21: And he hath smitten the Egyptian man, a man of appearance, and in the hand of the Egyptian [is] a spear, and he goeth down unto him with a rod, and taketh violently away the spear out of the hand of the Egyptian, and slayeth him with his own spear.
texts.2sa.23.22: These [things] hath Benaiah son of Jehoiada done, and hath a name among three mighty.
texts.2sa.23.23: Of the thirty he is honoured, and unto the three he came not; and David setteth him over his guard.
texts.2sa.23.24: Asahel brother of Joab [is] of the thirty; Elhanan son of Dodo of Beth-Lehem.
texts.2sa.23.25: Shammah the Harodite, Elika the Harodite,
texts.2sa.23.26: Helez the Paltite, Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite,
texts.2sa.23.27: Abiezer the Annethothite, Mebunnai the Hushathite,
texts.2sa.23.28: Zalmon the Ahohite, Maharai the Netophathite,
texts.2sa.23.29: Heleb son of Baanah the Netophathite, Ittai son of Ribai from Gibeah of the sons of Benjamin,
texts.2sa.23.30: Benaiah the Pirathonite, Hiddai of the brooks of Gaash,
texts.2sa.23.31: Abi-Albon the Arbathite, Azmaveth the Barhumite,
texts.2sa.23.32: Eliahba the Shaalbonite, [of] the sons of Jashen, Jonathan,
texts.2sa.23.33: Shammah the Hararite, Ahiam son of Sharar the Hararite,
texts.2sa.23.34: Eliphelet son of Ahasbai, son of the Maachathite, Eliam son of Ahithophel the Gilonite,
texts.2sa.23.35: Hezrai the Carmelite, Paarai the Arbite,
texts.2sa.23.36: Igal son of Nathan from Zobah, Bani the Gadite,
texts.2sa.23.37: Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Beerothite, bearer of the weapons of Joab son of Zeruiah,
texts.2sa.23.38: Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,
texts.2sa.23.39: Uriah the Hittite; in all thirty and seven.
texts.2sa.24.1: And the anger of Jehovah addeth to burn against Israel, and [an adversary] moveth David about them, saying, `Go, number Israel and Judah.'
texts.2sa.24.2: And the king saith unto Joab, head of the host that [is] with him, `Go to and fro, I pray thee, through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan even unto Beer-Sheba, and inspect ye the people -- and I have known the number of the people.'
texts.2sa.24.3: And Joab saith unto the king, `Yea, Jehovah thy God doth add unto the people, as they are, a hundred times, and the eyes of my lord the king are seeing; and my lord the king, why is he desirous of this thing?'
texts.2sa.24.4: And the word of the king is severe towards Joab, and against the heads of the force, and Joab goeth out, and the heads of the force, [from] before the king to inspect the people, even Israel;
texts.2sa.24.5: and they pass over the Jordan, and encamp in Aroer, on the right of the city that [is] in the midst of the brook of Gad, and unto Jazer,
texts.2sa.24.6: and they come in to Gilead, and unto the land of Tahtim-Hodshi, and they come in to Dan-Jaan, and round about unto Zidon,
texts.2sa.24.7: and they come in to the fortress of Tyre, and all the cities of the Hivite, and of the Canaanite, and go out unto the south of Judah, to Beer-Sheba.
texts.2sa.24.8: And they go to and fro through all the land, and come in at the end of nine months and twenty days to Jerusalem,
texts.2sa.24.9: and Joab giveth the account of the inspection of the people unto the king, and Israel is eight hundred thousand men of valour, drawing sword, and the men of Judah five hundred thousand men.
texts.2sa.24.10: And the heart of David smiteth him, after that he hath numbered the people, and David saith unto Jehovah, `I have sinned greatly in that which I have done, and now, O Jehovah, cause to pass away, I pray Thee, the iniquity of Thy servant, for I have acted very foolishly.'
texts.2sa.24.11: And David riseth in the morning, and the word of Jehovah hath been unto Gad the prophet, seer of David, saying,
texts.2sa.24.12: `Go, and thou hast spoken unto David, Thus said Jehovah: Three -- I am lifting up for thee, choose thee one of them, and I do [it] to thee.'
texts.2sa.24.13: And Gad cometh in unto David, and declareth to him, and saith to him, `Do seven years of famine come in to thee in thy land? or three months art thou fleeing before thine adversary -- and he pursuing thee? or are three days' pestilence in thy land? now, know and see what word I take back to Him sending me.'
texts.2sa.24.14: And David saith unto Gad, `I have great distress, let us fall, I pray thee, into the hand of Jehovah, for many [are] His mercies, and into the hand of man let me not fall.'
texts.2sa.24.15: And Jehovah giveth a pestilence on Israel from the morning even unto the time appointed, and there die of the people, from Dan even unto Beer-Sheba, seventy thousand men,
texts.2sa.24.16: and the messenger putteth forth his hand to Jerusalem to destroy it, and Jehovah repenteth concerning the evil, and saith to the messenger who is destroying among the people, `Enough, now, cease thy hand;' and the messenger of Jehovah was near the threshing-floor of Araunah the Jebusite.
texts.2sa.24.17: And David speaketh unto Jehovah, when he seeth the messenger who is smiting among the people, and saith, `Lo, I have sinned, yea, I have done perversely; and these -- the flock -- what have they done? Let, I pray Thee, Thy hand be on me, and on the house of my father.'
texts.2sa.24.18: And Gad cometh in unto David on that day, and saith to him, `Go up, raise to Jehovah an altar in the threshing-floor of Araunah the Jebusite;'
texts.2sa.24.19: and David goeth up, according to the word of Gad, as Jehovah commanded.
texts.2sa.24.20: And Araunah looketh, and seeth the king and his servants passing over unto him, and Araunah goeth out and boweth himself to the king -- his face to the earth.
texts.2sa.24.21: And Araunah saith, `Wherefore hath my lord the king come unto his servant?' and David saith, `To buy from thee the threshing-floor, to build an altar to Jehovah, and the plague is restrained from the people.'
texts.2sa.24.22: And Araunah saith unto David, `Let my lord the king take and cause to ascend that which is good in his eyes; see, the oxen for a burnt-offering, and the threshing instruments, and the instruments of the oxen, for wood;'
texts.2sa.24.23: the whole hath Araunah given, [as] a king to a king; and Araunah saith unto the king, `Jehovah thy God doth accept thee.'
texts.2sa.24.24: And the king saith unto Araunah, `Nay, for I do surely buy from thee for a price, and I do not cause to ascend to Jehovah my God burnt-offerings for nought;' and David buyeth the threshing-floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver,
texts.2sa.24.25: and David buildeth there an altar to Jehovah, and causeth to ascend burnt-offerings and peace-offerings, and Jehovah is entreated for the land, and the plague is restrained from Israel.

texts.2sa.1.1: Y aconteció después de la muerte de Saul, que vuelto David de la derrota de los Amalecitas, estuvo dos días en Siceleg:
texts.2sa.1.2: Y al tercero día aconteció, que llegó uno del campo de Saul, rotos sus vestidos, y esparcida tierra sobre su cabeza. Y llegando a David, postróse en tierra, y le hizo reverencia.
texts.2sa.1.3: Y preguntóle David: ¿De dónde vienes? Y él respondió: Heme escapado del campo de Israel.
texts.2sa.1.4: Y David le dijo: ¿Qué ha acontecido? Ruégote que me lo digas. Y él respondió: El pueblo huyó de la batalla, y también muchos del pueblo cayeron y son muertos: también Saul, y Jonatán su hijo murieron.
texts.2sa.1.5: Y dijo David a aquel mancebo que le daba las nuevas: ¿Cómo sabes que Saul es muerto, y Jonatán su hijo?
texts.2sa.1.6: Y el mancebo que le daba las nuevas respondió: Por casualidad vine al monte de Gelboé, y, he aquí Saul que estaba recostado sobre su lanza, y venían tras él carros y gente de a caballo:
texts.2sa.1.7: Y como él miró atrás, me vio, y me llamó: y yo dije: Heme aquí:
texts.2sa.1.8: Y él me dijo: ¿Quién eres tú? Y yo le respondí: Soy Amalecita.
texts.2sa.1.9: Y él me volvió a decir: Yo te ruego que te pongas sobre mí, y me mates, porque me toman angustias, y aun toda mi alma está en mí.
texts.2sa.1.10: Yo entonces púseme sobre él, y le maté: porque sabía que no podía vivir después de su caída. Y tomé la corona que tenía en su cabeza, y la ajorca que traía en su brazo, y las he traído acá a mi señor.
texts.2sa.1.11: Entonces David trabando de sus vestidos rompiólos, y lo mismo hicieron los varones que estaban con él.
texts.2sa.1.12: Y lloraron, y lamentaron; y ayunaron hasta la tarde por Saul y por Jonatán su hijo, y por el pueblo de Jehová, y por la casa de Israel, que habían caído a cuchillo.
texts.2sa.1.13: ¶ Y David dijo a aquel mancebo, que le había traído las nuevas: ¿De dónde eres tú? Y él respondió: Yo soy hijo de un extranjero, Amalecita.
texts.2sa.1.14: Y díjole David: ¿Cómo no hubiste temor de extender tu mano para matar al ungido de Jehová?
texts.2sa.1.15: Entonces David llamó a uno de los mancebos, y díjole: Llega, y mátale. Y él le hirió, y murió.
texts.2sa.1.16: Y David le dijo: Tu sangre sea sobre tu cabeza, pues que tu boca atestiguó contra ti, diciendo: Yo maté al ungido de Jehová.
texts.2sa.1.17: Y endechó David a Saul y a Jonatán su hijo, con esta endecha.
texts.2sa.1.18: Y dijo, que enseñasen al arco a los hijos de Judá. He aquí que así está escrito en el libro del derecho.
texts.2sa.1.19: ¶ La gloria de Israel, muertos sobre tus collados: ¡cómo han caído los valientes!
texts.2sa.1.20: No lo denunciéis en Get, no deis las nuevas en las plazas de Ascalón; porque no se alegren las hijas de los Filisteos: porque no salten de gozo las hijas de los incircuncisos.
texts.2sa.1.21: Montes de Gelboé, ni rocío ni lluvia caiga sobre vosotros; ni seáis tierras de ofrendas: porque allí fue desechado el escudo de los valientes, el escudo de Saul, como si no hubiera sido ungido de aceite.
texts.2sa.1.22: Sin sangre de muertos, sin sebo de valientes, el arco de Jonatán nunca volvió atrás, ni la espada de Saul se tornó vacía.
texts.2sa.1.23: Saul y Jonatán amados y queridos en su vida, en su muerte tampoco fueron apartados. Más ligeros que águilas, más fuertes que leones.
texts.2sa.1.24: Hijas de Israel llorád sobre Saul, que os vestía de escarlata en placeres: que adornaba vuestras ropas con ornamentos de oro.
texts.2sa.1.25: ¡Cómo han caído los valientes en medio de la batalla, Jonatán, muerto en tus alturas!
texts.2sa.1.26: Angustia tengo por ti, hermano mío Jonatán, que me fuiste muy dulce; más maravilloso me fue tu amor, que el amor de las mujeres.
texts.2sa.1.27: ¡Cómo han caído los valientes, y perecieron las armas de guerra!
texts.2sa.2.1: Después de esto aconteció que David consultó a Jehová, diciendo: ¿Subiré a alguna de las ciudades de Judá? Y Jehová le respondió: Sube. Y David tornó a decir. ¿Adónde subiré? Y él le dijo: a Hebrón.
texts.2sa.2.2: Y David subió allá, y con él sus dos mujeres Aquinoam Jezraelita, y Abigail, la mujer de Nabal del Carmelo.
texts.2sa.2.3: Y trajo también David consigo los varones que habían estado con él, cada uno con su familia: los cuales moraron en las ciudades de Hebrón.
texts.2sa.2.4: Y vinieron los varones de Judá, y ungieron allí a David por rey sobre la casa de Judá. Y dieron aviso a David, diciendo: Los de Jabes de Galaad son los que sepultaron a Saul.
texts.2sa.2.5: ¶ Y David envió mensajeros a los de Jabes de Galaad, diciéndoles: Benditos seáis vosotros de Jehová, que habéis hecho esta misericordia con vuestro señor Saul, que le habéis sepultado.
texts.2sa.2.6: Ahora pues Jehová hará con vosotros misericordia y verdad: y yo también os haré bien, por esto que habéis hecho.
texts.2sa.2.7: Esfuércense pues ahora vuestras manos, y sed valientes, pues que muerto Saul vuestro señor, los de la casa de Judá me han ungido por rey sobre sí.
texts.2sa.2.8: ¶ Y Abner, hijo de Ner, general del ejército de Saul, tomó a Is-boset, hijo de Saul, e hízole pasar al real.
texts.2sa.2.9: Y alzóle por rey sobre Galaad, y sobre Gessuri, y sobre Jezrael, y sobre Efraím, y sobre Ben-jamín, y sobre todo Israel.
texts.2sa.2.10: De cuarenta años era Is-boset, hijo de Saul, cuando comenzó a reinar sobre Israel, y reinó dos años: sola la casa de Judá seguía a David.
texts.2sa.2.11: Y fue el número de los días que David reinó en Hebrón sobre la casa de Judá, siete años y seis meses.
texts.2sa.2.12: Y Abner, hijo de Ner, salió del real a Gabaón con los siervos de Is-boset, hijo de Saul.
texts.2sa.2.13: Y Joab, hijo de Sarvia, y los criados de David salieron, y encontráronlos junto al estanque de Gabaón; y como se juntaron, los unos se pararon de la una parte del estanque, y los otros de la otra.
texts.2sa.2.14: Y dijo Abner a Joab: Levántense ahora los mancebos, y jueguen delante de nosotros. Y Joab respondió: Levanten.
texts.2sa.2.15: Entonces levantáronse, y pasaron doce por cuenta de Ben-jamín de la parte de Is-boset, hijo de Saul: y otros doce de los siervos de David.
texts.2sa.2.16: Y cada uno echó mano de la cabeza de su compañero, y metió su espada por el lado de su compañero, y cayeron a una: y fue llamado aquel lugar Helcat-assurim, el cual es en Gabaón.
texts.2sa.2.17: Y hubo aquel día una batalla muy recia, donde Abner y los varones de Israel fueron vencidos de los siervos de David.
texts.2sa.2.18: Y estaban allí los tres hijos de Sarvia, Joab, y Abisaí, y Asael. Este Asael era suelto de pies como un corzo del campo.
texts.2sa.2.19: El cual Asael siguió a Abner, yendo sin apartarse a diestra ni a siniestra en pos de Abner.
texts.2sa.2.20: Y Abner miró atrás, y dijo: ¿No eres tú Asael? Y él respondió: Sí.
texts.2sa.2.21: Entonces Abner le dijo: Apártate, o a la derecha, o a la izquierda, y préndete alguno de los mancebos, y tómate sus despojos. Y Asael no quiso apartarse de en pos de él.
texts.2sa.2.22: Y Abner tornó a decir a Asael: Apártate de en pos de mí, porque te heriré en tierra, y después ¿cómo levantaré mi rostro a tu hermano Joab?
texts.2sa.2.23: Y no queriendo él irse, hirióle Abner con la parte opuesta de la lanza, junto a la quinta costilla, y la lanza le salió por las espaldas, y cayó allí, y murió en aquel mismo lugar. Y todos los que venían por aquel lugar donde Asael había caído, y estaba muerto, se paraban.
texts.2sa.2.24: Y Joab y Abisaí siguieron a Abner, y púsoseles el sol, cuando llegaron al collado de Amma, que está delante de Gia, junto al camino del desierto de Gabaón.
texts.2sa.2.25: Y juntáronse los hijos de Ben-jamín en un escuadrón con Abner; y paráronse en la cumbre del collado.
texts.2sa.2.26: Y Abner dio voces a Joab, diciendo: ¿Consumirá la espada perpetuamente? ¿No sabes tú que al cabo se sigue amargura? ¿Hasta cuándo no has de decir al pueblo que se vuelvan de seguir a sus hermanos?
texts.2sa.2.27: Y Joab respondió: Vive Dios que si no hubieras hablado, ya desde esta mañana el pueblo hubiera cesado de seguir a sus hermanos.
texts.2sa.2.28: Entonces Joab tocó el cuerno, y todo el pueblo se detuvo, y no siguió más a los de Israel, ni peleó más.
texts.2sa.2.29: Y Abner y los suyos se fueron por la campaña toda aquella noche, y pasando el Jordán caminaron por todo Bet-orón, y vinieron al real.
texts.2sa.2.30: Joab también vuelto de seguir a Abner, juntando todo el pueblo, faltaron de los siervos de David diez y nueve hombres, y Asael.
texts.2sa.2.31: Y los siervos de David hirieron de los de Ben-jamín, y de los de Abner: trescientos y sesenta hombres murieron. Y tomaron a Asael, y sepultáronle en el sepulcro de su padre en Belén.
texts.2sa.2.32: Y caminaron toda aquella noche, Joab y los suyos: y amanecióles en Hebrón.
texts.2sa.3.1: Y hubo luenga guerra entre la casa de Saul, y la casa de David: mas David se iba fortificando, y la casa de Saul iba en diminución.
texts.2sa.3.2: Y nacieron hijos a David en Hebrón. Su primogénito fue Amnón de Aquinoam Jezraelita.
texts.2sa.3.3: Su segundo fue Queleab de Abigail, la mujer de Nabal, el del Carmelo; el tercero, Absalom, hijo de Maaca, hija de Tolmai rey de Gessur;
texts.2sa.3.4: El cuarto, Adonías, hijo de Haggit; el quinto, Safatias, hijo de Abital;
texts.2sa.3.5: El sexto, Jetraam de Egla mujer de David: estos nacieron a David en Hebrón.
texts.2sa.3.6: Y como había guerra entre la casa de Saul, y la de David, aconteció que Abner se esforzaba por la casa de Saul.
texts.2sa.3.7: Y Saul había tenido una concubina que se llamaba Resfa, hija de Aja: e Is-boset dijo a Abner: ¿Por qué has entrado a la concubina de mi padre?
texts.2sa.3.8: Y Abner se enojó en gran manera por las palabras de Is-boset, y dijo: ¿Soy yo cabeza de los perros de Judá? Yo he hecho hoy misericordia con la casa de Saul tu padre, con sus hermanos, y con sus amigos, y no te he entregado en las manos de David, y tú me has hecho hoy cargo del pecado de una mujer.
texts.2sa.3.9: Así haga Dios a Abner, y así le añada, que como ha jurado Jehová a David, así haga yo con él:
texts.2sa.3.10: Y que yo traspase el reino de la casa de Saul, y confirme la silla de David sobre Israel, y sobre Judá, desde Dan hasta Beer-seba.
texts.2sa.3.11: Y él no pudo responder palabra a Abner porque tenía temor de él.
texts.2sa.3.12: Y envió Abner mensajeros a David de su parte, diciendo: ¿Cúya es la tierra? Y que le dijesen: Haz alianza conmigo, y, he aquí que mi mano será contigo para volver a ti a todo Israel.
texts.2sa.3.13: Y él dijo: Bien. Yo haré contigo alianza: mas una cosa te pido; y es, que no me vengas a ver sin que primero traigas a Micol la hija de Saul, cuando vinieres a verme.
texts.2sa.3.14: Después de esto David envió mensajeros a Is-boset, hijo de Saul, diciendo: Restitúyeme a mi mujer Micol, la cual yo desposé conmigo por cien prepucios de Filisteos.
texts.2sa.3.15: Entonces Is-boset envió, y quitóla a su marido Faltiel, hijo de Lais.
texts.2sa.3.16: Y su marido fue con ella llorando por el camino en pos de ella hasta Bajurim: y Abner le dijo: Anda, vuélvete. Entonces él se volvió.
texts.2sa.3.17: Y habló Abner con los ancianos de Israel, diciendo: Ayer y anteayer procurabais que David fuese rey sobre vosotros;
texts.2sa.3.18: Ahora pues, hacédlo; porque Jehová ha hablado a David, diciendo: Por la mano de mi siervo David libraré a mi pueblo Israel de mano de los Filisteos, y de mano de todos sus enemigos.
texts.2sa.3.19: Y habló también Abner en oídos de Ben-jamín: y también fue Abner a decir a David a Hebrón todo el parecer de los de Israel, y de toda la casa de Ben-jamín.
texts.2sa.3.20: Vino pues Abner a David en Hebrón, y con él veinte hombres: y David hizo banquete a Abner, y a los que con él habían venido.
texts.2sa.3.21: Y dijo Abner a David: Yo me levantaré, e iré, y juntaré a mi señor el rey todo Israel, para que hagan contigo alianza, y tú reines sobre todo lo que desea tu alma. Y David envió a Abner, y él se fue en paz.
texts.2sa.3.22: ¶ Y he aquí los siervos de David y Joab, que venían del campo, y traían consigo gran presa. Y Abner ya no estaba con David en Hebrón, que ya él le había despedido, y él se había ido en paz.
texts.2sa.3.23: Y como Joab y todo el ejército que con él estaba vinieron, fue dado aviso a Joab, diciendo: Abner, hijo de Ner, ha venido al rey: y él le ha enviado, y se fue en paz.
texts.2sa.3.24: Entonces Joab vino al rey, y le dijo: ¿Qué has hecho? He aquí, habíase venido Abner a ti: ¿por qué pues le dejaste que se fuese?
texts.2sa.3.25: ¿Sabes tú que Abner, hijo de Ner, es venido para engañarte, y saber tu salida y tu entrada, y por entender todo lo que tú haces?
texts.2sa.3.26: Y saliéndose Joab de con David, envió mensajeros tras Abner, los cuales le volvieron desde el pozo de Sira, sin saberlo David.
texts.2sa.3.27: Y como Abner volvió a Hebrón, Joab le apartó al medio de la puerta hablando con él blandamente como de secreto, y allí le hirió junto a la quinta costilla por la muerte de Asael su hermano, y murió.
texts.2sa.3.28: Cuando David supo esto después, dijo: Yo soy limpio, y mi reino, delante de Jehová, para siempre, de la sangre de Abner, hijo de Ner:
texts.2sa.3.29: Caiga sobre la cabeza de Joab, y sobre toda la casa de su padre; que nunca falte de la casa de Joab hombre que padezca flujo, ni leproso, ni quien ande con bordón, ni quien muera a cuchillo, ni quien tenga falta de pan.
texts.2sa.3.30: Así que Joab y Abisaí su hermano mataron a Abner, porque él había muerto a Asael hermano de ellos en la batalla en Gabaón.
texts.2sa.3.31: Entonces David dijo a Joab, y a todo el pueblo que con él estaba: Rompéd vuestros vestidos, y ceñíos de sacos, y hacéd llanto delante de Abner: y el rey iba detrás de las andas.
texts.2sa.3.32: Y sepultaron a Abner en Hebrón: y alzando el rey su voz, lloró al sepulcro de Abner: y todo el pueblo también lloró.
texts.2sa.3.33: Y endechando el rey al mismo Abner, decía: ¿Murió Abner como muere el insensato?
texts.2sa.3.34: Tus manos no eran atadas, ni tus pies ligados con grillos. Como los que caen delante de los hijos de iniquidad, así caíste. Y añadieron todo el pueblo a llorar sobre él.
texts.2sa.3.35: Y como todo el pueblo viniese a dar de comer pan a David, siendo aun de día, David juró, diciendo: Así me haga Dios, y así me añada, si antes que se ponga el sol yo gustare pan, o otra cualquiera cosa.
texts.2sa.3.36: Así entendió todo el pueblo, y les plugo en sus ojos; porque todo lo que el rey hacía parecía bien en ojos de todo el pueblo.
texts.2sa.3.37: Y todo el pueblo, y aun todo Israel entendieron aquel día, que no había venido del rey, que Abner, hijo de Ner, muriese.
texts.2sa.3.38: Entonces el rey dijo a sus siervos: ¿No sabéis que ha caído hoy en Israel un príncipe, y grande?
texts.2sa.3.39: Que yo ahora aun soy tierno rey ungido: y estos hombres, los hijos de Sarvia, muy duros me son: Jehová dé el pago al que mal hace, conforme a su malicia.
texts.2sa.4.1: Como el hijo de Saul oyó que Abner había sido muerto en Hebrón, las manos se le descoyuntaron: y todo Israel fue atemorizado.
texts.2sa.4.2: Y tenía el hijo de Saul dos varones, los cuales eran capitanes de compañías: el nombre del uno era Baana, y el del otro era Recab, hijos de Remmón Berotita, de los hijos de Ben-jamín: porque Berot era contada con Ben-jamín.
texts.2sa.4.3: Estos Berotitas se habían huido en Getaim, y habían sido peregrinos allí hasta entonces.
texts.2sa.4.4: Y Jonatán el hijo de Saul tenía un hijo cojo de los pies, de edad de cinco años: que cuando la fama de la muerte de Saul y de Jonatán vino de Jezrael, su ama le tomó, y huyó: y yendo, huyendo de priesa, cayó el niño y quedó cojo: su nombre era Mifiboset.
texts.2sa.4.5: Los hijos de Remmón Berotita, Recab y Baana fueron, y entraron en la mayor calor del día en casa de Is-boset, el cual estaba durmiendo en su cámara la siesta.
texts.2sa.4.6: Y entraron en medio de la casa en hábito de mercaderes de grano, e hiriéronle junto a la quinta costilla, y escapáronse Recab y Baana su hermano.
texts.2sa.4.7: Los cuales como entraron en la casa, estando él en su cama en su cámara de dormir, le hirieron y mataron: y cortáronle la cabeza. Y tomando la cabeza caminaron toda la noche por el camino de la campaña.
texts.2sa.4.8: Y trajeron la cabeza de Is-boset a David en Hebrón, y dijeron al rey: He aquí la cabeza de Is-boset, hijo de Saul, tu enemigo, que procuraba matarte: y Jehová ha vengado hoy a mi señor el rey de Saul, y de su simiente.
texts.2sa.4.9: Y David respondió a Recab y a Baana su hermano, hijos de Remmón Berotita, y díjoles: Vive Jehová, que ha redimido mi alma de toda angustia,
texts.2sa.4.10: Que cuando uno me dio nuevas, diciendo: He aquí, Saul es muerto, el cual pensaba que traía buenas nuevas, yo le tomé, y le maté en Siceleg en premio de la buena nueva.
