texts.2sa.22.19: Los cuales en el día de mi calamidad me tomaron descuidado: mas Jehová fue mi bordón.
texts.2sa.22.20: Sacóme a anchura; me libró, porque puso su voluntad en mí.
texts.2sa.22.21: Pagóme Jehová conforme a mi justicia: y conforme a la limpieza de mis manos me dio la paga.
texts.2sa.22.22: Porque yo guardé los caminos de Jehová: y no me aparté impíamente de mi Dios.
texts.2sa.22.23: Porque delante de mí tengo todas sus ordenanzas: y sus fueros, no me retiraré de ellos.
texts.2sa.22.24: Y fui perfecto con él, y me guardé de mi iniquidad.
texts.2sa.22.25: Y pagóme Jehová conforme a mi justicia: y conforme a mi limpieza delante de sus ojos.
texts.2sa.22.26: Con el bueno eres bueno, y con el valeroso perfecto, eres perfecto.
texts.2sa.22.27: Con el limpio eres limpio: mas con el perverso, eres perverso.
texts.2sa.22.28: Y salvas al pueblo pobre: mas tus ojos, sobre los altivos, para abatirlos.
texts.2sa.22.29: Porque tú eres mi lámpara, oh Jehová: Jehová da luz a mis tinieblas.
texts.2sa.22.30: Porque en ti romperé ejércitos, y en mi Dios saltaré las murallas.
texts.2sa.22.31: Dios, perfecto su camino: la palabra de Jehová purificada, escudo es de todos los que en él esperan.
texts.2sa.22.32: Porque ¿qué Dios hay sino Jehová? ¿O quién es fuerte sino nuestro Dios?
texts.2sa.22.33: Dios es el que con virtud me corrobora, y el que escombra mi camino.
texts.2sa.22.34: El que hace mis pies como de ciervas, y el que me asienta en mis alturas.
texts.2sa.22.35: El que enseña mis manos para la pelea: y el que da que yo quiebre con mis brazos el arco de acero.
texts.2sa.22.36: Tú me diste el escudo de tu salud, y tu benignidad me ha multiplicado.
texts.2sa.22.37: Tú ensanchaste mis pasos debajo de mí, para que no titubeasen mis rodillas.
texts.2sa.22.38: Perseguiré mis enemigos, y quebrantarlos he, y no me volveré hasta que los acabe.
texts.2sa.22.39: Consumirlos he, y herirlos he; que no se levantarán. Y caerán debajo de mis pies.
texts.2sa.22.40: Ceñísteme de fortaleza para la batalla, y postraste debajo de mí los que contra mí se levantaron.
texts.2sa.22.41: Tú me diste la cerviz de mis enemigos, de mis aborrecedores, y que yo los talase.
texts.2sa.22.42: Miraron, y no hubo quien los librase; a Jehová, mas no les respondió.
texts.2sa.22.43: Yo los quebrantaré como a polvo de la tierra: como a lodo de las plazas los desmenuzaré, y los disiparé.
texts.2sa.22.44: Tú me libraste de contiendas de pueblos: tú me guardaste para que fuese cabeza de gentes: pueblos que no conocía, me sirvieron.
texts.2sa.22.45: Los extraños titubeaban a mí; en oyendo me obedecían.
texts.2sa.22.46: Los extraños se desleían, y temblaban en sus encerramientos.
texts.2sa.22.47: Viva Jehová, y sea bendita mi roca: sea ensalzado el Dios, que es la roca de mi salvamento.
texts.2sa.22.48: El Dios, que me ha dado venganzas, y sujeta los pueblos debajo de mí,
texts.2sa.22.49: Que me saca de entre mis enemigos: tú me sacaste en alto de entre los que se levantaron contra mí: librásteme del varón de iniquidades.
texts.2sa.22.50: Por tanto yo te confesaré en las gentes, oh Jehová, y cantaré a tu nombre.
texts.2sa.22.51: El que engrandece las saludes de su rey: y el que hace misericordia a su ungido David, y a su simiente para siempre.
texts.2sa.23.1: Estas son las postreras palabras de David. Dijo David hijo de Isaí: y dijo aquel varón que fue levantado alto, el ungido del Dios de Jacob, el suave en cánticos de Israel:
texts.2sa.23.2: El Espíritu de Jehová ha hablado por mí, y su palabra ha sido en mi lengua.
texts.2sa.23.3: El Dios de Israel me ha dictado: El Fuerte de Israel habló: Señoreador de los hombres, justo señoreador en temor de Dios.
texts.2sa.23.4: ¶ Y como la luz de la mañana cuando sale el sol, de la mañana sin nubes resplandeciente, cuando cae lluvia sobre la yerba de la tierra:
texts.2sa.23.5: No será así mi casa para con Dios: mas él ha hecho conmigo concierto perpetuo, ordenado en todas las cosas y seguro; por lo cual a toda mi salud, y a toda mi voluntad no así hará producir.
texts.2sa.23.6: Mas los hijos de Belial serán como espinas arrancadas todos ellos, las cuales nadie toma con la mano:
texts.2sa.23.7: Mas el que quiere tocar en ellas, ármase de hierro, y de una asta de lanza, y son quemadas en su lugar.
texts.2sa.23.8: ¶ Estos son los nombres de los varones valientes que tuvo David. El que se asentó en cátedra de sabiduría, principal de los tres, Adino Hesneo, que una vez fue sobre ochocientos muertos.
texts.2sa.23.9: Después de este fue Eleazar, hijo de Dodo, hijo de Ahohi, entre los tres valientes que estaban con David, cuando desafiaron a los Filisteos, que se habían juntado allí a la batalla, cuando subieron los de Israel.
texts.2sa.23.10: Este levantándose hirió a los Filisteos hasta que su mano se cansó, y quedó su mano pegada a la espada. Aquel día Jehová hizo gran salud, y el pueblo se volvió en pos de él solamente a tomar el despojo.
texts.2sa.23.11: Después de este fue Samma, hijo de Age, Arareo: Que habiéndose juntado los Filisteos en una aldea, había allí una suerte de tierra llena de lentejas, y el pueblo había huido delante de los Filisteos:
texts.2sa.23.12: Este entonces se paró en medio de la suerte de tierra, y defendióla, e hirió a los Filisteos, y Jehová hizo una gran salud.
texts.2sa.23.13: Estos tres que eran de los treinta principales, descendieron y vinieron en tiempo de la siega a David a la cueva de Odollam: y el campo de los Filisteos estaba en el valle de Rafaim.
texts.2sa.23.14: David entonces estaba en la fortaleza, y la guarnición de los Filisteos estaba en Belén.
texts.2sa.23.15: Y David tuvo deseo, y dijo: ¡Quién me diera de beber del agua de la cisterna de Belén, que está a la puerta!
texts.2sa.23.16: Entonces estos tres valientes rompieron en el campo de los Filisteos, y sacaron del agua de la cisterna de Belén, que estaba a la puerta, y tomaron, y trajéronla a David: mas él no la quiso beber, sino derramóla a Jehová, diciendo:
texts.2sa.23.17: Lejos sea de mí, oh Jehová, que yo haga esto. ¿La sangre de los varones que fueron por ella con peligro de su vida tengo de beber? Y no quiso beber de ella. Estos tres valientes hicieron esto.
texts.2sa.23.18: Y Abisaí hermano de Joab, hijo de Sarvia, fue el principal de tres: el cual alzó su lanza contra trescientos, los cuales mató, y tuvo nombre entre los tres.
texts.2sa.23.19: El fue el más noble de los tres, y el primero de ellos, mas no llegó a los tres primeros.
texts.2sa.23.20: Banaías, hijo de Joiada, hijo de un varón esforzado, grande en hechos, de Cabseel. Este hirió dos leones de Moab. Y él mismo descendió, e hirió un león en medio del foso en el tiempo de la nieve.
texts.2sa.23.21: Y el mismo hirió a un Egipcio, hombre de grande estatura; y el Egipcio tenía una lanza en su mano: y él descendió a él con un palo, y arrebató al Egipcio la lanza de la mano, y con su misma lanza le mató.
texts.2sa.23.22: Esto hizo Banaías, hijo de Joiada, y tuvo nombre entre los tres valientes.
texts.2sa.23.23: De los treinta fue el más noble; mas no llegó a los tres primeros. Y púsole David en su consejo.
texts.2sa.23.24: Asael hermano de Joab fue de los treinta: Elhanán, hijo de Dodo, de Belén:
texts.2sa.23.25: Semma de Harodi: Elica de Harodi.
texts.2sa.23.26: Heles de Falti: Ira, hijo de Acces, de Tecua:
texts.2sa.23.27: Abiezer de Anatot: Mobonnai de Husa:
texts.2sa.23.28: Selmón de Ahoh: Majarai de Netofat:
texts.2sa.23.29: Heleb, hijo de Baana de Netofat: Itai, hijo de Ribai, de Gabaat, de los hijos de Ben-jamín:
texts.2sa.23.30: Banaia de Faraton: Heddai del arroyo de Gaas:
texts.2sa.23.31: Abi-albón de Arbat: Azmavet de Barumi:
texts.2sa.23.32: Eliaba, de Salaboni. Los hijos de Jasén, Jonatán:
texts.2sa.23.33: Semma de Orori: Ahiam, hijo de Sarar, de Arar:
texts.2sa.23.34: Elifelet, hijo de Aasbai, hijo de Macati: Eliam, hijo de Aquitofel, de Gelon:
texts.2sa.23.35: Hesrai de Carmelo: Farai de Arbi:
texts.2sa.23.36: Igaal, hijo de Natán, de Soba: Bani de Gadi:
texts.2sa.23.37: Selec de Ammón: Naharai de Berot, escudero de Joab, hijo de Sarvia:
texts.2sa.23.38: Ira de Jetri: Gareb de Jetri:
texts.2sa.23.39: Urías Jetteo: todos treinta y siete.
texts.2sa.24.1: Y volvió el furor de Jehová a enojarse contra Israel, e incitó a David contra ellos a que dijese: Vé, cuenta a Israel, y a Judá.
texts.2sa.24.2: Y dijo el rey a Joab general del ejército que tenía consigo: Rodea todas las tribus de Israel, desde Dan hasta Beer-seba, y contád el pueblo, para que yo sepa el número del pueblo.
texts.2sa.24.3: Y Joab respondió al rey: Añada Jehová tu Dios al pueblo cien veces tantos como son, y que lo vea mi señor el rey; mas ¿para qué quiere esto mi señor el rey?
texts.2sa.24.4: Empero la palabra del rey pudo más que Joab, y que los capitanes del ejército: y salió Joab, de delante del rey con los capitanes del ejército, para ir a contar el pueblo de Israel.
texts.2sa.24.5: Y pasando el Jordán asentaron en Aroer, a la mano derecha de la ciudad que está en medio del arroyo de Gad, y junto a Jazer.
texts.2sa.24.6: Y después vinieron a Galaad, y a la tierra baja de Hodsi; y de allí vinieron a Danjaán, y al rededor de Sidón.
texts.2sa.24.7: Y vinieron a la fortaleza de Tiro, y a todas las ciudades de los Heveos, y de los Cananeos, y salieron al mediodía de Judá a Beer-seba.
texts.2sa.24.8: Y después que hubieron andado toda la tierra, volvieron a Jerusalem después de nueve meses y veinte días.
texts.2sa.24.9: Y Joab dio la cuenta del número del pueblo al rey: y fueron los de Israel ochocientos mil hombres fuertes, que sacaban espada: y de los de Judá fueron quinientos mil hombres.
texts.2sa.24.10: Y después que David hubo contado el pueblo, hirióle su corazón, y dijo David a Jehová: Yo he pecado gravemente por haber hecho esto; mas ahora Jehová, ruégote que traspases el pecado de tu siervo; porque yo he obrado muy neciamente.
texts.2sa.24.11: Y por la mañana cuando David se levantaba, fue palabra de Jehová a Gad profeta, vidente de David, diciendo:
texts.2sa.24.12: Vé, y habla a David: Así dijo Jehová: Tres cosas te ofrezco: tú te escogerás de estas la una, la cual yo haga.
texts.2sa.24.13: Y Gad vino a David, y denuncióle, y díjole: ¿Quiéres que te vengan siete años de hambre en tu tierra? ¿O que huyas tres meses delante de tus enemigos, y que ellos te persigan? ¿O que tres días haya pestilencia en tu tierra? Piensa ahora, y mira que responderé al que me envió.
texts.2sa.24.14: Entonces David dijo a Gad: En grande angustia estoy. Yo ruego que yo caiga en la mano de Jehová, porque sus miseraciones son muchas, y que yo no caiga en manos de hombres.
texts.2sa.24.15: Y Jehová envió pestilencia en Israel desde la mañana hasta el tiempo señalado: y murieron del pueblo, desde Dan hasta Beer-seba, setenta mil hombres.
texts.2sa.24.16: Y como el ángel extendió su mano sobre Jerusalem para destruirla, Jehová se arrepintió de aquel mal, y dijo al ángel que destruía el pueblo. Basta ahora: detén tu mano. Entonces el ángel de Jehová estaba junto a la era de Areuna Jebuseo.
texts.2sa.24.17: ¶ Y David dijo a Jehová, cuando vio al ángel que hería al pueblo: Yo pequé, yo hice la maldad: ¿Estas ovejas qué hicieron? Ruégote que tu mano se torne contra mí, y contra la casa de mi padre.
texts.2sa.24.18: Y Gad vino a David aquel día, y díjole: Sube, y haz un altar a Jehová en la era de Areuna Jebuseo.
texts.2sa.24.19: Y David subió conforme al dicho de Gad, que Jehová había mandado.
texts.2sa.24.20: Y mirando Areuna, vio al rey y a sus siervos que pasaban a él: y saliendo Areuna inclinóse delante del rey hacia tierra.
texts.2sa.24.21: Y dijo Areuna: ¿Por qué viene mi señor el rey a su siervo? Y David respondió: Para comprar de ti esta era para edificar en ella altar a Jehová, y que la mortandad cese del pueblo.
texts.2sa.24.22: Y Areuna dijo a David: Tome y sacrifique mi señor el rey lo que bien le pareciere. He aquí bueyes para el holocausto, y trillos, y otros aderezos de bueyes para leña.
texts.2sa.24.23: Todo lo da, como un rey, Areuna al rey: Y dijo Areuna al rey: Jehová tu Dios te sea propicio.
texts.2sa.24.24: Y el rey dijo a Areuna: No, sino por precio te lo compraré: porque no ofreceré a Jehová mi Dios holocaustos por nada. Entonces David compró la era y los bueyes por cincuenta siclos de plata.
texts.2sa.24.25: Y edificó allí David un altar a Jehová, y sacrificó holocaustos, y pacíficos, y Jehová se aplacó con la tierra, y cesó la plaga de Israel.

texts.2sa.1.1: And so it was, after the death of Saul, when David had returned from the smiting of the Amalekites, and David had abode in Ziklag two days,
texts.2sa.1.2: yea so it was, on the third day, that lo! a man came out of the camp, from Saul, with his clothes rent, and earth upon his head,—and so it was, when he came in unto David, that he fell to the earth, and did homage.
texts.2sa.1.3: And David said unto him, From whence comest thou? And he said unto him, Out of the camp of Israel, am I escaped.
texts.2sa.1.4: And David said unto him—How turned out the matter? tell me, I pray thee. And he said—The people have fled from the battle, yea moreover, many, of the people have fallen, and died, Yea moreover, Saul, and Jonathan his son, are dead.
texts.2sa.1.5: Then said David unto the young man who was telling him,—How knowest thou that Saul and Jonathan his son are dead?
texts.2sa.1.6: And the young man who was telling him said, It, so happened, that I was on Mount Gilboa, when lo! Saul, leaning upon his spear, and lo! the chariots and horsemen, hotly pursued him;
texts.2sa.1.7: so he turned behind him, and saw me,—and cried out unto me, and I said, Behold me!
texts.2sa.1.8: And he said unto me, Who art thou? And I said unto him, An Amalekite, am I.
texts.2sa.1.9: And he said unto me, I pray thee, take thy stand by me, and put me to death, for the cramp hath seized me,—even for as long as my life shall be in me.
texts.2sa.1.10: So I took my stand by him, and put him to death, for I perceived that he could not survive his fall,—so I took the crown that was on his head, and the bracelet that was on his arm, and have brought them in unto my lord, here.
texts.2sa.1.11: Then David took hold of his clothes, and rent them,—yea moreover, [so did] all the men who were with him.
texts.2sa.1.12: And they lamented aloud, and wept, and fasted until the evening,—for Saul, and for Jonathan his son, and for the people of Yahweh, and for the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.
texts.2sa.1.13: And David said unto the young man who was telling him, Whence art thou? And he said, Son of a sojourner—an Amalekite, am I.
texts.2sa.1.14: And David said unto him,—How wast thou not afraid to thrust forth thy hand, to destroy the Anointed of Yahweh?
texts.2sa.1.15: So David called one of the young men, and said,—Go near—fall upon him. And he smote him, that he died.
texts.2sa.1.16: And David said unto him, Thy blood, be upon thine own head,—for, thine own mouth, hath testified against thee, saying, I myself, put to death the Anointed of Yahweh.
texts.2sa.1.17: Then chanted David this dirge,—over Saul and over Jonathan his son;
texts.2sa.1.18: and he thought to teach the sons of Judah [the song of] the Bow,—lo! it is written in the Book of the Upright:—
texts.2sa.1.19: The beauty of Israel! on thy high plumes—slain! How have fallen—the mighty!
texts.2sa.1.20: Do not tell it in Gath, Do not publish it in the streets of Ashkelon,—lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the Uncircumcised triumph.
texts.2sa.1.21: Ye mountains in Gilboa! Be there neither dew nor rain upon you, nor fields of offerings,—for, there, were cast away, the shields of the mighty, The shield of Saul, unanointed with oil.
texts.2sa.1.22: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan ne’er drew back,—and, the sword of Saul, ne’er returned, empty.
texts.2sa.1.23: Saul and Jonathan, delightfully loving in their lives, even, in their death, were not divided,—Beyond eagles, were they swift, beyond lions, were they strong!
texts.2sa.1.24: Ye daughters of Israel! For Saul, weep ye,—who clothed you in crimson, [decked] with lovely things, who hung ornaments of gold on your apparel!
texts.2sa.1.25: How have fallen the mighty, in the midst of the battle! Jonathan, on thy high places, slain!
texts.2sa.1.26: I am distressed for thee, my brother, Jonathan! Delightful to me, exceedingly,—Wonderful, was thy love to me, passing the love of women.
texts.2sa.1.27: How have fallen the mighty, and perished the weapons of war!
texts.2sa.2.1: And it came to pass, after this, that David enquired of Yahweh, saying—Shall I go up into one of the cities of Judah? And Yahweh said unto him, Go up. And David said—Whither shall I go up? And he said—Unto Hebron.
texts.2sa.2.2: So David went up thither, and his two wives also,—Ahinoam, the Jezreelitess, and Abigail, wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
texts.2sa.2.3: His men also who were with him, did David bring up, every man with his household,—and they dwelt in the cities of Hebron.
texts.2sa.2.4: Then came the men of Judah, and anointed David there, to be king over the house of Judah. And they told David, saying, Men of Jabesh-gilead, were they who buried Saul.
texts.2sa.2.5: So David sent messengers unto the men of Jabesh-gilead,—and said unto them—Blessed, be ye of Yahweh, that ye did this lovingkindness unto your lord, unto Saul, and buried him.
texts.2sa.2.6: Now, therefore, Yahweh requite you with lovingkindness and truth,—moreover also, I, will requite you, for this noble deed, in that ye did this thing.
texts.2sa.2.7: Now, therefore, let your hands be made firm, and become ye sons of valour, for your lord Saul is dead,—and, me, moreover have the house of Judah anointed, to be king over them.
texts.2sa.2.8: But, Abner son of Ner, prince of the host that pertained unto Saul, took Ish-bosheth, son of Saul, and brought him over to Mahanaim;
texts.2sa.2.9: and made him king for Gilead, and for the Ashurites, and for Jezreel,—and over Ephraim, and over Benjamin, and over, all Israel.
texts.2sa.2.10: Forty years old, was Ish-bosheth son of Saul, when he began to reign over Israel, and, two years, reigned he,—but, the house of Judah, followed David.
texts.2sa.2.11: And it came to pass, that, the number of the days that David was king in Hebron, over the house of Judah, was seven years and six months.
texts.2sa.2.12: And Abner son of Ner, and the servants of Ish-bosheth, son of Saul, came out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.
texts.2sa.2.13: And, Joab son of Zeruiah, and the servants of David, went out from Hebron and met, by the pool of Gibeon, together, —and they sat down, these, by the pool, on the one side, and, those, by the pool, on the other side.
texts.2sa.2.14: Then said Abner unto Joab, Let the young men arise, I pray thee, and make sport before us. And Joab said—Let them arise.
texts.2sa.2.15: Then there arose, and went over by number,—twelve of Benjamin, pertaining to Ish-bosheth, son of Saul, and twelve, of the servants of David.
texts.2sa.2.16: And they caught every one his fellow by the head, with his sword in his fellow’s side, so they fell, together,—and that place was called Helkath-hazzadim ["Field of Plotters"], which is in Gideon.
texts.2sa.2.17: So the battle became exceeding obstinate, on that day,—and Abner and the men of Israel were defeated before the servants of David.
texts.2sa.2.18: Now there were there, three sons of Zeruiah, Joab, and Abishai, and Asahel,—and, Asahel, was light of foot as a wild gazelle.
texts.2sa.2.19: And Asahel pursued Abner,—and turned not, in going, to the right hand or to the left, from pursuing Abner.
texts.2sa.2.20: Then Abner looked behind him, and said—Art thou Asahel? And he said—I am.
texts.2sa.2.21: Then Abner said to him—Turn thee aside, to thy right hand, or to thy left, and lay thee hold on one of the young men, and take thee his armour. But Asahel would not turn aside from pursuing him.
texts.2sa.2.22: And Abner said, yet again, unto Asahel, Turn thee aside from pursuing me,—wherefore should I smite thee to the earth? how then should I lift up my face unto Joab, thy brother?
texts.2sa.2.23: Howbeit he refused to turn aside, wherefore Abner smote him with the hinder end of the spear, in the belly, that the spear came out behind him, and he fell there, and died on the spot,—and so it was, that, as many as came up to the place where Asahel fell and died, stood still.
texts.2sa.2.24: Then Joab and Abishai pursued Abner,—but, the sun, had gone in by the time, they, had come as far as the hill of Ammah, that overlooketh Giah, by way of the wilderness of Gibeon.
texts.2sa.2.25: And, when the sons of Benjamin had gathered themselves together after Abner, and become one band,—and had taken their stand on the top of a certain hill,
texts.2sa.2.26: then Abner cried aloud unto Joab, and said—To the uttermost, must the sword devour? Dost thou not well know that, bitter, shall it be, in the latter end? How long, then, wilt thou not bid the people turn back from pursuing their own brethren?
texts.2sa.2.27: Then said Joab—As God liveth, surely, if thou hadst not spoken, then in the morning, the people would of themselves have gone up, every man from pursuing his brother.
texts.2sa.2.28: So Joab blew with the horn, and all the people stood still, and they neither pursued Israel further,—nor fought any more.
texts.2sa.2.29: And, Abner and his men, journeyed through the waste plain all that night,—and crossed the Jordan, and went through all the Bithron, and entered Mahanaim.
texts.2sa.2.30: And, Joab, returned from pursuing Abner, and, when he had gathered together all the people, there were missing of the servants of David—nineteen men, and Asahel;
texts.2sa.2.31: but, the servants of David, had smitten of Benjamin, of the men of Abner,—[so that] three hundred and sixty men, had died.
texts.2sa.2.32: And they carried Asahel, and buried him in the grave of his father, which was in Bethlehem,—and Joab and his men journeyed all the night, and had daylight in Hebron.
texts.2sa.3.1: And the war between the house of Saul and the house of David was prolonged,—and, David, waxed stronger and stronger, and, the house of Saul, became weaker and weaker.
texts.2sa.3.2: And there were born unto David, sons, in Hebron,—and it came to press that—His firstborn was Amnon, by Ahinoam, the Jezreelitess;
texts.2sa.3.3: And his second Chileab, by Abigail, wife of Nabal the Carmelite, And the third Absolom, son of Maachah, daughter of Talmai, king of Geshur;
texts.2sa.3.4: And the fourth Adonijah, son of Higgith,—And the fifth Shephatiah, son of Abital;
texts.2sa.3.5: And the sixth Ithream, by Eglah wife of David. These, were born unto David, in Hebron.
texts.2sa.3.6: And it came to pass, while the war continued between the house of Saul and the house of David, that, Abner, shewed himself courageous for the house of Saul.
texts.2sa.3.7: Now, Saul, had a concubine, whose name, was Rizpah daughter of Aiah,—and [Ish-bosheth] said unto Abner, Why, wentest thou in, unto my father’s concubine?
texts.2sa.3.8: And it provoked Abner greatly, on account of the words of Ish-bosheth, and he said—Am I, the head of the dogs, that pertain unto Judah? To-day, would I deal in lovingkindness with the house of Saul thy father, towards his brethren, and towards his friends, and have not delivered thee into the hand of David,—and yet thou hast charged upon me the transgression of the woman, today.
texts.2sa.3.9: So, may God do unto Abner, and, so, may he add to him,—if, as Yahweh hath sworn unto David, even so, I deal not with him;
texts.2sa.3.10: by turning over the kingdom from the house of Saul,—and establishing the throne of David, over Israel and over Judah, from Dan, even unto Beer-sheba.
texts.2sa.3.11: And he could no further answer Abner, a word,—because he feared him.
texts.2sa.3.12: So Abner sent messengers unto David, on the spot, saying—Whose, is the land? Saying [also] —Solemnise thy covenant with me; and lo! my hand, shall be with thee, to bring round unto thee, all Israel.
texts.2sa.3.13: And he said—Good! I, will solemnise with thee a covenant,—but, one thing, must I ask of thee, saying—Thou shalt not see my face, except thou have brought in Michal, Saul’s daughter, when thou comest to see my face.
texts.2sa.3.14: And David sent messengers unto Ish-bosheth son of Saul, saying,—Give up my wife, Michal, whom I espoused to myself, for a hundred foreskins of Philistines.
texts.2sa.3.15: So Ish-bosheth sent and took her from her husband,—from Paltiel, son of Laish.
texts.2sa.3.16: And her husband went along with her, weeping as he went behind her, as far as Behurim,—when Abner said unto him—Go, return. And he returned.
texts.2sa.3.17: Then had Abner, speech, with the elders of Israel, saying,—In times past, ye were seeking David, to be king over you.
texts.2sa.3.18: Now, therefore, act,—for Yahweh, spake unto David, saying, By the hand of David my servant, will I save my people Israel, out of the hand of the Philistines, and out of the hand of all their enemies.
texts.2sa.3.19: And Abner also spake in the ears of Benjamin, —and Abner also went to speak in the ears of David, in Hebron, all that was pleasing in the eyes of Israel, and in the eyes of all the house of Benjamin.
texts.2sa.3.20: So, when Abner came in unto David, in Hebron, and, with him, twenty men, David made, for Abner, and for the men who were with him, a banquet.
texts.2sa.3.21: Then said Abner unto David—I will verily arise and go, and gather together unto my lord the king, all Israel—that they may solemnise with thee a covenant, so shalt thou reign over all that thy soul desireth. And David let Abner go, and he departed in peace.
texts.2sa.3.22: And lo! the servants of David, and Joab, came in from a raid, and, great spoil, brought they in with them; but, Abner, was not with David in Hebron, for he had let him go, and he had departed in peace.
texts.2sa.3.23: When, Joab, and all the host that was with him, had come in, then told they Joab, saying, Abner son of Ner hath been in unto the king, and he hath let him go, and he hath departed in peace.
texts.2sa.3.24: Then Joab came in unto the king, and said—What hast thou done? Lo! Abner came in unto thee. Wherefore is it that thou didst let him go, so that he is clean departed?
texts.2sa.3.25: Thou knowest Abner son of Ner, that, to deceive thee, he came,—and to take knowledge of thy going out, and thy coming in, and to take knowledge of all that thou art doing.
texts.2sa.3.26: And, when Joab had come out from David, he sent messengers after Abner, and brought him back from the well of Sirah,—but, David, knew it not.
texts.2sa.3.27: So Abner returned to Hebron, and Joab took him aside into the midst of the gate, to speak with him quietly,—and then smote him there, in the belly, that he died, for the blood of Asahel the brother of Joab.
texts.2sa.3.28: And, when David heard of it, after that, he said—Guiltless, am I and my kingdom before Yahweh, unto times age-abiding,—of the blood of Abner son of Ner.
texts.2sa.3.29: Let it be hurled upon the head of Joab, and against all his father’s house,—and let there not fail from the house of Joab—one that hath an issue, or a leper, or one that leaneth on a crutch, or that falleth by the sword, or that lacketh bread.
texts.2sa.3.30: Thus, Joab and Abishai his brother, slew Abner,—because he had caused the death of Asahel their brother, in Gibeon, in the battle.
texts.2sa.3.31: And David said unto Joab, and unto all the people who were with him,—Rend your clothes, and gird you with sackcloth, and lament aloud before Abner. And, King David himself, was following the bier.
texts.2sa.3.32: And they buried Abner in Hebron,—and the king lifted up his voice and wept, at the grave of Abner, and all the people wept.
texts.2sa.3.33: And the king addressed his dirge unto Abner, and said,—As a base man dieth, should Abner have died?
texts.2sa.3.34: Thy hands, were not bound, And, thy feet, near to fetters, were not brought, As one falleth before assassins, so didst thou fall! And again all the people wept over him.
texts.2sa.3.35: And, when all the people came near to get David to eat bread, while yet it was day, David sware, saying—So, let God do to me, and, so, let him add, if, before the sun go in, I taste bread, or anything else.
texts.2sa.3.36: And, all the people, took note of it, and it was noble in their eyes,—as, all that the king did, was, in the eyes of all the people, noble.
texts.2sa.3.37: So then all the people, and all Israel, took note, that day, that it was not of the king, to cause the death of Abner son of Ner.
texts.2sa.3.38: And the king said unto his servants,—Will ye not take note that, a prince and a great man, hath fallen this day, in Israel?
texts.2sa.3.39: And, I myself, this day, am weak, though anointed king, but, these men, the sons of Zeruiah, are more severe than I: Yahweh repay, the doer of wickedness, according to his wickedness.
texts.2sa.4.1: Now, when Ish-bosheth son of Saul heard that Abner had died in Hebron, his hands became feeble,—and, all Israel, were dismayed.
texts.2sa.4.2: And two men, captains of bands, pertained to Ish-bosheth son of Saul—the name of the one, was Baanah, and, the name of the other, Rechab—sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, of the sons of Benjamin,—for, even Beeroth, used to be reckoned unto Benjamin;
texts.2sa.4.3: and the Beerothites fled to Gittaim,—and have been sojourners there, until this day.
texts.2sa.4.4: And, Jonathan, son of Saul, had a son, lame of his feet,—five years old, was he, when tidings came in of Saul and Jonathan from Jezreel, so his nurse took him up, and fled, and it came to pass, when she started up to flee, that he fell and was lamed, and, his name, was, Mephibosheth.
texts.2sa.4.5: So then the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, took their journey and came in, about the heat of the day, unto the house of Ish-bosheth,—when, he, was lying on his noonday couch;
texts.2sa.4.6: and, thither, entered they as fro as the middle of the house, to fetch wheat, and they smote him in the belly,—and, Rechab and Baanah his brother, escaped.
texts.2sa.4.7: Thus they entered the house when, he, was lying on his bed, in his sleeping-chamber, and smote him, and slew him, and beheaded him,—and took his head, and journeyed by way of the waste plain all the night;
texts.2sa.4.8: and brought in the head of Ish-bosheth unto David, at Hebron, and said unto the king, Lo! the head of Ish-bosheth son of Saul, thine enemy, who sought thy life: so hath Yahweh given to my lord the king, avengement this day, on Saul and on his seed.
texts.2sa.4.9: Then David responded to Rechab and Baanah his brother, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said unto them,—By the life of Yahweh, who hath redeemed my soul out of all distress,
texts.2sa.4.10: when he that brought tidings to me, saying, Lo! Saul is dead, though, he, was as one that bringeth good tidings, in his own eyes, yet I seized him, and slew him in Ziklag,—which was how I gave him reward for his tidings:
texts.2sa.4.11: how much more, when, lawless men, have slain a righteous person, in his own house, upon his bed? …Now, therefore, must I not require his blood at your hands, and so consume you, out of the earth?
texts.2sa.4.12: David therefore commanded the young men, and they slew them, and cut off their hands, and their feet, and hanged them up over the pool, in Hebron,—but, the head of Ish-bosheth, took they, and buried in the grave of Abner, in Hebron.
texts.2sa.5.1: Then came all the tribes of Israel unto David, in Hebron,—and spake, saying—Behold us! thy bone and thy flesh, we are.
texts.2sa.5.2: Also, in time past, when Saul was king over us, thou, wast he that led out and brought in, Israel,—and Yahweh said to thee—Thou, shalt be shepherd unto my people, Israel, and, thou, shalt become leader over Israel.
texts.2sa.5.3: So all the elders of Israel came unto the king, in Hebron, and King David solemnised to them a covenant in Hebron, before Yahweh, —and they anointed David to be king over Israel.
texts.2sa.5.4: Thirty years old, was David when he began to reign,—forty years, he reigned:
texts.2sa.5.5: in Hebron, reigned he over Judah, seven years, and six months,—and, in Jerusalem, reigned he thirty and three years, over all Israel and Judah.
texts.2sa.5.6: Then went the king and his men, to Jerusalem, against the Jebusites, inhabiting the land,—and they spake to David, saying—Thou canst not come in hither, unless thou take away the blind and lame—Thinking, David will not come in hither.
texts.2sa.5.7: So then David captured the citadel of Zion,—the same, is the city of David.
texts.2sa.5.8: And David said, on that day—Whosoever is smiting the Jebusites, then let him reach as far as the aqueduct. But, as for the lame and the blind, they were the hated of David’s soul,—for which cause, they kept on saying, Blind and lame! he will not enter the place.
texts.2sa.5.9: So then David dwelt in the citadel, and called it, The City of David,—and David built round about, from Millo and inwards.
texts.2sa.5.10: And David went on and on waxing great,—Yahweh, God of hosts, being with him.
texts.2sa.5.11: Then Hiram, king of Tyre, sent messengers unto David, with cedar-wood, and carpenters, and masons, and they built a house for David.
texts.2sa.5.12: So David perceived that Yahweh had established him to be king over Israel,—and that he had exalted his kingdom, for the sake of his people Israel.
texts.2sa.5.13: And David took him yet more concubines and wives, out of Jerusalem, after he had come from Hebron, and there were, yet further, born unto David, sons and daughters.
texts.2sa.5.14: Now, these, are the names of the sons who were born unto him in Jerusalem,—Shammua and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon;
texts.2sa.5.15: and Ibhar and Elishua and Nepheg and Yaphia;
texts.2sa.5.16: and Elishama and Eliada, and Eliphalet.
texts.2sa.5.17: And, when the Philistine heard that they had anointed David to be king over Israel, then came up all the Philistines to seek to secure David, and David heard of it, and went down into the citadel.
texts.2sa.5.18: Now, the Philistines, had come,—and had spread themselves out in the vale of Rephaim.
texts.2sa.5.19: So then David enquired of Yahweh, saying,—Shall I go up against the Philistines? Wilt thou deliver them into my hand? And Yahweh said unto David—Go up; for I, will surely deliver, the Philistines into thy hand.
texts.2sa.5.20: And David entered Baal-perazim, and David smote them there, and said—Yahweh hath broken forth upon mine enemies, before me, like a breaking forth of waters. For this cause, called he the name of that place, Baal-perazim.
texts.2sa.5.21: And they left their images there,—and David and his men took them away.
texts.2sa.5.22: And, yet again, did the Philistines come up, —and they spread themselves out in the vale of Rephaim.
texts.2sa.5.23: So David enquired of Yahweh, and he said—Thou shalt not go up,—Get round behind them, and come in upon them, over against the mulberry-trees.
texts.2sa.5.24: And it shall be, when thou shalt hear a sound of marching in the tops of the mulberry-trees, then, shalt thou act with decision,—for, then, will Yahweh have gone forth before thee, to smite the host of the Philistines.
texts.2sa.5.25: And David did so, as Yahweh had commanded him,—and smote the Philistines, from Gibeon until thou enterest Gezer.
texts.2sa.6.1: And David, once more, gathered together all the choice young men in Israel, thirty thousand.
texts.2sa.6.2: Then David, and all the people that were with him, arose and went beyond Baale Judah,—to bring up from thence, the ark of God, the name whereof is called by the name of Yahweh of hosts, who inhabiteth the cherubim thereupon.
texts.2sa.6.3: So they carried the ark of God in a new waggon, and brought it out of the house of Abinadab, who was in Gibeah,—and, Uzza and Ahio, sons of Abinadab, were driving the new waggon.
texts.2sa.6.4: So they brought it out of the house of Abinadab, which was in Gibeah, with the ark of God,—and, Ahio, was going before the ark.
texts.2sa.6.5: And, David and all the house of Israel, were dancing for joy before Yahweh, with all boldness and with songs,—and with lyres, and with harps, and with timbrels, and with sistrums, and with cymbals.
texts.2sa.6.6: And, when they came as far as the threshing-floor of Nachon, Uzzah thrust forth his hand unto the ark of God, and took hold of it, for the oxen were restive.
texts.2sa.6.7: Then was kindled the anger of Yahweh, against Uzzah, and God smote him there, for the error,—so that he died there, by the ark of God.
texts.2sa.6.8: And it was a sadness unto David, for that Yahweh had broken in with a breach against Uzzah,—therefore called he that place, Perez-uzzah [as it is called] until this day.
texts.2sa.6.9: And David was afraid of Yahweh, on that day,—and said, How can the ark of Yahweh come unto me?
texts.2sa.6.10: So David would not remove unto him the ark of Yahweh, unto the city of David,—but David took it aside to the house of Obed-edom, the Gittite.
texts.2sa.6.11: And the ark of Yahweh abode in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite, three months,—and Yahweh blessed Obed -edom, and all his household.
texts.2sa.6.12: And it was told King David, saying, Yahweh hath blessed the household of Obed-edom, and all that he hath, because of the ark of God. David therefore went and brought up the ark of God, out of the house of Obed-edom, unto the city of David, with rejoicing.
texts.2sa.6.13: And so it was that, when they who bare the ark of Yahweh had stepped forward six paces, he sacrificed an ox and a heifer.
texts.2sa.6.14: And, David, was dancing with all boldness before Yahweh,—David, being girt with an ephod of linen.
texts.2sa.6.15: So, David and all the house of Israel, were bringing up the ark of Yahweh,—with triumphant shoutings, and with the sound of a horn.
texts.2sa.6.16: Now it so came about that, when the ark of Yahweh entered the city of David, Michal Saul’s daughter, looked out through the window, and saw King David, leaping and dancing before Yahweh, and she despised him, in her heart.
texts.2sa.6.17: So they brought in the ark of Yahweh, and set it in its place, in the midst of the tent which David had stretched out for it,—and David caused to go up ascending-sacrifices before Yahweh, and peace-offerings.
texts.2sa.6.18: And, when David had finished offering up the ascending-sacrifice and the peace-offerings, he blessed the people in the name of Yahweh of hosts.
texts.2sa.6.19: And he apportioned to all the people, to all the multitude of Israel, both to men and to women—to every one, a loaf of bread, and a sweet drink, and a raisin-cake,—and all the people went their way, every one unto his own house;
texts.2sa.6.20: and David returned, to bless his household. Then came forth Michal Saul’s daughter to meet David, and said—How honoured, to-day, was the king of Israel in disrobing himself to-day, in the sight of the handmaids of his servants, as one of the low people, might disrobe himself?
texts.2sa.6.21: And David said unto Michal, Before Yahweh, I will dance,—blessed, be Yahweh, who made choice of me above thy father, and above all his house, putting me in charge as leader over the people of Yahweh, over Israel,—therefore will I dance before Yahweh;
texts.2sa.6.22: and will make myself, yet more, lightly esteemed that this, and become lowly in mine own eyes,—nevertheless, with the handmaids of whom thou hast spoken, with them, shall I be honoured.
texts.2sa.6.23: Therefore, Michal Saul’s daughter, had no child,—unto the day of her death.
texts.2sa.7.1: And it came to pass, when the king had taken up his abode in his house,—and Yahweh had given him rest round about, from all his enemies,
texts.2sa.7.2: that the king said unto Nathan the prophet, See, I pray thee—I, have my abode in a house, of cedar, but, the ark of God, abideth in, the midst, of curtains.
texts.2sa.7.3: And Nathan said unto the king, All that is in thy heart, go—do,—for Yahweh is with thee.
texts.2sa.7.4: But so it was, in that night, that the word of Yahweh came unto Nathan, saying:
texts.2sa.7.5: Go and say unto my servant—unto David: Thus, saith Yahweh,—Shalt, thou, build me a house, for me to dwell in;
texts.2sa.7.6: seeing that I have not dwelt in a house, since the day that I brought up the sons of Israel out of Egypt, even unto this day,—but have been wandering in a tent as my habitation?
texts.2sa.7.7: Wheresoever I have wandered with any of the sons of Israel, spake I ever, a word, with any one of the tribes of Israel, whom I charged to shepherd my people Israel, saying,—Wherefore have ye not built me a house, of cedar?
texts.2sa.7.8: Now, therefore, thus, shalt thou say unto my servant, unto David: Thus, saith Yahweh of hosts, I myself, took thee away from the pasture, from after the flock,—to become leader over my people, over Israel;
texts.2sa.7.9: and was with thee, whithersoever thou didst go, and have cut off all thine enemies, from before thee,—and will make thee a name, like the name of the great ones who are in the earth;
texts.2sa.7.10: and will appoint a place for my people, for Israel, and will plant them, and they shall inhabit their place, and be unsettled no more,—neither shall the sons of perversity again humiliate them, as at first;
texts.2sa.7.11: even from the day when I put judges in charge over my people Israel, thus will I give thee rest from all thine enemies. And Yahweh must tell thee that, a house, will Yahweh make for thee.
texts.2sa.7.12: And it shall be that, when thy days shall be fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, then will I raise up thy seed after thee, which proceedeth from thine own body,—and I will establish his kingdom.
texts.2sa.7.13: He, shall build a house for my name,—and I will establish his kingly throne unto times age-abiding:
texts.2sa.7.14: I, will become his father, And, he, shall become my son: If he commit iniquity, then will I correct him, with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the sons of men;
texts.2sa.7.15: But, my lovingkindness, shall not depart from him,—as I caused it to depart from Saul, whom I caused to depart from before thee.
texts.2sa.7.16: So shall thy house and thy kingdom be made steadfast unto times age-abiding, before thee,—thy throne, shall be established unto times age-abiding.
texts.2sa.7.17: According to all these words, and according to all this vision, so, spake Nathan unto David.
texts.2sa.7.18: Then entered King David, and tarried before Yahweh,—and said—Who am, I, My Lord, Yahweh, and what is my house, that thou hast brought me, hitherto;
texts.2sa.7.19: and hast yet further made this seem little in thine eyes, My Lord, Yahweh, in that thou hast spoken, even of the house, of thy servant, for a great while to come? This, then is the law of manhood, O My Lord, Yahweh!
texts.2sa.7.20: What more, then, can David yet further speak unto thee,—seeing that, thou thyself knowest thy servant, O My Lord Yahweh?
texts.2sa.7.21: For the sake of thine own word, and according to thine own heart, hast thou done all this great thing,—making it known unto thy servant.
texts.2sa.7.22: For this cause, hast thou magnified thyself, O Yahweh Elohim,—for there is none like unto, thee, yea there is no God besides thee, according to all that we have heard with our ears.
texts.2sa.7.23: Who, then, is like thy people, like Israel, a nation alone in the earth? whom God went to redeem for himself as a people, so to make himself a name, and to do for you the great deed, fearful things also for thy land, to make way for thy people, whom thou hadst redeemed for thyself, out of Egypt, [dealing with] nations and their god’s;
texts.2sa.7.24: and hast established for thyself thy people Israel—for thyself as a people, unto times age-abiding,—thou thyself, also, O Yahweh, becoming their God.
texts.2sa.7.25: Now, therefore, O Yahweh Elohim, the word which thou hast spoken concerning thy servant, and concerning his house, confirm thou, unto times age-abiding,—and do, as thou hast spoken:
texts.2sa.7.26: that thy name may be age-abidingly magnified, saying, Yahweh of hosts, is God over Israel, and so, the house of thy servant David, be established before thee.
texts.2sa.7.27: For, thou, O Yahweh of hosts, God of Israel, hast unveiled the ear of thy servant, saying—A house, will I build for thee. For this cause, hath thy servant found in his heart, to pray unto thee, this prayer.
texts.2sa.7.28: Now, therefore, O My Lord, Yahweh, thou, art God, and, thy words, shall prove true,—therefore hast thou spoken unto thy servant this goodness.
texts.2sa.7.29: Now, therefore, be pleased to bless the house of thy servant, that it may continue age-abidingly before thee,—for, thou, O My Lord, Yahweh, hast spoken, therefore, with thine own blessing, shall the house of thy servant be age-abidingly blessed.
texts.2sa.8.1: And it came to pass, after this, that David smote the Philistines, and subdued them,—and David took the bridle of the metropolis, out of the hand of the Philistines.
texts.2sa.8.2: And he smote Moab, and measured them with the line casting, them down to the ground, and be measured with two lines to put to death, and with one full line to keep alive,—so the Moabites became David’s, as servants, bringing gifts.
texts.2sa.8.3: And David smote Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah,—when he went to lay his hand on the River Euphrates.
texts.2sa.8.4: And David captured from him, a thousand and seven hundred horsemen, and twenty thousand footmen,—and David destroyed all the chariots, but reserved of them, a hundred chariots.
texts.2sa.8.5: And, when the Syrians of Damascus came to help Hadadezer, king of Zobah, David smote of the Syrians, twenty-two thousand men.
texts.2sa.8.6: Then David put garrisons in Syria of Damascus, and the Syrians became David’s, as servants bringing gifts,—and so Yahweh gave victory unto David, whithersoever he went.
texts.2sa.8.7: And David took the shields of gold which had come to the servants of Hadadezer,—and brought them to Jerusalem;
texts.2sa.8.8: also, from Betah and from Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, did King David take bronze, exceeding much.
texts.2sa.8.9: And, when Tou king of Hamath heard that David had smitten all the forces of Hadadezer,
texts.2sa.8.10: then Tou sent Hadoram his son unto King David, to ask after his welfare, and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer and had smitten him, for Hadadezer had had wars with Tou,—and, in his hand, were vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and vessels of bronze.
texts.2sa.8.11: Them also, did King David hallow unto Yahweh,—with the silver and the gold which he had hallowed from all the nations which he had subdued:
texts.2sa.8.12: from Syria, and from Moab, and from the sons of Ammon, and from the Philistines, and from Amalek,—and from the spoil of Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
texts.2sa.8.13: And David made a name, when he returned from his smiting of the Syrians in the valley of salt,—eighteen thousand.
texts.2sa.8.14: And he put, in Edom, garrisons, throughout all Edom, put be garrisons, and so it was that all Edom became servants unto David,—and Yahweh gave victory unto David, whithersoever he went.
texts.2sa.8.15: And David reigned over all Israel,—and so it was that David used to execute justice and righteousness for all his people;
texts.2sa.8.16: and, Joab, son of Zeruiah, was over the army,—and, Jehoshaphat, son of Ahilud, was remembrancer.
texts.2sa.8.17: And, Zadok, son of Ahitub, and Abimelech, son of Abiathar, were priests,—and, Seraiah, was scribe;
texts.2sa.8.18: and, Benaiah, son of Jehoiadah, was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites,—and, the sons of David, became, chief rulers.
texts.2sa.9.1: And David said, Is there yet one left unto the house of Saul,—that I may show him lovingkindness, for the sake of, Jonathan?
texts.2sa.9.2: Now, unto the house of Saul, belonged a servant, whose name, was Ziba, and, when they had called him unto David, the king said unto him—Art, thou, Ziba? And he said—Thy servant!
texts.2sa.9.3: Then said the king—Is there never a man remaining unto the house of Saul, that I may show him the lovingkindness of God? And Ziba said unto the king, There remaineth a son unto Jonathan, lame in his feet.
texts.2sa.9.4: And the king said to him, Where is he? And Ziba said unto the king, Lo! he, is in the house of Machir son of Ammiel, in Lo-debar.
texts.2sa.9.5: Then sent King David,—and fetched him out of the house of Machir son of Ammiel, from Lo-debar.
texts.2sa.9.6: Now, when Mephibosheth, son of Jonathan, son of Saul, came in unto David, he fell on his face and did homage. And David said, Mephibosheth? And he said, Lo! thy servant.
texts.2sa.9.7: And David said to him—Do not fear, for I will, indeed shew, thee lovingkindness, for the sake of Jonathan thy father, and will restore unto thee all the land of Saul thy father,—but, thou thyself, shall eat bread at my table, continually.
texts.2sa.9.8: And he did homage, and said—What is thy servant,—that thou hast turned towards such a dead dog as I?
texts.2sa.9.9: Then the king called for Ziba, Saul’s servant, and said unto him,—All that pertained unto Saul and unto all his house, have I given unto the son of thy lord:
texts.2sa.9.10: therefore shalt thou till for him the ground, thou, and thy sons, and thy servants, and shalt bring in, so that thy lord’s son may have bread to eat, but, Mephibosheth, thy lord’s son, shall continually eat bread at my table. Now, Ziba, had fifteen sons, and twenty servants.
texts.2sa.9.11: Then said Ziba unto the king, According to all that my lord the king shall command his servant, so, will thy servant do,—but, Mephibosheth, is to eat at the table of David, as one of the sons of the king.
texts.2sa.9.12: Now, Mephibosheth, had a little son, whose name, was Micha. And, all that dwelt in the house of Ziba, were servants unto Mephibosheth.
texts.2sa.9.13: So, Mephibosheth, dwelt in Jerusalem, for, at the table of the king, continually, had he to eat,—he being lame, in both his feet.
texts.2sa.10.1: And it came to pass, after this, that the king of the sons of Ammon died,—and that Hanun his son reigned in his stead.
texts.2sa.10.2: Then said David—I will shew lovingkindness unto Hanun son of Nahash, as his father shewed, unto me, lovingkindness. So David sent to comfort him, by the hand of his servants, as to his father,—and the servants of David came into the land of the sons of Ammon.
texts.2sa.10.3: Then said the rulers of the sons of Ammon unto Hanun their lord—Is David honouring thy father, in thine eyes, that he hath sent unto thee comforters? Is it not, for the sake of exploring the city, and spying it out, and overthrowing it, that David hath sent his servants unto thee?
texts.2sa.10.4: Wherefore Hanun took David’s servants, and shaved off half their beards, and cut off their upper garments in the middle, as far as their buttocks,—and let them go.
texts.2sa.10.5: And, when they told David, he sent to meet them, because the men were greatly ashamed,—and the king said—Tarry at Jericho, until your beards be grown, then shall ye return.
texts.2sa.10.6: And, when the sons of Ammon saw that they had made themselves odious with David, the sons of Ammon sent and hired the Syrians of Beth-rehob, and the Syrians of Zoba—twenty thousand footmen, and of king Maacah—a thousand men, and men of Tob—twelve thousand men.
texts.2sa.10.7: And, when David heard of it, he sent Joab and all the army of heroes,
texts.2sa.10.8: And the sons of Ammon came out, and set in array for battle, at the entrance of the gate,—whereas, the Syrians of Zoba, and of Rehob, and the men of Tob and of Maacah, were by themselves, in the field.
texts.2sa.10.9: And, when Joab saw that the front of the battle was towards him, before and behind, he chose out of all the chosen men of Israel, and set them in array against the Syrians;
texts.2sa.10.10: while, the rest of the people, he delivered into the hand of Abishai his brother,—and set [them] in array against the sons of Ammon.
texts.2sa.10.11: And he said—If the Syrians be too strong for me, then shalt thou become my deliverance,—but, if, the sons of Ammon, be too strong for thee, then will I come with deliverance to thee.
texts.2sa.10.12: Be strong, and let us put forth our strength, for the sake of our people, and for the sake of the cities of our God,—and, Yahweh, do what is good in his own eyes.
texts.2sa.10.13: And Joab drew nigh, and the people that were with him, to fight against the Syrians,—and they fled before him.
texts.2sa.10.14: And, when, the sons of Ammon, saw that the Syrians had fled, then fled they before Abishai, and entered the city,—so Joab returned from the sons of Ammon, and entered Jerusalem.
texts.2sa.10.15: And, when the Syrians saw that they were defeated before Israel, they gathered themselves together;
texts.2sa.10.16: and Hadadezer sent and brought out the Syrians that were beyond the River, and they entered Helam,—Shobach the prince of the host of Hadadezer being before them.
texts.2sa.10.17: And, when it was told David, he gathered together all Israel, and passed over the Jordan, and entered Helam,—and the Syrians set themselves in array to meet David, and fought with him.
texts.2sa.10.18: Then fled the Syrians before Israel, and David slew of the Syrians seven hundred chariots, and forty thousand horsemen,—Shobach also, prince of their host, smote he, that he died, there.
texts.2sa.10.19: And, when all the kings who were servants to Hadadezer saw that they were defeated before Israel, they made peace with Israel, and served them,—and the Syrians feared to give help any more unto the sons of Ammon.
texts.2sa.11.1: And it came to pass, at the return of the year, at the time of the going forth of kings, that David sent Joab, and his servants with him, and all Israel, and they destroyed the sons of Ammon, and laid siege to Rabbah,—but, David, was remaining in Jerusalem.
texts.2sa.11.2: And it came to pass that, at eventide, David arose from his couch, and walked to and fro on the roof of the king’s house, when, from the roof, he saw a woman bathing herself,—the woman being exceeding beautiful to look upon.
texts.2sa.11.3: And David sent and enquired after the woman,—and one said—Is not, this, Bath-sheba, daughter of Eliam, wife of Uriah the Hittite?
texts.2sa.11.4: And David sent messengers, and fetched her, and she came in unto him, and he lay with her, she having purified herself from her uncleanness,—and she returned unto her own house.
texts.2sa.11.5: And the woman, having conceived, sent and told David, and said, I am with child.
texts.2sa.11.6: Then sent David unto Joab, Send unto me Uriah the Hittite. So Joab sent Uriah unto David.
texts.2sa.11.7: And, when Uriah had come in unto him, David asked—how Joab prospered, and how the people prospered, and how the war prospered.
texts.2sa.11.8: Then said David unto Uriah, Go down unto thy house, and bathe thy feet. And, when Uriah went out of the house of the king, there followed him, a present from the king.
texts.2sa.11.9: But Uriah slept at the entrance of the king’s house, with all the servants of his lord,—and went not down unto his own house.
texts.2sa.11.10: And it was told David, saying, Uriah went not down, unto his own house. So David said unto Uriah—Was it not, from a journey, thou didst come? why, then, hast thou not been down unto thine own house?
texts.2sa.11.11: And Uriah said unto David—The ark, and Israel and Judah, are dwelling in huts and, my lord Joab, and the servants of my lord, on the face of the field, are encamped, Was, I, then, to enter my own house, to eat and to drink and to lie with my wife? By thy life, yea by the life of thy soul, I could not do this thing.
texts.2sa.11.12: Then said David unto Uriah—Abide here to-day also, and, to-morrow, will I let thee go. So Uriah abode in Jerusalem that day, and the morrow.
texts.2sa.11.13: And David called him, and he did eat before him, and drank, and he made him drunk,—and he went forth in the evening to lie down on his bed, with the servants of his lord, but, unto his own house, went he not down.
texts.2sa.11.14: And so it was, in the morning, that David wrote a letter unto Joab,—and sent it by the hand of Uriah;
texts.2sa.11.15: and he wrote in the letter, saying,—Set ye Uriah in the forefront of the hottest battle, and retire ye from him, that he be smitten and die.
texts.2sa.11.16: So it came to pass, when Joab was laying siege to the city, that he put Uriah in the place where he knew that the men of valour, were.
texts.2sa.11.17: And forth sallied the men of the city, and fought with Joab, and there fell some of the people, of the servants of David,—then died also, Uriah the Hittite.
texts.2sa.11.18: So Joab sent and told David all the news of the battle;
texts.2sa.11.19: and he charged the messenger saying,—When thou hast ended all the news of the battle, in speaking unto the king,
texts.2sa.11.20: then shall it be, if the king’s anger arise, and he say unto thee, Why came ye near unto the city, to fight? Knew ye not, that they would shoot from off the wall?
texts.2sa.11.21: Who smote Abimelech son of Jerubbaal? Did not, a woman, cast on him an upper millstone from off the wall, that he died, in Thebez? Wherefore came ye near unto the wall? Then shalt thou say—Moreover, thy servant, Uriah the Hittite, died.
texts.2sa.11.22: And the messenger went his way,—and came in, and told David, all that Joab had sent him [to tell].
texts.2sa.11.23: And the messenger said unto David, The men were too strong for us, and sallied forth against us, in the field,—so we were drawn against them as far as the opening of the gate.
texts.2sa.11.24: Then did the archers shoot upon thy servants, from off the wall, and there died some of the servants of the king,—moreover also, thy servant, Uriah the Hittite, died.
texts.2sa.11.25: Then said David unto the messenger—Thus, shalt thou say unto Joab,—Let not this thing be grievous in thine eyes, for, now this one, and then that one, doth the sword devour,—make hot thy battle against the city, and overthrow it; Thus embolden thou him.
texts.2sa.11.26: And, when Uriah’s wife heard that Uriah her husband was dead, she made loud lamentation over her lord.
texts.2sa.11.27: And, when the time of mourning had passed, David sent and received her into his house, and she became his wife, and bare him a son. But the thing which David had done was wicked in the eyes of Yahweh.
texts.2sa.12.1: So then Yahweh sent Nathan the prophet unto David,—who therefore came unto him and said to him—Two men, there were in a certain city, the one, rich, and, the other, poor.
texts.2sa.12.2: The, rich, man had flocks and herds exceeding many;
texts.2sa.12.3: whereas the, poor, man had, nothing,—save one little lamb, which he had made his own, and sustained, and it had grown up with him and with his children, all together,—of his own morsel, used it to eat, and, out of his own cup, used it to drink, and, in his own bosom, used it to lie, and it was to him, as a daughter.
texts.2sa.12.4: Now there came a traveller to the rich man, but he thought it a pity to take of his own flock, or his own herd, to make ready for the wayfarer who had come to him,—so he took the lamb of his poor neighbour, and made ready for the man who had come to him.
texts.2sa.12.5: Then was kindled the anger of David against the man, fiercely,—and he said unto Nathan, By the life of Yahweh, doomed to death, is the man that hath done this;
texts.2sa.12.6: and, the lamb, shall he pay back sevenfold,—because he did this thing, and, for that he had no pity.
texts.2sa.12.7: Then said Nathan unto David: Thou, art the man! Thus, saith Yahweh, God of Israel—I, anointed thee to be king over Israel, and, I, delivered thee out of the hand of Saul;
texts.2sa.12.8: and gave unto thee the household of thy lord, and the wives of thy lord, into thy bosom, and gave unto thee the house of Israel and Judah. And, if this had been too little, I could have further given thee more and more of such things.
texts.2sa.12.9: Wherefore, hast thou despised the word of Yahweh, by doing that which is wicked in mine eyes? Uriah the Hittite, hast thou smitten with the sword, and, his wife, hast thou taken to thyself to wife, yea, him, hast thou slain with the sword of the sons of Ammon!
texts.2sa.12.10: Now, therefore, the sword shall not depart from thy house, unto age-abiding times,—because thou hast despised me, and taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be thy wife.
texts.2sa.12.11: Thus, saith Yahweh,—Behold me! raising up over thee calamity out of thine own household, and I will take thy wives, before thine eyes, and give unto thy neighbour, and he will lie with thy wives, in the eyes of this sun.
texts.2sa.12.12: For, thou, didst it, in secret,—but, I, will do this thing, before all Israel, and before the sun.
texts.2sa.12.13: And David said unto Nathan, I have sinned against Yahweh. Then said Nathan unto David,—Yahweh also, hath put away thy sin, thou shalt not die!
texts.2sa.12.14: Nevertheless, because thou hast greatly blasphemed Yahweh, by this thing, the very son that is born to thee, shall, die.
texts.2sa.12.15: And Nathan departed unto his own house,—and Yahweh struck the child that the wife of Uriah had borne unto David, and it fell sick.
texts.2sa.12.16: David therefore earnestly sought God in behalf of the boy,—and David kept a fast, and used to go in and pass the night, and lie upon the ground.
texts.2sa.12.17: And the elders of his house stood up over him, to raise him from the ground,—but he would not, neither would he eat food with them.
texts.2sa.12.18: And it came to pass, on the seventh day, that the child died,—but the servants of David feared to tell him that the child was dead, for said they—Lo! while the child was living, we spake unto him, and he hearkened not unto our voice, how then can we say unto him, The child is dead, and so he do [himself] harm?
texts.2sa.12.19: But, when David saw that his servants were whispering among themselves, then understood David that the child was dead,—and David said unto his servants—Is the child, dead? And they answered—Dead!
texts.2sa.12.20: Then David arose from the ground, and bathed and anointed, and changed his apparel, and, entering into the house of Yahweh, bowed himself down,—then came he into his own house, and asked, and they set before him food, and he did eat.
texts.2sa.12.21: Then said his servants unto him, What is this thing that thou hast done? For the child’s sake, while living, thou didst fast and weep, but, as soon as the child was dead, thou didst arise and eat food.
texts.2sa.12.22: And he said,—While yet the child lived, I fasted, and wept,—for I said—Who knoweth whether Yahweh may not grant me favour, and the child live?
texts.2sa.12.23: But, now, that he is dead, wherefore should I go on fasting? can I bring him back again? I am going unto him, but, he, will not come back unto me.
texts.2sa.12.24: And David consoled Bath-sheba his wife, and went in unto her, and lay with her,—and she bare a son, and called his name, Solomon, and Yahweh loved him.
texts.2sa.12.25: And he sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet, and called his name Jedidiah [="Beloved of Yah"], for Yahweh’s sake.
texts.2sa.12.26: And Joab fought against Rabbah, of the sons of Ammon,—and captured the royal city.
texts.2sa.12.27: Then Joab sent messengers unto David,—and said—I have fought against Rabbah, I have also captured the city of the waters.
texts.2sa.12.28: Now, therefore, gather thou together the rest of the people, and encamp against the city, and capture it,—lest, I, capture the city, and it be called by my name.
texts.2sa.12.29: So David gathered together all the people, and went to Rabbah,—and fought against it, and captured it.
texts.2sa.12.30: Then took he the crown of Milcom from off his head, the weight thereof, being a talent of gold, with the precious stones, and it remained on the head of David,—the spoil of the city also, brought he forth in great abundance;
texts.2sa.12.31: the people also that were therein, brought he forth, and put them to the saw, and to threshing sledges of iron, and to axes of iron, and made them pass through the brickkiln, and thus used he to do unto all the cities of the sons of Ammon. And David and all the people returned unto Jerusalem.
texts.2sa.13.1: And it came to pass, after this, that, Absolom, son of David, having a beautiful sister, whose name, was Tamar, Amnon son of David loved her.
texts.2sa.13.2: And it so troubled Amnon, that he made himself ill on account of Tamar his sister, for, a virgin, was she, and it was monstrous in Amnon’s own eyes, to do, anything, unto her.
texts.2sa.13.3: But, Amnon, had a friend, whose name, was Jonadab, son of Shimeah, David’s brother,—and, Jonadab, was a very cunning man.
texts.2sa.13.4: So he said to him,—Why art thou looking so wretched—a king’s son too—morning by morning? Wilt thou not tell me? And Amnon said to him, With Tamar, my brother Absolom’s sister, am I in love.
texts.2sa.13.5: And Jonadab said unto him: Take to thy bed, and feign thyself ill,—and, when thy father cometh in to see thee, then shalt thou say unto him—I pray thee, let Tamar my sister come, that she may give me food, and let her prepare, before mine eyes, some delicacy, to the end that I may see [it made], and so eat at her hand.
texts.2sa.13.6: So Amnon took to his bed, and feigned himself ill,—and, when the king came in to see him, Amnon said unto the king—I pray thee, let Tamar my sister come, and make ready before mine eyes a couple of cakes, that I may eat at her hand.
texts.2sa.13.7: So David sent unto Tamar, in the house—saying,—Come, I pray thee, to the house of Amnon thy brother, and prepare him enticing food.
texts.2sa.13.8: And Tamar went to the house of Amnon her brother, he having taken to his bed,—and took dough and kneaded it, and folded it before his eyes, and baked the cakes.
texts.2sa.13.9: Then took she the pan and put them out before him, but he refused to eat. And Amnon said—Have forth every one from me. And they went out every one from him.
texts.2sa.13.10: Then said Amnon unto Tamar—Bring the food into the chamber, that I may eat out of thine own hand. So Tamar took the cakes which she had made, and brought them in to Amnon her brother, in the chamber.
texts.2sa.13.11: And, when she brought them unto him to eat, he took hold of her, and said to her, Come lie with me, my sister!
texts.2sa.13.12: But she said to him—Nay! my brother, do not force me, for it should not be done so in Israel,—do not commit this vileness.
texts.2sa.13.13: And, I,—whither could I take my reproach? Thou, too, wouldest be as one of the vile fellows, in Israel. Now, therefore, speak, I pray thee, unto the king, for he would not withhold me from thee.
texts.2sa.13.14: But he would not hearken unto her voice,—and, being stronger than she, forced her, and lay with her.
texts.2sa.13.15: Then did Amnon hate her with a very great hatred, for, greater, was the hatred wherewith he hated her, than the love wherewith he had loved her,—so Amnon said to her—Rise—begone!
texts.2sa.13.16: But she said to him—No occasion for this greater wrong, after what thou hast done with me, to put me away! Nevertheless he would not hearken unto her;
texts.2sa.13.17: but called his young man who waited on him, and said—I pray you, put forth this woman from me, outside,—and bolt the door after her.
texts.2sa.13.18: Now she had upon her a long tunic, for, so, used king’s daughters to apparel themselves, when they were virgins, in robes. And his attendant took her forth, outside, and bolted the door, after her.
texts.2sa.13.19: And Tamar put ashes upon her head, and, the long tunic that was upon her, she rent,—and put her hand upon her head, and went her way, crying out as she went.
texts.2sa.13.20: And Absolom her brother said unto her—Hath, Amnon thy brother, been with thee? Now, therefore, my sister, hold thy peace—thy brother, he is, do not lay to thy heart, this thing. But Tamar remained, and was desolate in the house of Absolom her brother.
texts.2sa.13.21: And, King David, heard all these things,—and it angered him greatly.
texts.2sa.13.22: And Absolom spake not with Amnon, either bad or good,—though Absolom hated Amnon, because he had forced Tamar his sister.
texts.2sa.13.23: And it came to pass, after two years of days, that Absolom had, sheepshearers in Baal-hazor, which is beside Ephron,—and Absolom invited all the king’s sons.
texts.2sa.13.24: Absolom came also unto the king, and said, See, I pray thee, thy servant hath, sheepshearers,—I pray thee, let the king and his servants go with thy servant.
texts.2sa.13.25: And the king said unto Absolom—Nay! my son, do not, I pray thee, let us all go, lest we be burdensome upon thee. And, though he urged him, he would not go, but blessed him.
texts.2sa.13.26: Then said Absolom, If not, then, I pray thee, let Amnon my brother go with us. And the king said unto him, Wherefore should he go with thee?
texts.2sa.13.27: And Absolom urged him,—so he let Amnon and all the king’s sons go with him.
texts.2sa.13.28: Now Absolom had commanded his young men, saying—Mark, I pray you, when the heart of Amnon is merry with wine, and I say unto you—Smite ye Amnon, then shall ye put him to death, do not fear,—have not, I myself, commanded you? Be bold, and show yourselves to be sons of valour.
texts.2sa.13.29: So Absolom’s young men did to Amnon as Absolom had commanded. Then arose all the king’s sons, and rode away—each man on his mule, and fled.
texts.2sa.13.30: And it came to pass, while, they, were yet on the road, that, the report, reached David, saying,—Absolom hath smitten all the king’s sons, and there is not left of them, one.
texts.2sa.13.31: And the king arose, and rent his garments, and lay on the ground,—and all his servants who stood by rent their garments.
texts.2sa.13.32: Then responded Jonadab son of Shimeah David’s brother, and said—Let not my lord say that they have put, all the young men—the king’s sons, to death; for, Amnon alone, is dead; for, by the bidding of Absolom, was it appointed, from the day that he forced Tamar his sister.
texts.2sa.13.33: Now, therefore, let not my lord the king lay to his heart such a thing—to say, All the king’s sons, are dead,—but, Amnon alone, is dead.
texts.2sa.13.34: Now Absolom had fled. And the young man that was watching lifted up his eyes and looked, and lo! much people, coming on the road behind him, on the mountain-side.
texts.2sa.13.35: So Jonadab said unto the king, Lo! the king’s sons, are come,—according to the word of thy servant, so hath it come to pass.
texts.2sa.13.36: And so it was, as he made an end of speaking, that lo! the king’s sons, came, and lifted up their voice and wept,—the king also, and all his servants, wept with an exceeding great weeping.
texts.2sa.13.37: But, Absolom, had fled, and had taken his journey unto Talmai son of Ammihud, king of Geshur. And David the king mourned for his son continually,
texts.2sa.13.38: But, Absolom, had fled, and had taken his journey to Geshur,—and it came to pass that he was there three years.
texts.2sa.13.39: And the spirit of the king pined to go forth unto Absolom,—for he had consoled himself over Amnon, in that he was dead.
texts.2sa.14.1: And Joab, son of Zeruiah, perceived that the heart of the king was towards Absolom.
texts.2sa.14.2: So Joab sent to Tekoa, and fetched from thence, a wise woman,—and said unto her—I pray thee, feign thyself a mourner, and put on, I pray thee, mourning apparel, and do not anoint thyself with oil, but be as a woman that hath, these many days, been mourning for the dead;
texts.2sa.14.3: so shalt thou come in unto the king, and speak unto him, after this manner. And Joab put the words in her mouth.
texts.2sa.14.4: And, when the woman of Tekoa came in unto the king, she fell on her face to the ground, and did homage,—and said—Save, O king!
texts.2sa.14.5: And the king said to her—What aileth thee? And she said—Of a truth, a widow woman, am I, for my husband is dead.
texts.2sa.14.6: Now, thy maidservant, had two sons, and they two strove together in the field, with none to tear them apart,—so the one smote the other, and slew him.
texts.2sa.14.7: Lo! therefore, all the family hath risen up against thy maidservant, and have said: Give up him that hath smitten his brother, that we may put him to death, for the life of his brother, whom he hath slain, that we may destroy, the heir also. So will they quench my ember that is left, and make my husband without name or remainder, on the face of the ground.
texts.2sa.14.8: And the king said unto the woman—Go to thy house, and, I, will give command concerning thee.
texts.2sa.14.9: Then said the woman of Tekoa unto the king, Upon me, my lord, O king, be the iniquity, and upon the house of my father, —but, the king and his throne, be guiltless.
texts.2sa.14.10: And the king said,—He that speaketh unto thee, bring him in unto me, and he shall, no more, annoy thee.
texts.2sa.14.11: Then said she: Let the king, I pray thee, remember Yahweh thy God; so that the blood-redeemer may not make utter ruin, and that they destroy not my son. And he said—By the life of Yahweh, not one hair of thy son shall fall to the earth.
texts.2sa.14.12: Then said the woman, Pray let thy maidservant speak unto my lord the king, a word. And he said—Speak.
texts.2sa.14.13: And the woman said, Wherefore, then, hast thou devised the like of this, for the people of God; and yet the king, in speaking this word, is verily guilty, unless the king, bring back his fugitive?
texts.2sa.14.14: For, when we, die, we become as water poured on the ground, which cannot be gathered up again,—therefore doth God not take away the life, but deviseth plans so as not to thrust out from him, a fugitive.
texts.2sa.14.15: Now, therefore, [is it] that I have come to speak unto the king my lord this word, because the people kept putting me in fear,—so thy maidservant said—Do let me, I pray you, speak unto the king! peradventure the king will fulfil the request of his handmaid.
texts.2sa.14.16: For the king can hearken, to rescue his handmaid out of the power of the man who would seek to destroy both me and my son together, out of the inheritance of God.
texts.2sa.14.17: So thy maidservant said, Pray let the word of my lord the king be comforting,—for, as the messenger of God, so is my lord the king, in hearing the good and the bad, Yahweh thy God, then, be with thee.
texts.2sa.14.18: Then responded the king, and said unto the woman, Nay, now! do not hide from me, the thing which I am about to ask thee. And the woman said, Pray let my lord the king speak.
texts.2sa.14.19: Then said the king, Is, the hand of Joab, with thee, in all this? And the woman answered and said—By the life of thy soul, my lord, O king, there is no way to the right or to the left, of anything that my lord the king hath spoken, for, thy servant Joab himself, charged me, and, himself, put, in the mouth of thy maidservant, all these words:
texts.2sa.14.20: for the purpose of turning round the face of the matter, hath thy servant Joab done this thing,—my lord being wise, as with the wisdom of a messenger of God, in knowing all that is [done] in the land.
texts.2sa.14.21: Then said the king unto Joab, See, I pray thee, I a have done this thing,—go then—bring back the young man, Absolom.
texts.2sa.14.22: So Joab fell with his face to the earth, and did homage, and blessed the king,—and Joab said—To-day, doth thy servant know, that I have found favour in thine eyes, my lord O king, in that the king hath fulfilled the request of thy servant.
texts.2sa.14.23: And Joab arose, and went to Geshur,—and brought Absolom to Jerusalem.
texts.2sa.14.24: And the king said—Let him go round to his own house, and, my face, let him not see. So Absolom went round, unto his own house, and, the face of the king, saw he not.
texts.2sa.14.25: Now, like unto Absolom, was there no man handsome in all Israel, to be greatly praised,—from the sole of his foot, even unto the crown of his head, there was not, in him, a blemish.
texts.2sa.14.26: And when he polled his head—and it was at every year’s end that he used to poll it, because it was heavy upon him, therefore he used to poll it—he would weigh the hair of his head, two hundred shekels, by the royal standard.
texts.2sa.14.27: And there were born to Absolom three sons, and one daughter, whose name, was Tamar,—she, was a woman beautiful to look upon.
texts.2sa.14.28: So Absolom dwelt in Jerusalem two years of days,—and, the face of the king, had he not seen.
texts.2sa.14.29: Then sent Absolom unto Joab, to send him unto the king, but he would not come to him,—so he sent yet a second time, but he would not come.
texts.2sa.14.30: Then said he unto his servants—See, the allotted portion of Joab, adjoineth me, and, he, hath barley there, go, and set it on fire. So the servants of Absolom set the portion on fire.
texts.2sa.14.31: Then rose Joab, and went unto Absolom, in his house,—and said unto him, Wherefore, have thy servants set the portion that pertaineth to me, on fire?
texts.2sa.14.32: And Absolom said unto Joab—Lo! I sent unto thee, saying—Come hither, that I may send thee unto the king, saying—Wherefore, am I come from Geshur? I, might as well have yet been there. Now, therefore, let me see the face of the king, and, if there is in me iniquity, then let him put me to death.
texts.2sa.14.33: So Joab came unto the king, and told him, and the king called for Absolom, and he came in unto the king, and bowed himself down with his face to the ground, before the king,—and the king kissed Absolom.
texts.2sa.15.1: And it came to pass, after this, that Absolom prepared him chariots and horses,—and fifty men, to run before him.
texts.2sa.15.2: And Absolom used to rise up early, and take his stand beside the way of the gate,—and so it was—when any man who had a controversy would come unto the king for judgment, then Absalom called unto him, and said: Of what city, art, thou? And he said, Of one of the tribes of Israel, is thy servant. And Absolom said unto him,
texts.2sa.15.3: See! thy cause, is good and right,—but, to hear it, thou hast no one, from the king.
texts.2sa.15.4: And Absalom said, Oh would that I were appointed to judge in the land! that, unto me, might come every man having a complaint or a defence, then would I see him righted.
texts.2sa.15.5: Moreover, so it used to be, that, when any man came near to do him homage, he would put forth his hand, and lay hold of him, and kiss him.
texts.2sa.15.6: And Absolom did, after this manner, to all Israel who came for judgment, unto the king,—so Absolom stole away the heart of the men of Israel.
texts.2sa.15.7: And it came to pass, at the end of forty years, that Absolom said unto the king—Let me go, I pray thee, that I may pay my vow which I have vowed unto Yahweh, in Hebron;
texts.2sa.15.8: for thy servant vowed, a vow, while I abode in Geshur in Syria, saying,—If Yahweh, will but bring me back, unto Jerusalem, then will I serve Yahweh,
texts.2sa.15.9: And the king said unto him—Go and prosper! So he arose and went to Hebron.
texts.2sa.15.10: And Absolom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying,—When ye hear the sound of the horn, then shall ye say, Absolom hath become king in Hebron!
texts.2sa.15.11: And, with Absolom, went two hundred men, out of Jerusalem, who, having been bidden, were going in their simplicity,—neither knew they anything.
texts.2sa.15.12: And Absalom sent and called Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s counsellor, out of his city, out of Gilo, when he was offering sacrifices,—and so it was that the conspiracy was strong, and, the people, went on multiplying with Absolom.
