texts.2sa.15.13: Then came one bearing tidings unto David, saying,—It hath come about, that the heart of the men of Israel goeth after Absolom.
texts.2sa.15.14: Then said David, to all his servants who were with him in Jerusalem—Arise and let us flee, or we shall have no way of escape from the face of Absolom,—make speed to depart, lest he make speed, and so overtake us, and bring down misfortune upon us, and smite the city with the edge of the sword.
texts.2sa.15.15: And the king’s servants said unto the king,—According to all that my lord the king shall choose, here are thy servants.
texts.2sa.15.16: So the king went forth, with all his household attending him,—but the king left ten women who were concubines, to keep the house.
texts.2sa.15.17: Thus then the king went forth, with all the people attending him,—and they came to a stand at a place that was far off.
texts.2sa.15.18: And, all his servants, were passing on beside him, and all the Cherethites, and all the Pelethites, —and, all the Gittites—six hundred men, who had accompanied him from Gath,—were passing on before the king.
texts.2sa.15.19: Then said the king, unto Ittai the Gittite, Wherefore shouldest, thou also, go with us? return and abide with the king, for, a stranger, art thou, moreover also, an exile, art thou from thine own country.
texts.2sa.15.20: Only yesterday, camest thou, and, today, shall I let thee wander with us, on our journey, seeing that, I, am going, whithersoever I may? Return and take back thy brethren with thee, and may Yahweh deal with thee in lovingkindness and faithfulness.
texts.2sa.15.21: But Ittai answered the king, and said,—By the life of Yahweh, and by the life of my lord the king, surely, in whatsoever place, my lord the king, may be, whether for death or for life, there will, thy servant, be.
texts.2sa.15.22: Then said David unto Ittai—Go, and pass on. So Ittai the Gittite passed on, with all his men, and all the little ones that were with him.
texts.2sa.15.23: And, fall the land, was weeping, with a loud voice, and, all the people, were passing on,—the king also, was passing on, through the torrent-bed of Kidron, and all the people were passing on over the face of the way leading to the wilderness.
texts.2sa.15.24: And lo! Zadok also, and all the Levites with him, were bearing the ark of the covenant of God, and they set down the ark of God, and Abiathar went up, until all the people had made an end of passing over out of the city.
texts.2sa.15.25: Then said the king unto Zadok, Take back the ark of God into the city,—if I find favour in the eyes of Yahweh, then will he bring me back, and let me see both him and his habitation,
texts.2sa.15.26: but, if thus, he say, I have no delight in thee, here I am, let him do unto me as may be good in his eyes.
texts.2sa.15.27: And the king said, unto Zadok the priest, Art thou not, a seer? return into the city, in peace,—and Ahimaaz thine own son, and Jonathan son of Abiathar—your two sons, with you.
texts.2sa.15.28: See! I, am tarrying in the waste plains of the wilderness—until there come word from you, to tell me.
texts.2sa.15.29: So Zadok and Abiathar took back the ark of God to Jerusalem,—and abode there.
texts.2sa.15.30: Now, David, was going up by the ascent of Olivet, weeping as he went up, with his head covered, himself, passing on barefoot,—and all the people who were with him, covered every man his head, and went up, weeping as they went.
texts.2sa.15.31: And, unto David, it was told, saying, Ahithophel, is among the conspirators with Absolom. And David said, Turn to foolishness, I pray thee, the counsel of Ahithophel, O Yahweh.
texts.2sa.15.32: And it came to pass, when David reached the summit, where he bowed himself down unto God, that lo! there met him, Hushai the Archite, his tunic rent, and earth upon his head.
texts.2sa.15.33: And David said unto him,—If thou pass over with me, then shalt thou become unto me, a burden;
texts.2sa.15.34: but, if, to the city, thou return, then canst thou say unto Absolom—Thy servant, I, O king, will be, as, the servant of thy father, I was formerly, so will I, now, be thy servant: thus shalt thou frustrate for me the counsel of Ahithophel.
texts.2sa.15.35: And hast thou not, with thee, there Zadok and Abiathar the priests? so then it shall be, that, what thing soever thou shalt hear out of the house of the king, thou shalt tell to Zadok and to Abiathar, the priests.
texts.2sa.15.36: Lo! they have there with them, their two sons, Ahimaaz for Zadok, and Jonathan for Abiathar,—so shall ye send, by their hand, unto me, everything which ye shall hear.
texts.2sa.15.37: So Hushai, David’s friend, went into the city,—when, Absolom, was about to enter Jerusalem.
texts.2sa.16.1: Now, David, had passed on but a little from the summit, when lo! Ziba, servant of Mephibosheth, met him,—with a couple of asses saddled, and, upon them, two hundred cakes of bread, and one hundred cakes of raisins, and one hundred summer fruits, and a skin of wine.
texts.2sa.16.2: And the king said unto Ziba, What meanest thou, by these? And Ziba said—The asses, are for the king’s household, to ride on, and, the bread and the summer fruits, are for the young men to eat, and, the wine, is for drink to such as are faint in the wilderness.
texts.2sa.16.3: Then said the king, And where is thy lord’s son? And Ziba said unto the king—Lo! abiding in Jerusalem, for he said, To-day, will the house of Israel, restore unto me, the kingdom of my father.
texts.2sa.16.4: Then said the king unto Ziba, Lo! thine, is all that pertained to Mephibosheth. And Ziba said—I have done homage, that I might find favour in thine eyes, my lord O king.
texts.2sa.16.5: And, when King David had come as far as Bahurim, lo! from thence a man coming out, of the family of the house of Saul, whose name, was Shimei son of Gera, coming out and cursing as he came.
texts.2sa.16.6: And he pelted, with stones, David and all the servants of King David,—all the people, and all the mighty men, being on his right hand and on his left.
texts.2sa.16.7: And, thus, said Shimei, when he cursed,—Out! Out! thou man of bloodshed, and man of the Abandoned One!
texts.2sa.16.8: Yahweh, hath brought back upon thee, all the shed-blood of the house of Saul, in whose stead thou hast reigned, and Yahweh hath delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absolom thy son,—and, here thou art, in thy ruin, for that, a man of bloodshed, thou art.
texts.2sa.16.9: Then said Abishai, son of Zeruiah, unto the king—Wherefore should this dead dog curse my lord the king? I pray thee, let me cross over and take off his head.
texts.2sa.16.10: But the king said, What have I in common with you, ye sons of Zeruiah? thus, he curseth, because, Yahweh, hath said unto him—Curse David. Who then can say, Why hast thou done thus?
texts.2sa.16.11: Then said David unto Abishai, and unto all his servants, Lo! my own son who sprang from my body, is seeking my life,—then how much more, now, a Benjamite? Let him alone, and let him curse, for, Yahweh, hath permitted him.
texts.2sa.16.12: It may be, that Yahweh will behold with his eye,—and that Yahweh will return me good, for his cursing this day.
texts.2sa.16.13: And, when David and his men went along in the way, Shimei, was going along on the side of the hill over against him, cursing as he went, pelting him with stones, and throwing dust.
texts.2sa.16.14: And the king and all the people that were with him arrived, weary,—and they refreshed themselves there.
texts.2sa.16.15: And, Absolom and all the men of Israel, entered Jerusalem,—and Ahithophel with him.
texts.2sa.16.16: And it came to pass, when Hushai the Archite, the friend of David, came in unto Absolom, that Hushai said unto Absolom: Long live the king! Long live the king!
texts.2sa.16.17: Then said Absolom unto Hushai, Is, this, thy lovingkindness unto thy friend? Wherefore wentest thou not with thy friend?
texts.2sa.16.18: And Hushai said unto Absolom, Nay! but, whom Yahweh, and all this people, and the men of Israel have chosen, his, will I be, and, with him, will I dwell.
texts.2sa.16.19: And, again, whom, should, I serve? Should it not be in presence of his son? as I served in presence of thy father, so, will I continue thy presence.
texts.2sa.16.20: Then said Absolom unto Ahithophel,—Give ye your counsel, what we shall do.
texts.2sa.16.21: And Ahithophel said unto Absolom, Go in unto thy father’s concubines, whom he hath left to keep the house,—so shall all Israel hear that thou hast made thyself odious unto thy father, and the hands of all that are with thee, shall be strengthened.
texts.2sa.16.22: And they stretched out for Absolom a tent, upon the house-top,—and Absolom went in unto his father’s concubines, in the sight of all Israel.
texts.2sa.16.23: Now, the counsel of Ahithophel which he counselled in those days, was as if a man had enquired at the oracle of God,—so, was all the counsel of Ahithophel, both to David, and also to Absolom.
texts.2sa.17.1: Then said Ahithophel unto Absolom: I pray thee, let me choose for myself, twelve thousand men, and arise, and pursue David to-night;
texts.2sa.17.2: and let me come upon him, when, he, is weary, and weak-handed, so shall I strike him with terror, and all the people who are with him shall flee,—then will I smite the king alone:
texts.2sa.17.3: that I may bring back all the people unto thee,—when all return—[save] the man whom thou art seeking, all the people, will be at peace.
texts.2sa.17.4: And the saying was right in the eyes of Absolom, —and in the eyes of all the elders of Israel.
texts.2sa.17.5: Then said Absolom, I pray you, call ye Hushai the Archite also,—and let us hear what is in, his, mouth, also.
texts.2sa.17.6: And, when Hushai came in unto Absolom, Absolom spake unto him, saying—After this manner, hath Ahithophel spoken, shall we do what he saith? if not, thou, speak.
texts.2sa.17.7: Then said Hushai unto Absolom,—Not good, is the counsel that Ahithophel hath given—at this time.
texts.2sa.17.8: And Hushai said—Thou, knowest thy father and his men—that, men of might, they are, and, embittered in soul, they are, like a bear bereaved of her young, in the field,—thy father also, is a man of war, and will not lodge with the people.
texts.2sa.17.9: Lo! by this time, hath, he, hidden himself in some pit, or other place,—and it shall be, as soon as he falleth upon them at the first, that he that hearkeneth for tidings will hear [of it], and will say—There is a defeat among the people that are following Absolom:
texts.2sa.17.10: then will, even the son of valour himself, whose heart is as the heart of a lion, utterly melt,—for all Israel do know that, a man of might, is thy father, and that, sons of valour, are they who are with him.
texts.2sa.17.11: Therefore I counsel—that there be a general gathering together unto thee of all Israel, from Dan even unto Beer-sheba, as the sand that is by the sea for multitude,—and that, thine own presence, be going on in their midst.
texts.2sa.17.12: So shall we come upon him in some place where he hath been found, yea, we, shall be upon him, as when the dew falleth upon the ground,—and there shall not be left of him, or of the men that are with him, so much as one.
texts.2sa.17.13: But, if, into a city, he withdraw, then will all Israel bring up unto that city, ropes,—and we will drag it down unto the ravine, until there be not found in that place, so much as a small stone.
texts.2sa.17.14: Then said Absolom and all the men of Israel, Better, is the counsel of Hushai the Archite, than the counsel of Ahithophel. Yahweh, indeed, had given charge to frustrate the wise counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that Yahweh might bring upon Absolom, ruin.
texts.2sa.17.15: So Hushai said unto Zadok and unto Abiathar the priests, Thus and thus, did Ahithophel counsel Absolom and the elders of Israel,—and, thus and thus, have, I, counselled.
texts.2sa.17.16: Now, therefore, send quickly, and tell David, saying,—Do not lodge to-night in the waste plains of the wilderness, thou must, even pass over, lest the king be swallowed up, and all the people who are with him.
texts.2sa.17.17: Now, Jonathan and Ahimaaz, were staying by En-rogel, and a maidservant was to go and tell them, and, they, were to go and tell King David,—for they might not be seen to enter the city.
texts.2sa.17.18: And, though a young man did see them, and told Absolom, yet they both departed quickly, and entered the house of a man in Bahurim, and, he, had a well in his court, into which they went down;
texts.2sa.17.19: and the woman took and spread the cover over the face of the well, and spread thereon her pounded corn,—so nothing was known.
texts.2sa.17.20: Then came the servants of Absolom unto the woman in the house, and said—Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan? And the woman said to them—They have passed over the stream of water. And, when they had searched and not found, they returned to Jerusalem.
texts.2sa.17.21: And it came to pass, after those had gone, that these came up out of the well, and went, and told King David,—and said unto David,—Arise ye and pass quickly over the water, for, thus and thus, hath Ahithophel counselled against you.
texts.2sa.17.22: So David arose, and all the people who were with him, and passed over the Jordan, by the morning light, so much as one, was not lacking, who had not passed over the Jordan.
texts.2sa.17.23: Now, when, Ahithophel, saw that his counsel was not followed, he saddled his ass, and arose and went unto his own house, unto his own city, and gave charge unto his household, and hanged himself, and died, and was buried in the grave of his father.
texts.2sa.17.24: When, David, had come to Mahanaim, Absolom, had passed over the Jordan, he and all the men of Israel with him.
texts.2sa.17.25: Now Absolom had appointed, Amasa, instead of Joab, over the army,—Amasa, being the son of a man whose name was Ithra the Ishmaelite, who went in unto Abigail, daughter of Nahash, sister of Zeruiah, mother of Joab.
texts.2sa.17.26: And Israel and Absolom encamped in the land of Gilead.
texts.2sa.17.27: And it came to pass, when David entered Mahanaim, that Shobi son of Nahash of Rabbah of the sons of Ammon and Machir son of Ammiel of Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite, of Rogelim,
texts.2sa.17.28: brought, sleeping rugs, and basins, and earthen vessels, and wheat and barley, and meal and roasted corn,—and beans and lentils, and parched pulse;
texts.2sa.17.29: and honey and cream, and sheep, and cheese of kine, for David, and for the people that were with him, to eat,—for they said, The people, are hungry and weary and thirsty, in the wilderness.
texts.2sa.18.1: Then David mustered the people that were with him,—and set over them, captains of thousands, and captains of hundreds.
texts.2sa.18.2: And David sent forth the people—a third part, under the hand of Joab, and, a third part, under the hand of Abishai son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, and, a third part, under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. Then said the king, unto the people, I myself, will, surely go forth, with you.
texts.2sa.18.3: But the people said—Thou must not go forth, for, if we, flee, they will not regard us, neither, if half of us die, will they regard us, for, thou, compared with us, [art worth] ten thousand,—now, therefore, it will be better that thou come to us out of the city, with succour.
texts.2sa.18.4: And the king said unto them, Whatever is best in your eyes, I will do. And the king stood beside the gate, while, all the people, came out by hundreds and by thousands.
texts.2sa.18.5: And the king charged Joab and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Deal gently, for my sake, with the young man, even Absolom. And, all the people, heard when the king charged all the captains, for the sake of Absolom.
texts.2sa.18.6: So the people went forth into the field against Israel,—and the battle took place in the forest of Ephraim.
texts.2sa.18.7: Then were the people of Israel defeated there, before he servants of David,—and the slaughter there was great, on that day—twenty thousand.
texts.2sa.18.8: And the battle there was spread out over the face of all the land,—and the forest devoured more of the people than the sword devoured on that day.
texts.2sa.18.9: Now, when Absolom met the servants of David, Absolom, was riding upon a mule, and the mule came under the thick branches of a large oak, and his head caught hold of the oak, and he was suspended between heaven and earth, the mule that was under him passing on.
texts.2sa.18.10: And a certain man saw it, and told Joab,—and said—Lo! I saw Absolom suspended in an oak.
texts.2sa.18.11: Then said Joab to the man that was telling him, Lo! since thou sawest him, why didst thou not smite him there, to the ground? then should I have been bound to give thee ten pieces of silver, and a girdle.
texts.2sa.18.12: And the man said unto Joab, Though I were weighing upon my palm a thousand pieces of silver, yet would I not put forth my hand against the son of the king,—for, in our hearing, the king Charged thee and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Watch any man who [would touch] the young man Absolom.
texts.2sa.18.13: Otherwise, had I dealt with my life falsely (and nothing can be hid from the king), then, thou thyself, wouldst have stood aloof.
texts.2sa.18.14: And Joab said, Not thus, may I tarry before thee. And he took three darts in his hand, and thrust them into the heart of Absolom, while he was yet alive in the midst of the oak.
texts.2sa.18.15: Then came round ten young men who bare Joab’s armour,—and smote Absolom, and slew him.
texts.2sa.18.16: Then Joab blew with a horn, and the people returned from pursuing Israel,—for Joab had restrained the people.
texts.2sa.18.17: And they took Absolom, and cast him, in the forest, into a large pit, and raised up over him a very great heap of stones,—and, all Israel, fled, every man to his home.
texts.2sa.18.18: But, Absolom, had taken, and raised up for himself, in his lifetime, the pillar that is in the king’s vale, for he said, I have no son, to keep in remembrance my name, so he called the pillar after his own name, and it is called Absolom’s monument unto this day.
texts.2sa.18.19: Then, Ahimaaz, son of Zadok, said, Let me run, I pray thee, and carry tidings unto the king,—how that Yahweh hath vindicated him, at the hand of his enemies.
texts.2sa.18.20: And Joab said to him—Not a man to bear tidings, art thou this day, but thou shalt bear tidings another day,—but, this day, shalt thou not bear tidings, for this cause, that, the king’s son, is dead.
texts.2sa.18.21: Then said Joab to a Cushite, Go tell the king, what thou hast seen. And the Cushite bowed himself down to Joab, and ran.
texts.2sa.18.22: Then, yet again, said Ahimaaz son of Zadok unto Joab. But, be what may, do, I pray thee, let, me also, run, after the Cushite. And Joab said—Wherefore is it that, thou, wouldst run, my son, when, thou, hast no tidings of, any profit?
texts.2sa.18.23: But, be what may, I will run. So he said to him—Run. Then ran Ahimaaz by the way of the plain, and got beyond the Cushite.
texts.2sa.18.24: Now, David, was sitting between the two gates,—and the watchman went on to the top of the gate-house, upon the wall, and lifted up his eyes, and looked, and lo! a man, running alone.
texts.2sa.18.25: So the watchman called out, and told the king. And the king said, If he is alone, there are tidings in his mouth. And he came on nearer and nearer.
texts.2sa.18.26: Then saw the watchman another man, running, so he called out unto the porter, Lo! a man, running alone. And the king said. This one also, beareth tidings.
texts.2sa.18.27: Then said the watchman, It seemeth, to me, that, the running of the foremost, is like the running of Ahimaaz son of Zadok. And the king said, A good man, is he, and, with good tidings, he cometh.
texts.2sa.18.28: Then called out Ahimaaz, and said unto the king, Peace! And he bowed himself down to the king, with his face to the earth,—and said—Blessed, be Yahweh thy God, who hath surrendered the men who were lifting up their hand, against my lord the king.
texts.2sa.18.29: And the king said, Is it, well, with the young man—Absolom? Then said Ahimaaz—I saw a great crowd, when Joab sent the king’s servant and [me] thy servant, but I knew not what [it meant].
texts.2sa.18.30: And the king said, Aside! stand, here. So he turned aside, and stood.
texts.2sa.18.31: Then lo! the Cushite, coming in,—and the Cushite said—Tidings, getteth my lord the king, how that Yahweh hath vindicated thee to-day, at the hand of all them who had risen up against thee.
texts.2sa.18.32: And the king said unto the Cushite—Is it, well, with the young man—Absolom? Then said the Cushite—Be, like the young man, the enemies of my lord the king, and all who have risen up against thee, for harm.
texts.2sa.18.33: Then was the king deeply moved, and went up to the chamber over the gate, and wept,—and, thus, he said as he went—O my son Absolom, my son—my son—Absolom! could, I, but have died in thy stead, O Absolom, my son—my son!
texts.2sa.19.1: And it was told Joab,—Lo! the king, is weeping and mourning over Absolom.
texts.2sa.19.2: So the victory, on that day, was turned into mourning, with all the people,—for the people heard, on that day, saying, The king is distressed for his son.
texts.2sa.19.3: And the people stole away, on that day, to go into the city,—as people steal away who are put to shame, when they flee in battle.
texts.2sa.19.4: But, the king, muffled his face, and the king made outcry, with a loud voice,—O my son Absolom, O Absolom, my son, my son!
texts.2sa.19.5: Then came Joab unto the king, in the house, —and said—Thou hast, to-day, covered with shame the faces of all thy servants, who have rescued thy life to-day, and the lives of thy sons and thy daughters, and the lives of thy wives, and the lives of thy concubines;
texts.2sa.19.6: by loving them who hated thee, and hating them who loved thee,—for thou hast declared, to-day, that, nothing to thee, are princes or servants, for I perceive, to-day, that, if, Absolom, had lived, and, all we, to-day had died, that, then, it had been right in thine eyes.
texts.2sa.19.7: Now, therefore, rise—go forth, and speak unto the heart of thy servants,—for, by Yahweh, have I sworn, that, if thou do not go forth, not a man shall tarry with thee to-night, and this will be to thee, a greater misfortune, than all the misfortune that hath come upon thee from thy youth until now.
texts.2sa.19.8: So the king arose, and took his seat in the gate,—and, to all the people, was it told, saying—Lo! the king, is sitting in the gate. Then came all the people before the king, but, Israel, had fled every man to his home.
texts.2sa.19.9: And it came to pass that all the people were reproaching one another, throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying,—the king, delivered us out of the hand of our enemies, and, he, rescued us out of the hand of the Philistines, but, now, he hath fled out of the land, away from Absolom;
texts.2sa.19.10: and, Absolom, whom we anointed over us, hath died in the battle. Now, therefore, why are, ye, silent as to bringing back the king?
texts.2sa.19.11: And, King David, sent unto Zadok and unto Abiathar the priests, saying, Speak ye unto the elders of Judah, saying, Wherefore should ye be behindhand, in bringing back the king unto his home,—seeing that, the speech of all Israel, hath come unto the king, regarding his home?
texts.2sa.19.12: Mine own brethren, are ye, my bone and my flesh, are ye,—wherefore then should ye be behindhand in bringing back the king?
texts.2sa.19.13: And, unto Amasa, shall ye say, Art not, thou, my bone and my flesh? So, let God do to me, and, so, let him add, if thou become not, prince of the army, before me continually, instead of Joab.
texts.2sa.19.14: Thus bowed he the heart of all the men of Judah, as one man,—and they sent unto the king, Return, thou, and all thy servants.
texts.2sa.19.15: Then the king returned, and came as far as the Jordan,—and, Judah, came to Gilgal, to go and meet the king, to escort the king over the Jordan.
texts.2sa.19.16: Then hastened Shimei, son of Gera, the Benjamite, who was of Bahurim,—and came down, with the men of Judah, to meet King David.
texts.2sa.19.17: And, a thousand men, were with him, out of Benjamin, Ziba also, servant of the house of Saul, and his fifteen sons and twenty servants, with him,—and they went through the Jordan, before the king.
texts.2sa.19.18: But the ferry-boat kept crossing, to bring over the household of the king, and to do what was good in his eyes. And, Shimei, son of Gera, fell down before the king, when he had passed over the Jordan;
texts.2sa.19.19: and he said unto the king—Let not my lord impute to me iniquity, neither do thou remember the perverseness of thy servant, on the day that thou wentest out, my lord O king, from Jerusalem, that the king should lay it upon his heart.
texts.2sa.19.20: For thy servant doth know, that, I, sinned, —lo! therefore, I have arrived to-day, as the first of all the house of Joseph, to come down to meet my lord the king.
texts.2sa.19.21: Then responded Abishai, son of Zeruiah, and said, For this, shall not Shimei be put to death, for that he cursed the Anointed of Yahweh?
texts.2sa.19.22: But David said, What have I in common with you, ye sons of Zeruiah, for ye would become to me, to-day, a very traitor! Shall there, to-day, be put to death a man in Israel? for do I not know, that, to-day, I, am king over Israel?
texts.2sa.19.23: Then said the king unto Shimei—Thou shalt not die. And the king sware to him.
texts.2sa.19.24: And, Mephibosheth, son of Saul, came down to meet the king,—he had neither dressed his feet, nor trimmed his beard, nor, his clothes, had he washed, from the day the king departed, until the day that he entered in peace.
texts.2sa.19.25: And it came to pass, when he entered Jerusalem to meet the king, that the king said unto him, Wherefore wentest thou not with me, Mephibosheth.
texts.2sa.19.26: And he said, My lord, O king, my servant, betrayed me, —for thy servant said—I will even saddle me mine ass, that I may ride thereon, and go with the king, for, lame, is thy servant.
texts.2sa.19.27: And he hath slandered thy servant, unto my lord the king,—but, my lord the king, is as a messenger of God, do therefore what is good in thine own eyes.
texts.2sa.19.28: For, when all the house of my father were nothing better than dead men, unto my lord the king, then didst thou set thy servant among them that used to eat at thy table,—what then have I further, by way of right, or to cry out any further unto the king?
texts.2sa.19.29: Then the king said unto him, Wherefore shouldst thou speak any further of thine affairs? I have said—Thou and Ziba, shall share the land.
texts.2sa.19.30: And Mephibosheth said unto the king, Even the whole, let him take,—now that my lord the king hath entered, in peace, into his own house.
texts.2sa.19.31: And, Barzillai the Gileadite, came down from Rogelim,—and passed, with the king, over the Jordan, to escort him over the Jordan.
texts.2sa.19.32: Now, Barzillai, was very aged, eighty years old,—and, he himself, had sustained the king, throughout his sojourn in Mahanaim, for he was, an exceeding great man.
texts.2sa.19.33: So then the king said unto Barzillai,—Thou, come over with me, and I will sustain thee with me, in Jerusalem.
texts.2sa.19.34: But Barzillai said unto the king,—Like unto what, are the days of the years of my life, that I should come up with the king, to Jerusalem.
texts.2sa.19.35: Eighty years old, am I to-day—could I discern between good and bad? or could thy servant taste what I might eat, and what I might drink? or could I hearken any more to the voice of singing men and singing women? Wherefore, then, should thy servant yet be a burden unto my lord the king?
texts.2sa.19.36: Just a little way, will thy servant pass over the Jordan with the king,—but wherefore should the king recompense me with this reward?
texts.2sa.19.37: Let thy servant, I pray thee, turn back again, that I may die in mine own city, by the grave of my father, and my mother. But here is thy servant Chimham—let him pass over with my lord the king, and do unto him that which may be good in thine eyes.
texts.2sa.19.38: Then said the king, With me, shall Chimham pass over, and, I, will do unto him that which shall be good in thine eyes,—and, whatsoever thou shalt choose to lay upon me, I will do for thee.
texts.2sa.19.39: And, when all the people had passed over the Jordan, then, the king, passed over, —and the king kissed Barzillai, and blessed him, and he returned unto his own place.
texts.2sa.19.40: And the king passed over to Gilgal, and, Chimham, passed over with him,—and, all the people of Judah, escorted the king, yea moreover, half the people of Israel.
texts.2sa.19.41: Then lo! all the men of Israel, were coming unto the king,—and they said unto the king—Why did our brethren the men of Judah steal thee away, and escort the king and his household over the Jordan, and all the men of David with him?
texts.2sa.19.42: And all the men of Judah made answer unto the men of Israel—Because the king is, near of kin, unto us, wherefore, then, is it, that ye are angry over this matter? Have we, eaten, at the king’s cost? or hath he, bestowed any gifts, on us?
texts.2sa.19.43: And the men of Israel answered the men of Judah, and said—Ten parts, have we in the king, therefore, even in David, have we more right than ye. Why, then, made ye light of us, so that our word was not heard first as to bringing back our king? And, the words of the men of Judah, were fiercer than, the words of the men of Israel.
texts.2sa.20.1: Now, in that place, there happened to be an abandoned man, whose name, was Sheba son of Bichri, a man of Benjamin,—so he blew a horn, and said—We have no share in David, Nor inheritance have we in the son of Jesse, Every man to his home, O Israel!
texts.2sa.20.2: Then went up all the men of Israel from following David, to follow Sheba son of Bichri,—but, the men of Judah, clave unto their king, from the Jordan, even as far as Jerusalem.
texts.2sa.20.3: And David entered into his own house, in Jerusalem, and the king took the ten women, the concubines whom he had left to keep the house, and put them in ward, and sustained them, but, unto them, went he not in,—so they were shut up until the day of their death, in lifelong widowhood.
texts.2sa.20.4: Then said the king unto Amasa, Assemble me the men of Judah, within three days,—and, thou, here, take thy stand!
texts.2sa.20.5: So Amasa went, to assemble Judah,—but he tarried beyond the fixed time, which he had appointed him.
texts.2sa.20.6: Then said David unto Abishai, Now, shall Sheba son of Bichri, do us more harm than Absolom,—thou, take the servants of thy lord, and pursue him, lest he have got him into fortified cities, and so have escaped our eye.
texts.2sa.20.7: Then went out after him—the men of Joab, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites, and all the mighty men,—and they went out from Jerusalem, to pursue Sheba son of Bichri.
texts.2sa.20.8: When, they, were by the great stone which is in Gibeon, Amasa, had arrived before them. Now, Joab, was girded about with his war-coat as his upper garment, and, over it, a girdle with a sword, fastened upon his loins, in the sheath thereof, and, it, came out and fell.
texts.2sa.20.9: Then said Joab unto Amasa, Art thou, well, my brother? And Joab took Amasa by the beard with his right hand, to kiss him.
texts.2sa.20.10: Amasa not heeding the sword that was in the hand of Joab, he smote him therewith in the belly, and shed out his bowels to the ground, and [struck] him not again, and he died. So, Joab and Abishai his brother, pursued Sheba son of Bichri.
texts.2sa.20.11: Now, a man, stood over him, of the young men of Joab,—and said—Whosoever is well pleased with Joab, and whosoever pertaineth to David, let him follow Joab.
texts.2sa.20.12: But, Amasa, was wallowing in blood, in the midst of the highway,—and, when the man saw that all the people stood still, he moved Amasa, out of the highway into the field, and cast over him a garment, as soon as he saw that every man that came up to him stood still.
texts.2sa.20.13: When he had removed him out of the highway, every man passed on, after Joab, to pursue Sheba son of Bichri.
texts.2sa.20.14: And he passed on throughout all the tribes of Israel, unto Abel and unto Beth-maachah, and all the Berites,—and they were called together, and came in, yea and followed him.
texts.2sa.20.15: So they came, and laid siege against him, in Abel, Beth-maachah, and they cast up a mound against the city, so that it stood within a rampart, —and, all the people who were with Joab, were battering the wall to throw it down.
texts.2sa.20.16: Then cried a wise woman out of the city,—Hear ye! hear ye! I pray you, say unto Joab, Come near hither, and let me speak unto thee.
texts.2sa.20.17: So he came near unto her, and the woman said,—Art thou Joab? And he said,—I am. And she said unto him,—Hear thou the words of thy handmaid. And he said, I do hear.
texts.2sa.20.18: Then spake she, saying,—They, used to speak, in former times, saying, Enquire, in Abel! And, so, they ended it.
texts.2sa.20.19: I, am of the peaceable among the faithful in Israel,—thou, art seeking to put to death a city, and a mother in Israel, wherefore wouldst thou swallow up the inheritance of Yahweh?
texts.2sa.20.20: Then answered Joab and said,—Far be it! far be it from me! I will neither swallow up nor lay waste.
texts.2sa.20.21: Not so, is the matter! but, a man of the hill country of Ephraim, Sheba son of Bichri, his name, hath lifted up his hand against the king, even against David, give up him alone, and I will depart from the city. And the woman said unto Joab, Lo! his head, shall be cast unto thee, through the wall.
texts.2sa.20.22: So the woman came unto all the people in her wisdom, and they cut off the head of Sheba son of Bichri, and cast it out unto Joab. And he blew with a horn, and they dispersed themselves from the city, every man to his home; but, Joab, returned to Jerusalem unto the king.
texts.2sa.20.23: And, Joab, was [restored] unto all the army of Israel,—And, Benaiah, son of Jehoiada, was over the Cherethites and over the Pelethites,
texts.2sa.20.24: And, Adoniram, was over the tribute,—And, Jehoshaphat, son of Ahilud, was the remembrancer;
texts.2sa.20.25: And, Sheva, was scribe,—And, Zadok and Abiathar, were priests;
texts.2sa.20.26: Moreover also, Ira the Jairite, was chief ruler unto David.
texts.2sa.21.1: And there came to be a famine, in the days of David, for three years, year after year, so then David sought the face of Yahweh,—and Yahweh said—It respecteth Saul and his house, as to bloodshed, in that he put to death the Gibeonites.
texts.2sa.21.2: The king therefore called the Gibeonites, and said unto them (now, the Gibeonites, were, not of the sons of Israel, but of the remnant of the Amorites, with whom, the sons of Israel, had entered into an oath, and Saul had sought to smite them, in his jealousy for the sons of Israel and Judah)—
texts.2sa.21.3: wherefore David said unto the Gibeonites—What shall I do for you, and wherewith shall I make propitiation, so that ye may bless the inheritance of Yahweh?
texts.2sa.21.4: And the Gibeonites said unto him—It is not a matter with us of silver or gold, with Saul or with his house, neither would we have a man put to death in Israel. And he said,—What do ye say I should do for you?
texts.2sa.21.5: Then said they unto the king, The man who consumed us, and who thought to have destroyed us from taking a place within any of the bounds of Israel,
texts.2sa.21.6: let there be delivered up to us—seven men of his sons, and we will crucify them unto Yahweh in Gibeah of Saul, the chosen of Yahweh. And the king said, I, will deliver them up.
texts.2sa.21.7: But the king had pity upon Mephibosheth, son of Jonathan, Saul’s son,—because of the oath of Yahweh that was between them, between David and Jonathan, Saul’s son.
texts.2sa.21.8: So the king took the two sons of Rizpah daughter of Aiah, whom she had borne to Saul, even Armoni and Mephibosheth,—and the five sons of Michal daughter of Saul, whom she had borne to Adriel son of Barzillai, the Meholathite;
texts.2sa.21.9: and delivered them up into the hand of the Gibeonites, and they crucified them in the mountain, before Yahweh, so they seven fell together,—they being put to death in the first days of harvest, in the beginning of the barley harvest.
texts.2sa.21.10: Then Rizpah daughter of Aiah, took sackcloth, and spread it out for herself, on the rock, from the beginning of harvest, until water poured out upon them from the heavens,—and suffered neither the birds of the heavens to rest on them by day, nor the wild beasts of the field, [to devour them] by night.
texts.2sa.21.11: And it was told David,—what Rizpah daughter of Aiah, Saul’s concubine, had done.
texts.2sa.21.12: So David went and fetched the bones of Saul, and the bones of Jonathan his son, from the owners of Jabesh-gilead,—who stole them from the broadway of Beth-shan, where the Philistines had hanged them, on the day when the Philistines had smitten Saul in Gilboa;
texts.2sa.21.13: and he brought up from thence the bones of Saul, and the bones of Jonathan his son,—and they gathered together the bones of them who had been crucified;
texts.2sa.21.14: so they buried the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son in the land of Benjamin, in Zelah, in the grave of Kish his father, thus did they all that the king commanded,—and God suffered himself to be entreated for the land, after this.
texts.2sa.21.15: And the Philistines had yet again a war with Israel,—so David went down, and his servants with him, and fought the Philistines, and David became faint.
texts.2sa.21.16: So, Ishbi-benob, who was of the descendants of the giant, the weight of whose spear-head, was three hundred shekels of bronze, he also being newly armed, thought to smite David;
texts.2sa.21.17: but Abishai son of Zeruiah, came to his help, and smote the Philistine, and slew him. Then, sware the men of David unto him, saying—Thou must not go forth any more with us, to battle, that thou quench not the lamp of Israel.
texts.2sa.21.18: And it came to pass, after this, that there was yet again a battle in Gob, with the Philistines,—then, Sibbekai the Hushathite smote Saph, who was of the descendants of the giant.
texts.2sa.21.19: And there was yet again a battle in Gob with the Philistines,—when Elhanan son of Jaare-oregim of Bethlehem, smote Goliath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.
texts.2sa.21.20: And there was yet again a battle in Gath; when there was a man of stature, with six fingers on each hand, and six toes on each foot, twenty-four in number; he also, having been born to the giant;
texts.2sa.21.21: but, when he reproached Israel, Jonathan son of Shimeah David’s brother, smote, him.
texts.2sa.21.22: These four, had been born to the giant in Gath,—but they fell by the hand of David, and by the hand of his servants.
texts.2sa.22.1: And David spake unto Yahweh, the words of this song, in the day when Yahweh had rescued him, out of the hand of all his enemies, and out of the hand of Saul;
texts.2sa.22.2: and he said,—Yahweh, was my mountain crag and my stronghold, and my deliverer—mine;
texts.2sa.22.3: My God, was my rock, I sought refuge in him,—My shield, and my horn of salvation, my high tower, and my refuge, My Saviour! from violence, thou didst save me.
texts.2sa.22.4: As one worthy to be praised, called I on Yahweh,—And, from my foes, was I saved.
texts.2sa.22.5: When the breakers of death had encompassed me,—the torrents of perdition, made me afraid,—
texts.2sa.22.6: the meshes of hades, had surrounded me,—the snares of death had confronted me,
texts.2sa.22.7: In my distress, called I on Yahweh, Yea, unto my God, did I call,—and he hearkened, out of his temple, unto my voice, and, my cry for help, was in his ears!
texts.2sa.22.8: Then did the earth shake and quake, the foundations of the heavens, were deeply moved,—yea they did shake, because he was angry,
texts.2sa.22.9: There went up a smoke in his nostrils, and, a fire out of his mouth, devoured,—live coals, were kindled from it:
texts.2sa.22.10: Then he stretched out the heavens, and came down,—and, thick gloom, was under his feet;
texts.2sa.22.11: Then he rode on a cherub, and flew,—and was seen on the wings of the wind;
texts.2sa.22.12: And made of the darkness around him, pavilions,—gathering of waters, clouds of vapours.
texts.2sa.22.13: Out of the brightness before him, were kindled live coals of fire;
texts.2sa.22.14: Thunder from the heavens, did Yahweh give forth,—yea, the Highest, uttered his voice;
texts.2sa.22.15: And he sent forth arrows, and scattered them,—lightning, and confused them;
texts.2sa.22.16: Then appeared the channels of the sea, were uncovered the foundations of the world,—at the rebuke of Yahweh, the blast of the breath of his nostrils;
texts.2sa.22.17: He sent from on high, he took me,—he drew me out of many waters;
texts.2sa.22.18: He rescued me from my foe, in his might,—from them who hated me, because they were too strong for me:
texts.2sa.22.19: They confronted me, in the day of my necessity,—then became Yahweh my stay:
texts.2sa.22.20: And brought out, into a large place, even me,—he delivered me, because he delighted in me:
texts.2sa.22.21: Yahweh rewarded me, according to my righteousness—according to the cleanness of my hands, he repaid me:
texts.2sa.22.22: For I had kept the ways of Yahweh,—and not broken away from my God;
texts.2sa.22.23: For, all his regulations, were before me,—and, as for his statutes, I turned not from them.
texts.2sa.22.24: So became I blameless towards him,—and kept myself from mine iniquity:
texts.2sa.22.25: Yahweh therefore repaid me, according to my righteousness,—according to my pureness before his eyes.
texts.2sa.22.26: With the loving, thou didst show thyself loving,—with the blameless hero, thou didst show thyself blameless;
texts.2sa.22.27: With the pure, thou didst show thyself pure,—but, with the perverse, thou didst shew thyself ready to contend:
texts.2sa.22.28: And, a patient people, thou didst save,—but, thine eyes, were on the lofty—thou layedst them low;
texts.2sa.22.29: For, thou, wast my lamp, O Yahweh,—and, Yahweh, enlightened my darkness;
texts.2sa.22.30: For, by thee, I ran through a troop,—by my God, I leapt over a wall.
texts.2sa.22.31: As for God, blameless is his way,—the speech of Yahweh, hath been proved, a shield, he is to all who seek refuge in him.
texts.2sa.22.32: For who is a GOD, save Yahweh? and who a Rock, save our God?
texts.2sa.22.33: GOD, is my fortress of strength,—and shewed to the blameless his way;
texts.2sa.22.34: Planting my feet like the hinds’,—yea, on my high places, he caused me to stand;
texts.2sa.22.35: Teaching my hands, to war,—so that a bow of bronze was bent by mine arms;
texts.2sa.22.36: Thus didst thou grant me, as a shield, thy salvation,—and, thy condescension, made me great.
texts.2sa.22.37: Thou didst widen my stepping-places, under me,—so that mine ankles faltered not:
texts.2sa.22.38: I pursued my foes, and destroyed them,—and returned not, till they were consumed;
texts.2sa.22.39: So I consumed them, and crushed them, and they rose not again,—thus fell they under my feet:
texts.2sa.22.40: Thus didst thou gird me with strength, for the battle,—thou subduedst mine assailants under me:
texts.2sa.22.41: And, as for my foes, thou didst give me their neck,—yea, them who hated me, that I might destroy them:
texts.2sa.22.42: They cried out, but there was none to save,—unto Yahweh, but he answered them not.
texts.2sa.22.43: Then did I beat them in pieces, like the dust of the earth,—like the clay of the lanes, did I crush them, stamp them down.
texts.2sa.22.44: Thus didst thou rescue me from the contentions of my people, didst keep me to be the head of nations:—a people whom I had not known, served me;
texts.2sa.22.45: The sons of the foreigner, came cringing unto me,—at the hearing of the ear, they submitted to me,—
texts.2sa.22.46: The sons of the foreigner, were disheartened, and came quaking, out of their fortresses.
texts.2sa.22.47: Yahweh liveth, and blessed be my rock,—and exalted be the God (of the rock) of my salvation:—
texts.2sa.22.48: The GOD who hath avenged me, and brought down peoples under me;
texts.2sa.22.49: And brought me forth from among my foes,—yea, from mine assailants, hast thou set me on high, from the man of violence, hast thou delivered me.
texts.2sa.22.50: For this cause, will I praise thee, O Yahweh, among the nations,—and, to thy name, will I touch the strings:—
texts.2sa.22.51: Who hath made great the victories of his King,—and shown lovingkindness to his Anointed One, to David and to his Seed, unto times age-abiding.
texts.2sa.23.1: Now, these, are the last words of David,—The oracle of David, son of Jesse, Yea the oracle of The man raised up on high, The Anointed of the God of Jacob, the Delight of the Songs of Israel:
texts.2sa.23.2: The Spirit of Yahweh, spake in me,—And, his word, was on my tongue;
texts.2sa.23.3: Said the God of Israel, Unto me, spake the Rock of Israel:—One Ruling over Men, A Righteous One, ruling in the reverence of God,
texts.2sa.23.4: Is even as the light of the morning when ariseth the sun,—A morning, without clouds, [As] from brightness, [and] from rain, the fresh shoots out of the earth.
texts.2sa.23.5: When, not so, was my house with GOD, Then, a covenant age-abiding, he appointed me, Ordered in all things and guarded, Now that it is all my salvation and all my desire, Will he not make it shoot forth?
texts.2sa.23.6: But, as for the abandoned, like thorns to be tossed away are they all,—For, not with the hand, can they be taken;
texts.2sa.23.7: But, the man that would touch them, Must fence himself with iron, and the shaft of a spear,—Then, with fire, shall they be, consumed, on the spot!
texts.2sa.23.8: These, are the names of the mighty men, who belonged to David,—The president a Tachmonite head of the charioteers, the same, was Adino the Eznite, for eight hundred, slain at one time.
texts.2sa.23.9: And, after him, Eleazar son of Dodo, son of Ahohi,—in the hero-class of mighty men, with David, when they reproached the Philistines, they were gathered together there to battle, but the men of Israel had gone up;
texts.2sa.23.10: he, however, arose and smote among the Philistines until his hand was weary, and his hand clave unto his sword, so Yahweh wrought a great victory on that day,—the people, coming back after him, only to strip the slain.
texts.2sa.23.11: And, after him, Shammah son of Agee, the Hararite,—and, when the Philistines were gathered together into a troop, there being at hand an allotment of field-land full of lentils, but, the people, having fled from the face of the Philistines,
texts.2sa.23.12: then took he his stand in the midst of the allotment, and defended it, and smote the Philistines,—and Yahweh wrought a great victory.
texts.2sa.23.13: And three of the thirty chiefs descended, and came in, towards harvest, unto David, unto the cave of Adullam,—although, a troop of Philistines, were encamped in the vale of Rephaim;
texts.2sa.23.14: and, David, then was in a stronghold,—and, a garrison of Philistines, was then in Bethlehem.
texts.2sa.23.15: And David longed, and said,—Who will give me to drink water out of the well of Bethlehem, that is within the gate?
texts.2sa.23.16: And the three mighty men brake through the camp of Philistines, and drew water out of the well of Bethlehem, that was within the gate, and bare it, and brought it in unto David,—yet would he not drink, but poured it out unto Yahweh,
texts.2sa.23.17: and said—Be it far from me, O Yahweh, that I should do this! is it not the blood of the men who went with their lives [in their hands]? So he would not drink it. These things, did the three mighty men.
texts.2sa.23.18: And. Abishai brother of Joab son of Zeruiah, he, was chief of three, in that he brandished his spear against three hundred whom he slew; and, he, had a name among three.
texts.2sa.23.19: Was he not most honourable, of the three, and so became their captain? Nevertheless, unto the three, he attained not.
texts.2sa.23.20: Benaiah also, son of Jehoiadah, son of an active man, hero of many a deed, a man of Kabzeel, he, smote the two sons of Ariel of Moab, he, also went down and smote a lion in the midst of a pit, on a day of snow;
texts.2sa.23.21: he, also smote an Egyptian, who was of valiant bearing, and, in the hand of the Egyptian, was a spear, but he went down unto him with a staff,—and wrested the spear out of the hand of the Egyptian, and slew him with his own spear.
texts.2sa.23.22: These things, did Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and, he, had a name among three mighty men.
texts.2sa.23.23: He was the most honourable, of thirty, although, unto the three, he attained no,—so David added him to his council.
texts.2sa.23.24: Asahel, brother of Joab, was among the thirty,—Elhanan, son of Dodo, of Bethlehem;
texts.2sa.23.25: Shammah, the Harodite; Elika, the Harodite;
texts.2sa.23.26: Helez, the Paltite, Ira, son of Ikkesh, the Tekoite;
texts.2sa.23.27: Abiezer, the Anathothite, Mebunnai, the Hushathite;
texts.2sa.23.28: Zalmon, the Ahohite, Maharai, the Netophathite;
texts.2sa.23.29: Heleb, son of Baanah, the Netophathite,—Ittai, son of Ribai, of Gibeah, of the sons of Benjamin;
texts.2sa.23.30: Benaiah, a Pirathonite, Hiddai, of the torrents of Gaash;
texts.2sa.23.31: Abi-albon, the Arbathite, Azmaveth, the Barhumite;
texts.2sa.23.32: Eliahba, the Shaalbonite, (Of) the sons of Jashen, Jonathan;
texts.2sa.23.33: Shammah, the Hararite, Ahiam, son of Sharar, the Ararite;
texts.2sa.23.34: Eliphelet, son of Ahasbai, son of the Maacathite. Eliam, son of Ahithophel, the Gilonite.
texts.2sa.23.35: Hezro, the Carmelite, Paarai, the Arbite;
texts.2sa.23.36: Igal, son of Nathan, of Zobah, Bani, the Gadite;
texts.2sa.23.37: Zelek, the Ammonite,—Naharai, the Beerothite, armour bearers to Joab son of Zeruiah;
texts.2sa.23.38: Ira, the Ithrite, Gareb, the Ithrite;
texts.2sa.23.39: Uriah, the Hittite, In all, thirty and seven.
texts.2sa.24.1: And again was the anger of Yahweh kindled against Israel,—so that he suffered David to be moved against them, saying, Go, count Israel and Judah.
texts.2sa.24.2: The king, therefore, said unto Joab, captain of the force, who was with him—Go to and fro, I pray thee, throughout all the tribes of Israel, from Dan even unto Beer -sheba, and number ye the people,—so shall I know the sum of the people.
texts.2sa.24.3: Then said Joab unto the king—Yea, Yahweh thy God add unto the people, how many soever they be, a hundredfold, and [suffer] the eyes of my lord the king, to see it,—but, my lord the king, wherefore doth he find pleasure in this thing?
texts.2sa.24.4: Notwithstanding, the word of the king prevailed against Joab, and over the captains of the force,—so Joab went forth, with the captains of the force, before the king, to number the people—Israel.
texts.2sa.24.5: And they passed over the Jordan,—and encamped in Aroer, on the right side of the city, that is in the midst of the ravine of Gad, even towards Jazer.
texts.2sa.24.6: Thus came they to Gilead, and unto the land of Tahtim-hodshi,—and came to Dan-jaan, and round about Zidon;
texts.2sa.24.7: and entered the fortress of Tyre, and all the cities of the Hivites, and of the Canaanites,—and they went out to the South of Judah, even to Beer-sheba.
texts.2sa.24.8: So, when they had gone to and fro throughout all the land, they came, at the end of nine months and twenty days, unto Jerusalem.
texts.2sa.24.9: And Joab delivered up the sum of the number of the people, unto the king,—and there were found to be, in Israel, eight hundred thousand men of valour, drawing the sword,—and, the men of Judah, five hundred thousand men.
texts.2sa.24.10: And the heart of David smote him, after he had reckoned up the people,—and David said unto Yahweh—I have sinned greatly, in what I have done, Now, therefore, O Yahweh, take away, I beseech thee, the iniquity of thy servant, for I have done very foolishly.
texts.2sa.24.11: And, when David arose in the morning, the word of Yahweh, had come unto Gad the prophet, the seer of David, saying:
texts.2sa.24.12: Go and speak unto David—Thus, saith Yahweh, Three things, do I offer thee,—choose thee one of them, that I may do it unto thee.
texts.2sa.24.13: So Gad came in unto David, and told him,—and said to him: Shall there come unto thee seven years of famine in thy land? Or, for three months, wilt thou flee before thine enemies while, they, pursue thee? Or shall there be, for three days, pestilence in thy land? Now, consider and see, what, answer, I shall return to him that sent me.
texts.2sa.24.14: And David said unto Gad—I am in a great strait,—let us fall, I pray thee, into the hand of Yahweh, for, manifold, are, his compassions, but, into the hand of man, let me not fall.
texts.2sa.24.15: So Yahweh sent forth a pestilence throughout Israel, from the morning even unto the time appointed,—and there died of the people, from Dan even unto Beer-sheba, seventy thousand men.
texts.2sa.24.16: But, when the messenger stretched out his hand towards Jerusalem, to destroy it, then relented Yahweh as to the evil, and he said to the messenger who was destroying the people—Enough! now, stay thy hand. And, the messenger of Yahweh, was by the threshing-floor of Araunah the Jebusite.
texts.2sa.24.17: Then said David unto Yahweh, when he saw the messenger who was smiting the people, yea he said—Lo! I, have sinned, and, I, have done perversely, but what have, these sheep, done? Let thy hand, I pray thee, be against me, and against the house of my father!
texts.2sa.24.18: And Gad came unto David, on that day,—and said unto him—Go up, rear thou unto Yahweh an altar, in the threshing-floor of Araunah the Jebusite.
texts.2sa.24.19: So David went up, according to the word of Gad, as Yahweh had commanded.
texts.2sa.24.20: And Araunah looked out, and saw the king, and his servants, passing over unto him—so Araunah went forth, and did homage unto the king, with his face to the ground.
texts.2sa.24.21: Then said Araunah, Wherefore, hath my lord the king come unto his servant? And David said—To buy of thee the threshing-floor, to build an altar unto Yahweh, that the plague may be stayed from off the people.
texts.2sa.24.22: Then said Araunah unto David, Let my lord the king accept it and cause to ascend what is good in his own eyes,—see! the oxen for the ascending-sacrifice, and the threshing-sledges and ox-yokes for wood.
texts.2sa.24.23: The whole, did Araunah give, as a king to a king. And Araunah said unto the king, Yahweh thy God, accept thee!
texts.2sa.24.24: But the king said unto Araunah—Nay! but I will, buy, it of thee, for a price, and will not cause to ascend unto Yahweh my God, offerings that have cost me nothing. So David bought the threshing-floor, and the oxen, for fifty shekels of silver;
texts.2sa.24.25: and David built there an altar unto Yahweh, and caused to go up ascending-sacrifices and peace-offerings,—then was Yahweh entreated for the land, and the plague was stayed from Israel.

texts.2sa.1.1: Aconteció después de la muerte de Saúl, que vuelto David de la derrota de los amalecitas, estuvo dos días en Siclag.
texts.2sa.1.2: Al tercer día, sucedió que vino uno del campamento de Saúl, rotas sus vestiduras y puesta tierra sobre su cabeza; y llegando a David, se postró en tierra e hizo reverencia.
texts.2sa.1.3: Y le dijo David: ¿De dónde vienes? Y él respondió: Se me ha escapado del campamento de Israel.
texts.2sa.1.4: David le dijo: ¿Qué ha acontecido? Te ruego que me lo digas. Y él respondió: El pueblo huyó de la batalla, y también muchos del pueblo cayeron y son muertos; también Saúl y Jonatán su hijo han muerto.
texts.2sa.1.5: Dijo David a aquel joven que le daba las nuevas: ¿Cómo sabes que han muerto Saúl y Jonatán su hijo?
texts.2sa.1.6: El joven que le daba las nuevas respondió: Casualmente vine al monte de Gilboa, y hallé a Saúl que se apoyaba sobre su lanza, y venían tras él carros y gente de a caballo.
texts.2sa.1.7: Y como él miró hacia atrás, me vio y me llamó; y yo dije: Heme aquí.
texts.2sa.1.8: Y me preguntó: ¿Quién eres tú? Y yo le respondí: Soy amalecita.
texts.2sa.1.9: Él me volvió a decir: Te ruego que te pongas sobre mí y me mates, porque se han apoderado de mí las angustias, pues mi vida está aún toda en mí.
texts.2sa.1.10: Yo entonces me puse sobre él y le maté, pues sabía que no podía vivir después de su caída; y tomé la corona que tenía en su cabeza, y la argolla que traía en su brazo, y las he traído aquí a mi señor.
texts.2sa.1.11: Entonces David, trabando de sus vestiduras, las rasgó; y lo mismo hicieron todos los hombres que estaban con él.
texts.2sa.1.12: Y lloraron y lamentaron y ayunaron hasta la noche, por Saúl y por Jonatán su hijo, por el pueblo de Yahvé y por la casa de Israel, porque habían caído a filo de espada.
texts.2sa.1.13: Y David dijo a aquel joven que le había traído las nuevas: ¿De dónde eres tú? Y él respondió: Yo soy hijo de un extranjero, amalecita.
texts.2sa.1.14: Y le dijo David: ¿Cómo no tuviste temor de extender tu mano para matar al ungido de Yahvé?
texts.2sa.1.15: Entonces llamó David a uno de sus hombres, y le dijo: Ven, y arremete contra él. Y él lo hirió, y murió.
texts.2sa.1.16: Y David le dijo: Tu sangre sea sobre tu cabeza, pues tu boca atestiguó contra ti, diciendo: Yo maté al ungido de Yahvé.
texts.2sa.1.17: Y endechó David esta endecha sobre Saúl y sobre Jonatán su hijo,
texts.2sa.1.18: y dijo que enseñasen el canto del arco a los hijos de Judá. He aquí que está escrito en el libro de Jasar:
texts.2sa.1.19: ¡Tu gloria, oh Israel, ha perecido sobre tus montes! ¡Cómo han caído los valientes!
texts.2sa.1.20: No lo deis a entender en Gat, Ni deis las nuevas en las plazas de Ascalón; Para que no se alegren las hijas de los filisteos, Para que no salten de gozo las hijas de los incircuncisos.
texts.2sa.1.21: Montes de Gilboa, Ni caiga sobre vosotros rocío ni lluvia, ni seáis campos de ofrendas; Porque allí fue desechado el escudo de los valientes, El escudo de Saúl, como si no hubiera sido ungido con aceite.
texts.2sa.1.22: Sin sangre de muertos, sin grosura de valientes, El arco de Jonatán nunca volvió atrás, Ni la espada de Saúl volvió vacía.
texts.2sa.1.23: Saúl y Jonatán, amados y queridos en su vida, En su muerte no fueron apartados. Más ligeros eran que águilas, Más fuertes que leones.
texts.2sa.1.24: Hijas de Israel, llorad por Saúl, Que os vestía de escarlata con deleites, Que adornaba vuestras ropas con ornamentos de oro.
texts.2sa.1.25: ¡Cómo han caído los valientes en medio de la batalla! ¡Jonatán, muerto en tus alturas!
texts.2sa.1.26: Angustia tengo por ti, hermano mío Jonatán, Que me fuiste muy dulce. Más maravilloso me fue tu amor Que el amor de las mujeres.
texts.2sa.1.27: ¡Cómo han caído los valientes, Y perecieron las armas de guerra!
texts.2sa.2.1: Después de esto, David consultó a Yahvé, diciendo: «¿Debo subir a alguna de las ciudades de Judá?». Yahvé le dijo: «Sube». David dijo: «¿Adónde subiré?» Dijo: «A Hebrón».
texts.2sa.2.2: David subió allí con sus dos mujeres, Ahinoam la jezreelita y Abigail la mujer de Nabal el carmelita.
texts.2sa.2.3: David hizo subir a sus hombres que estaban con él, cada uno con su familia. Vivían en las ciudades de Hebrón.
texts.2sa.2.4: Vinieron los hombres de Judá y allí ungieron a David como rey de la casa de Judá. Le dijeron a David: «Los hombres de Jabes de Galaad fueron los que enterraron a Saúl».
texts.2sa.2.5: David envió mensajeros a los hombres de Jabes de Galaad y les dijo: «Benditos seáis por Yahvé, porque habéis mostrado esta bondad con vuestro señor, con Saúl, y lo habéis enterrado.
texts.2sa.2.6: Que el Señor les muestre su bondad y su verdad. Yo también te recompensaré por esta bondad, porque has hecho esto.
texts.2sa.2.7: Ahora, pues, fortalece tus manos y sé valiente, porque Saúl, tu señor, ha muerto, y también la casa de Judá me ha ungido como rey sobre ellos.»
texts.2sa.2.8: Abner, hijo de Ner, capitán del ejército de Saúl, había capturado a Isboset, hijo de Saúl, y lo había llevado a Mahanaim.
texts.2sa.2.9: Lo hizo rey de Galaad, de los asuritas, de Jezreel, de Efraín, de Benjamín y de todo Israel.
texts.2sa.2.10: Isboset, hijo de Saúl, tenía cuarenta años cuando comenzó a reinar sobre Israel, y reinó dos años. Pero la casa de Judá siguió a David.
texts.2sa.2.11: El tiempo que David fue rey en Hebrón sobre la casa de Judá fue de siete años y seis meses.
texts.2sa.2.12: Abner hijo de Ner, y los siervos de Isboset hijo de Saúl, salieron de Mahanaim a Gabaón.
texts.2sa.2.13: Joab, hijo de Sarvia, y los siervos de David salieron a su encuentro junto al estanque de Gabaón, y se sentaron, el uno a un lado del estanque y el otro al otro.
texts.2sa.2.14: Abner dijo a Joab: «¡Por favor, que los jóvenes se levanten y compitan ante nosotros!» Joab dijo: «¡Que se levanten!»
texts.2sa.2.15: Entonces se levantaron y pasaron por número: doce por Benjamín y por Isboset, hijo de Saúl, y doce de los siervos de David.
texts.2sa.2.16: Cada uno de ellos agarró a su adversario por la cabeza y le clavó la espada en el costado a su compañero; así cayeron juntos. Por eso aquel lugar de Gabaón se llamó Helkath Hazzurim.
texts.2sa.2.17: La batalla fue muy dura aquel día, y Abner y los hombres de Israel fueron derrotados ante los servidores de David.
texts.2sa.2.18: Los tres hijos de Sarvia estaban allí: Joab, Abisai y Asael. Asael era ligero de pies como una gacela salvaje.
texts.2sa.2.19: Asael persiguió a Abner. No se volvió ni a la derecha ni a la izquierda de seguir a Abner.
texts.2sa.2.20: Entonces Abner miró detrás de él y dijo: «¿Eres tú, Asahel?» Respondió: «Lo es».
texts.2sa.2.21: Abner le dijo: «Vuélvete a tu derecha o a tu izquierda, agarra a uno de los jóvenes y toma su armadura». Pero Asahel no quiso dejar de seguirlo.
texts.2sa.2.22: Abner le dijo de nuevo a Asael: «Apártate de seguirme. ¿Por qué habría de tirarte al suelo? ¿Cómo podría entonces mirar a la cara a tu hermano Joab?»
texts.2sa.2.23: Sin embargo, él se negó a apartarse. Entonces Abner, con el extremo posterior de la lanza, lo golpeó en el cuerpo, de modo que la lanza salió por detrás de él; y allí cayó y murió en el mismo lugar. Todos los que llegaron al lugar donde cayó y murió Asael se detuvieron.
texts.2sa.2.24: Pero Joab y Abisai persiguieron a Abner. El sol se puso cuando llegaron a la colina de Amma, que está frente a Giah por el camino del desierto de Gabaón.
texts.2sa.2.25: Los hijos de Benjamín se reunieron en pos de Abner y se convirtieron en un solo grupo, y se pusieron en la cima de la colina.
texts.2sa.2.26: Entonces Abner llamó a Joab y le dijo: «¿La espada va a devorar para siempre? ¿No sabes que al final será amarga? ¿Cuánto tiempo pasará entonces, antes de que pidas al pueblo que vuelva de seguir a sus hermanos?»
texts.2sa.2.27: Joab dijo: «Vive Dios, si no hubieras hablado, seguramente por la mañana el pueblo se habría ido, y no habría seguido cada uno a su hermano».
texts.2sa.2.28: Así que Joab tocó la trompeta, y todo el pueblo se detuvo y no persiguió más a Israel, y no lucharon más.
texts.2sa.2.29: Abner y sus hombres recorrieron toda aquella noche el Arabá, y pasaron el Jordán, atravesaron todo Bitrón y llegaron a Mahanaim.
texts.2sa.2.30: Joab regresó de seguir a Abner, y cuando reunió a todo el pueblo, faltaban diecinueve hombres de David y Asael.
texts.2sa.2.31: Pero los siervos de David habían herido a los hombres de Abner, de modo que murieron trescientos sesenta hombres.
texts.2sa.2.32: Recogieron a Asael y lo enterraron en la tumba de su padre, que estaba en Belén. Joab y sus hombres pasaron toda la noche, y el día amaneció en Hebrón.
texts.2sa.3.1: Hubo una larga guerra entre la casa de Saúl y la de David. David se hacía cada vez más fuerte, pero la casa de Saúl se debilitaba cada vez más.
texts.2sa.3.2: A David le nacieron hijos en Hebrón. Su primogénito fue Amnón, de Ahinoam la jezreelita;
texts.2sa.3.3: y su segundo, Chileab, de Abigail la mujer de Nabal el carmelita; y el tercero, Absalón, hijo de Maaca la hija de Talmai, rey de Gesur;
texts.2sa.3.4: y el cuarto, Adonías, hijo de Haggit; y el quinto, Sefatías, hijo de Abital;
texts.2sa.3.5: y el sexto, Itream, de Egla, mujer de David. Estos le nacieron a David en Hebrón.
texts.2sa.3.6: Mientras había guerra entre la casa de Saúl y la de David, Abner se hizo fuerte en la casa de Saúl.
texts.2sa.3.7: Saúl tenía una concubina que se llamaba Rizpa, hija de Aja; e Ishboset le dijo a Abner: «¿Por qué te has metido con la concubina de mi padre?»
texts.2sa.3.8: Entonces Abner se enojó mucho por las palabras de Ishboshet, y dijo: «¿Soy yo una cabeza de perro que pertenece a Judá? Hoy me muestro bondadoso con la casa de tu padre Saúl, con sus hermanos y con sus amigos, y no te he entregado en manos de David; ¡y sin embargo me acusas hoy de una falta con respecto a esta mujer!
texts.2sa.3.9: Que Dios haga lo mismo con Abner, y más aún, si, como Yahvé ha jurado a David, no hago lo mismo con él:
texts.2sa.3.10: transferir el reino de la casa de Saúl y establecer el trono de David sobre Israel y sobre Judá, desde Dan hasta Beerseba.»
texts.2sa.3.11: No pudo responder a Abner ni una palabra más, porque le tenía miedo.
texts.2sa.3.12: Abner envió mensajeros a David en su nombre, diciéndole: «¿De quién es la tierra?» y diciendo: «Haz tu alianza conmigo, y he aquí que mi mano estará contigo para traer a todo Israel a tu alrededor.»
texts.2sa.3.13: David dijo: «Bien. Haré un tratado contigo, pero te pido una cosa. Esto es, que no verás mi rostro a menos que primero traigas a Mical, la hija de Saúl, cuando vengas a ver mi rostro».
texts.2sa.3.14: David envió mensajeros a Isboset, hijo de Saúl, diciéndole: «Entrégame a mi esposa Mical, a quien me dieron en matrimonio por cien prepucios de los filisteos.»
texts.2sa.3.15: Ishbosheth envió y la separó de su marido, Paltiel hijo de Laish.
texts.2sa.3.16: Su marido la acompañó, llorando, y la siguió hasta Bahurim. Entonces Abner le dijo: «¡Vete, vuelve!», y regresó.
texts.2sa.3.17: Abner se comunicó con los ancianos de Israel, diciendo: “En tiempos pasados, ustedes buscaban que David fuera rey sobre ustedes.
texts.2sa.3.18: ¡Ahora, pues, háganlo! Porque Yahvé ha hablado de David, diciendo: ‘Por la mano de mi siervo David, salvaré a mi pueblo Israel de la mano de los filisteos y de la mano de todos sus enemigos’.”
texts.2sa.3.19: Abner también habló en los oídos de Benjamín; y Abner también fue a hablar en los oídos de David en Hebrón todo lo que le parecía bien a Israel y a toda la casa de Benjamín.
texts.2sa.3.20: Y Abner vino a David a Hebrón, y veinte hombres con él. David hizo un banquete a Abner y a los hombres que estaban con él.
texts.2sa.3.21: Abner dijo a David: «Me levantaré e iré y reuniré a todo Israel ante mi señor el rey, para que hagan un pacto contigo y para que reines sobre todo lo que tu alma desee.» David despidió a Abner, y éste se fue en paz.
texts.2sa.3.22: He aquí que los siervos de David y Joab venían de una incursión y traían consigo un gran botín; pero Abner no estaba con David en Hebrón, pues éste lo había despedido y se había ido en paz.
texts.2sa.3.23: Cuando llegó Joab y todo el ejército que estaba con él, le dijeron a Joab: «Abner hijo de Ner vino al rey, y él lo ha despedido, y se ha ido en paz.»
texts.2sa.3.24: Entonces Joab se acercó al rey y le dijo: «¿Qué has hecho? He aquí que Abner ha venido a ti. ¿Por qué lo has despedido, y ya se ha ido?
texts.2sa.3.25: Tú conoces a Abner, hijo de Ner. Vino a engañarte y a conocer tu salida y tu entrada, y a saber todo lo que haces».
texts.2sa.3.26: Cuando Joab salió de David, envió mensajeros en busca de Abner, y lo trajeron de vuelta del pozo de Sira; pero David no lo sabía.
texts.2sa.3.27: Cuando Abner regresó a Hebrón, Joab lo apartó en medio de la puerta para hablar con él en voz baja, y lo golpeó allí en el cuerpo, de modo que murió por la sangre de su hermano Asael.
texts.2sa.3.28: Después, cuando David lo oyó, dijo: «Yo y mi reino quedamos libres de culpa ante el Señor para siempre por la sangre de Abner, hijo de Ner.
texts.2sa.3.29: Que caiga sobre la cabeza de Joab y sobre toda la casa de su padre. Que no falte de la casa de Joab ninguno que tenga una baja, o que sea leproso, o que se apoye en un bastón, o que caiga por la espada, o que le falte el pan.»
texts.2sa.3.30: Entonces Joab y su hermano Abisai mataron a Abner, porque éste había matado a su hermano Asael en Gabaón en la batalla.
texts.2sa.3.31: David dijo a Joab y a todo el pueblo que estaba con él: «Rasguen sus ropas, vístanse de saco y hagan duelo frente a Abner». El rey David siguió el féretro.
texts.2sa.3.32: Enterraron a Abner en Hebrón; el rey alzó la voz y lloró ante la tumba de Abner, y todo el pueblo lloró.
texts.2sa.3.33: El rey se lamentó por Abner y dijo: «¿Debe morir Abner como muere un tonto?
texts.2sa.3.34: Sus manos no fueron atadas, ni sus pies fueron puestos en grilletes. Como un hombre cae ante los hijos de la iniquidad, así caíste tú». Todo el pueblo volvió a llorar por él.
texts.2sa.3.35: Todo el pueblo vino a exhortar a David a que comiera pan mientras fuera de día; pero David juró diciendo: «Que Dios me haga así, y más, si pruebo el pan o cualquier otra cosa, hasta que se ponga el sol.»
texts.2sa.3.36: Todo el pueblo se dio por enterado, y les pareció bien, pues todo lo que hacía el rey le parecía bien a todo el pueblo.
texts.2sa.3.37: Así que todo el pueblo y todo Israel comprendieron aquel día que no era del rey matar a Abner hijo de Ner.
texts.2sa.3.38: El rey dijo a sus siervos: «¿No sabéis que hoy ha caído un príncipe y un gran hombre en Israel?
texts.2sa.3.39: Hoy soy débil, aunque he sido ungido rey. Estos hombres, los hijos de Sarvia, son demasiado duros para mí. Que el Señor recompense al malhechor según su maldad».
texts.2sa.4.1: Luego que oyó el hijo de Saúl que Abner había muerto en Hebrón, las manos se le desmayaron, y todo Israel se turbó.
texts.2sa.4.2: Tenía el hijo de Saúl dos hombres, capitanes de bandas de merodeadores; el nombre de uno era Baana, y el del otro Recab, hijos de Rimón beerotita, de los hijos de Benjamín (porque Beerot era también contada con Benjamín,
texts.2sa.4.3: pues los beerotitas habían huido a Gitaim, y moran allí como forasteros hasta hoy).
texts.2sa.4.4: Y Jonatán hijo de Saúl tenía un hijo cojo de los pies. Tenía cinco años de edad cuando llegó de Jezreel la noticia de la muerte de Saúl y de Jonatán, y su nodriza lo tomó y huyó; y mientras huía apresuradamente, se le cayó el niño y quedó cojo. Su nombre era Mefiboset.
texts.2sa.4.5: Vinieron, pues, los hijos de Rimón beerotita, Recab y Baana, y llegaron en lo más recio del calor del día a casa de Isboset, el cual estaba durmiendo la siesta en su cámara.
texts.2sa.4.6: Y he aquí que entraron en medio de la casa como para tomar trigo, y le hirieron en la quinta costilla; y Recab y Baana su hermano escaparon.
texts.2sa.4.7: Pues cuando entraron en la casa, estando él acostado en su lecho en su cámara de dormir, lo hirieron y lo mataron, y le cortaron la cabeza, y tomando su cabeza, caminaron por el camino del Arabá toda la noche.
texts.2sa.4.8: Y trajeron la cabeza de Isboset a David en Hebrón, y dijeron al rey: He aquí la cabeza de Isboset hijo de Saúl tu enemigo, que buscaba tu vida; y Yahvé ha vengado hoy a mi señor el rey de Saúl y de su simiente.
texts.2sa.4.9: Y David respondió a Recab y a su hermano Baana, hijos de Rimón beerotita, y les dijo: Vive Yahvé que ha redimido mi alma de toda angustia,
texts.2sa.4.10: que cuando uno me dio nuevas, diciendo: He aquí Saúl es muerto, imaginándose que traía buenas nuevas, yo lo prendí y le maté en Siclag, en pago de sus nuevas.
texts.2sa.4.11: ¿Cuánto más a los malos hombres que mataron a un hombre justo en su casa, sobre su lecho? ¿No he de demandar yo ahora su sangre de vuestra mano, y quitaros de la tierra?
texts.2sa.4.12: Entonces David mandó a los mancebos, y ellos los mataron, y les cortaron las manos y los pies, y los colgaron sobre el estanque en Hebrón. Mas tomaron la cabeza de Isboset, y la enterraron en el sepulcro de Abner en Hebrón.
texts.2sa.5.1: Vinieron todas las tribus de Israel a David en Hebrón, y hablaron diciendo: Henos aquí, hueso tuyo y carne tuya somos.
texts.2sa.5.2: Y aun antes de ahora, cuando Saúl reinaba sobre nosotros, eras tú quien sacabas a Israel a la guerra y lo volvías a traer. Además Yahvé te ha dicho: «Tú apacentarás a mi pueblo Israel, y tú serás príncipe sobre Israel».
texts.2sa.5.3: Vinieron, pues, todos los ancianos de Israel al rey en Hebrón, y el rey David hizo con ellos pacto en Hebrón delante de Yahvé; y ungieron a David por rey sobre Israel.
texts.2sa.5.4: Treinta años tenía David cuando comenzó a reinar, y reinó cuarenta años.
texts.2sa.5.5: En Hebrón reinó sobre Judá siete años y seis meses, y en Jerusalén reinó treinta y tres años sobre todo Israel y Judá.
texts.2sa.5.6: Entonces marchó el rey con sus hombres a Jerusalén contra los jebuseos que moraban en aquella tierra; los cuales hablaron a David, diciendo: Tú no entrarás acá, pues aun los ciegos y los cojos te echarán (queriendo decir: David no puede entrar acá).
texts.2sa.5.7: Pero David tomó la fortaleza de Sión, la cual es la ciudad de David.
texts.2sa.5.8: Y dijo David aquel día: Todo el que hiriere a los jebuseos, suba por el canal y hiera a los cojos y a los ciegos, a los cuales el alma de David aborrece. Por esto se dijo: Ciego ni cojo no entrará en la casa.
texts.2sa.5.9: Y David moró en la fortaleza, y la llamó Ciudad de David; y edificó alrededor desde Millo hacia adentro.
texts.2sa.5.10: Y David iba creciendo y aumentando en poder, y Yahvé Dios de los Ejércitos estaba con él.
texts.2sa.5.11: E Hiram rey de Tiro envió embajadores a David, y madera de cedro, y carpinteros, y canteros para la piedra, los cuales edificaron una casa a David.
texts.2sa.5.12: Y entendió David que Yahvé le había confirmado por rey sobre Israel, y que había exaltado su reino por amor de su pueblo Israel.
texts.2sa.5.13: Y tomó David más concubinas y mujeres de Jerusalén después que vino de Hebrón, y le nacieron más hijos e hijas.
texts.2sa.5.14: Estos son los nombres de los que le nacieron en Jerusalén: Samúa, Sobab, Natán, Salomón,
texts.2sa.5.17: Oyendo los filisteos que David había sido ungido por rey sobre Israel, subieron todos los filisteos para buscar a David; y cuando David lo oyó, descendió a la fortaleza.
texts.2sa.5.18: Y vinieron los filisteos, y se extendieron por el valle de Refaim.
texts.2sa.5.19: Entonces consultó David a Yahvé, diciendo: ¿Subiré contra los filisteos? ¿Los entregarás en mi mano? Y Yahvé respondió a David: Sube, porque ciertamente entregaré a los filisteos en tu mano.
texts.2sa.5.20: Y vino David a Baal-perazim, y allí los venció David, y dijo: Yahvé ha roto a mis enemigos delante de mí, como brecha de aguas. Por esto llamó el nombre de aquel lugar Baal-perazim.
texts.2sa.5.21: Y dejaron allí sus ídolos, y David y sus hombres los quemaron.
texts.2sa.5.22: Y los filisteos volvieron a venir, y se extendieron en el valle de Refaim.
texts.2sa.5.23: Y consultando David a Yahvé, él le respondió: No subas, sino rodéalos, y vendrás a ellos por enfrente de las balsameras.
texts.2sa.5.24: Y cuando oigas un estruendo de marcha por las copas de las balsameras, entonces te moverás; porque Yahvé saldrá delante de ti a herir el campamento de los filisteos.
texts.2sa.5.25: Y David lo hizo así, como Yahvé se lo había mandado; e hirió a los filisteos desde Geba hasta llegar a Gezer.
texts.2sa.6.1: David volvió a juntar a todos los escogidos de Israel, treinta mil.
texts.2sa.6.2: Y se levantó David y partió con todo el pueblo que tenía consigo de Baale de Judá, para hacer subir de allí el arca de Dios, sobre la cual es invocado el Nombre, el nombre de Yahvé de los Ejércitos, que mora entre los querubines.
texts.2sa.6.3: Pusieron el arca de Dios sobre un carro nuevo, y la llevaron de la casa de Abinadab, que estaba en el collado; y Uza y Ahío, hijos de Abinadab, conducían el carro nuevo.
texts.2sa.6.4: Y cuando lo llevaron de la casa de Abinadab, que estaba en el collado, con el arca de Dios, Ahío iba delante del arca.
texts.2sa.6.5: Y David y toda la casa de Israel danzaban delante de Yahvé con toda suerte de instrumentos de madera de haya; con arpas, salterios, adufes, castañuelas y címbalos.
texts.2sa.6.6: Cuando llegaron a la era de Nacón, Uza extendió su mano al arca de Dios y la sostuvo; porque los bueyes tropezaban.
texts.2sa.6.7: Y el furor de Yahvé se encendió contra Uza, y Dios le hirió allí por su temeridad, y murió allí junto al arca de Dios.
texts.2sa.6.8: Y se entristeció David por haber herido Yahvé a Uza, y fue llamado el lugar aquel Fares-uza, hasta el día de hoy.
texts.2sa.6.9: Y temiendo David a Yahvé aquel día, dijo: ¿Cómo ha de venir a mí el arca de Yahvé?
texts.2sa.6.10: De modo que David no quiso traer para sí el arca de Yahvé a la ciudad de David; y la hizo llevar David a casa de Obed-edom geteo.
texts.2sa.6.11: Y estuvo el arca de Yahvé en casa de Obed-edom geteo tres meses; y bendijo Yahvé a Obed-edom y a toda su casa.
texts.2sa.6.12: Fue dado aviso al rey David, diciendo: Yahvé ha bendecido la casa de Obed-edom y todo lo que tiene, a causa del arca de Dios. Entonces David fue, y trajo el arca de Dios de casa de Obed-edom a la ciudad de David con alegría.
texts.2sa.6.13: Y cuando los que llevaban el arca de Yahvé habían dado seis pasos, él sacrificó un buey y un carnero cebado.
texts.2sa.6.14: Y David danzaba con toda su fuerza delante de Yahvé; y estaba David vestido con un efod de lino.
texts.2sa.6.15: Así David y toda la casa de Israel conducían el arca de Yahvé con júbilo y sonido de trompeta.
texts.2sa.6.16: Cuando el arca de Yahvé llegó a la ciudad de David, aconteció que Mical hija de Saúl miró desde una ventana, y vio al rey David que saltaba y danzaba delante de Yahvé; y le menospreció en su corazón.
texts.2sa.6.17: Metieron, pues, el arca de Yahvé, y la pusieron en su lugar en medio de una tienda que David le había levantado; y sacrificó David holocaustos y ofrendas de paz delante de Yahvé.
texts.2sa.6.18: Y cuando David hubo acabado de ofrecer los holocaustos y ofrendas de paz, bendijo al pueblo en el nombre de Yahvé de los Ejércitos.
texts.2sa.6.19: Y repartió a todo el pueblo, y a toda la multitud de Israel, así a hombres como a mujeres, a cada uno una torta de pan, y un pedazo de carne y una torta de pasas. Y se fue todo el pueblo, cada uno a su casa.
texts.2sa.6.20: Volvió luego David para bendecir su casa; y saliendo Mical a recibir a David, dijo: ¡Cuán honrado ha quedado hoy el rey de Israel, descubriéndose hoy delante de las criadas de sus siervos, como se descubre desvergonzadamente un cualquiera!
texts.2sa.6.21: Entonces David respondió a Mical: Fue delante de Yahvé, quien me eligió preferido a tu padre y a toda tu casa, mandándome que fuese príncipe sobre el pueblo de Yahvé, sobre Israel. Por tanto, danzaré delante de Yahvé.
texts.2sa.6.22: Y aun me haré más vil que esta vez, y seré bajo a tus ojos; pero seré honrado delante de las criadas de quienes has hablado.
texts.2sa.6.23: Y Mical hija de Saúl nunca tuvo hijos hasta el día de su muerte.
texts.2sa.7.1: Aconteció que cuando el rey habitaba ya en su casa, y Yahvé le había dado reposo de todos sus enemigos alrededor,
texts.2sa.7.2: el rey dijo al profeta Natán: Mira ahora, yo habito en casa de cedro, y el arca de Dios está entre cortinas.
texts.2sa.7.3: Y Natán dijo al rey: Anda, y haz todo lo que está en tu corazón, pues Yahvé está contigo.
